It also announced plans to establish a Centre for AI. Along with Jaiswal, the 12th foundation day of the institute was presided over by Saurabh Garg, Secretary, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation MoSPI, as the chief guest. Several senior district administration officials and industry leaders also attended the event.

articleTitle: Kerala reopens probe against Gyanesh Kumar in 2006 graft case that saw Malaysian engineer’s suicide
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Police denies permission for Jantar Mantar protest over SIR issue, tightens security
description: The chief project manager of the road project had left a purported suicide note naming Kumar, who was the secretary of the state PWD at the time
body_raw: The Kerala Home Department has ordered the reopening of a Vigilance probe into alleged corruption in a road-related work from 2006 - when Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar served as the secretary of the state Public Works Department PWD. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala ordered a reinvestigation in the case, wherein a probe was launched against Kumar following the suicide of a Malaysian engineer, Lee See Been, who was then chief project manager of a major road work undertaken by PATI-BEL, an Indo-Malaysian venture, in the state. Kumars name had allegedly figured in two notes he purportedly left behind before dying by suicide in Kuala Lumpur. Kumar was sent to central deputation soon after. The road project, known as Kerala State Transport Project KSTP, was funded by the World Bank. Chennithala told the media on Sunday that he received a complaint alleging the 2006 Vigilance probe had been compromised under external pressure. I have directed the Vigilance to probe into the matter thoroughly. Gyanesh Kumars name had figured in the suicide note that the Malaysian engineer addressed to his wife and the company director. He said, Vigilance had examined the matter in 2006. However, the probe did not go ahead, although Kumar was transferred out of the PWD. Now, I have got a complaint from Congress leader Malayankeezhu Venugopal regarding the issue. I had discussed the matter with Chief Minister V D Satheesan and decided to order a comprehensive probe in this regard. The Indian Express reached out to the CEC and the EC spokesperson through email but did not receive a response. Senior CPIM leader M Vijayakumar, who had served as law minister in 2006 under the then V S Achuthanandan government, said Vigilance had begun probe into the matter, but no FIR was registered as the purported suicide notes were not made available in Kerala. Senior IUML leader M K Muneer, who was the state PWD minister from 2001 to 2006, said, It was being said that the engineer had left behind a suicide note. Nobody had seen it and what it contained. We do not know what he had written. Speaking to the media in Kozhikode, he said, A comprehensive probe is required into the entire issue. The then government led by the CPIM did not take the probe forward. I welcome it. Chennithala said that the 2006 probe was abandoned midway but Vigilance is capable of taking the probe ahead after two decades. When I get a complaint as the minister in charge of the Vigilance, I am duty-bound to order a probe, he said. PATI-BEL had undertaken the renovation of a few stretches of major roads in the state at a cost of Rs 216 crore. However, construction of the assigned roads got delayed due to alleged laxity in land acquisition from 2001 to 2006.

articleTitle: Concerns over women’s safety at Kolkata 5-star hotel after back-to-back arrests
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Man held for harassing woman at nightclub of 5-star hotel in Kolkata
description: The Kolkata police have arrested a 56-year-old Noida businessman for allegedly molesting two women from Nagaland in the lobby. Last week, the police had arrested a man for allegedly assaulting a woman at the hotel's nightclub.
body_raw: Safety concerns have surfaced at a luxury five-star hotel in Kolkata for the second time in a single week following the arrest of a 56-year-old man for allegedly molesting two women from Nagaland in the hotel lobby. The Kolkata police arrested Palash Ray, a businessman from Noida, after identifying and tracking him using CCTV footage. According to the Kolkata police, the incident took place between 12.30 am and 1 am Sunday, while the complainant and her companion were in the hotel lobby. The victims submitted a signed written complaint alleging that an unknown man touched them inappropriately, outraging their modesty. During the investigation, CCTV footage of the hotel lobby was thoroughly checked. The complainant duly identified the accused, and his movements were tracked down before he was apprehended from his room, a senior Kolkata police officer said, confirming that the investigation is ongoing. The police charged the accused with assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty. Second incident at same hotel The arrest marks the second serious criminal offence reported at the prominent luxury hotel within a week. In an earlier incident, the police arrested Mohammad Rafe Azim, 24, a resident of Beniapukur, for allegedly assaulting a 20-year-old woman and using obscene language inside the hotels nightclub around 2 am on September 27. In that case, the victim alleged that the accused and his associates blocked her path, physically assaulted her, and used abusive language before fleeing. That case was booked under charges of outraging modesty, insulting modesty of a woman, voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, and abetment. The police arrested him from Tiljala, and the probe is underway, Kunal Agarwal, Additional Commissioner of Police Crime, then said.

articleTitle: 5 gadgets I recommended to help my friends build the perfect WFH setup
articleFeaturedImageAlt: WFH gear
description: From the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i and Samsung Galaxy S26 FE to the Logitech MK250 keyboard, here are five gadgets to give your work-from-home setup a makeover.
body_raw: A month ago, two of my friends told me they were off to South Goa and Pabbar Valley. I assumed it was a short trip to recharge after their hectic work schedules. But then they told me they had recently switched to freelancing gigs with a US-based company and wanted to temporarily move away from the city, working remotely from offbeat locations instead. More and more people in my circle are either becoming independent contributors or choosing freelancing over full-time work. Maybe thats what the future of work looks like in the AI era. In fact, during a recent group video call, my friends, who are all writers and editors but arent tech nerds like me, asked about the essential tech they would need to set up a work-from-home WFH space and give their workspaces a makeover. As someone who travels frequently for work and occasionally works from home, I know what its like to work remotely. Based on my own experience of working from home on a regular basis, I have found that you need the right gear and other essentials to stay productive and comfortable. I recommended five gadgets, including essential peripherals, to my friends to help them set up their home offices-and tested them over several weeks. The list includes the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i, Samsung Galaxy S26 FE, Logitech MK250 keyboard and mouse combo, Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 earbuds, and Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W. Together, I feel these devices helped them build a mobile office that allows them to work productively from virtually anywhere Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i 15-inch, Intel Ultra 5 322 processor Rs 1,17,791 A computer is the bare minimum for setting up a mobile office at home, whether you are a developer, coder, or writer. Since my friends are writers, I recommended the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i, which I tested for several weeks. This is a mid-tier Windows laptop and has its share of flaws but my overall experience has been pretty impressive. Perhaps one of the most impressive things about the IdeaPad Slim 3i is its keyboard. I have spent the past week typing on it, including most of this review, and at no point have I felt that the keyboard was underwhelming. For writers, the keyboard is where their hands live, so it had to be good. The trackpad is good, although its missing haptic feedback. The chip is an Intel Core Ultra 5 322 processor, one of Intels newer processors. In everyday use, its plenty fast. Browsing, writing, email, SlackWhatsApp, video calls, light photo editing, dozens of browser tabs, a music app - all running together-were handled without complaint. The 16GB RAM is the one that most likely matter to most people, since companies these days are shipping laptops with 8GB RAM due to memory crisis. The 15.3-inch display isnt colour-graded for creative work, nor does it have an OLED panel, but its sharp, bright, and pleasant to use. To my surprise, the battery lasted 12 hours, which is enough to get through a full workday on a single charge with the brightness at a usable level and meaningful workloads running. Where I do have a few complaints about the IdeaPad Slim 3i is its build quality, which lacks a premium feel. The chassis isnt as refined as the MacBook Air, which is a letdown considering the notebooks asking price of over a lakh. At 1.5kg, the notebook is reasonably portable. It can easily be slipped into a backpack and carried while travelling. However, when it comes to design, it reminds me of notebooks from the pre-Covid era. The IdeaPad Slim 3i isnt a cheap laptop, and its asking price may seem high. But honestly, if you are in the market for a new laptop, almost every notebook can feel overpriced these days. I will leave the final decision to my readers. That being said, I do think the IdeaPad Slim 3i is a laptop for normal people. It delivers on the things that matter without making unnecessary compromises. For most people, the IdeaPad Slim 3i could be the answer. Samsung Galaxy S26 FERs 72,999 onwards When my friends asked me which smartphone they should buy, two options immediately came to mind. However, this time around, they wanted to stick to their budget while also looking for a phone that would last for several years and still have a premium feel. Its a shame about the recent price increase, but even at the new price, my top pick remains the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE for a reason. The S26 FE has the looks that matches the latest flagship S26 devices, meaning the phone has the same glass back and the triple-camera island on the back at the top left. I liked the design and build of the device. It has aluminum sides and an all- flat screen and a an IP68 rating that can survive a dunk in water. The phone has a 6.7-inch OLED display, which is impressive, and supports a smooth 120Hz refresh rate. I wish it came with an LTPO panel, as that would allow the refresh rate to automatically adjust from 1Hz to 120Hz, helping to conserve battery life. The peak brightness is also good, at around 1,900 nits. Inside, theres an Exynos 2500, Samsungs own processor, which I found to deliver better performance and efficiency than the S25 FEs Exynos 2400. For everyday tasks such as browsing, gaming, and photography, I found the performance to be reasonably good. The S26 FEs 256GB of storage and 8GB of RAM may feel limiting for some users, especially those who take a lot of photos or play demanding games. Unfortunately, this is the only configuration available in India. I wish Samsung had offered a 12GB RAM variant, even at a higher price. At least then, consumers would have had the option to choose. The 4,900-mAh battery can easily last a day on a single charge. The phone supports 45-watt wired charging or 15-watt wireless charging. And while its is Qi2-compatible, there are no magnets for easy docking. Samsungs One UI 9 is clean, highly customisable, and comes with a number of AI features. I particularly liked Now Brief, which creates a personalised feed combining weather, health updates, videos, and calendar events throughout the day. The S26 FE retains the same camera setup as last year, with a 50MP main camera, 12MP ultrawide, 8MP telephoto, and 12MP selfie camera. Dont expect it to beat the S26 Ultra or iPhone 18 Pro Max- it simply isnt in the same league. However, I liked the picture quality I got in broad daylight, with plenty of detail, sharpness, and a good dynamic range. I also noticed improvements to the night mode, as well as the phones video-recording capabilities. The telephoto camera, which supports 3x optical zoom, is another useful addition, particularly for capturing subjects from a distance without sacrificing too much detail. The S26 FE is a really good phone if youre an Android user. Its not a flagship-grade device, but its a solid choice for the average user looking for a semi-premium smartphone. Keep an eye out for deals and discounts on the S26 FE in the coming days, and you may be able to get the device for even less. Logitech MK250 Rs 2195 One of my friends had been working from home for five years when he started experiencing neck pain. He was advised to raise his laptop to eye level and use a standalone keyboard and mouse. I have tried a variety of keyboards over the years, and a few days ago, the new Logitech MK250 caught my eye. This is a wireless keyboard and mouse combo that costs just Rs 2,195. The best part is that I dont have to worry about USB dongles anymore. Both the keyboard and mouse connect via Bluetooth, so neither device takes up a USB port. The MK250s Bluetooth connectivity is especially useful on modern laptops with limited ports. It keeps both USB-C ports free for charging and other accessories, while allowing me to easily switch the keyboard and mouse between a laptop, tablet, and desktop without having to search for or carry a USB receiver. The keyboard features a full-size layout with a dedicated number pad. If you work with spreadsheets or frequently enter numerical values, having a dedicated number pad makes data entry much faster. The keys are spacious and quiet to type on, making the keyboard suitable for both home-office and open-office environments. The mouse is ergonomically shaped to fit either hand. It uses optical tracking for smooth movement across various surfaces, including desks, tables, and mouse pads. It has three buttons, which should be enough for most people, while the scroll wheel provides smooth and precise scrolling without requiring you to click through every line. Both devices are battery-powered, but the battery life should be long enough that you will forget they even need batteries. Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 Rs 29,990 While finalising the list, I came across a pair of old-school headphones with a built-in microphone that I initially wanted to recommend to my friends. But after hearing about their typical day and their love for music, I thought the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 might be the perfect fit for them, which I also happen to test them for weeks. The Momentum True Wireless 5 are expensive pair of wireless earbuds, but they provide the best audio quality of any true wireless earbuds I have tried recently and a reasonably better noise cancellation. The Momentum 5s have a sleeker, more rounded design that makes them comfortable to wear for hours. They arent designed for intense workouts, but they are well suited to everyday activities such as walking. I tested the Copper colourway and liked its distinctive look, which stands out from Apples AirPods Pro and Sonys wireless earbuds. The earbuds have an IP54 rating for dust and water resistance, so they should be fine in most everyday conditions. The outer shell of the earbuds features capacitive touch controls that work extremely well. The controls can be customised for single, double, and triple taps, as well as tap-and-hold gestures. Where I think they really shine is in audio quality. They feature 7mm TrueResponse dynamic transducers. While the specifications may look similar to those of their predecessor, I found that software and processing improvements have helped improve the overall sound quality. In my testing, the Momentum 5s performed particularly well with pop and dance music. Madonnas Danceteria and Mikas Relax, Take It Easy sounded excellent, with well-balanced vocals. The bass is deep, while the highs are crisp and clear. The Sennheiser Smart Control Plus app offers basic EQ settings, which I found adequate but nothing exceptional. The earbuds also support aptX codecs and offer Hi-Res and Lossless audio modes for better sound quality. However, these settings can cause connection dropouts, especially in crowded or busy areas. They can last up to 40 hours on a single charge with the included charging case. The Momentum TW 5 also delivers improved noise cancellation, providing stronger noise isolation without relying as much on a tight seal. That being said, Apple and Bose are still ahead of Sennheiser when it comes to delivering superior noise cancellation. Overall, I felt the Momentum True Wireless 5 offer the best of both worlds, delivering impressive sound quality and effective noise cancellation. They are a premium pair of wireless earbuds that offer luxe features such as Dolby Atmos for a more immersive listening experience, as well as a replaceable battery that helps extend their lifespan. Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W Rs 5499 Once, I was working remotely from the hills, and I vividly remember it was dusk. There was no power, and the deadline for submitting my story was fast approaching. That day, what saved me was the portable laptop charger I had with me, something I never thought I would need it. Since then, I have always kept a long-lasting power bank with me, and I recommend one to my friends who work remotely or from home. The latest addition to my mobile workflow is the Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W, which was recently launched in India for Rs 5,499. I have it and been testing it for a week or so. With a boxy form factor, the power bank is technically pocketable, but I would recommend keeping it in a sling bag or backpack. The design is quite nice- it feels premium and solid, while the glass front with the built-in display adds to its appeal. The screen is operated using a button that is large, indented, and easy to find without looking. One press turns on the display, allowing you to scroll through battery information. The power bank comes with a compact USB-C cable capable of supporting charging speeds of up to 120W. The second USB-C port on the side can deliver up to 45W to another device. Performance from the Xiaomi 20,000mAh Power Bank has been solid. The 20,000mAh capacity is enough to charge two smartphones alongside a MacBook Air and AirPods and a smartwatch. The power bank supports up to 165W charging and a range of standards, including PD 3.0 with PPS and QC 2.0, 3.0, and 3.5. For me, though, the screen on the power bank is the real star of the show. Sure, it isnt necessary for a power bank, but its the easiest way I have seen to check how much battery remains or how long the power bank will take to recharge. Another good thing is that I can fly with the power bank, though it depends on the rules set by each airline.

articleTitle: NEET PG answer keys out, but candidates call it ‘eyewash’; here’s why
articleFeaturedImageAlt: NEET PG answer keys out, but candidates call it 'eyewash'; here is why
description: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences earlier said it would release the answer keys and candidates' response sheets to comply with a Supreme Court order ensuring transparency.
body_raw: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences NBEMS has released the answer keys for NEET PG 2026, the postgraduate medical entrance examination held on August 30 and September 5. Earlier this week, the NBEMS clarified that it issued candidates scorecards along with section-wise question IDs and their corresponding answer keys. Soon after the answer keys were released, candidates who had initially welcomed the move found themselves questioning the boards approach to disclosure. While the document included candidates responses alongside the questions and answers, the release of the answer keys, with only the question IDs and other limited details visible, left many questioning how far the move actually went in ensuring transparency. On social media, several candidates described the exercise as eyewash and merely a formality, arguing that making only the question IDs available did little to clarify the evaluation process and, in some cases, only added to the confusion. Also Read NEET PG 2026 cut-off falls to 6-year low Why does it change? The NBEMS had earlier announced through the NEET PG 2026 information bulletin that it would release the answer keys and candidates response sheets in compliance with the Supreme Courts April 29, 2025, order that directed the board to make raw scores, answer keys, and normalisation details publicly available to ensure transparency. Speaking to indianexpress.com, a 30-year-old aspirant from Jaipur and a former junior resident at Guru Nanak Eye Centre, New Delhi, said, I was hopeful that when the answer keys are out, if I am not able to make the cut-offs, I will still be able to understand where I lost marks. This would help in preparing for any subsequent rounds. What is visible in NEET PG 2026 answer keys? As announced by the NBEMS and as confirmed by candidates, upon accessing the answer keys in the candidate login, only these fields are shown - Section-wise question IDs in the sequence in which they appeared in the candidates question paper. - Status of each response, including whether the question was answered or not attempted. - Correct answer key ID 1234 for every question. - Response marked by the candidate against each question. - Score awarded for each question as per the examination scheme. Why are these details insufficient for candidates? The aspirant clarifies, In NEET PG, the order in which the questions and their options appear is not the same for all candidates. During the actual exam, the questions are shuffled within the section. Examination authorities often resort to jumbling the order of questions and answer options to protect the tests integrity and, to a large extent, restrict chances of malpractice. According to the aspirant, Since the sequence of questions within a section was shuffled, question IDs and their corresponding correct option ID appeared differently for candidates. We have no way of knowing or recalling which question ID is against what actual question, and what we have answered. Also Read NMC releases institute and course-wise seat matrix While the NBEMS has released the correct answer key ID, the information remains irrelevant for candidates because the explicit questions and their correct answers have not been disclosed. Without knowing the exact question and its corresponding correct answer, candidates cannot independently verify whether the answer has been marked correctly. Another candidate, a practising junior doctor at a hospital in Madhya Pradesh, told Indianexpress.com that other nationally organised public entrance and qualifying exams issue answer keys where the questions and their answers are visible to candidates. CUET UG and PG, NEET UG, JEE Mains and Advanced - all these exams issue answer keys. Why can we not expect the same rigour for NEET-PG? he said. Can candidates raise objections? Neither of the notices issued by the NBEMS on September 24 and October 1 mentions an objection window or any procedure for candidates to challenge the answers. In its circular issued on September 24, the board said, Each and every question asked in both the question papers of NEET PG 2026 was reviewed by faculty members from the concerned speciality area after the conduct of NEET-PG 2026 to recheck for technical correctness of the questions as well as answer keys. The board announced that none of the questions was found technically incorrect, further eliminating any provision for candidates to challenge the question paper. IMA official challenges answer key in Supreme Court Meanwhile, Dr Dhruv Chauhan, national spokesperson of the Indian Medical Associations Junior Doctors Network IMA-JDN and founder of the Legal Cell for All India Doctors, has moved the Supreme Court with a public interest litigation PIL challenging the NEET-PG 2026 answer keys. The petition seeks greater transparency in the evaluation process, demanding that the complete question paper be made available along with the corresponding answers and the options actually marked by candidates, rather than merely the serial numbers of the questions and responses. Dr Chauhan told indianexpress.com, The aspirants wanted only one thing, that is transparency in the exam. He added, Our legal team will pursue this in the larger benefit of the medical students, and have also called for a time-bound objection window to address any discrepancies. With the matter now before the Supreme Court, candidates await clarity on whether directions will be issued to make the complete question paper and answer details available, and whether that happens before counselling begins.

articleTitle: ‘Lacklustre, sleepy, sluggish…’: Brazilian media on 4-0 win over India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vinicius played in the first half of the match between India and Brazil. (Express Photo by Partha Paul)
description: Brazilian media didn't seem to be too impressed with the national team's 4-0 win over India at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata.
body_raw: Brazil beat India 4-0 in the first-ever senior mens football friendly between the two sides at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata. While that scoreline normally points out to a thrashing, in this case, it was a respectable scoreline for India. Ranked 138th in the world, India have never even come close to qualifying for the World Cup since they qualified by default for the 1950 edition before withdrawing. Brazil, on the other hand, are famously the most succesfull team in the history of the competiton and ranked sixth in the world. This reality seems to have not escaped the Brazilian media either, in which a majority of the opinions expressed after the match seemed to be criticising the Selecao. UOL, an outlet owned by the Folha group which is among Brazils media conglomerates, said Once again failing to impress, the Brazilian national team thrashed the weak India team - ranked 138th in the FIFA rankings - 4-0 in a routine manner in Kolkata. Even against a weak opponent, the Brazilian team started the match in a sleepy, sluggish, and uninspired manner. Vini Jr. had plenty of space on the left, but couldnt take advantage of it and made mistakes in his playmaking. Translated from Portuguese. Terra news said that Brazil left a lot to be desired in their win over one of the weakest rivals the Canarinhos have ever faced. Leading daily O Globo says that the match looked like a training session and that Brazil lacked offensive impetus. Despite their superiority and the scoreline, the Brazilian team failed to translate their control of the match into offensive numbers, creating few chances throughout the game, said the report. Former Former Brazil midfielder Felipe Melo was critical of how they played in this game and the two friendlies they played in Australia before that. Brazil only managed to draw the first of the two matches 1-1, which was their first game after their stunning 2-1 defeat to Norway in the World Cup round of 16. They won the second match 4-2. Brazil has been taking steps backward. The first game against Australia was below what they showed in the World Cup, the second, even though they improved, was also below par. And this third game, despite four goals, was also below par. Im hopeful that Brazil will improve, but in practice, theyve regressed compared to their last World Cup game against Norway, said Melo on Sportv. Melo accepted the fact that the Brazilians may not be used to playing in the kind of humidity that they had to deal with in Kolkata. However, the former Inter Milan midfielder felt that the players didnt seem to have the right attitude. A guy can play badly, but he needs to have the right attitude. Martinelli came on and showed attitude, as did others. Samuel Lino had a bit more attitude and scored two goals. If he had more time, he would have scored more, Melo concluded. Trivela, the Brazilian football news outlet, questioned the sense behind the match for the Brazilian Football Confederation CBF, considering the empty seats that could be seen at the stadium. A lackluster 4-0 victory for the Brazilian team marked the friendly against India this Saturday. It will be a friendly match remembered for failing to achieve even the main objective of the Brazilian Football Confederation CBF, wrote Trivelas report Carlos Vinicius Amorim in the piece. The stadium not being very full raises questions about the CBFs choice. The friendly match in India is justifiable, something long awaited by the population, but only if it were affordable for fans. The report goes on to state that a number of regions in Brazil has not hosted the national teams matches for decades. Instead of playing twice in Australia and once in India with inaccessible tickets, they could serve the population of some of these states. Furthermore, the president of the CBF Brazilian Football Confederation, Samir Xaud, promised to get closer to the Brazilian people after the World Cup. For now, its just talk, the piece concluded.

articleTitle: ‘Organised and difficult’: Carlo Ancelotti on India after Brazil’s 4-0 victory
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vinicius Junior in action against India at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on Saturday. (Express photo by Partha Paul)
description: Brazil are currently the world’s 6th ranked team while India are languishing in 138th spot. Despite that, Brazil only opened the scoring in the 28th minute
body_raw: The Indian football teams friendly against five-time world champions Brazil ended with a 4-0 scoreline in favour of the visitors at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on Saturday, but Selecao boss Carlo Ancelotti praised the Indian team for being organised and making it difficult for them to score their opening goal. Brazil are currently the worlds 6th ranked team while India are languishing in 138th spot. Despite that, Brazil only opened the scoring in the 28th minute, through a goal from Estevao. Then, the floodgates opened. A goal from Pedro ensured the teams went to the half-time break with Brazil leading 2-0. Samuel Lino scored a second half brace to complete the rout. India played their part well. They tried to play their game they defended, they were organised, they tried to play counter-attack. I think that they played a good game. We had difficulty opening the score, but the moment we opened the score with Estevao, we had more opportunities to control the game better, Ancelotti said at the post-match press conference. We feel good. It was a good experience. I think it was a good game, entertaining, with good intensity, and India did their part. Talking about his own team, Ancelotti said I think we defended well. We could have defended better if we had a couple of chances in the counter-attack, but I think for us its important not to concede a goal. Obviously we have to improve some mechanisms in defence, but we had a new defence that never played together, so maybe not everything was perfect. Again, the message is that we are happy to be here. We tried to do our best we tried to show our best quality to all the people who love Brazil and love football, and I hope they enjoyed the night.

articleTitle: After ‘black day’ over women’s safety, Ahmedabad’s Nirma university steps up security
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nirma University students hold Black day protest, Nirma University Black day protest, Nirma Black day protest, Ahmedabad news, Gujarat news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Students observed a “black day” alleging inaction by Nirma University over their complaint about a construction worker’s objectionable behaviour towards women on campus.
body_raw: Ahmedabads Nirma University has imposed stricter control over construction workers movement on campus following a massive protest against alleged inaction after a worker engaged in objectionable behaviour towards women students. On Thursday, students observed a black day in protest against the private universitys administration over a complaint they had filed over the incident reported on September 29. A video of the incident was shared on social media, raising concerns about women students safety on campus. In the first official statement issued since the incident, the universitys executive registrar stated that the police registered an FIR after the university immediately informed them and that all investigations and action regarding the incident are being carried out appropriately. However, women residents of the hostel said that when they reported the incident to the female security staff, they were told not to wear shorts inside the hostel. They also alleged that the university administration ignored their complaint. Net cloth around girls hostel One of the students said that instead of taking action against the worker, the authorities installed a green net cloth around the girls hostel. The university has further strengthened its security arrangements and imposed stricter control over the movement of workers at the construction site, the statement added. According to the university statement, the worker was on the ninth floor of the construction site of the new H5 hostel building, which is approximately 100 feet away from the H4 girls hostel. Investigation into incident involving professor This is the second incident at the university where students have raised concerns about their safety. H K Patel, a professor associated with the electronics and instrumentation course, allegedly grabbed a student by the collar and threatened him during an event on September 19. The statement added that the university has constituted a three-member inquiry committee in connection with the incident and that the investigation is in progress. It is also noteworthy that both parties had apologised to each other on 21 September 2026 and no complaint had been submitted to the university, the statement said.

articleTitle: 10 am to 5 pm: Karnataka High Court fixes parole window for murder convicts’ wedding
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court murder convicts parole wedding
description: Observing that moral objections cannot override legal entitlements, the Karnataka High Court granted a seven-hour parole window to two life convicts who murdered the woman's husband so they can marry.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court last week granted a limited one-day parole to two life convicts, a man and a woman convicted of conspiring and murdering the womans husband, allowing them to solemnise their marriage. The court observed that moral objections cannot override a legal entitlement when no statutory prohibition exists. Justice MG S Kamal at the Dharwad bench passed the order on September 28 on a writ petition filed by Shridhar Arjun Talawar and Siddavva alias Priyanka Jagamutti, both aged 23 and residents of Bhairanatti in Mudalagi taluk, Belagavi district. Currently lodged in the Belagavi central jail, the duo sought directions for their release or, alternatively, 90 days of general parole to conduct their marriage and related ceremonies. Siddavva was married to Shankar Siddappa Jagamutti, 25, but developed a relationship with Sridhar Talawar. Considering Shankar an obstacle to their relationship, the duo conspired to eliminate him. On July 17, 2023, shortly after Shankars birthday, Shridhar stabbed Shankar to death at a temple with Siddavvas assistance before fleeing. Following their arrest, a local court in Belagavi district convicted both of murder on July 30, 2024, sentencing them to life imprisonment alongside a fine of Rs 3 lakh. Moral question and legal rights Addressing the unique circumstances, the High Court noted that the petitioners decision to marry aligns with the prosecutions original conspiracy theory regarding their motive. The petitioners have now decided to get married, which was indeed the conspiracy theory proposed by the prosecution. This poses a moral question as to whether they are entitled to parole to get married when the accusation against them was that they had conspired to eliminate the husband of petitioner No.2 Siddavva. However, legally, there is no such prohibition. Moral consciousness cannot overtake the legal entitlement to get married, the order stated. The court further noted that the right to marry serves a recognised social function and cannot be denied purely on moral considerations in the absence of explicit statutory bars. While the state government argued that the prison manual contains no provisions for granting parole on marriage grounds, it also confirmed upon the courts query that jail regulations do not permit solemnising marriages within prison premises. The court directed prison authorities to grant parole between 10 am and 5 pm on a date chosen by the petitioners, subject to administrative convenience. An adequate number of police personnel, to be deputed by the jailer, shall accompany the petitioners and remain present during the ceremony. The petitioners must be returned to jail by 5 pm on that day, the court directed.

articleTitle: ‘Had 27 paise in his pocket’: Shabana Azmi recalls Javed Akhtar’s early struggles in Mumbai
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shabana Azmi celebrates 62 years of Javed Akhtar moving to Mumbai.
description: Shabana Azmi marked 62 years since her husband, veteran poet, screenwriter and lyricist Javed Akhtar, first arrived in Mumbai with just 27 paise in his pocket.
body_raw: On this day, 62 years ago, veteran screenwriter, lyricist, and poet Javed Akhtar first stepped foot into Mumbai. He left home in Gwalior, Uttar Pradesh, and took a train to Mumbai, the proverbial city of dreams, getting down at the Mumbai Central station on October 4, 1964. More than six decades later, his wife and veteran actor Shabana Azmi celebrated the occasion with an Instagram post on Sunday. Shabana Azmi recalls Javed Akhtars early Mumbai days 4th Oct 1964. A young lad arrived at Bombay Central Station with 27 naye paise in his pocket but with big dreams in his eyes, wrote Shabana in the Instagram caption, along with the picture of a young Javed Akhtar. Life gave him several hard knocks. He slept on the footpaths, at the railway stations, and in the compound of many a studio. A day came when he had nothing to eat for 3 days and the only clothes he had were the shreds on his body, she added. Recalling how Javed refused to give up despite those hardships, Shabana continued, On the edge of despair, when he could have given up, he said to himself, Main yunhi marne ke liye nahin paida nahin hua tha. Yeh din badlenge I wasnt born to die like just like that. These days will change, as they did. 4th October, 1964 a 19-year-old, almost penniless. 4th October, 2026, decades later a life that has given India some of its most memorable words. This is the story of Javed Akhtar. Shabana Azmi ended the post by turning Javed Akhtars journey into a message of hope for others Some journeys begin with almost nothing. Except a dream. If he can do it, so can you. Never give up. In the comments section of the video, celebrities including Javed Akhtars daughter and filmmaker Zoya Akhtar, actors Hrithik Roshan, Dia Mirza, Divya Dutta, and Amruta Subhash, among others, shared red heart emojis. The boy continues to dream and build fire emoji, commented music composer Ankur Tewari. Javed Akhtar on his early days of struggle In the 2024 Amazon Prime Video India docuseries Angry Young Men, Javed Akhtar also looked back at his early days of struggle in Mumbai. I decided that after my graduation, Id go to Mumbai and work as an assistant director, hopefully with either Guru Dutt or Raj Kapoor. I was sure that after a couple of years of doing this, Id definitely become a director, he recalled. After living with his father and legendary poet Jan Nisar Akhtar, Javed then moved out and slept wherever he found a place, from friends homes to railways stations, parks, studio compounds, corridors, and benches. Some days, Id walk all the way from Dadar to Bandra, because I didnt have money for bus fare. Some days, it would strike me that I hadnt eaten for two days. I would always think to myself that if one day, a biography were to be written about me, this would make for an incredible moment, he added. After Javed Akhtar swore to himself that hed see better days, better days did follow. Eventually, he joined forces with Salim Khan to become arguably Indias most formidable writer duo. Salim-Javed wrote seminal films like Hathi Mere Sathi 1971, Yaadon Ki Baaraat 1973, Seeta Aur Geeta 1973, Zanjeer 1973, Deewaar 1975, Sholay 1975, Don 1978, Trishul 1978, Shaan 1980, and Shakti 1982, among others. However, Javed confessed that the days of hunger left such an indelible impact on his psyche that even after having all the luxuries in the world today, hes unable to believe its true at times. I stay in five-star hotels, in huge suites with large double beds. And I look back on how I came to Mumbai, in a third-class compartment that didnt even have any room to sit. I remember how I was deprived of sleep, and how tired I was. All I needed was a fraction of the room I had now, he said. Also Read - So we dont end up in jail Kapil Sharma on why he watches younger comics The veteran poet also admitted that he still experiences imposter syndrome and sometimes feels as though he is having an out-of-body experience while enjoying the luxuries he has earned after a lifetime of hard work. They bring out so much food, and I always wonder where this food was on the days I had nothing to eat. To this day, I feel like I havent deserved this food. I cant get over that, he added, teary-eyed, in the docuseries.

articleTitle: ‘I danced wearing frocks on local stages in Agra’: Dupahiya 2 actor Sparsh Shrivastava
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sparsh Shrivastava
description: In Dupahiya, Sparsh Shrivastava’s character Bhugol Jha is an aspiring actor who makes reels dressed as a girl to attract followers.
body_raw: Dupahiya Season 2, set in the fictional village of Dhadakpur in Bihar, is now streaming on Amazon Prime Video. Ahead of the seasons premiere, Sparsh Shrivastava and Renuka Shahane opened up about the preparation that went into playing Bhugol Jha and Pushpalata Yadav, respectively, in the show. Elated by the comment, Sparsh looked at the camera and recorded a message for his mother Mom, you always wanted a daughter, right? Asked if he faced any challenges while portraying a girl, the 27-year-old shared, I think they were already within me because when I was small, my mother taught me the dance form, Kathak. Ive learned Kathak for three years. So those gestures, that grace was already there somewhere. In childhood, I even danced wearing frocks on local stages in Agra. So, I think it was always there somewhere down the line. But its been a really long time since I practiced that art form again. Watch the full video interview with Dupahiya Season 2 cast and crew here Despite his early training in Kathak, Sparsh said getting back into the groove for the role took some time. The Vibe actor shared, So when I started rehearsing this time and the last time in season one when we did it, it was a bit taxing, but slowly I got it right. But you know, the most difficult part is wearing the exact dress, the ghagra, choli, and that blouse is so tight. And how it fits, I mean, its very tough to be in that outfit. So, hats off to all the girls. The actor admitted that mastering the Bihari dialect was challenging for her and said that, as a Maharashtrian, it took her some time to become familiar with it. So, we had a language expert, Ravi ji, who trained me. He trained me the most because I was the least familiar with the dialect. And it took me a long time to get comfortable with the accent. And finally, now its so in me now that sometimes I speak Hindi like that. Because I find it so interesting that you can say the most hard-hitting things, and say it in a way, succinctly its delightful. So, now I am very comfortable. articleTitle: ‘Sent 6.3 ft cake in tempo’: How Tips Music won over Subhash Ghai after Saudagar rejection
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ramesh Taurani, Subhash Ghai, Prakash Jha and Mahesh Thakur at an event
description: In a recent interview, Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani recalled why Subhash Ghai did not give Tips the music rights to his 1991 film Saudagar. They also revealed how they convinced the filmmaker to rope in Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes.
body_raw: Tips Music, co-founded by brothers Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani, has released several hit soundtracks from Subhash Ghais films, including Khal Nayak 1993, Pardes 1997, Taal 1999 and Yaadein 2001. In a recent interview, the Taurani brothers recalled why Ghai did not give Tips the music rights to his 1991 film Saudagar. They also revealed how they convinced the filmmaker to rope in composer duo Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes. When the Saudagar cassette was released, we sent Subhash ji a 6-foot-3-inch cake During a chat with Komal Nahta, Ramesh Taurani recalled approaching Subhash Ghai before he sold the music of his film Saudagar to HMV. Subhash jis film Saudagars music wasnt sold yet, but he told me that he had commited to HMV. I asked him to give the music to us, so he asked me to come next time. He gave the music to them. When the Saudagar cassette was released, we sent Subhash ji a 6-foot-3-inch cake, which said, Saudagar, Saudagar, TIPS ke saath Sauda kar, he shared. When the cake reached his house, the filmmaker was very happy and promised to sign Tips Music for his next film. My associate went to deliver the cake, but it wasnt fitting in a car, so it got delivered in a tempo. He Subhash Ghai went to his house, he was so happy, and he called all the distributors to his house at night. He praised me in front of them, saying that this man doesnt have my music or anything, but still sent such a beautiful letter to me with a cake, Ramesh said. Later, Ramesh Taurani reached out to Subhash Ghai for the music rights of Khalnayak. Then, I went to him for Khalnayak. Subhash ji told me that all the distributors had asked him to take Nadeem-Shravan instead of Laxmikant-Pyarelal for the film. Subhash ji called Nadeem, but he kept negotiating on the price. Subhash ji got angry that he was not talking about music but only money. He eventually went to Laxmikant ji and said that hes ready to pay double the amount. He signed him on by paying a token amount of Rs 5 lakh, he recalled. While Ramesh lied to his brother Kumar Taurani about the actual price demanded by Laxmikant, the success of the song Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai made everything fruitful. Finally, Laxmi ji said that I will not take less than Rs 1 crore. I asked him to take Rs 70, 80 lakhs. Kumar had said that we wont pay more than Rs 75 lakhs. I gave him a nod for Rs 1 crore. When I came back, I told Kumar that the deal was done in Rs 81 lakhs. He complained why I paid Rs 6 lakhs over and above the decided amount. As soon as I left Subhash jis office, the news was everywhere in the media, Khalnayaks music has been sold at Rs 1 crore. I told Kumar that it is false news, he said. The producer continued, When Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai was released, it was a superhit the same day without any promotions. We released the song in the morning and it was being played in a party at night. I told Kumar that we will have to pay Rs 10 lakhs more because the song is already a hit. Years later, Subhash Ghai considered Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes, but his previous experience with the duo made him wary of negotiating their fees. Later, when Trimurti and its music flopped, Subhash Ghai asked for my advice for his film Pardes. He took the names of 2-3 music directors and asked for my suggestion, I told him to take Nadeem-Shravan. He then told me the Saudagar story. I gave him the guarantee that Nadeem will not talk money with you he will just received whatever youll give, Ramesh Taurani shared. Ramesh further added, I spoke to Nadeem and told him to do Subhash jis film without talking about his fees, and he agreed. He said, You will give me the money, na. He had the perspective that if hes giving great music, he should get his due. Everyone used to complain that his music is repetitive, but still everyone went back to him because it used to work. The best part about Pardes music was that it had Subhash Ghais touch. The music of Pardes, Khalnayak and Saudagar, all directed by filmmaker Subhash Ghai, was hugely successful.
