articleTitle: Disenfranchising millions arbitrary, no whataboutery can justify it: SC judge
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan warns wholesale disenfranchisement under Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls violates Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution
description: “From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters' list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body,” Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said
body_raw: Amid the row over the SIR of electoral rolls against which petitions have been filed in the Supreme Court, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, a judge of the top court, said Sunday that any process that leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of the Constitution. No amount of whataboutery can justify it, he said. Justice Bhuyan said detaching an Indian citizen from the right to vote would be akin to taking out the soul from the body. Speaking at the valedictory ceremony of Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court competition at Nalsar University of Law, Hyderabad, he said, If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second-class citizens in their own country, in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order, which we have adopted under the Constitution of India, he said. Speaking on the significance of universal adult suffrage, especially in the context of India, Justice Bhuyan said, From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body. He said the earliest articulation of adult franchise in India can be traced to the Constitution of India Bill, 1895, also known as the Swaraj Bill. Speaking about the debate in the Constituent Assembly on universal adult suffrage, he said, In the draft Constitution, which was debated by the Constituent Assembly, there were two articles of relevance, though included subsequently. These were Articles 289A and 289B. Draft Article 289A became Article 325 and draft Article 289B became Article 326 of the Constitution of India. Article 326 gives meaning and content to the equality principle enshrined in Article 14. Article 325 of the Constitution of India declares that there shall be one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency for election to the Lok Sabha or to the Legislature of a State no person shall be ineligible for inclusion in any such roll or claim to be included in any electoral roll for any such constituency on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or any of them. As per Article 326 of the Constitution, election to the Lok Sabha and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage. In other words, every person who is a citizen of India and who is not less than 18 years of age prior to March 28, 1989, it was 21 years and who is not disqualified under the Constitution of India or by any law made by the appropriate legislature on the ground of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice, shall be entitled to be registered as a voter at any such election, he said. Quoting Dr B R Ambedkar, Justice Bhuyan said, Justifying universal adult suffrage, Dr Ambedkar said since we have taken a very important decision, which practically nullifies the past, it is better that the Constitution should, in express terms, state it is the basis for insertion of Articles 289A and 289B in the draft Constitution, which are now Articles 325 and 326. Dr Ambedkars closing speech warned that the right to vote and the Indian citizens entitlement to adult suffrage should be written into the Constitution of India, instead of being left to the whims of parliamentary legislation, he said. Justice Bhuyan said, Adoption of universal adult franchise reflects the determined opinion of the Constituent Assembly that years of freedom struggle and the revolt against foreign rule made the adoption of universal adult franchise a natural choice and an essential ingredient of democracy, which we have adopted as the form of governance. Therefore, it was an act of faith for our founding fathers in the common man of India and in his pragmatism and wisdom. It was the first step taken to achieve equality in India. One may be a billionaire, and one may be a rickshaw-puller. Yet both will have their votes, and the value of their votes would be equal. Likewise, a socially high-placed temple priest on the one hand and a person belonging to the lowest strata of the society compelled to work as a manual scavenger have an equal vote with equal value. This is the transformational vision of the Indian Constitution, he said. In his concluding remarks, he congratulated Nalsar students for being what students, especially law students, should be.

articleTitle: Kumkum, Sujeet named inaugural recipients of Jaspal Rana & Raja Randhir Singh awards
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Archer Kumkum Mohor and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal with their medals at Asian Games 2026. (AP)
description: IOA honours the two standout performers of India's Asian Games campaign in Aichi-Nagoya
body_raw: Archer Kumkum Anil Mohod and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal have been named the first-ever recipients of the Jaspal Rana Award and the Raja Randhir Singh Award respectively by the Indian Olympic Association, in recognition of their performances at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The awards have been instituted by the IOA to honour the best female and male sportspersons of the Games, and to commemorate the legacy of two stalwarts of Indian sport who passed away earlier this year. Kumkum, 17, making her Asian Games debut, claimed three medals, including two gold, and was central to ending South Koreas long-standing dominance in womens recurve archery. Alongside Ankita Bhakat and Kirti, she won the womens recurve team gold, snapping South Koreas run of seven consecutive Asian Games titles dating back to the 1998 Bangkok Games. ALSO READ Surfeit of silver paints a picture of what could have been for India at Asiad Kumkum then followed it up with gold in the individual event, ensuring South Koreas women failed to win a recurve gold at the Asian Games for the first time in the disciplines history. Her individual gold also secured a quota place for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Sujeet, 23, was named the inaugural recipient of the Raja Randhir Singh Award after winning gold in the mens 65kg freestyle wrestling category. He produced one of the most dramatic performances of the Games, defeating reigning Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka of Japan in the semifinal before staging a remarkable comeback in the gold-medal bout against Abdulmazhid Kudiyev, trailing 2-9 with time running out before fighting back to secure a 10-9 victory. ALSO READ How Kumkum Mohod beat best in world to win historic archery gold in Asiad Sujeet also continued Indias strong tradition in the 65kg category, following Olympic medallists Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, who won gold in the same weight class at the 2014 and 2018 Asian Games respectively. The IOA will felicitate Kumkum and Sujeet at a ceremony in the coming days. India finished fourth in the Asian Games medal standings with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Rs 2,400 crore Mokama rail bridge opens: 2 new lines boost Delhi-Howrah train capacity
articleFeaturedImageAlt: New Mokama rail bridge over the Ganga in Bihar. (Image: East Central Railway)
description: Mokama’s new rail bridge over the Ganga is now open for train operations, adding two railway lines and strengthening North-South Bihar connectivity.
body_raw: Indian Railways has commissioned Mokamas new rail bridge over River Ganga in Bihar. Built at a cost of around Rs 2,400 crore, the new bridge will further strengthen rail connectivity between North and South Bihar. This will also provide an additional route for passenger and freight train operations. The new bridge has been constructed parallel to the existing Rajendra Pul and has a double railway line. It was opened for train operations after receiving the required safety approval from the Commissioner of Railway Safety CRS, Eastern Circle. The CRS conducted the safety inspection of the new bridge and the associated doubled and electrified railway line on October 3 and 4, 2026.Following the safety clearance, train operations have started on the new bridge. Speaking to Indianexpress.com, Saraswati Chandra, Chief Public Relations Officer CPRO, East Central Railway, said the new Mokama rail bridge has been commissioned and train operations began around midnight. He added that train number 15483 Mahananda Express was the first train to cross the newly commissioned bridge. Location of new Mokama rail bridge The new Mokama rail bridge has been constructed about 50 metres towards the Patna side of the existing Rajendra Pul, which has been in service since 1959. The project spans around 15.5 km, including a 1.9-km main bridge over the Ganga connecting Mokama and Barauni. The main bridge comprises 17 steel spans, while the project also includes around 3.6 km of rail viaducts. Besides the main bridge, the project includes eight minor bridges, two road overbridges and three rail-over-rail structures. According to the CPRO, the new bridge has been planned in a way that requires minimum changes to the approaches of the existing bridge. It connects to the existing railway stations on both sides of the Ganga. Existing Rajendra Pul to continue carrying trains The railway official said that the new bridge will not replace the existing Rajendra Pul. Thus, the train operations will continue on the old bridge as well. He added that with the new double-line bridge alongside the existing bridge, the route will now have three railway lines, increasing capacity for train movement. It will significantly boost capacity on the busy Delhi-Howrah rail corridor. Better train connectivity between North and South Bihar The new bridge will provide an additional rail route between North and South Bihar, while also strengthening connectivity towards the northeastern parts of the country. According to the official, railway traffic in the corridor is expected to increase by around 2.5 times. The higher capacity is also expected to make freight movement smoother and reduce transportation time and costs. This could benefit the movement of essential goods as well as trade and commercial activity in the region, he stated. However, for passengers, the two new lines will help Railways manage train operations more efficiently on this important route.

articleTitle: Remembering Ashok Singhal, karmayogi who worked with diligence and detachment
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ashok Singhal: Karmayogi who worked with diligence and detachment
description: He gave up the possibilities of a personal life and chose national service. He attained fame, but remained detached from it. He provided leadership, but never sought credit for himself. He struggled, but never for personal gain.
body_raw: For Bharat, this is a moment of nation-building, with renewed self-confidence, moving from a sense of self-denial towards self-pride and awakening. This transformation can be described as the resurgence of Bharat. Ashok Singhals name stands in the foremost ranks among the great men whose tireless efforts made this transformation possible. Though he received many accolades from Hindu hriday samrat to the pioneer of the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, one word that can describe his personality would be karmayogi - the one who performed his duties with a spirit of selflessness. He did not take credit for any success but dedicated it to God with a sense of detachment. Any praise would make him uncomfortable. To rise above honour and dishonour, fame and infamy, and continue walking the path of duty with equanimity is the mark of a karmayogi and a true swayamsevak. This quality was clearly visible in Ashok jis life. Ashok ji was exceptionally talented student, born into a distinguished and accomplished family. One of his brothers served in the Indian Police Service and the other was a successful businessman. Ashok ji himself studied engineering in Metallurgy at Banaras Hindu University. Instead of pursuing a personal career, he chose to dedicate his life to the nation. He was an intensely realised sadhaka like Swami Vivekananda. His spiritual pursuit was centred not on himself, but on society and the nation. Ashok ji, as a student, came into contact with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. He had the privilege of receiving the guidance of professor Rajendra Singh, affectionately known as Rajju bhaiya and Bhaurao Deoras. He also received the guidance of Pujya Sri Guruji Golwalkar. The influence of these great men was clearly reflected in his dedication, diligence, determination, management skills, organisational ability and foresight that inspired him to be a Sangh Pracharak. When Ashok ji was the Prant Pracharak of Delhi Prant, the Meenakshipuram conversion incident raised concern throughout society. Ashok ji was entrusted with organising the Virat Hindu Sammelan in Delhi. Bringing together different sections of society, including Dr Karan Singh as the president, and revered sants from different sects, he successfully turned the plan into reality. Due to this display of impeccable organisational skills, he was given the responsibility of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad, which he took up with the same dedication and diligence. Untouchability has been a serious social challenge before Hindu society for centuries and without ending it the vision of a harmonious society cannot be realised. Going beyond symbolic gestures such as community meals, he urged revered sants to convey to Hindu society that untouchability has not been in tune with the fundamentals of Hindu dharma by visiting and staying at Scheduled Caste community settlements. Shri Kameshwar Chaupal laying the foundation stone of the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple on November 9, 1989, when revered sants and dharmacharyas were present on the occasion, or acharyas having meal at the Dom Rajas home in Varanasi, were important messages of social harmony. It strengthened the belief that social discrimination could be ended to build a harmonious Hindu society. The Ram Janmabhoomi movement was one of the most widespread socio-religious movements of modern Bharat. Programmes such as the Ram-Janki Rath Yatra, Shila Pujan, Charan-Paduka Pujan and Ramjyoti generated widespread public awakening across the country. Ashok ji played an important role. Even in difficult circumstances, his faith remained a source of inspiration for the karyakartas. He firmly believed This is the work of Ram ji. Ram ji Himself will take care of this work. The Mandir was not completed during his lifetime, but the movement to which he had provided direction, organisation and energy for decades reached its culmination after his demise, until the Pran Pratishtha of Shri Ram Lalla happened on January 22, 2024. Ashok jis sphere of influence extended far beyond the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. His initiatives and guidance were notable in several areas, including the protection of Ram Setu, the Amarnath Yatra, research on cow-based products and the conservation of cattle, social harmony, connecting the intellectual class with Hindu thought. His working style reflected a remarkable combination of scientific outlook, organisational ability, adhyatmik and national conscience. The greatest characteristic of his personality was that he never stopped after achieving a goal. As soon as one goal was achieved, he moved towards the next. For him, organisation was the means, society was the end, and service to the nation was the purpose of life. He gave up the possibilities of a personal life and chose national service. He attained fame, but remained detached from it. He provided leadership, but never sought credit for himself. He struggled, but never for personal gain. That is why the life of Ashok Singhal is not merely the story of an individual. It is an inspiring chapter of dedication, inner pursuit, organisation and karmayoga. The writer is Sarkaryavah, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh

articleTitle: Ramachandra Guha at Idea Exchange: ‘Maybe it’s a new generation that will find their own Gandhi, which will be different from mine and yours’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ramachandra Guha: ‘Maybe it’s a new generation that will find their own Gandhi, which will be different from mine and yours’
description: Ramachandra Guha is one of India’s leading public intellectuals who has written on Gandhi, apart from other significant themes, including the environment. It isn’t just that this interaction was timed around Gandhi Jayanti, but that his new book Arguments With Gandhi (HarperCollins) discusses the interactions of the Mahatma across multiple themes and registers.
body_raw: Historian Ramachandra Guha on his book Arguments With Gandhi, why Gandhi has both followers and critics, the points where Gandhi and Ambedkar diverge and converge and why student protests should go beyond these two national figures. The session was moderated by Vikas Pathak, Deputy Associate Editor, The Indian Express Vikas Pathak In your book, you refer to the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ABVP and the appropriation of figures like Bhagat Singh and Subhas Chandra Bose. Why do you think theres this tendency to appropriate figures who were either with the Indian National Congress or revolutionaries with Left leanings? Theres a general answer and a specific answer. The general answer is that the Hindu Right, whose ideological ancestors would be the Hindu Mahasabha and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh RSS, never really participated in the freedom struggle. There were two important strands in that movement, one was embodied in the Indian National Congress, which articulated a philosophy of non-violence, and the secondary strand was of revolutionary violence. Now, the Hindu Right either were agnostic on the question of the freedom struggle or in some critical moments, supported the colonial state. Thats the general answer. The specific answer is that although the Hindu Right has a strong dislike for the Congress, much of their criticism is against Nehru but Gandhi, for them, is anathema. For two reasons. One being that Gandhi believed in equal rights for Muslims and he eventually died for the cause of Hindu-Muslim harmony. The secondary reason is that he practised non-violence, which is regarded by sections of the Hindu Right as effeminate, not combative enough. So, given that they have no pre-history of participating in the freedom struggle, they are looking for anyone, who at any stage, quarrelled with Gandhi. On the Hindu Right and Gandhi Gandhi is anathema for the Hindu Right because he believed in equal rights for Muslims and he practised non-violence. They are looking for anyone who, at any stage, quarrelled with him The case of Patel is different. The appropriation of Patel is actually only over the last eight or nine years. It has a different context. The trimurti trinity that I begin my book with was a statue erected by the ABVP on the Delhi University campus, which had Savarkar, who belongs to them - he is an ideological precursor of the government that is in power today - along with Bose and Bhagat Singh, who would have been appalled to be clubbed with Savarkar. But they are united in the mind of the Hindu Right because all three, at different stages of their career, opposed Gandhi. Vikas Pathak But, there is counter argument that there were other figures too who did not participate in the freedom struggle but they were active in the public sphere. There was Ambedkar, Swami Vivekananda, Aurobindo. You are right. There were many strands that were not narrowly anti-colonial but the origins of these different strands cannot be collapsed. Ambedkar and RSS are also not on the same page. But my book is thematic. Its a book of ideas and arguments political arguments, social reform arguments, moral arguments, economic arguments. Its not part of this endless debate. The intention of my book is to take these four large ideas non-violence, justice, religion, and economy and progress, and see what Gandhi tried to articulate, how it was opposed by different people and to what extent the critics were right and to what extent Gandhis original position holds. Vikas Pathak Over the last 10-12 years, there has been a tendency to pit freedom fighters against one another. It is as if Nehru is on one side and Patel, Bose and Bhagat Singh on the other side, which they were not. Later, it was JP and Patel, who actually did not see eye to eye. How do you see this? There are two aspects to that question. One is within the Congress party. As you point out, Nehru and Patel had differences but the Congress was a broad church, and in the interest of the party and of building the nation, they submerged their differences and worked together. And there were genuine differences between the Congress and other strands. Between the Congress and Bhagat Singh, and the revolutionary movement, there was this question of violence versus non-violence. As for Bose, the difference arose on the question of whom to support in World War II the British or the Nazis. These differences were genuine in the context of the 1920s and 30s, but in the context of the Hindu Right, Bose and Bhagat Singh are on the same side as Gandhi because they do not believe in Hindu supremacy. So that is where this appropriation is so tendentious and mischievous. On student protests and references The young kids at Jantar Mantar had Ambedkar, they had Nehru, sometimes they had Bhagat Singh, I wish they also had Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, and Rabindranath Tagore Vikas Pathak Gandhi, despite his global stature, is attacked by multiple streams, theres a Hindutva attack, the communist attack, the Ambedkarite attack. How do you explain this? Theres a fourth attack, the economic modernisers attack, who say Gandhi was a backward reactionary. He exalted the village economy and was anti-development. Thats the interesting thing about working on Gandhi His ideas provoke debate, disagreement and sometimes outright hostility and that makes him a fascinating figure for historians. Immediately after Independence, there was a cult of Gandhi, there was Gandhi Jayanti, there was Gandhi on the currency note, and every prime minister would go to Rajghat. That was excessive but have we turned the other way? Have we demonised him excessively? Dont we still need him if you want to cultivate Hindu-Muslim harmony, if you want to have a civil public discourse, if you want to be sensitive to the environmental dimensions of economic development? But Gandhi has come back into public conversation in the last few months because of the students protest. CJPs Ashutosh Ranka often praises Gandhi but Abhijeet Dipke, an Ambedkarite Mahar from Maharashtra, said, We read Ambedkar and Gandhi. Devyani Onial The Chipko Movement used the Gandhian method of non-violent resistance. In that context, how do you see the big-ticket infrastructure push in the ecologically fragile hills? For this, Ill have to go back 40 years. My doctoral dissertation was on peasants and forests in the Himalayas. Early in my research, I met two remarkable Gandhians, both in their 90s Chandi Prasad Bhatt from Garhwal and Radha Bhatt from Kumaon - thats the kind of legacy that the environmental movement must carry forward. Gandhi never used the word environmentalism but I have a chapter in my book called Gandhis Precocious Environmentalism, where I talk about his ideas on forests, on water, on soil fertility, his critique of chemical agriculture, his austere lifestyle and his warnings that the globalisation of Western-style industrialisation. I think what has happened in Uttarakhand, particularly with large dams, with mines, and the Char Dham highway, and even possibly a railway line, from Rishikesh to Karnaprayag is just crazy. Vikas Pathak Do you think that Gandhi and Ambedkar can be seen as converging or complementary? Their social locations were different, so in their lifetime, they were bound to disagree. Gandhi was a guilt-ridden upper-caste reformer practising the path of self-purification. Ambedkar was a Dalit who had experienced oppression himself and was practising the path of self-respect. Ambedkar was 23 years younger than Gandhi, it was almost like a father-son debate. But after their death, given that caste inequality still exists, they have to be brought together. And that, I think, is the wisdom of young people like Dipke. Vikas Pathak On the Gandhi-Ambedkar debate regarding separate electorates, which one do you prefer? Im agnostic on this. In the book, I talk about post-Ambedkarites, who criticised joint electorates. I have a section on Kanshi Ram, who called Dalits elected in joint electorates chamchas because he felt that they will be answering to the whims of the upper-caste majority that helped elect them. On the other hand, today, there are 543 Lok Sabha constituencies because there are joint electorates and a Dalit vote in almost every one of those 543 constituencies. They can radically reshape the result of any election conducted fairly, which is why every political party pays obeisance to Ambedkar, much more than they do to Gandhi, or to an Adivasi leader like Birsa Munda or Jaipal Singh. Because Adivasis are concentrated in Adivasi electorates. So, Adivasis can probably influence something like 80 to 100 seats in the Lok Sabha Dalits could affect 500. Now, if you were to have separate electorates, Dalits would only affect about 75 or 80, 15 per cent of the seats. Its a complicated argument, and today, provided the voting is free and fair, they are not struck off the rolls inside some kind of arbitrary SIR, I am not sure that separate electorates are the answer. We need more independent-minded Dalit candidates, more ministers in positions of authority, not just token presidents or parties but maybe even prime ministers and home ministers. I dont think theres a straightforward case for separate electorates. Shiny Varghese Gandhi romanticised villages but do you think the future of our cities was not given enough thought? To give an overall picture, when it comes to non-violence, in a context like India, Gandhi was dead right. When it comes to Hindu-Muslim harmony, he was dead right. When it comes to economic policy, I think he was neither dead right nor dead wrong. The people who opposed him were dead wrong because they practised a kind of energy-intensive, capital-intensive, resource-gathering industrialisation, first under state planning and now under the neo-liberal economy. The environmental consequences have been the same. So the people who opposed it were dead wrong. But Gandhi was not dead right either. His was a moderating influence. You may still need some skyscrapers, some centralisation. So I see him not as someone who gave an economic blueprint. His ideas were a moderating influence even for cities. For instance, in Bangalore, where I live, why not practise more water conservation, why not have more green spaces, why not privilege public transport? Rather than the chief minister deciding what is good for Bangalore, why not have the local councils, the municipality decide? So I think Gandhi as an economic thinker is prescient about the environmental and social devastation he offers us some ideas that can nudge us towards a less destructive, more sustainable path. Aakash Joshi There has been criticism of Gandhi, especially abroad, at university campuses around race, some of his physical and sexual practices and gender. How much of him was a genuine engagement, given the honesty with which he wrote? Section two of my book, which is called Justice, has three chapters. The first chapter is called Caste The Life and Afterlife of the Gandhi-Ambedkar Debate the second chapter is called Gender The Partial Unmaking of a Reluctant Patriarch and the third chapter has the straightforward title, Was Gandhi a Racist? And I trace the evolution of his views very carefully. I show that as a young man, he was a racist. He went to South Africa in his early 20s carrying the prejudices of his time - an upper-caste Indian obsessed with skin colour, thinking Africans are backward, thinking Indians are more or less equal to Europeans as two great old civilisations but the Africans are lost in the forest kind of thing But then how his views changed over time when he was in South Africa and he returned to India and was a principal anti-racist in the last decades of his life. Its easy to cherry-pick Gandhi, quote him from Volume 6 of the Collected Works and forget what he said on the same subject in Volume 40 or Volume 86. He was a racist as a young man, and he slowly shed his prejudices, and this is part of Gandhis deep and essential humanity. Hes always growing, hes always listening, hes always modifying his views. Even on technology. He never wholeheartedly accepts Western industrialisation but he can see the benefits of what science can offer. Aakash Joshi In the last 10-odd years, we have seen history becoming a battleground as well as a government project. How do you see this? Obviously the BJP has taken this to an extreme. They use the rewriting of history to promote a kind of crude majoritarian agenda and to distort events so that a Hindu king now happens to have won a battle he actually lost. But the Congress is not above criticism either. In 2018, the Congress came to power in Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. I am someone who believes that historians - Clio, the muse of history was an anarchist - should not associate with states. Within weeks of the Congress coming to power, I got letters from ministers saying, Please address all of us on Jawaharlal Nehru, not on Savarkar, because Savarkar cant be known. And the Congress textbooks in the 1960s and 70s were not perfect. However, those produced during the UPA regime of 20042009 were excellent. There was a visionary director of the NCERT, Krishna Kumar. For history textbooks, he had recruited a very good team headed by Neeladri Bhattacharya. He curated a series of textbooks which was not just Prithviraj versus Akbar, Nehru versus Savarkar, but around themes, particularly in ancient and medieval India, around housing, food, dress, forms of transportation and how these changed and evolved. Now those are beautiful ways of introducing young people to the nuances and complexities of history and changes over time. Khushi Sinha Do you think India needs a modern-day Gandhi? India does not need a modern-day Gandhi. It does not need a modern-day Ambedkar. It does not need a modern-day Nehru. It does not need a modern-day Tagore. It does not need a modern-day Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay. Although those are the five modern Indians I admire most. It needs a synthesis of all of these renewed for our times. I think in one of Ambedkars great speeches in the last meeting of the Constituent Assembly, he warned against the dangers of hero worship. He said bhakti in religion is a route to the salvation of the soul, bhakti in politics is a route to eventual dictatorship. He was prescient about Indira Gandhi, he would have been prescient about Narendra Modi. We cant have one leader, we must have a bouquet of ideas. So, to the young kids of Jantar Mantar - they had Ambedkar, they had Nehru, sometimes they had Bhagat Singh - I wish they had Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, possibly also Tagore, but Im very happy they did not have Savarkar, Hedgewar and Golwalkar, those are exactly what we do not need. Vikas Pathak Freedom fighters usually are most popular in the region to which they belonged, like Bose is in Bengal and Bhagat Singh in Punjab. But the irony is that Gandhi is not an icon in Gujarat and Nehru is not an icon in Prayagraj, from where he came. How would you explain this? Gandhi drew on dissenting traditions within the state. He drew on poet Narsinh Mehta, who preached compassion and tolerance. So when it came to his religious pluralism, maybe he was an anomaly. But you pointed out something very interesting - Khushwant Singh once criticised Tagore, and the entire West Bengal legislative assembly stood up and censured him. You cannot criticise Savarkar in Maharashtra, Ambedkar among the Dalits. Gandhi in India belongs to everyone and to no one. Nehru at least belongs to the Congress party, which has been run by his descendants for some time. Gandhi belongs to everyone. And maybe its a new generation that will find their own Gandhi, which will be different from mine and yours.

articleTitle: Newborn found dead inside Madhya Pradesh hospital. Then, doctors noticed marks around her neck
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Newborn found dead inside MP hospital. Then, doctors noticed marks around her neck
description: What initially appeared to be a sudden deterioration in the newborn’s condition became a suspected murder case after doctors noticed marks around her neck and blood coming from her mouth.
body_raw: A newborn girl was allegedly strangled to death, within 16 hours of her birth, at a hospital in Madhya Pradeshs Ashoknagar district, with police now probing the family members. The baby, born to a couple from the Chanderi area, was admitted to the hospital shortly after birth and was being kept under medical observation. By Saturday afternoon, she was dead. What initially appeared to be a sudden deterioration in the newborns condition became a suspected murder after doctors noticed marks around her neck and blood coming from her mouth. An initial medical investigation showed that there were some marks on the infants neck. Furthermore, blood was also spotted on her face. We are questioning the infants family members, said a police officer. Police said the examination subsequently found ligature or compression marks around the babys neck, indicating that she could have been strangled, the officer said. The finding prompted investigators to reconstruct the few hours between her admission and her death, including who had handled the baby, who had entered the ward and when she was last seen alive. The baby was born late on Friday night, around 11.50 pm, and was admitted to the Special Newborn Care Unit SNCU soon after. She was found dead between about 3 pm and 4 pm on Saturday, less than 16 hours after her birth. A health official from the district said hospital staff immediately took the newborn to the SNCU after she was found unresponsive. Doctors examined the child and found that she had already died. The baby had blood coming from her mouth and marks resembling pressure around her neck. Given these circumstances, the hospital treated the death as suspicious and informed the police, following which the body was sent for post-mortem examination, the official said. The newborn was the second daughter of her parents. Investigators are, therefore, examining whether the babys gender and the familys circumstances could have played a role in her killing. The possibility of a family member being responsible for the death has emerged also because access to the child was restricted. Besides, the absence of CCTV cameras inside the SNCU has also made it difficult to immediately ascertain how she was killed.

articleTitle: New Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh: ‘We have no wajood or aukaat outside Punjab and Congress’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pargat Singh: ‘We have no wajood and aukaat outside Punjab & Congress’
description: “I have always been a team player… Goal is to ensure victory (in 2027 elections) for team (Congress). I will take everyone along,” Pargat Singh tells The Indian Express
body_raw: Amid the raging factionalism and infighting within the Punjab Congress, the party leadership has appointed three-time Jalandhar Cantonment MLA and former India hockey captain Pargat Singh, as its state unit president. In an interview with The Indian Express, Singh, 62, speaks about a range of issues, including the state Congresss internal dynamics, his predecessor Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, and his plans for the Assembly polls due in February 2027. Excerpts The rift between Warring and former CM Charanjit Singh Channi has been out in the open. Now that you have taken over, how will you ensure that you do not appear inclined to one side, and what would be Warrings role now? Differences of opinion must exist in democracies and political parties. In a democracy, there is no place for dictatorship. I have taken everything positive as our target is much bigger. There are no factions. The organisation is united and there is a single target of winning the Assembly polls. One thing is clear for us as party workers we have no wajood existence and aukaat standing outside Punjab and without the Congress. When there is no existence without the party and state, where does the question of factionalism arise from? It is just a narrative that has been created. In the Congress, everyone has the right to speak their mind. Can anyone in the BJP or AAP speak openly against their leadership? Recently, the AAP suspended its Maur MLA Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana after he publicly raised the issue of teacher shortage. Is that democracy? Everyone is important and has a role to play according to his or her strength. We have to work together with Punjab as our focus and bring back the glory of brand Punjab. You describe yourself as a full-back who intends to take everyone along. What does this mean? I have always been a team player. As a hockey player, I played as a full-back. Like anyone else in the team, the full-back has a particular role. We need to identify where every player fits and give them a role accordingly. At the end of the day, the goal is to ensure victory for the team. Keeping that aim in mind, I will take everyone along. While the Congress has said it will fight the Assembly polls under a collective leadership, several leaders are seen as contenders to the CMs post. How do you plan to handle the situation? The decision on the chief minister is the prerogative of the legislators. Winning the election matters before that. Candidates will be selected based on merit, surveys, winnability and character. Apart from these criteria, there must not be any other consideration. Our priority is to build a strong organisation and win a majority of the 117 seats. All senior leaders have agreed that victory is paramount in the first place. On what plank would the Congress contest the 2027 Assembly polls? Our focus is to revive brand Punjab, which means every issue related to the state like the law-and-order situation, drugs, economy, Punjabs mounting debt, farming, womens safety come into the picture. Like they BJP ask the Congress for hisaab-kitaab accountability for our 70-year rule, we will ask them about the 12 years they were in power. Also, we will ask for accountability from the AAP. We are not here to make illogical allegations. Our focus is to present the Congresss clear Punjab-centric narrative. The state has its own identity and concerns. We need to make Punjab the centre of our politics. Punjab is likely to see a multi-cornered contest with the BJP, Shiromani Akali Dal SAD, Akali Dal Waris Punjab De and Congress taking on the AAP. How do you view the WPD Waris Punjab De? The WPD is like any other political party in the state. I see it just like that. Everyone has a right to float a party and contest elections. I wish them good luck. For me, what matters is to make the Congress victorious.

articleTitle: Karnataka to Maharashtra, why states are reviving campus polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka to Maharashtra, why states are reviving campus polls
description: A key reason why some states are looking to revive student union polls is that there are signs of youth unrest, with a perception gaining ground that it would be better if elected outfits could channel youth energies in conventional directions.
body_raw: Stalled for years in many universities across India, student union elections seem to be making a comeback. While Karnataka has given the green signal to the student body polls, in Madhya Pradesh the High Court gave orders earlier this year that the student union elections be held in the state. In Maharashtra, the Higher and Technical Education Department constituted a 12-member committee headed by former Mumbai University Vice-Chancellor Prof Suhas Pednekar to work out a framework for the student union polls, giving the panel a month to submit its report. In Odisha too, the state government is in talks with stakeholders to resume student union polls. In UP, the ABVP the RSS student wing has met people at the top levels demanding that elections in universities be resumed, ABVP national media co-convenor Abhinav Mishra told The Indian Express. Current scenario There have been no student body elections in Jamia Millia Islamia since 2006. In the Banaras Hindu University BHU, there have been no student body elections since 1996, and 2018 in Aligarh Muslim University AMU. Since 2018, Allahabad University has also not had the student union elections, while the central University of Himachal Pradesh has not seen such polls since 2019. The University of Ladakh has also not had the student union elections since 2024. Among the central universities, the Jawaharlal Nehru University JNU, Delhi University DU, Assam University, University of Hyderabad UoH, University of Kerala and the Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University still hold regular elections to their student unions. Among the state universities, Panjab University, Chandigarh, has regular student union elections. Jadavpur University in Kolkata has not seen student union elections since 2020. While Patna University has regular elections, all other Bihar universities have seen elections being stalled in 2018. In UP, there has been a ban on the student union elections in the state universities since 2018 due to frequent violence. Polls in Chaudhary Charan Singh University, Meerut, were halted in 2017 itself, and those in Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and University of Lucknow in 2016 and 2012, respectively. In most Gujarat state universities, the student body polls were discontinued in 2023. Student unrest On many campuses, episodic violence related to student politics led to a sentiment against elections, and many believe that some universities of repute declined student polls because of this factor. The result elections stopped happening across many states. However, as the recent violence in Lovely Professional University LPU shows, violence can happen even without elections. In fact, an ABVP leader not wanting to be named said the elected student unions actually play the role of a safety valve and prevent uncontrolled violence. Elections provide a platform for students to air their grievances. The kind of violence that took place in LPU is partly because private universities dont have elected student unions. These unions can channel the grievances of students in a structured manner, he said. Another reason why some state governments are looking to revive elections in universities is that there are signs of youth unrest across India, the Cockroach Janta Party CJP-led protests being an example, with a perception gaining ground that it would be better if elected student outfits could channel youth energies in conventional directions. Salience of student bodies Student political workers believe there are several advantages to having elections in colleges and universities. They train political workers and provide a future leadership to the country, training young political workers how to engage with demands of their constituency. They also make students more aware of the stances of political organisations on various national issues-especially in campuses such as JNU, Jadavpur University and UoH. There are everyday advantages too. Students can access accommodations, get help in administrative procedures, and have a safety net when elected student unions are in place. An ABVP leader said that the behavior of the police in thanas close to campuses where elected student unions exist is often different from campuses without elections. The police are more responsible when they know there are elected student unions to be dealt with, he said, adding that these unions are also the best means to convey the concerns and grievances of students to the university administration. For student organisations like the ABVP and NSUI the Congresss student wing, elections in universities are the only way to assess their presence and strength, and their activists see elections to various posts as a key outcome of their activism. However, a student leader who did not wish to be identified pointed out why many state governments had been wary of the student union elections. The Chief Ministers dont want a power centre to emerge in the form of an elected student union president they want their loyalists to occupy important positions. Also, the CMs often think that a student union election is perceived as a referendum on the performance of the state government. A BJP CM would not want the NSUI to win, and a Congress CM would not want the ABVP to win. So, they prefer to stall polls. The victory of the ABVP in the DU polls soon after the CJP-led protests at Jantar Mantar during June-July against the BJP-led Centre over alleged irregularities in the education and exam system was seen as a reality check for the Opposition camp.

articleTitle: Team depth to individual gaps: India’s Asian Games report card for 2028 Olympics
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Indian contingent during the Asian Games closing ceremony in Nagoya, Japan, Sunday. (AP Photo)
description: Talent spotting, investment under lens; officials say performance ‘encouraging’: India finished fourth at the Asian Games with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, 85 in all. It fell short of the 100-medal target and finished 21 medals behind its record haul in Hangzhou.
body_raw: Between the 2022 Asian Games in Chinas Hangzhou and the latest edition that wound up Sunday in Japans Nagoya, the Government spent Rs 97.84 crore under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme TOPS. Only two per cent of it, approximately, translated to gold medals this time. Teenager Kumkum Mohod won arguably Indias biggest individual gold despite not being in the flagship scheme Suruchi Singh, the shooter, was added only recently, while her mixed team partner, Kamaljeet Singh, isnt on the list Neeru Dhanda, who won a trap gold in shooting, remains outside the TOPS core group, too. Thirteen of Indias 21 golds came in team events, some of which arent in the Olympics, while 19 of its 27 silvers came in individual events. These numbers present different stories from Nagoya the first about talent identification, the second on allocation of considerable investment in elite sport, and the third offering encouragement and a warning - there is growing depth in team events but athletes are struggling in individual events to make that final push from silver to gold. India finished fourth at the Asian Games with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, 85 in all. It fell short of the 100-medal target and finished 21 medals behind its record haul in Hangzhou. We may have lost a few medals compared to Hangzhou but individual performances were satisfying, Adille Sumariwala, the Athletics Federation of India spokesperson, said. Going just on the basis of medals may not be the only way to judge. Improvement in performance is what should be tracked for future preparation for Olympic Games. Though the gold rush of the last two days ensured a heady end to a dwindling campaign, the overall number does not tell the entire story. Start with the gold. More than half of Indias gold medals came from events where several athletes contributed to one result -cricket, kabaddi, hockey, archery, athletics relays and shooting. The individual events produced a different pattern. Those 19 silvers came from athletes who had already negotiated the difficult part of reaching an Asian Games final but could not make that push to gold. That makes the gold medals of Kumkum, Suruchi-Kamaljeet and Neeru significant. Kumkum was not part of TOPS when she became Indias first individual Asian Games champion in womens recurve. Suruchi was added to the programme only recently before winning shooting mixed team gold along with Kamaljeet Singh, who, too, isnt part of TOPS. Neeru remains in the developmental group despite becoming Indias first womens trap champion at the Asian Games. Collectively, these three medals translate to Rs 3.5 lakh of TOPS funding - three gold medallists, three Olympic hopefuls who were either outside or only recently inside the established priorities of the countrys elite funding system. According to the Sports Ministry, Rs 97.84 crore was spent under TOPS during the Asian Games cycle. The money goes towards customised training programmes, foreign exposure, specialised coaches, support staff and equipment. Of this, it turned out, Rs 2.05 crore was spent on athletes who ultimately won gold. Under the Annual Calendar for Training and Competitions programme, which funds camps, tournaments, coaches salaries and other competition expenses, the Government spent another Rs 702.86 crore between 2023 and 2026. Only 12.5 per cent of that spending was associated with gold medals in Nagoya. A senior official of a federation governing an Olympic sport in the country said The pattern was seen during the Paris Olympics too, and raises a question over whether the system is identifying the athletes who will eventually deliver at the biggest events early enough for that investment to follow them. When contacted, a Sports Ministry official said, The performance of the contingent has been very encouraging and players have performed creditably. Some disciplines have not performed up to their potential but there have been some incredible results. The official said TOPS follows a dynamic and continuous evaluation process. The TOPS team closely monitors emerging and established elite athletes, with regular assessments to ensure that deserving athletes are inducted into the Development and Core Groups based on their performance, potential and medal prospects, the official said. Nagoya also confronted some of Indias traditional strongholds with reality checks. In badminton, India failed to win an individual medal for the first time in 12 years. The sport had already returned empty-handed from the Paris Olympics, its first medal-less Olympic campaign since 2012. In weightlifting, Mirabai Chanus silver was Indias first Asian Games medal in the sport since 1998. At 32, she remains the countrys most established name, but the only one doing the heavy lifting, with no obvious successor. Athletics and shooting, which won 51 medals combined in Hangzhou, contributed 39 this time athletics 24, shooting 15. According to the Sports Ministry official, there will now be a review of the performance. Where performance has been below expectations, a thorough assessment will be undertaken to identify gaps, draw lessons and strengthen preparations, with a clear focus on the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games, the official said, adding that the review would have been conducted irrespective of whether performance exceeds expectations or falls short of targets. Archery provided one of the clearest signs of what is possible. Indias womens recurve team ended South Koreas 28-year Asian Games reign before Kumkum won the individual title, evidence that a younger generation is now capable of challenging a programme that has dominated the event for decades. Womens hockey offered another example of how quickly a programme can change. After missing the Paris Olympics, the players went through specialised penalty-corner and goalkeeping clinics with foreign experts, while 11 injured players received rehabilitation support. In Nagoya, they beat China for gold and secured qualification for Los Angeles. Mens wrestling produced Aman Sehrawat and Sujeet Kalkal as gold medallists. Ankush Panghal, Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda helped return boxing to the top of the Asian Games podium. Womens pistol shooting, where India has considerable depth, continued to produce results. These are the reasons Nagoya can offer encouragement ahead of Los Angeles. The Asian Games are a mid-term examination before the Olympics. India has shown depth in several team events, new names have emerged in individual sports and established athletes remain capable of providing a foundation for the next cycle. The gaps are clear, too.

articleTitle: Mad Sandhu murder: Punjabi influencer was set to enter Bigg Boss, says father
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjabi influencer Mad Sandhu was set to enter Bigg Boss, says father
description: Two gangsters claim they ordered the hit: 'was ruining new generation'.
body_raw: Punjabi LGBTQI social media influencer and makeup artist Mad Sandhu, who was murdered Saturday, was set to enter reality television show Bigg Boss as a wildcard contestant later this month, his friends and family said. The 30-year-old, whose real name was Madhusudan Sandhu, had built a following through his outspoken social media presence and was preparing for a major break in his career. He was to enter the Bigg Boss house on October 29, had completed the necessary paperwork, but had not made the information public, according to his father Bhupinder Singh. He was due to leave for Mumbai to take part in show on on October 20, Bhupinder Singh, said. On Sunday, the family cremated Sandhu. Sandhu died of gunshot wounds after two motorcycle borne assailants opened fire at him in Amritsar outside a car wash. The killing sent shockwaves through Amritsar, with Sandhus family saying he had previously received online abuse and threats over his outspoken social media presence and his association with the LGBTQ community. He had also approached the police several times seeking protection, his father said. The murder took another turn after two gangsters separately claimed responsibility for the killing in social media posts. Gangster Goldy Dhillon was the first to claim responsibility, alleging that Sandhu was ruining the new generation and warning others who, according to him, promoted similar content on social media platforms. Spain-based alleged gangster Lucky Johal subsequently disputed Dhillons claim and said he was responsible for the killing. Johal allegedly said the murder was not motivated by money or personal gain but by what he described as an attempt to protect Punjabs culture and environment. He also threatened another influencer, Arupreet, whose content he claimed was similar to Sandhus. Police have not established the veracity of either claim. Amritsar Police Commissioner Harmanbir Singh Gill said, police has obtained significant leads regarding the shooters and expressed confidence that arrests would follow. Sabndhu was eldest of three siblings. His father is a retired Punjab police sub-inspector, while his mother is a homemaker. The family originally lived on Sultanwind Road before moving to the Manawala area along the Amritsar-Jalandhar road. Recalling his sons childhood, Bhupinder Singh said Sandhu had expressed his individuality and gender identity from an early age. From early childhood, he was different. We initially tried to change him, but later we understood that this is how God has made him, he told The Indian Express. The family later became supportive of Sandhus choices, his father said. We never restricted him from living his life on his own terms. After completing Class 12, Sandhu trained as a makeup artist at a private institute and later established his own salon and makeup business in Amritsar. His work took him into the Punjabi entertainment industry, where he worked with actors and attended events in Mumbai. His reported selection for Bigg Boss marked another milestone in his career. He was supposed to go to Bigg Boss as a wildcard entry, his father said. Sandhus public profile, however, had also made him a controversial figure at times. In April 2025, he publicly supported the cancellation of a Pride parade in Amritsar and appealed to members of the LGBTQ community not to turn the issue into a confrontation with wider society. If society does not want to accept these things right now, or if it isnt ready for them yet, then we shouldnt force it, he had said. He had also urged members of the community to take cultural and religious sentiments into consideration. According to his family, Sandhu had faced hostility and threats from several people, including some Nihang factions. His father said Sandhu had informed police about the threats and submitted applications seeking protection, including one several months before his death. He would just go to work, work to home, home to work, his father said, describing the cautious routine Sandhu had adopted. The family said they had received no ransom demand. Police are now investigating the circumstances of the shooting, including the identity of the assailants and the competing social-media claims of responsibility.

articleTitle: Manipur: Kuki man found dead day after abduction
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Manipur: Kuki man found dead a day after abduction
description: The incident comes against the backdrop of renewed Kuki-Naga tensions in Manipur, particularly in parts of Kangpokpi district and neighbouring areas.
body_raw: A DAY after he was allegedly abducted from his field in Kangpokpi district of Manipur, a 71-year-old Kuki man was on Sunday found dead-with his hands tied behind his back-in a nearby forest, sources said. The man was identified as Hemjang Haokip of Khunkho Kuki village near Leimakhong. He was reported missing after his field hut was set ablaze on Saturday. Haokips farm trousers, shirt and sweater were recovered during a search on Sunday, following which security forces deployed sniffer dogs and intensified the operation to trace him. His body was subsequently found in a nearby forest. The circumstances surrounding Haokips death and the identity of those responsible were not immediately known. According to initial reports, heavy rainfall on Saturday had kept many villagers away from their fields, and the incident came to light only in the evening. Haokip was known to frequently spend the night at his field hut. After learning that the hut had been burnt and Haokip was missing, villagers launched a search that continued until dark but failed to locate him. The Kuki Youth Organisation KYO, Leimakhong block, had earlier demanded Haokips immediate and safe return and urged the authorities and security agencies to intensify the search and take action against those responsible. The Khunkho Kuki Village Authority had also condemned the abduction and issued a 24-hour ultimatum for Haokips safe and unconditional release, warning of widespread democratic protests if he was not released. The Committee on Tribal Unity, Sadar Hills, had separately appealed for Haokips safe release. Meanwhile, the Ariang Khunkhu Naga Village Authority, in a clarification issued on Sunday, expressed solidarity with Haokips family and said neither the village nor its residents had any involvement in his disappearance. The Naga village authority appealed against unverified allegations and speculation, warning that such claims could create unnecessary distrust and tension between the two villages, which it said had maintained peaceful and cordial relations for decades. The incident comes against the backdrop of renewed Kuki-Naga tensions in Manipur, particularly in parts of Kangpokpi district and neighbouring areas.

articleTitle: 30 years on, why Mumbai’s slum rehab moves more people into slums than homes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: 30 years on, Why Mumbai's slum rehab moves more people into slums than homes
description: For every resident who gets a new flat under the slum rehabilitation, nearly 10 move to other slums, finds a study of 15 years of projects. Only a third were finished. Residents are evicted first and wait years for homes. Even the SRA admits the problem.
body_raw: To make Mumbai slum-free. That was the idea behind the Slum Rehabilitation Act, introduced in 1995. Thirty years on, a study of slum rehabilitation projects from 2007 to 2022 has found that for every resident rehoused on site, 9.5 others who are eligible are displaced to other slums. The finding comes from a working paper by Alishuba Philip, a PhD student of economics at the University of Zurich, presented in July at the National Bureau of Economic Research NBER Summer Institute 2026 Real Estate conference in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The task the Act set out to achieve was herculean rehousing millions of residents from unsafe informal settlements into proper buildings on the same site, while unlocking acres of precious real estate. As per the Census 2011, 42 per cent of Mumbais 12 million people live in slums. From its inception till October 2025, the Slum Rehabilitation Authority SRA built 2,79,307 rehabilitation homes. The study Titled Slum Redevelopments and Evictions in a Developing Megacity, the paper tracks slum redevelopment projects, the locations of their residents and daytime satellite data over 15 years, from 2007 to 2022. Data from the SRA covered projects, approvals and timelines for a sample of 254 projects, out of 592 slum projects in the period. Philip digitised around 8,00,000 pages of electoral roll data and tracked residents through their names and other details, including fathers or spouses name, age and gender. Satellite data from Google Earth provided another layer of verification, allowing her to track a projects progress from slum to construction site to building. I set out to do this paper because we have very little evidence on what happens to residents when slums are redeveloped, both in historical settings in the developed world and in developing countries today, Philip told The Indian Express over email. Ideally, such programs should have follow-up surveys that track residents over time regardless of where they live to study how redevelopment affects them, but this is rarely the case. Tracking people through voter rolls has a catch the same person can show up twice. Philip found that about 2 per cent of entries looked like duplicates, even after matching names, fathers names and ages. Philip did her calculations again in three different ways to see if the duplicates were messing things up. In one, she removed the possible duplicates entirely. In another, where someone appeared twice, she kept them only once. In the third, she counted the possible duplicates but treated them as less important. The findings didnt change. Duplicate names are unlikely to be driving the findings, she said. Far from the finishing line What Philip found is that the scheme fails more often than not. Only one-third of the approved SRA projects she tracked between 2007 to 2022 reached completion. Twenty-nine per cent of approved projects never started. Residents were neither evicted nor rehoused. Thats because the SRA relies on private builders, who rehouse slum dwellers for free and in return get extra floor space to sell, on the same plot or, through Transferable Development Rights TDR, elsewhere in the city. Whether a builder starts work, the paper notes, depends on expected economic returns. If the project doesnt promise enough profit, it stays on paper. Builders can often choose to wait for bylaws and regulations to change that would make the project more profitable for them, said Hussain Indorewala, assistant professor at the Kamla Raheja Vidyanidhi Institute of Architecture, who has studied the scheme over the years. SRA schemes also need the consent of 51 per cent of slum dwellers, down from 70 per cent earlier. Conflicts between the builder and residents, or between residents and their managing committee, can sink a project before it starts. Stuck midway Even when a project begins, with evictions and demolitions, there is no guarantee of the promised home. Philip found that 37 per cent of approved SRA projects had started but were yet to be completed. That leaves slum dwellers in limbo, uprooted from their communities, work and schools, with little savings to keep them afloat. They get either transit rent or transit accommodation to tide them over. But the rent often stops, while transit accommodation can become a permanent home. I have resigned myself to the fate that there will be no rent payments after two years, said Shankar Patil, a resident of Lumbini Bagh Cooperative Society, a slum settlement in Govandi on the brink of an SRA project. With others in his slum pocket ready for redevelopment and taking two years of transit rent, Patils opposition carried no weight. The builder is giving Rs 14,000 per month as rent. While I have chosen to move into a building in Panvel, moving further away, most here prefer to move into slum homes in the vicinity, paying Rs 5,000 in rent and using the rest to run their homes. His suspicion comes from his own backyard. Around 10 years ago, the settlement of Bhim Wadi, behind my home, went into redevelopment. But midway, all progress on it stopped. There were 190 families living there, who all went their own ways, he said. The project is nearing completion only now. The cost of delay The longer the delay, the less likely it is that slum dwellers will make it out of slums at all. Philip found that slum redevelopment projects take an average of six years to build. In her sample, most residents who successfully moved from a slum home to formal housing on the same site had their projects completed within four years. On paper, rebuilding slums on the same site should let residents stay close to their work, schools and neighbours, while giving them a proper home. In practice, the paper notes, the slum has to be cleared before construction begins. So eviction is immediate, while the asset arrives only if and when construction is completed. Residents lose their homes on day one and may wait years, or forever, for the new ones. The paper also offers a possible fix. Reducing this lag, through stricter enforcement of construction timelines, interim housing support, or phased demolition and construction, is therefore central to how effective in-situ redevelopment is. Slum to slum Approval of a redevelopment project raises the probability of a resident moving into formal housing by only six percentage points, Philip found. On the other hand, the probability of living in other slums increases by 22 percentage points. Put another way, for every person who moves from a slum home into formal housing on the same site, 9.5 others who are eligible for a redeveloped home are displaced to other slums. The broader takeaway is that delays and non-completion matter for the extent to which slum redevelopment translates into transitions out of slum living even when residents are eligible for an apartment in the redeveloped slum. This raises questions about whether in-situ rehabilitation is the right model to follow at all for slum residents, given that it features a delay in compensation by design, said Philip. She is now studying what causes construction delays and plans to send the paper to journals once that is complete. What the SRA says A senior SRA official acknowledged the problems. The estimate the SRA began with, that around 5 lakh homes were needed to rehouse slum residents has jumped to 13-14 lakh. This is because slums have proliferated, and agencies have been unable to prevent encroachments, he said. It is true that a lot of slum redevelopment projects dont take off even after approvals, the official said. He gave three reasons. The first is rising expectations. As the government has increased entitlements of home sizes over the years, the expectation of slum dwellers has increased, he said. The second is opposition from residents who stand to get nothing. In slums, families often build upward, adding floors they live in or rent out. Those living on the upper floors are not eligible for a free flat under the scheme, except in Dharavi. Top floor residents, who are ineligible, often object and get projects stalled, the official said. The third is the unexpected. And occasionally, events like covid delay projects, making them run into 10 years. The Maharashtra government has now turned to cluster redevelopment for areas over 50 acres, banking on private muscle. When such projects are taken up by a government body like the SRA or MMRDA, they need only government approval, not the consent of slum dwellers. Action against inactive developers, who have submitted and gotten approvals for redevelopment proposals on paper but have not proceeded with any work on ground, has also been ramped up, with over 450 developers terminated in the past three years. Perhaps in the next 5 years, the slums around us will no longer be around, the official said. The study does not cover residents who do move into in-situ formal housing but do not stay there for long, another established problem with slum redevelopment. It is well established that once slum residents are rehabilitated into their in situ rehabilitation buildings, not all of them continue to stay there, said Indorewala. They may lose their livelihood, and the costs of living in a high-rise building, like maintenance, are more - which may lead to them renting out the units. If the family is faced with distress, they may sell and go somewhere else.

articleTitle: Nirmala Sitharaman writes: Next-Gen GST & India’s next phase of growth
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nirmala sitharaman
description: "Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, Next-Gen GST was conceived with two connected purposes: to reduce and rationalise rates, and to make compliance easier," writes Nirmala Sitharaman.
body_raw: INDIAS AMBITION to become a Viksit Bharat requires an economy in which enterprises of every size can grow, wherever they begin. Over the past 12 years, our government has worked to create those conditions. GSTs introduction in 2017 established a common national framework for indirect taxation. Next-Gen GST carries that effort forward, drawing on nine years of implementation and the experience of taxpayers and states. Under Prime Minister Narendra Modis vision, Next-Gen GST was conceived with two connected purposes to reduce and rationalise rates, and to make compliance easier. The rate changes took effect on September 22, 2025. The next phase of process reforms will come before the GST Council shortly. Together, these efforts seek to give households relief, businesses greater certainty and taxpayers a system in which they can fulfil their obligations without avoidable difficulty. The states have been partners throughout. They brought their priorities and experience to the Council, helped shape the decisions and undertook their implementation. I thank them for that commitment. GSTs progress rests on this willingness to pursue a shared national purpose while respecting each governments responsibilities. The results provide grounds for confidence. Between October 2025 and July 2026, the value of reported taxable supplies grew by 25.8 over the corresponding period a year earlier. A lighter rate structure has been accompanied by a substantial expansion in reported economic activity. This is an encouraging foundation for a reform intended to support both enterprise and public finances. That resilience is visible in the latest revenue figures. Gross GST collections reached Rs 12.46 lakh crore during April-September 2026, up 11.6 over the corresponding period last year. Every month from June through September recorded double-digit annual growth together, collections for these four months accelerated by nearly 15. Net collections, after refunds, also grew by 10.4 over the half-year. Taxpayer relief has coexisted with growth in the resources available for development. The breadth of the expansion matters as much as its scale. Reported taxable supplies grew across all 11 sector groups and all major states. In an economy as diverse as Indias, this spread is significant. Growth across sectors and regions creates opportunities for more businesses to participate in expanding markets, and for more communities to benefit from the demand, investment and employment that follow. Reported sales to consumers B2C also rose by 26.7 in the post-reform comparison. When tax relief is reflected in prices, families have more room to meet other needs or save. Consumer relief and enterprise growth are closely connected the purchasing power of households sustains demand for the goods and services that businesses provide. The benefits can extend from the household to the retailer, the supplier and the producer. For small and medium enterprises, a national market is valuable when it opens a practical route to customers beyond their immediate surroundings. Businesses in Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns should be able to build those relationships while continuing to invest and employ people locally. Enterprises expanding into these towns, in turn, can create opportunities for local suppliers and distributors. GSTs common framework supports these connections simpler administration must make them easier to sustain. Participation in that framework is substantial. GST registrations across central and state jurisdictions stood at approximately 1.71 crore at the end of August, up nearly 15 from a year ago. For the April-July 2026 tax periods, GSTR-3B returns filed by their due dates were 12.6 higher than for the same periods last year. These improvements place a corresponding responsibility on the administration regular compliance must be supported by reliable service, clear guidance and timely resolution of difficulties. The functioning of input tax credit is another important part of this experience. The post-reform figures show that the share of tax liability discharged through credits rose, while accumulated credit declined relative to taxable supplies. This is encouraging for businesses that depend on the effective use of eligible credit. For a smaller firm, working capital determines how readily it can purchase inputs, fulfil an order and take on the next one. Refunds are equally relevant. Approximately Rs 1.80 lakh crore was refunded during April-September. Returning amounts due to businesses is part of a well-functioning tax system. Greater predictability in this process would help enterprises plan purchases and production with more confidence. The taxpayers experience of receiving an eligible refund is an important measure of administrative performance. The states also have a stronger revenue position. Their aggregate SGST receipts, including their share of IGST settlements, grew by about 16 during April-September this year. These resources support investment in infrastructure and public services, which improve the conditions in which families and enterprises pursue their aspirations. The gains can therefore reinforce one another household relief supports demand, enterprise strengthens economic activity, and public revenues help sustain development. The experience also points to the work ahead. A growing system must remain attentive to the costs it imposes on smaller participants. Their time and resources are limited. Each improvement in filing, credit or refunds should allow more of those resources to be devoted to running and expanding a business. The proposals before the Council on 7 October have been developed through sustained work with the states. They address registration, returns, refunds, disputes and improved flow of input tax credit, with the aim of reducing the time and cost of compliance. Taxpayer experience must continue to guide implementation. GSTs growing maturity gives us a stronger foundation for the next stage of reform. The same commitment to clarity, certainty and respect for the taxpayer guides our work on direct taxes. A dependable tax system enables enterprises to plan beyond their immediate obligations and invest in opportunities that take time to mature. Giving them that confidence, wherever they operate, helps build the economic strength of a Viksit Bharat as envisioned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Nirmala Sitharaman is the Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs

articleTitle: ‘Got the law involved’: FBI chief Kash Patel gets engaged to longtime girlfriend Alexis Wilkins
