articleTitle: Can’t save ‘eroded’ marriage just by legally preserving it: Orissa High Court backs divorce
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Orissa High Court Marriage Divorce Cruelty
description: The Orissa High Court held that compelling a wife to resume a marriage marked by sustained mental anguish and eroded trust would be unrealistic.
body_raw: The Orissa High Court recently refused to reverse a divorce granted by a family court, observing that the sanctity of a marriage cant be saved by preserving only the legal form of the relationship when its foundation has been substantially eroded. Chief Justice Harish Tandon and Justice Chittaranjan Dash were hearing an appeal filed by a husband against a family court order by which a divorce was granted to his wife on the ground of cruelty. Marriage undoubtedly carries a sanctity which the court must ordinarily endeavour to preserve. But the sanctity of marriage is not served by preserving only the legal form of the relationship when the substantive foundation of that relationship has been substantially eroded. Mutual respect, trust, companionship and a willingness to make reasonable adjustments are not peripheral attributes of matrimonial life they constitute its very foundation, the October 1 order read. The high court added, Where those attributes have been progressively lost and the relationship has become a source of sustained mental pain and anguish, the court cannot shut its eyes to the reality of the relationship merely because its deterioration cannot be fitted into one isolated or neatly defined category of conduct. According to the husband, the couple got married on October 20, 2021, following which they initially resided at Visakhapatnam before shifting to Hyderabad, where they worked in the Information Technology sector. The husband alleged that the couple later developed differences and the wife left the matrimonial home in June 2023 and went to Rayagada along with her parents, after which she filed a case for divorce on the basis of cruelty before the family court. On January 27, 2024, the family court dissolved the marriage. The husband then moved the high court with the current appeal. Wrongly dissolved marriage Advocate S K Dwivedy, appearing for the husband, argued that the family court had wrongly dissolved the marriage on the basis of cruelty, as the allegations of the wife were neither proved by evidence and nor were they enough to be called cruelty under the Hindu Marriage Act. He further stated that the husband had also instituted a case for resuming the marriage, which reflected his intention to continue the relationship. Advocate T K Mishra, representing the wife, submitted that she had specifically named acts of physical and mental cruelty meted out to her during the marriage, along with evidence. He added that the husbands conduct had caused mental agony to the wife and rendered continuation of the matrimonial relationship impossible. Continuing discord The high court stated that ordinary wear and tear of married life, trivial irritations, occasional quarrels or differences arising in the course of matrimonial life cannot, by themselves, furnish a ground for dissolution of marriage. The conduct complained of must be of such a nature and degree as to cause a reasonable apprehension that it would not be possible for the parties to continue living together. According to the bench, Mental cruelty, by its very nature, may not always be capable of direct proof, and the effect of the conduct upon the mind of the spouse has to be assessed having regard to the circumstances, the status and background of the parties and the nature of the relationship. The high court observed that the evidence given by the wife could not be reduced to a case of a stray quarrel or an isolated matrimonial disagreement. As per the court, the allegations of physical assault and the specific incidents stated by the wife when seen as a whole, present a continuing course of discord. The court noted that the final separation of the couple was not an event occurring in isolation but the culmination of an already deteriorated matrimonial relationship and that according to the evidence there was not merely a difference in perception between two spouses, but a relationship in which the essential element of mutual confidence had substantially eroded. It further noticed that even when the parties were brought face to face before this court on March 20, the relationship could not be restored rather, both expressed their desire to bring the marital tie to an end. While granting divorce to the couple, the high court said that it did not grant a decree of divorce just because they were separated or wanted to end the marriage, but the foundation of the decree remains the cruelty established from the evidence. Accordingly, it refused to interfere with the family courts order and held that the matrimonial relationship has lost its essential character and that compelling the Respondent-Wife to resume such a relationship would be unrealistic.

articleTitle: Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI to be ‘SpaceXSI’: Where does ‘super intelligence’ term come from?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence tool Grok was used to launch strikes against Iran
description: Musk is joining US President Trump’s push to replace ‘AI’ with ‘SI’. But what does super intelligence mean, what are its origins, and why is it a contested term?
body_raw: Elon Musk has said that he will rename SpaceXs AI unit to closely reflect the term US President Donald Trump has been pushing, super intelligence or SI, instead of artificial intelligence. The tech billionaire in a post on X on Sunday, October 4, said that the name of SpaceXAI will be changed to SpaceXSI. However, he did not provide any further details regarding the Grok-makers rebrand. Yes, we will make that change, Musk said in a reply to a user on X asking him about the possibility of renaming SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI. The SpaceX CEO is one of the first bold-faced names in Big Tech looking to embrace Trumps preferred term for AI. Earlier, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang also said that data centres should now be referred to as superintelligence factories. These proposed name changes come days after tech CEOs and AI industry leaders met with Trump at the White House, and signed onto an agreement of voluntary safety standards that Trump said was morally binding. The voluntary pact primarily involves AI frontier companies teaming up with an independent external auditor to assess that models are operating as intended and implement internal controls to ensure that their AI agents do not hack systems. However, several critics have argued that AI is facing a crisis of public trust and a name change is unlikely to resolve mounting concerns over safety risks posed by the rapidly evolving technology. A look at Trumps super intelligence push Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Trump said, From this point forward, all of United States documents, and hopefully the worlds will be changed to use the much more accurate term super as opposed to artificial. So its super intelligence. The US president has even signed an executive order renaming artificial intelligence to super intelligence in order to better capture the fact that the technology does much more than imitate or automate discrete aspects of human intelligence. The executive order further requires US government agencies at the federal level to use the new term, or SI, when referring to the technology in public communications, websites, reports and policy documents. Michael Kratsios, director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, has reportedly been tasked with figuring out whether an official definition of the new term should be modified or expanded, as per the order. On one hand, AI industry leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have called for a deliberate slowdown of frontier AI progress and urged the government to implement federal guardrails on frontier AI models, Trump has so far opposed regulation. He has also repeatedly dismissed whistleblowers warnings of AI security risks as overblown and a hoax. The Trump administration has also set up a task force or Super Intelligence Force, which will be tasked with producing a report on the risks and opportunities of AI within 120. The group will be led by Trumps newly appointed AI czar, Jay Clayton, who also serves as the director of national intelligence. Meanwhile, California Governor Gavin Newsom has looked to counter Trumps super intelligence push by issuing an executive order of his own, requiring state agencies to refer to the technology only as artificial intelligence or AI. Super intelligence is clearly not coming from the White House - thats why California continues to lead, Newsom said in a statement. What does SI mean in the AI space? So far, super intelligence has been used by AI industry executives and researchers to refer to an AI system with cognitive capabilities that essentially outperform humans in all aspects of thinking. Currently, such an AI system is hypothetical and does not exist. The term is also a severely contested one. Proponents of AI often use it to describe systems that surpass human abilities and bring major benefits. On the other hand, AI safety advocates have warned that such systems could outpace human control and may lead to the extinction of human beings. There are several other terms in AI discourse that are closely related to super intelligence, but slightly vary in meaning. For instance, artificial super intelligence ASI, has its roots in a 2014 book titled Superintelligence Paths, Dangers, Strategies written by controversial philosopher Nick Bostrom. OpenAI has been pursuing artificial general intelligence AGI, which is an umbrella term used to refer to technology that outperforms humans in several tasks without specifically being trained to do so. However, in September 2024, Sam Altman outlined a heady vision of ASI and what it would be like to live in a world with such technology. It is possible that we will have superintelligence in a few thousand days it may take longer, but Im confident well get there, Altman wrote in his 2024 blog post titled The Intelligence Age. Another term popularised by a tech CEO is personal superintelligence. In August 2025, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg published a letter outlining his vision for personal superintelligence, which is rooted in the idea that people should use AI to achieve their personal goals. Metas vision is to bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We believe in putting this power in peoples hands to direct it toward what they value in their own lives. This is distinct from others in the industry who believe superintelligence should be directed centrally towards automating all valuable work, and then humanity will live on a dole of its output, he said.

articleTitle: Anti-CEC stir: Journalist detained 2 days after she alleged sexual harassment by cops
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police personnel detain All India Students' Association (AISA) National President Neha Bora during the ‘Citizens’ March’ from India Gate to Jantar Mantar, in New Delhi on Sunday. (ANI Photo)
description: The protesters had camped outside Parliament Street police station overnight, demanding against officers who allegedly sexually assaulted three women journalists
body_raw: The protest against the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged irregularities in Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls entered its fourth consecutive day on Monday, with the Delhi Police registering six FIRs and arresting 18 people in connection with the alleged instances of violence that broke out during a NSUI demonstration and for circulating AI generated poster of policemen, officers said on Monday. Among the six FIRs, four were related to violence, vandalism and rioting during the NSUI demonstration, one tied to an alleged attack on a CISF personnel and another related to circulating a fake poster that showed an officer allegedly sexually harassing a woman. Meanwhile, one of the three women journalists who had alleged sexual harassment by Delhi Police personnel while covering the anti-CEC protest has been detained along with 16 others on Monday, for camping overnight outside Parliament Street police station, demanding action against the officers. The same day also saw a CISF constable allegedly getting attacked with a knife by a protester amid an NSUI demonstration at Jantar Mantar. The developments came amid continued demonstrations near Jantar Mantar and growing demands for a probe into the allegations made by three female journalists, who have accused police personnel of sexually assaulting them while they were reporting on the stir on October 3. A senior police officer said restrictions under prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS had been imposed across the New Delhi district. According to the officer, gatherings were not permitted at Parliament Street because it is not an authorised protest location. On Monday morning, around 17 people who had spent the night outside the Parliament Street police station were detained. The group, comprising freelance journalists, YouTubers and one of the alleged victims of sexual assault, had gathered to demand registration of an FIR and action against the officers accused in the alleged sexual harassment case. The protesters were detained individually and taken by bus to Delhi Cantonment Police Station, officers said. The woman who has alleged harassment told reporters that the group wanted to enter the police station and meet senior officers to find out the status of her complaint. The detainees were subsequently released in the evening. The police had on Sunday confirmed receiving three separate complaints from female journalists alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during the October 3 demonstration near Jantar Mantar. The complaints have been handed over to the Crime Branch. Meanwhile, a separate incident involving a CISF constable was reported during an NSUI demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Monday afternoon. The constable deployed for law-and-order duties was allegedly attacked with a knife by a protester, officers said. The constable, identified as Vikram Kumar, was reportedly moving a young man away from the barricades towards the designated protest area when the man allegedly pulled out a knife and attempted to strike him in the neck, police said. Kumar allegedly raised his hand to protect himself, suffering a cut and scratches on his right elbow, officers said. Kumar was taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital and was later discharged. Security personnel at the site detained the alleged attacker and handed him over to the police, officers said. In a purported video recorded after the incident, Kumar said he immediately informed his senior officers after the alleged attack. Police are questioning the accused to determine how he obtained the knife and what prompted the alleged assault. Around 50 NSUI protesters were also detained during the demonstration and later released. Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janta Party CJP expressed support for the women who have alleged sexual harassment and demanded action against the police personnel named in the complaints. CJP legal team head Ratna Singh alleged on X that the woman complainant and others demanding registration of an FIR were detained and claimed that some detainees were assaulted. Police, however, denied the allegation of manhandling, saying the protesters resisted detention while male and female personnel were escorting them to the bus.

articleTitle: Michael Bracewell 6th to opt out of central contract with New Zealand this season
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Michael Bracewell has said that he remains available for the five-match T20I series against India. (AP Photo/Anjum Naveed)
description: Michael Bracewell is the sixth player to have opted for a "casual contract" with New Zealand for the 2026/27 season.
body_raw: All-rounder Michael Bracewell has become the latest New Zealand player to opt for a casual contract with the national team for the 202627 season to play in the Big Bash League in Australia, New Zealand Cricket said in a statement on Monday. The 35-year-old will be replaced on the central contract list by Northern Districts batter and former Wellington Firebirds captain Nick Kelly, who earns his first national contract eleven years after making his First Class debut, said NZC. The development comes after a month after Mark Chapman made a similar move. Other star names to have opted out of a central contract for the 202627 season are Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert. NZC further said that Bracewell remains available for selection for New Zealands upcoming five-match T20I series at home against India. The big-ticket series, part of Indias full tour of New Zealand that will also include a three-match ODI series and two Test matches, starts on October 22. The backing from New Zealand Cricket for me to take this opportunity at this stage of my career means a lot, Bracewell is quoted as saying in NZCs statement. As a white-ball only player, this felt like too good of an opportunity to pass up. Im still very much committed to the BLACKCAPS and cant wait to be involved in the upcoming India tour and future white-ball series. Ive also got my eyes firmly fixed on the opportunity to be involved in the inaugural NZ20 which is set to be introduced from next summer. New Zealand head coach Rob Walter said that he was happy that Kelly has got a central contract. The 33-year-old has played eight ODIs and seven T20Is for New Zealand. Nick stuck his hand up with his performances against Bangladesh and the West Indies in what was at times challenging batting conditions, said Walter. He has more than 300 professional matches under his belt and is one of the best fielders in the country, so he adds a lot to our contracted group.

articleTitle: Bengaluru techie drowns in abandoned quarry during Instagram trekking group’s outing
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru trekker drowning
description: Following an exhaustive two-day search, rescuers retrieved the body of techie Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay from a vast, waterlogged quarry pit near Yellammanadoddi.
body_raw: What began as a promising long-weekend getaway for a group of trekkers connected through Instagram ended in heartbreak near Jigani on the outskirts of Bengaluru. Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay, 30, an IIT Delhi postgraduate and associate user experience UX designer living in Halasuru, drowned after taking a dip in an abandoned, water-filled stone quarry. Originally from Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, Vinay built his career in Bengaluru over the past four years. On October 2, he set out for a holiday trek with eight companions met through an Instagram trekking circle, including his fiance, a veterinary doctor. Midway through their journey, the group paused at a massive stone quarry near Yellammanadoddi. Decommissioned nearly 15 years ago, the pit had gradually become a deep rainwater reservoir, tempting the trekkers to step in for a swim. The group spent nearly an hour and a half playing in the water before the outing took a sudden, fatal turn around 5.30 pm, when his friends realised Vinay was missing. For some time, I think the group might not have noticed Vinay. It appeared that he knew swimming and are investigating under what circumstances he drowned, a police officer said. Challenging search operation His friends attempts to find him were unsuccessful, leading to an urgent distress call to the Jigani police. Local residents also joined in to help, though the vast quarry presented a significant challenge. It is an abandoned quarry. Not many go to that place. We got to know around 6 pm on the day of the incident, and it was a very vast place to search, said Kalappa, a local resident. A desparate search operation unfolded over the next two days. Initial efforts by local Fire and Emergency Services expanded to include teams from the State Disaster Response Force SDRF, the National Disaster Response Force NDRF, and local divers. Authorities also called renowned expert scuba diver Eshwar Malpe and his team from coastal Karnataka to join the rescue efforts. Following a non-stop effort, rescue crews retrieved Vinays body at around 9 am on Sunday. The Jigani police registered a case of unnatural death based on a complaint filed by his brother.

articleTitle: ‘Mere paternity dispute not enough’: Kerala High Court refuses to order child’s DNA test
articleFeaturedImageAlt: paternity DNA test father child domestic violence case kerala high court
description: The court held that DNA test cannot be sought simply because the child's paternity is disputed. Before directing such a test, there must be initial material establishing non-access between spouses during the period under consideration.
body_raw: The Kerala High Court has refused to order the DNA test of a minor child to determine paternity, holding that such testing cannot be sought routinely without preliminary proof that the spouses had no access to each other during the relevant period. Justice Jobin Sebastian was dealing with a plea in connection with a domestic violence proceeding in which the husband sought a direction for the couples minor child to undergo a DNA test to ascertain paternity. In the absence of specific pleadings and prima facie material demonstrating non-access between the spouses during the relevant period, a direction for DNA profiling cannot be sought as a matter of course merely on the basis of an allegation disputing paternity, the court said on September 26. The ruling held that a DNA test is not to be directed routinely and may be ordered only in appropriate and deserving cases where the court finds such examination necessary for the proper adjudication of the dispute. Unless non-access between the spouses during the relevant period is prima facie established, evidence cannot be permitted for the purpose of disproving the paternity of a child born during the subsistence of the marriage, it observed. Husband disputes childs paternity The case arose from proceedings under the provisions of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, initiated by a woman and her minor child before the trial court. They sought maintenance and return of the womans gold ornaments. During the pendency of those proceedings, the husbandrespondent disputed that he was the minor childs biological father. He filed an application seeking a direction for the child to undergo a DNA test, claiming that it would establish that he was not the childs biological father. He also contended that the woman had agreed to undergo the DNA test during mediation. The trial court, however, dismissed the application. Aggrieved, the husband approached the high court challenging the order. Marriage raises presumption of childs legitimacy The court observed that proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act are meant to adjudicate allegations of domestic violence and provide legal reliefs, and not to determine the biological parentage of a child. It noted that the marital relationship between the parties was undisputed. Since there was no material showing that the husband had no access to the wife during the relevant period, the presumption under the Indian Evidence Act operates in favour of the childs legitimacy. The court explained that Section 112 of the Indian Evidence Act embodies a rule of public policy intended to protect the legitimacy of children born during a valid marriage. The ruling said that such legitimacy is conclusive unless it is shown that the spouses had no access to each other when the child could have been conceived. It further observed, A consensual understanding reached during mediation cannot, by itself, compel a court to order a DNA examination unless the court independently finds that such an examination is legally permissible, necessary, and justified in the facts and circumstances of the case. Parties cannot, by consent, require a court to pass an order contrary to law or public policy. Since there was no material establishing non-access, the presumption of legitimacy remained operative. The high court, hence, found that the magistrate was justified in refusing to direct the DNA examination and dismissed the petition.

articleTitle: Egyptian shopkeeper catches child falling from balcony: ‘Had no time to think’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Man saves kid falling from balcony video in Egypt
description: CTV footage from Giza Governorate captured the moment shopkeeper Ahmed Ragab sprang into action to catch a 4-year-old boy who fell from a second-floor balcony after briefly tangling in a washing line.
body_raw: An Egyptian shopkeeper has become an internet hero after rescuing a four-year-old boy who fell from a second-floor balcony in Giza Governorate. CCTV captured the incident, and the video has gone viral on social media. According to a report in Khaleej Times, Ahmed Ragab was standing outside his fathers shop in a densely populated neighbourhood when he heard screams and noticed the child falling from the balcony of a nearby building. The boy initially landed on a washing line attached to the balcony. The tangled clothesline briefly slowed his fall, giving Ragab enough time to react, the report added. The video shows him running straight to the child and catching him before he hit the ground. After catching the boy, Ragab is seen looking towards the balcony before walking away with the child in his arms. Watch here View this post on Instagram A post shared by Al Jazeera English aljazeeraenglish No time to think Speaking to local media, Ragab said he did not have time to think about the risks before rushing to save the child. I had no time to think or calculate the risks. All that was on my mind was to try to save this child before he hits the ground, a local media outlet quoted him as saying, as per Khaleej Times. Ragab, who works at his fathers shop, recalled hearing screams before seeing the boy tangled in the washing line and then falling towards the ground. He said he was shaken after the rescue and struggled to process what had happened. I lost my nerve, he said. The video quickly gained traction, drawing numerous reactions. Several users hailed Ragab, with one commenting, With those reflexes, he was really the right person in the right place at the right time, a user wrote. Wow wow wowwww, glad the right manhero was right there and that child is ok, another user commented. Thats quick response saves the Life. A brave work, a third user reacted.

articleTitle: Rs 2.5 cr film Premada Ooralli beats Yash’s Toxic to emerge as most profitable Kannada movie
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Premada Ooralli
description: The financial constraints during the making of Premada Ooralli were so severe that, on one occasion, Kumar even asked his mother to pawn her mangalsutra, or thaali in Kannada, to help complete the shoot.
body_raw: Another small-budget film is becoming the talk of the town. This time, Kannada romantic drama Premada Ooralli has witnessed a remarkable jump at the box office. After opening at just Rs 9 lakh, the film earned Rs 3.5 crore on its tenth day, taking its total India net collection to Rs 16.96 crore. Made on a modest budget of just Rs 2.5 crore, Premada Ooralli is being touted as one of the most profitable films in Kannada cinema, alongside Love Mocktail 3 and Karavali. The film continues to draw audiences, with multiple shows in Bengaluru filling up even on a Monday, according to BookMyShow. From no shows to housefull According to industry tracker Sacnilk, the film opened to just Rs 9 lakh across 60 shows, partly because it did not feature a major Kannada star. However, word-of-mouth helped the film gain momentum almost immediately. On day two, Premada Ooralli saw its earnings rise by Rs 14 lakh, while the number of shows increased by 21. On day three, it earned Rs 55 lakh across 155 shows, recording a 55 occupancy. The film continued to grow even on weekdays, earning Rs 65 lakh on its first Monday and Rs 95 lakh on Tuesday. On its second Sunday, it collected Rs 3.85 crore, taking its India net total to Rs 14.57 crore at that point. Within 10 days, the film had crossed the one-million footfall mark in theatres. On its 11th day, Premada Ooralli had already crossed the Rs 1 crore mark, with the film running across 311 shows. Premada Ooralli to become the most profitable Kannada film While Toxic was one of the biggest Kannada releases of the year, the film failed to make an impact at the box office and reportedly could not recover its massive budget of over Rs 500 crore. Meanwhile, Love Mocktail 3, made on a reported budget of Rs 2 crore, earned Rs 18.55 crore at the box office, delivering nearly 10 times its investment. It was subsequently regarded as one of the most profitable Kannada films of the 21st century. Premada Ooralli, however, is now threatening to surpass that record, having already come close to its lifetime collection within just 10 days. Featuring a cast of relatively new faces, the film is directed by National Award-winning filmmaker Manoj Kumar. He won the National Award for Best Feature Film in Kannada for his debut film Akshi, which was made on a budget of just Rs 23 lakh and shot over 55 days. Produced by Vannila Entertainment, Janakamma Productions and Mukul Gowda Productions, the film stars Rangayana Raghu, Shree Raam, Thapaswini Poonacha and Ramika Shivu. The films trailer has garnered over 2.3 million views, while its songs have also found an audience online. Several tracks have clocked millions of views, with Eru Peru Hrudaya alone garnering 4.5 million views on YouTube. But the films journey to the big screen was far from easy. ALSO READ Rakul Preet distances herself from Vashu Bhagnani I-T raids No Benami property Begged people to give the film a chance By the time the shoot wrapped up, the makers had virtually no budget left for marketing. Their solution was unconventional they printed wedding-style invitation cards, boarded buses and trains, handed them to commuters and begged people to give the film a chance. Speaking to Cinema Express, Manoj Kumar recalled how the film initially struggled to find an audience. They plastered posters on autorickshaws we truly owe those drivers. At 1030 AM that Friday, not a whisper. By 130 PM, complete silence. Then came the 630 PM show, and word-of-mouth caught fire. What started across roughly 60 centres surged to 450 by Sunday. Jayanna Combines rolled in like a JCB to clear the path. Distributor Jayanna told us, Every single show through Sunday is houseful till October 4, even you wont get a ticket. Despite National Award win, director had no work Manoj Kumars return to filmmaking comes five years after his debut, but the gap was not by choice. Despite winning a National Award for Akshi, he struggled to find work. After winning the National Award for Akshi, I couldnt even find work people assumed backing an art-house director meant losing money. Devendra, our co-writer and producer, stepped up with his savings, he said. The financial constraints during the making of Premada Ooralli were so severe that, on one occasion, Kumar even asked his mother to pawn her mangalsutra, or thaali in Kannada, to help complete the shoot. When the director had to pawn his mothers mangalsutra Thapaswini Poonacha, one of the films leads, recalled the emotional incident. It was 630 PM, fading daylight, and our artificial rain water ran completely dry. Local villagers pumped water from their borewell to help us. Just then, Manoj sir stepped aside to call his mother, which Shree Ram and I overheard. Keep your thaali ready to pawn tomorrow todays budget is over, and if we dont get the shot now, we must extend the shoot. That broke us emotionally. Sir had told me Rukminis tears must never spill carelessly, they had to brim right in the eye. In that one single take, the rain, camera angles, and our emotions locked into place. When he yelled cut, hugged us, and told his mother, Keep your thaali, we finished in one take, I simply broke down. Premada Oorallis success is part of a larger trend in 2026, which has seen several small-budget films make an outsized impact at the box office across regional industries, including Hindis Hanuman Ansh, Marathis Deool Band 2 and Malayalams Bethlehem Kuduma Unit. In 2025, Gujarati film Laalo was all over the news for earning over Rs 120 crore after being made on a budget of just Rs 1.2 crore.

articleTitle: How a drug drop in Rohini led Delhi Police to heroin worth Rs 50 crores in Lucknow
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lucknow raid
description: Delhi Police crack an inter-state drug network and seize 6.25 kg of heroin from a drug manufacturing unit in Lucknow
body_raw: Heroin worth around Rs 50 crore was seized on Sunday from a drug manufacturing unit in Lucknow, which the supply chain led Delhi Police to after it intercepted a drug delivery in Delhis Rohini on September 16. On the night of September 16, a team of police from Rohinis Special Staff division had stopped a white SUV in Sector 32 of the Begumpur area. In the car was 58-year-old Laxman Hooda who was carrying 300 grams of heroin to deliver to a client, said police. Officers said that they had received a tip-off about this delivery and were waiting there for Hooda. 300 grams of Heroin and 3 lakh cash were recovered from his Grand Vitara car, which was also seized, said DCP Shashank Jaiswal. According to police, Hooda told them about his supplier, a resident of Delhis Raghubir Nagar named Anil, alias Bhola, who was on the run. Police traced him to Haryanas Sonipat and arrested him there, seizing yet another 500 gram package of heroin from him. Then, police said, Anil told them that he was getting his supply from a man he identified as Bablu from Lucknow. It took police another 15 days to zero in on the identity and location of this supplier. When they found him, they also found over 6 kg of heroin. On the basis of technical surveillance and human intelligence, on 04.10.2026, a raid was conducted at a heroin manufacturing facility in Sita Colony, Jankipuram, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, and Bablu, was apprehended. During the raid, 6.275 Kg of freshly manufactured heroin was recovered, said DCP Jaiswal. This quantity of heroin, police said, is valued at about Rs. 50 crores in the international market. Inside the Sita Colony house, a whole cache of drug mixing supplies was found 2.504 kg Sodium, 787 grams Acetic Anhydride, one tub, gas cylinder, mixer grinder, utensils, polythene, an electronic weighing machine, and a wooden basket. Police said that Bablu told them during interrogation that all the supplies had come from Bareilly, from a man he identified as Ruksar Ali. Ruksar Ali Raju, the main source supplierowner of the manufacturing facility, was traced and apprehended from Bareilly, UP after a prolonged and intensive pursuit of 120 km, said DCP Jaiswal. This was the second big heroin bust in Rohini this year. In April, the cops apprehended a family-run heroin operation in Rohini, which led them, again, to Bareilly and other parts of UP, leading to the recovery of a batch worth Rs. 16 crores. The source of this was traced to Manipur, where two men were allegedly procuring opium poppy-from which heroin is extracted-from a woman in the Indo-Myanmar border.

articleTitle: Dead drops in Punjab to godowns in MP, how drug kingpin’s syndicate operated
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh, alias Navab Virk, sits inside an aircraft following his deportation from Turkiye to India. (Handout via PTI Photo)
description: A Delhi court has remanded the ‘drug kingpin’, who was deported from Turkey, to 10 days’ police custody.
body_raw: Narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh, accused of running an international heroin syndicate, allegedly told investigators that drugs were delivered through dead drops - buried at multiple locations in Punjab and stored in godowns in Madhya Pradesh - according to the prosecution. A Delhi court on Saturday remanded the 34-year-old to 10 days custody of the Delhi Police Special Cell, which told the court it needed to recover the drugs, trace the syndicates supply chain, and identify other people involved in the alleged trafficking network. Navpreet, 34, was deported from Turkiye and arrested at Delhi airport on Saturday. Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced his deportation in a post on X, saying Singh had obtained Turkish citizenship using the false identity of Navab Virk. The 2021 heroin case Navpreet was produced before Special Judge, Narcotic Drugs And Psychotropic Substances NDPS, Anuradha Shukla, at Rouse Avenue court on October 3 in a case dating back to July 2021. The Special Cell had then arrested a man in South Delhi and followed the trail to Faridabad, where a total of 358.08 kg of heroin was seized. During submissions, Special Public Prosecutor SPP Akhand Pratap Singh told the court, There is ample evidence against this accused Navpreet in form of his connection with co-accused Gurpreet and Gurjyot Singh, from whom huge quantity of heroin in total 358.08 kilogram was recovered. He also submitted that the co-accused had made disclosure statements against Navpreet. A cheque book recovered from the premises of co-accused Ramandeep belonged to the accused, the court order recorded. The court noted that Navpreet was declared a proclaimed offender on February 16, 2022. According to the prosecution, he had avoided investigation and court proceedings for more than four years. The court order also recorded the prosecutions submission that Navpreet had inflicted injuries on his hand and stomach when he was being handed over to the Special Cell. He was taken to Medanta Hospital at the Delhi Airport for medical treatment. Police seek to trace supply chain, identify associates According to the Special Cells remand papers, it sought Navpreets custody to question him about the alleged syndicates operations, his movements and the preparation of his passport in Delhi, as well as to confront him with statements made by other accused. It also sought to identify and apprehend other alleged suppliers, financiers, carriers and facilitators. The disclosure of the accused is on record wherein he has stated that he used to deliver drugs through dead drop, SPP Singh told the court. In a dead drop, a consignment is left at an agreed location for someone else to collect later. SPP Singh said Navpreet had told investigators that drugs had been buried at several places in Punjab and that he could identify the locations and help recover them. . the accused, in his disclosure, also stated that his associates, Labba and Manna, had taken godowns in MP where drugs were kept and there is a house in Punjab also which can be identified, the order reads. Judge Shukla said, The investigation necessitates police custody of the accused to recover the buried drugs which were dead dropped and other drugs which accused has stated that he has kept hidden to unearth the supply chain, source and transportation route for identification of other persons involved in procurement, transportation, storage and distribution and to establish complete financial trail connected with the illegal drug trade. The accused has to be taken to Punjab and MP for investigation purposes. For the needful to be done, 10 days police custody is being sought, which seems reasonable, the NDPS Judge said in the order. Navpreet is also an accused in a 2022 terror case lodged by the Special Cell. The case pertains to using funds allegedly obtained from selling narcotics to finance terror activities. A trail in Punjab Navpreet is from Wazir Bhulla village in the Beas area of Amritsar. He was first arrested in Punjab in a drug smuggling case in 2013 and was acquitted in 2017. Navpreets name re-surfaced in October 2024, when the Punjab Police counter-intelligence wing seized 105 kg of heroin at Baba Bakala. The two men arrested at that time were allegedly his associates. The India-based operations of the alleged drug syndicate were run by his cousin, Prabhdeep Singh alias Harry. Prabhdeep was extradited from Azerbaijan on May 13 by the Central Bureau of Investigation in coordination with the Special Cell.

articleTitle: ‘We were in love for 1.5 years’: Jason Sanjay on how his only relationship before Sigma ended
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Director Jason Sanjay, who has spoken publicly for the first time about his only romantic relationship
description: Director Jason Sanjay has revealed details about his only romantic relationship, a year-and-a-half-long college romance that ended in a mutual breakup while he was studying overseas.
body_raw: Jason Sanjay, director of Sigma and the son of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay, has spoken publicly for the first time about his personal life, revealing that he has had only one romantic relationship, a college romance that lasted about a year and a half before ending in a mutual breakup. The period following the breakup was when he fully committed himself to making Sigma. There was only one love. It was a long time ago, when we were in college. We were in love for about a year and a half, Jason Sanjay said in a conversation with VJ Siddhu. It was a mutual breakup. We both talked to each other and broke up. Jason Sanjay, who studied filmmaking, said the breakup happened while he was overseas. The distance, he said, made the experience both isolating and clarifying. Also Read Sigma movie review Jason Sanjays debut has the vision but not the script to match Asked how he coped, Jason Sanjay answered, During the breakup, I used to listen to all the love songs of Yuvan Shankar Raja. The director later revealed that he deliberately stayed away from social media during and after the breakup.I didnt have any plans to post stories on Instagram. If we post stories after the breakup and then reconnect, we cant get out of it. So we kept a distance between us. I always control myself to not do things that I dont want to do, Jason Sanjay said. Jason Sanjay said he is at peace with the relationship and its ending. Im okay now. It was good at the time. We move on with our lives, he said. And then came the line that connects his personal life to his professional one After that, I got down to Sigmas business. About Sigma Sigma, an action-adventure heist comedy, stars Sundeep Kishan in the lead alongside Faria Abdullah, Raju Sundaram, Sampath Raj, Shiv Panditt, Anbu Thasan and Yog Japee. The music is composed by S Thaman, cinematography is by Krishnan Vasant, editing by Praveen KL and VFX by Hariharasuthan. The film is produced by Subaskaran under Lyca Productions. The film was originally scheduled to release on July 31, but was postponed to avoid clashing with Vijays final film Jana Nayagan. The movie was released worldwide on October 2.

articleTitle: IIT Madras offers executive courses; here’s how to apply
articleFeaturedImageAlt: IIT Madras launches executive education programs
description: IIT Madras has started the registration process for these courses on the official portal, code.iitm.ac.in, with candidates required to apply online by paying the prescribed enrolment fees.
body_raw: The Indian Institute of Technology IIT Madras is offering a set of executive education certificate courses from October to November 2026, spanning areas such as electric vehicles, manufacturing, construction technology, ESG and supply chain management. Designed by the institutes Centre for Outreach and Digital Education CODE, the courses are aimed at professionals and learners looking to build skills aligned with emerging industry and job-market requirements. The upcoming offerings also mark a widening of IIT Madras executive education portfolio beyond its traditional engineering and technology focus, with courses covering business and sustainability-related domains. The registration process for these courses has started by IIT Madras on the official portal of CODE at code.iitm.ac.in, with candidates required to apply online by paying the prescribed enrolment fees. The upcoming executive education course cohorts include Certificate Program on Electric Vehicles CPEV This is a short-term executive certificate programme being offered on electric vehicles EVs by the CODE at IIT Madras in collaboration with industry experts. In this programme, the foundational theory will cover technical areas such as batteries, motors, power electronics, EMI or EMC, market, cost, and industry-specific fields like vehicle engineering and development. articleTitle: Supreme Court refuses to intervene in pleas challenging Great Nicobar Project
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Great Nicobar Project, Great Nicobar Project case, Supreme Court Great Nicobar Project, Calcutta High Court Great Nicobar Project PIL, Forest Rights Act violations, Great Nicobar PIL, Great Nicobar tribal rights, Great Nicobar environmental case, Meena Gupta Great Nicobar Project PIL, Great Nicobar infrastructure project, Supreme Court news, Calcutta High Court, Indian express news
description: The Centre had challenged the Calcutta High Court order rejecting its objection to petitions filed by retired IAS officer Meena Gupta against the Great Nicobar project.
body_raw: The Supreme Court Monday refused to intervene in a Calcutta High Court order, that allowed PILs challenging alleged Forest Rights Act violations in the Great Nicobar Project to proceed, saying the matter was already pending before the high court. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also pointed out that the main case is pending for final arguments and is listed for hearing on November 25 and 26. The Centre argued that the project was of great national importance and the maintainability of such Public Interest Litigations goes to the root of the matter. If I am able to place something more regarding maintainability, please allow us to place that submission. Do not close the door on maintainability because something very important turns on that, Attorney General of India R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre, submitted before the court. Justice Bagchi observed that the high court had already ruled on maintainability and that the question now was on how far public interest survives, which would be considered there. Do they become integrated completely with the mainstream, or do we keep them with their unique identity and the identity of their culture? Preservation of culture is a constitutionally protected fundamental right, Justice Bagchi said, referring to the projects impact on indigenous communities. Let the high court take necessary steps to complete pleadings in the other matters and make an endeavour to hear the cases on the date fixed, the bench noted. What Calcutta High Court said The Centre had approached the top court challenging the Calcutta High Courts May 6 judgement, which rejected its objection to PILs filed by retired IAS officer Meena Gupta. Guptas petitions challenge decisions linked to the Great Nicobar Project, including alleged violations of the Forest Rights Act in obtaining consent from tribal communities and notifications reducing eco-sensitive buffer zones around Galathea and Campbell Bay National Parks. The Centre had argued that Gupta, a resident of Hyderabad, lacked legal standing and that a project involving a proposed port, airport, power plant, and defence infrastructure could not be challenged through a PIL. Rejecting the objection, the Calcutta High Court held, There is no thumb rule regarding the aspect of locus standi. It would not be expedient to lay down any general rule which would govern all cases under all circumstances. The high court also said that merely because a project involves substantial public expenditure, it is not insulated from judicial review, observing that a project involving huge expenditure must proceed in accordance with governing laws holding the field. What is the Great Nicobar Project The Great Nicobar Project is a proposed large-scale development programme that involves building a major transhipment port, airport, power plant, and other infrastructure, along with associated roads and development, at an estimated cost of around Rs 72,000 crore. The project has faced criticism over its potential impact on tribal communities and their rights alleged violations of the Forest Rights Act and environmental clearance norms changes to protections around ecologically sensitive areas such as Galathea Bay and Campbell Bay and the large-scale diversion of forest land and its impact on wildlife and biodiversity. The Centres position is that the project is of major strategic and national importance, including because of Great Nicobars location near major international shipping routes.

articleTitle: Why more Indian students are choosing Ireland over UK, Europe for education
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ireland Trinity college Dublin
description: Latest data shows Indian students now form the largest international cohort in Irish universities, driven by lower total costs, a thriving tech sector, and favourable post-study work norms.
body_raw: Written by Sameer Anasingaraju Ireland is increasingly emerging as a preferred destination for Indian students pursuing higher education abroad, with its English-speaking environment, shorter postgraduate courses and post-study work opportunities drawing students away from traditional destinations like the United Kingdom UK and other European countries. According to the Ireland Higher Education Authority HEA, 44,535 non-Irish-domiciled enrolments were recorded in higher education in 2024-25, a 10.2 per cent increase from the previous year. Indian students formed the largest international cohort, accounting for 20.6 per cent of these enrolments, around 9,175 students. While the numbers may be modest compared with the number of students who go abroad every year for studies, the uptick is unmistakable. From just over 2,000 students in 2017-18, the numbers rose steadily before the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted international student mobility. The recovery after the pandemic, however, was followed by a much sharper rise. Enrolments crossed 4,000 in 2021-22, then jumped to 7,070 in 2023-24. By 2024-25, the figure had climbed to 9,175, meaning Ireland was receiving more than four times as many Indian students as it did seven years earlier. The particularly steep increase in the last two years suggests that Irelands appeal is no longer limited to a small group of students, but is becoming a mainstream alternative for Indians considering education in the UK, US and other European countries. The English factor For many, Irelands use of English as the primary language of instruction is one of its biggest advantages over countries like Germany and the Netherlands, alongside shorter masters programmes, particularly when comparing overall costs. Tanishka Prabhu, 22, from Pune, studied at Griffith College Dublin from 2023-2025 and now works in Ireland. I came here for my bachelors. Mostly Indians come for masters here. When I came in January 2023, there were very few Indian students. But now they are here in huge numbers, Prabhu said. I chose Ireland because my elder sister also did her masters here, and while researching, we found out that expenses are lower than in Europe. It is an English-speaking country, and the weather is extremely nice too. Saanvi Gambhir, pursuing a masters in finance at University College Cork, had initially considered Germany. I chose Ireland as the post-study norms are much better than the UK. I was planning for Germany, but there is also the language barrier there. Here, theres no such issue. Aman Nanda, also pursuing finance at University College Cork, compared Ireland with the UK. I was initially planning for the UK, but I chose Ireland because the quality of life, education, and economy are much better than there, he said. My experience has been really amazing. Everyone is extremely nice and helpful here, with absolutely zero racism towards Indians. The course quality is excellent, and so are the teachers teaching it. Sadaf Sheikh, 28, is pursuing an LLM at Trinity College Dublin and initially considered the Netherlands. I wanted to go to the Netherlands, but it is much more costly than Ireland. Here the masters is only for one year, and we can work for two years after it is over. Sustainable career at affordable cost For Akheel Sisal, going abroad was a childhood dream, but the real question was where education could lead to a sustainable career without overwhelming costs. After his MBA in Pune and experience as a data analyst, he explored European colleges, but consultancies flagged his undergraduate record as a hurdle - until Ireland emerged unexpectedly. I started checking with friends studying in Ireland, and they told me the IT market was growing, there were job opportunities, and the process was relatively easy, Sisal recalls. Compared to the uncertainty of the United States - high tuition, heavy loans, visa concerns - Ireland seemed more manageable. The US was never an option because of the uncertainty, he says. Some of my friends had hefty loans and were still struggling to pay them back. Despite being warned his profile might not secure admission, Sisal received three acceptance letters and chose National College of Irelands one-year Masters in Data Analytics, with a E4,000 scholarship on a E15,000 fee. I asked if I would have to study from huge notebooks and prepare for written examinations. They told me the programme was much more practical and lab-focused. I knew then that this was where I wanted to go. Before graduating, he secured a full-time role and now works as a data and AI manager. Consultants see a pattern Education consultants in Pune also report rising interest. Digvijay Sawant of Imperial Overseas Educational Consultants said Ireland particularly attracts students in technology, pharma, and management. There is a rise in recent years of people going to Ireland. Ireland is known for three things IT, pharma, and management, noting the country is often called the Silicon Valley of Europe. In other European countries or the US, the masters programme is for two years. In Ireland, it is only for one year. After that, you can stay back for two years. Also, there is no language barrier. Costs are also down because youre only paying for 1 year of education instead of two, Sawant said. The seats for Ireland are getting filled very fast. Last year, we sent around 20-25 students to Ireland. We are currently on track to beat that number this year, he said. With inputs from Kalyani Lad. Sameer Anasingaraju is an intern with The Indian Express.

articleTitle: CJI Surya Kant: Any modified Form 6 not approved by Supreme Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court Election Commission of India SIR Form 6 Gyanesh Kumar
description: Referring to The Indian Express report, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy argued that the Election Commission had made an 'unlawful alteration' to Form 6, targeting first-time voters.
body_raw: In response to an argument on the unlawful modifications made to Form 6, which new voters have to fill, Chief Justice of India CJI Surya Kant on Monday said that the Supreme Court hadnt approved any of the modifications to Form 6 and indicated that the court will examine who had modified it upon receiving a report from the Election Commission. The statement came when a three-judge bench headed by the CJI was hearing the petitions filed against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. For the first time, the Election Commissions online version of the electors registration form, known as Form 6, included a new section that seeks the status of the applicants parents vis-a-vis the last Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, even though the statutory form itself has not been amended. The Election Commission, however, removed the SIR declaration added to Form 6 from its ECINET application portal in states where the SIR has concluded. The poll body had on September 26 announced that for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used. Referring to The Indian Express report, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy argued, Let me give you an illustration.since it pertains to most recently, for instance, Delhi. Let us see how the SIR was conducted in Delhi. Form 6 has two new conditions added. Those Forms 6 were circulated. Neither the petitioner is now allowed to be on the roll. I got a notice also.based on this new Form 6, which cannot, under the schedule, be modified. Responding to Guruswamy, the CJI said, Lets be very clear. Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let us also be clear that when the report will be produced, we will like to see who has modified what. Form 6 coverage The Indian Express had reported on the Election Commissions September 26 press note on Form 6. The ECI had then said the form prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules will apply outside the SIR period. The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used, it read. Guruswamy was arguing a petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, which stated, Defying this binding majority, respondent number 3 Gyanesh Kumar, acting in concert with respondent number 6 DG-IT, altered Form 6 digitally on the ECINet portal in July 2026. On August 13, 2026, Commissioner Sandhu formally recorded that this alteration was unauthorised and illegal and was causing arbitrary harassment to young, eligible first-time electors, ordering its immediate withdrawal. Despite this, the unauthorised form was kept live on the portal. The plea argues there was a unilateral and illegal alteration of statutory Form 6 for first-time young voters without legislative authority or amendment of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 which could be termed unauthorised and illegal by a majority of the Commission. The petition further alleged that the act of the Chief Election Commissioner of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bears no reasonable nexus or legal connection to his official duties. Such an act falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability, it added.

articleTitle: India’s HPV vaccine Cervavac gets WHO’s safety nod
articleFeaturedImageAlt: hpv
description: Previously approved for its use in India by the drug controller, Cervavac is administered for the prevention of diseases caused by the four HPV types
body_raw: Cervavac, Indias first indigenously developed gender-neutral quadrivalent Human Papillomavirus vaccine qHPV developed by Serum Institute of India has got the prequalification status by the World Health Organization WHO. This regulatory milestone marks the 32nd WHO prequalification for productsbiologicals received by Serum Institute of India. Inclusion on the WHO List of Prequalified Vaccines allows Cervavac to be procured by United Nations UN agencies. The vaccine targets HPV types 6, 11, 16 and 18. It is indicated for girls and boys aged nine through 26 years. Adar Poonawalla, Chief Executive Officer, Serum Institute of India, said, WHO prequalification of CERVAVAC is an important step in strengthening the global response to HPV. This milestone reflects the effectiveness of the vaccine and creates the opportunity for countries to prevent HPV-related risks. We are pleased to see this indigenously developed vaccine reach this achievement, and look forward to contributing to immunisation coverage, advancing global healthcare Previously approved for its use in India by the Drugs Controller General of India DCGI, Cervavac is administered for the prevention of diseases caused by the four HPV types. This includes the prevention of anal cancer in boys and young men, and cervical, vulvar, vaginal, and anal cancers in girls and young women. It is also indicated in preventing genital warts, as applicable to the indicated population. Cervavac is indicated in girls and women between 9 through 26 years of age for the prevention of cervical, vulvar, vaginal and anal cancer caused by HPV types 16 and 18, and genital warts caused by HPV types 6 and 11. Cervavac is indicated in boys and men 9 through 26 years of age for the prevention of anal cancer caused by HPV types 16 and 18, and genital warts caused by HPV types 6 and 11. Those between 9 and 14 years of age receive Cervavac according to a two-dose schedule 0.5 mL at 0, 6 months, while individuals 15 to 26 years of age receive a three -dose 0.5 mL at 0, 2, 6 months schedule. The vaccine is administered intramuscularly. Cervavac is available in 1-dose vials of 0.5 ml and 2-dose vials of 1.0 ml presentations.

articleTitle: ‘He asked if I had AIDS’: Gayathri Suresh on her past toxic ‘situationship’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 alumna Gayathri Suresh about a toxic relationship.
description: Evicted Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 contestant Gayathri Suresh once opened up about a past toxic relationship in the house, revealing the shocking aftermath of her viral 2021 car accident.
body_raw: Although Bigg Boss Malayalam is known for delivering shocking surprises from time to time, even the shows biggest fans didnt expect to see actor Gayathri Suresh evicted from the ongoing edition of the Mohanlal-hosted show on its second day itself. Even more surprising was the way she re-entered the house on Day 9. Now, after about three weeks, Gayathri has bid farewell to the reality series once and for all. Gayathri was one of the eight contestants who were shown the door during the past weekends mass eviction. A few days before she stepped out the front door, she made certain remarks, revealing the darkest and most painful chapter of her personal life, which have caught peoples attention. Must Read My father married around 20 people Sreelakshmi Arackal reveals traumatic childhood Gayathri Suresh on the incident that traumatised her the most During one of the tasks, Bigg Boss asked her, If you got an opportunity to speak to the person who hurt you the most in life, what would you say? Gayathri then opened up about a past situationship that scarred her emotionally. Many people have hurt me in my life. but what hurt me the most, or rather what traumatised me the most, happened when I was embroiled in a controversy in 2021. At that time, I was in a situationship. I thought it was a relationship, but looking back now, I think it was just a situationship, she recalled. Although that person displayed major red flags from the beginning, the actor said she still gave him multiple chances to correct himself, as that was her nature. Im someone who notices everyones red flags quickly. Yet, I give people three chances, and then theyre out of my life. In the first week of our relationship, he asked me if I had AIDS. At that moment, I cut him off, she said. But then, you dont know if youre being too negative, always looking for red flags. Hence, I continued the relationship. Later, I found out that he was in a relationship with someone else. While I am based in Thrissur, he lives in Ernakulam, and there, he was in a relationship with another girl, the actor revealed. Gayathri Suresh on her viral 2021 car accident She continued, At that time, I was at rock bottom myself. Yes, I also have a lot of bad habits, so I wouldnt say I am a perfect person. But I have a good heart and dont want to hurt anyone. Then he started ignoring me completely. One day, I put my foot down and told him I had to see him, so he came. We were together in a car when the controversial accident happened. Also Read Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr For the unversed, in October 2021, the car Gayathri Suresh was travelling in with a male friend, who was behind the wheel at the time of the incident, reportedly collided with another vehicle. Instead of stopping immediately, they allegedly drove away. The occupants of the second vehicle pursued them and eventually forced them to stop. Soon, a crowd gathered, and the matter escalated. Videos of the incident also went viral. During the Bigg Boss task, she further recalled, The police came and took him to the station following the accident. After coming back, he left me alone in a cafe and went to see his other girlfriend. That was the most traumatising thing for me. ICYMI Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner Avinash Mishra takes home trophy and Rs 20 lakh She added, So if I were to see him again, I would say, Thank you so much. I can clearly imagine what his girlfriend went through because it was a narcissistic relationship and there was narcissistic abuse. So if I see him now, Id say, Thank you so much for going after someone else. Otherwise, I would have had to suffer in that relationship. I grew because of that. I decided then that I would get better and grow. Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 mass eviction Jaseela Parveen, Sumesh Chandran, Sreelakshmi Arackal, Loletta, Rakesh, RJ Anjali and Mridula were the other seven contestants to exit Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 along with Gayathri Suresh. Meanwhile, a day after the mass eviction, four wildcard contestants - Nilina Elizabeth Joseph, Vedangi Cherukattu, Vipin Das Nair, and Suvarna Pulthukkiyil - entered the house.
