articleTitle: ‘So much more at peace’: Aishwarya Lekshmi on life after quitting social media
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Aishwarya Lekshmi spoke about attaining peace after quitting social media
description: Actress Aishwarya Lekshmi has spoken about her decision to quit social media, saying she is 'in a better place in life' since stepping away.
body_raw: Actress Aishwarya Lekshmi has said she is so much more at peace since stepping away from social media, while acknowledging that the reasons that drove her off the platforms still exist. On the other hand, producer Soundarya Rajinikanth defended the platforms as a necessary professional tool that crosses a line when criticism turns personal. Aishwarya, who deactivated her social media accounts earlier this year, said the decision has given her a sense of calm she did not have before. Its falling in place. Im happy with my life as it is right now. So much more at peace than I was while I was on social media, she said in a conversation with Puja Talwar. She added, I do see that the things that were the reason I made the decision to get out of social media still prevail in certain quantities. But at least Im not there always watching it and getting affected by things like that. Im generally in a better place in life. Soundarya Rajinikanth, who sat along Aishwarya Lekshmi and Arjun Das during the promotional interaction for their Netlfix series Love, offered a producers perspective on the same issue. I think you cant deny the fact that social media does play a part. But where it crosses the line is when professional stops and personal attacks or comments start, Soundarya Rajinikanth said, adding, Even for us as producers, we do look into Instagram forecasting. We do want to know the comments. We do want to know how a trailer is received. Thats not something Im going to deny. Also Read Felt exposed to viciousness Why Aishwarya Lekshmi has no plans to return to social media She then drew a distinction between the experience of people behind the camera and those in front of it. Its different for our artistes because theyre in front of the camera. Its different for makers, storytellers because were behind the camera. Maybe we dont get targeted as insensitively as they do. It is difficult for them, so I understand why Aishwarya took the step that she did. Soundarya Rajinikanth said social media could work for the industry if the culture around it improved. If people have a little bit more sensitivity when they come on social media, itll make everything pleasant. We do need social media today. But I still feel it can be a lot cleaner than what it is, she said. Aishwarya Lekshmi was careful not to dismiss social media entirely. She acknowledged the power the platforms have given to independent creators and cited the example of Hashir, the Kerala-based Instagram influencer and content creator whose popularity on the platform led to him being cast as the lead in Vaazha 2, which went on to become one of the highest-grossing Malayalam films in history. The powers also with them content creators now. Earlier, you could say the industry didnt choose you. But now you also have a way to showcase your talent or build yourself up in a way that you cannot be ignored. In Kerala, one of the highest-grossing films recently was Vaazha 2, which was led by one of the most popular Instagram influencers, Hashir. Wonderful actor. People love him, Aishwarya said. But for Aishwarya Lekshmi, the professional benefits of being on social media were no longer worth the personal cost of what it was doing to her mental health. I do see that side. But personally, I was done.

articleTitle: Problem with school History books isn’t just the facts. It’s what they aren’t teaching
articleFeaturedImageAlt: history
description: The real issue lies in shifting the emphasis increasingly to lionised accounts of certain periods in history and presenting the past as a set of acts by a variety of actors engaged in religious antagonism. The interrogative character of historical studies is less frequently seen in these textbooks
body_raw: In recent decades, the periodic revisions of Indian school History textbooks have become increasingly tenuous and worrying. From the invention of fictitious narratives to the erasure or inappropriate abridgement of important periods in history, revisions have assumed several questionable forms. The new textbooks tend to present pieces of information that are sometimes contrary to facts, besides contradicting their own statements in some instances. The larger purpose of these textbook revisions is to present a communally informed account of Indias past that conceives of history as a story of antagonistic groups forced to share a geopolitical territory. History is the discipline that tells us how we reached the present and what it meant to live in times when human lives were organised differently. Human lives were transformed by deep-seated processes involving the introduction and increased use of metals, tools and weapons, fire, agriculture, livestock farming, the wheel, alphabets and numbers, money, monumental architecture and more. Ideas, ranging from god, value, valour and hierarchy to justice, equality, democracy and peace, have shaped human lives in profound ways. A lesson in History involves a nuanced understanding of this journey. Do the new History textbooks in our schools live up to this mandate? No, they do not. NCERTs new Social Science textbook for Grade IX, Understanding Society India and Beyond - Part 2, is the latest in a series of contestable textbook revisions. Released last Tuesday, the book putatively aims to equip students with the skills that are needed to grow. and to enhance their analytical, descriptive, and narrative capabilities. As it turns out, there is much to be desired in the book on these counts. Consider the chapter, Indias Long Road to Independence, which is meant to be an account of a decisive phase in Indian history. The chapter turns out to be an assorted set of events presented chronologically. Little is said in it of historical processes that might encourage critical thinking. Colonialism and nationalism are not defined or discussed in conceptual terms, and processes such as the growth of literature, the development of capitalism and the course of constitutional reforms are nowhere seen. There isnt a word on Ripons local self-governance initiative or the Morley-Minto or the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms. The chapter begins with a big question How did a land of diverse geographies, languages and religions come together to challenge and finally end nearly two centuries of British rule? This is precisely the kind of question that encourages critical thinking, but the chapter ends without touching upon any of the issues that the big question flags. Another chapter, Cultural Currents 13th to 17th Centuries, puts off a conscientious reader with its embarrassing big question How did Indian culture endure and continue to grow richer during this period despite invasions and an unstable political context? The chapter states that religious differences between the Islamic invaders and the local population were so striking that there wasnt really a meeting ground in sight for a time. The power of the Bhakti tradition, along with Sufism, allegedly helped India overcome this crisis. The chapter posits that monotheistic Islam and a religion with several schools of thought were marked by a stark difference. A few pages later, it argues that Islams idea of the oneness of god was already present in the Upanishads. One is left wondering what the stark difference was all about This chapter holds that Islamic invasions led to the imprisonment of women and their sale as slaves. As a natural consequence, women began to make their public appearances less frequent. The use of purdah, ghunghat and other forms of veiling are presented in the chapter as an attempt to protect women from the invaders. The 10th-century traveller Abu Zayds words are cited as evidence to the effect that Indian women wore no veil before the advent of Islam. It is, then, mighty uncertain what Rama was referring to in the Pratima, a play attributed to Bhasa, when he told Sita, apaniyataam avagunthanam, remove your veil. And what was Sudraka speaking of in the Mricchakatika when he said that Sarvilaka covered Vasantasena with a veil vasantasenaam avagunthya after she relinquished her life as a courtesan? These arent the only factual inaccuracies in the book. There are several more. But the challenge that such textbooks pose is not with deliberate misrepresentation of facts or contradictory information. A learned class teacher can address these inadequacies in the classroom effortlessly. The real issue lies in shifting the emphasis increasingly to lionised accounts of certain periods in history and presenting the past as a set of acts by a variety of actors engaged in religious antagonism. The interrogative character of historical studies is less frequently seen in these textbooks. Students are told of thousands of soldiers marching, but not how the soldiers were fed or from where they sourced their weapons. Students are told of high-quality steel produced in ancient India but not how the furnaces worked. Students are told of fire sacrifices by the Vedic people, but not told what it took to produce and maintain fire in an age when lighters and matchsticks did not exist. Students are given a checklist of great advances in astronomy but not told what an armillary sphere is and how it worked. Students are told that Bankim Chandra wrote the Anandamath but not told how the schools of the day equipped children to be literate enough to read Bankim. The schools that made Indians literate in the past 200 years have contributed in no small measure to the making of India as we have known it in our lifetime. This important lesson from the past should inform every line that a textbook committee decides to include in a book meant for our schoolchildren. The writer is associate professor of History at IIT Mandi, Himachal Pradesh

articleTitle: Woman goes under knife for ‘pointed’ nose, left with ‘crooked’ one, wins Rs 65,000 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: cosmetic surgery nose job delhi woman hospital refund medical negligence consumer news
description: The doctor claimed that the complainant approached him with problem of bulbous nose and wanted refinement of her tip. It was stated that she specifically wanted cosmetic rhinoplasty for a well-defined and sharper nose.
body_raw: A Delhi District Consumer Commission has directed a doctor to pay Rs 65,000 to a woman who underwent cosmetic nose surgery, observing that while aesthetic dissatisfaction and medical negligence are distinct, the cosmetic outcome cannot be ignored, as the primary objective of cosmetic surgery is to make individuals appear beautiful. A bench of president Monika Aggarwal Srivastava and members Rajender Dhar and Ritu Garodia said the procedures purpose is to improve appearance and found shortcomings in service. The primary objective of cosmetic surgery is to make individuals appear beautiful. Aesthetics is frequently the focal point of the procedure. However, dissatisfaction with the aesthetic outcome and proof of medical negligence are two distinct matters and cannot be treated as synonymous, the bench observed on September 25. At the same time, it held that the aesthetic outcome cannot be completely disregarded in a cosmetic-surgery case because the very purpose of such a procedure is to improve the patients appearance. The ruling noted that the complainant has filed photographs which indicate that the tip of the nose has been turned a little up and the nose appears to be a little crooked. It added that the complainant also underwent a revision surgery by another doctor. Woman challenged nose job outcome The matter concerned a woman who approached the consumer commission alleging deficiency in service against a doctor and the hospital over the outcome of a cosmetic rhinoplasty surgery. Rhinoplasty surgery, commonly called a nose job, is a plastic surgery procedure that changes the size, shape, or proportions of the nose. The complainant had approached the doctor with concerns relating to the shape of her nose. A CT scan showed deviation of the nasal septum towards the right, following which she was advised open rhinoplasty with functional tip plasty and septoplasty. Septoplasty is a surgical procedure to straighten a deviated nasal septum, the wall of bone and cartilage that divides your nostrils. She underwent the surgery in January 2023, after paying Rs 1.30 lakh. After the surgery, she alleged that the nose tip had been positioned upwards, that the nose remained crooked, and that she continued to face breathing problems. She also alleged that the nasal packs were not properly fixed and that she had to undergo a revision procedure. The complainant later underwent a revision rhinoplasty with septal reconstruction by another doctor, incurring an expense of Rs 4.60 lakh. She wanted sharper nose Doctor The doctor, on the other hand, maintained that the complainant had been informed about the risks, had given informed consent, and had been told that the shape of the nose could change during the healing process. It was stated that the complainant approached him with a problem of a bulbous nose tip and wanted refinement of her nose tip. It was stated that she specifically wanted cosmetic rhinoplasty for a well-defined and sharper nose. Nose appeared crooked Order The commission noted that the complainant had undergone rhinoplasty after paying Rs 1.30 lakh, and the medical records confirmed that she had a deviated nasal septum and was advised open rhinoplasty with functional tip plasty and septoplasty. It was found from the photographs that the tip of the complainants nose had turned slightly upwards and appeared somewhat crooked, forcing her to undergo a revision surgery by another doctor. Considering the shortcomings in the service, the commission directed the doctor to pay 50 per cent of the Rs 1.30 lakh paid for the surgery. Takeaway The judgment clarified that while aesthetic dissatisfaction alone does not establish medical negligence, cosmetic outcomes remain relevant. It recognises shortcomings in cosmetic surgery as deficient service and provides consumers a remedy where the intended aesthetic outcome is not achieved. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi helpline 011-23379146 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Calcutta High Court clears 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition on disputed land
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Calcutta High Court, Durga Puja 2026, Kolkata Durga Puja dispute, Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, Kolkata news, Haridevpur Police Station, Kolkata land dispute Durga Puja, Justice Saugata Bhattacharya, Calcutta HC Durga Puja order, Kolkata eviction suit land dispute
description: The Calcutta High Court has allowed a registered society to hold its 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition at a disputed Kolkata property, without deciding ownership rights.
body_raw: A 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition at a disputed Kolkata property recently got clearance from the Calcutta High Court, which directed the police to allow the Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, a registered society, to hold this years celebration despite the ongoing eviction issue. The court, however, said in the October 1 order that it would not decide the ownership rights, leaving that issue to the civil court. Justice Saugata Bhattacharya said that the earlier high court order stopping a Durga Puja in a residential building, relied upon by the respondent, was not applicable as they lacked permission from the flat owners. The judge also noted that the respondent Trust had not demonstrated any right, title ot interest over the disputed land. There might be rivalry between petitioner registered society and respondent no.5 Trust in convening Durga Puja, but there is no denial of the fact that petitioner has been convening Durga Puja for the last fifty-six years at the said premises, the order said. It added that the court was not an appropriate forum to decide the right, title and interest of a party over the land in question, and without making any observation in this regard, it directed the police to grant permission for holding Durga Puja this year. Durga Puja vs disputed land Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, a registered society, and its secretary approached the Calcutta High Court seeking permission to hold Durga Puja in 2026 on the land where it has been organising the puja for more than 50 years. The land was involved in a pending eviction suit filed by a trust against the society. Senior Advocate Indranil Roy, appearing for the society, submitted that the power of attorney holder of the co-owners had permitted, on September 10, to hold the puja. She submitted that other necessary permissions have been accorded on the designated portal by Calcutta Electric Supply Corporation, Fire and Emergency Services and Pollution Control Board, but the police authority had not granted permission. The counsel sought directions to the police authority to accord permission to enable the Parishad to convene Durga Puja on the land in 2026. Senior Advocate Kaushik Gupta, on behalf of the Trust, submitted that it had the right over the land in question and that, devoid of their permission, Parishad was not authorised to convene Durga Puja on the said land. Noting that the Parishad had been convening the Durga Puja for 56 years, the court directed the deputy commissioner of police, South West Division, Kolkata and the officer-in-charge, Haridevpur Police Station, to grant permission to the society for holding Durga Puja for the present year by October 5.

articleTitle: Hardeep Puri among two Union Ministers dropped from BJP’s UP list for Rajya Sabha polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma (left).
description: Union MoS B L Verma also dropped as BJP balances caste and regional equations in its list of eight candidates for October 16 UP Rajya Sabha polls
body_raw: The BJP on Monday announced eight candidates for the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh, leaving out Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma, whose terms in the Upper House are set to end next month. Puri is currently the Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas. Verma is the Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and Social Justice and Empowerment. With their Rajya Sabha terms ending on November 25 and the BJP not renominating them, they can continue as the Union ministers for up to six months without being a member of either House of Parliament, as per the constitutional provisions. The omission of the two ministers names was seen as an indication that there could be a reshuffle of the Union ministry in the coming months. BJP calculations The BJPs list of Rajya Sabha candidates from UP comprises three OBC faces, two Brahmins, two Dalits and one Thakur nominee. The list increases the share of OBCs and Dalits because the eight seats falling vacant had two OBCs, two Thakurs, two Brahmins along with one Dalit and one Sikh. Among the OBC candidates this time is Dharampal Singh, the BJP MLA from Bareillys Aonla and a minister in the Yogi Adityanath-led government, where he holds the Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development portfolio. Singh is a Lodh, with his nomination seen as a replacement for Verma who also belongs to the community. The Lodh group is influential in the Bundelkhand and Rohilkhand regions of UP, which has traditionally backed the BJP. Its support for the party is also linked to former UP CM late Kalyan Singh, a Lodh leader who was one of the BJPs tallest OBC leaders. The other two OBC nominees in the BJPs list are Prakash Pal, state president of the partys OBC Morcha who hails from Kanpur district, and Shruti Gangwar of Bareilly. Shruti, an IIT graduate, is the daughter of Jharkhand Governor Santosh Gangwar. She has been politically active in the Bareilly-Baheri region. The two Brahmin nominees are Radha Kant Ojha, a lawyer from Prayagraj and younger brother of former minister Shivakant Ojha, and Gopi Krishna Pandey of Kanpur, who has worked in the partys farmer and youth wings. The BJPs Dalit candidates are former Barabanki MP Priyanka Singh Rawat, a state party vice-president, and Vidya Sagar Sonkar from Jaunpur, former MLC and state party general secretary. The eighth nominee Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan, former MLA from Agra, is a state BJP general secretary in charge of the western region. He has been involved in several key party campaigns. Upper House contest UPs 10 Rajya Sabha seats falling vacant have had eight BJP members-Hardeep Singh Puri, Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brij Lal, B L Verma, Dinesh Sharma and Seema Dwivedi. Dinesh Sharma vacated his seat last month following his appointment as the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Lieutenant Governor. The BJP has not re-nominated any of the remaining seven MPs. The principal Opposition Samajwadi Party SP has renominated veteran leader Ram Gopal Yadav, uncle of party president Akhilesh Yadav, whose current term is also ending next month. The party has fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani as its second Rajya Sabha candidate. The SP has enough strength in the UP Assembly to get its two candidates elected for the Upper House. Nathwani, 40, is the son of Parimal Nathwani, Director, Corporate Affairs for Reliance Industries Ltd RIL, who was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jharkhand as an NDA-backed Independent in the June 2026 election, securing his fourth consecutive term in the Upper House. Another Rajya Sabha seat from UP is falling vacant due to retirement of Ramji Gautam, currently the lone BSP representative in Parliament. The BJP and the SP have the numbers to smoothly win seven and two seats respectively. However, a contest is likely to take place for the remaining one seat, with the SP planning to field a third candidate. The contest would take place in the run-up to the high-stakes UP Assembly elections slated for February 2027. Currently, there are 396 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly. Each Rajya Sabha candidate, therefore, will require 37 first-preference votes to win. The SP has 101 MLAs. However, its effective strength is 100 as Chail MLA Puja Pal, who continues to figure in the House records as an SP member, has switched to the BJP and is currently its state vice-president. With the support of two Congress MLAs, the SP has 102 votes, nine short of the first-preference votes required to ensure the victory of its third candidate. The BJP has 255 MLAs with its NDA allies adding another 33 members Apna Dal S 13, RLD 9, SBSP 6, and NISHAD Party 5. With the support of Puja Pal unaffiliated MLAs Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, and Abhay Singh who were expelled from the SP in June 2025 for cross-voting in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls and two MLAs of the Raja Bhaiyya-led Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, the NDAs effective tally could reach 294, two short of the required 296 37 for each first-preference votes to ensure a win for its eight candidates. The BJP is placing its bets on MLAs Rakesh Pandey, Vinod Chaturvedi and Ashutosh Maurya, who had also cross-voted in 2024 but still continue to be listed as SP members in the Assembly records as Akhilesh had not expelled them citing their good conduct. Chaturvedi told The Indian Express that he would vote in favour of a BJP candidate in the Rajya Sabha polls.

articleTitle: Flydubai attack: How Israel’s security lapses almost led to another ‘October 7’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: flydubai
description: A series of revelations show how there was sufficient opportunity for authorities in three countries to prevent Flight FZ1073 co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami from even getting anywhere near the cockpit, let alone almost causing a crash.
body_raw: As the dust has begun to settle around last weeks flydubai flight incident, the initial euphoria regarding a potential terrorist attack being averted has given way to the realisation that there were security failures on multiple fronts in three countries Israel, Oman, and the United Arab Emirates UAE. A series of revelations showed how there was sufficient opportunity for authorities to prevent the Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight FZ1073 co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami from even getting anywhere near the cockpit, let alone attacking his captain - the Indian pilot Smit Machchhar - mid-flight using an emergency axe that almost caused a crash. We explain what these revelations are and how they indicate serious lapses on part of Israels security system. How Oman Air stopped Hamam al-Hammami from flying. Hammami, 29, was born to an Omani father and Syrian mother. Although a Dubai resident, he frequently travelled to Syria during the countrys prolonged civil war, where Islamist rebels fought against the Bashar al-Assad regime. Investigators in the flydubai incident said they were looking at the possibility of radicalisation during his time in Syria. He then went on to study in Australia. He joined Oman Air in 2018 and became a pilot by 2022, although authorities raised concerns in 2024 about his radical views after he was found browsing extremist websites. He was disallowed from flying and made to undergo a deradicalisation programme, following which he was assigned an administrative job. After leaving Oman Air in 2025, Hammami tried to join the Moroccan national carrier Royal Air Maroc but wasnt hired. He eventually joined the budget carrier flydubai, owned by Dubais flagship airline Emirates, in February 2026. .but the UAE didnt Flydubai has been in the midst of an aggressive hiring spree to fuel its growth. Global demand for pilots is high and to meet its requirements, the airline set up a programme in 2025 to train pilots. It also operates its own flight training centre. As things stand, international aviation licensing works on a country-by-country basis. Citing sources, The Wall Street Journal reported that Oman mishandled the situation had Oman withdrawn Hammamis pilot licence over its concerns, the matter wouldve been flagged to the UAE and other Gulf countries. At the time of hiring, flydubai didnt contact Oman to verify his experience, although a criminal-background check was done, sources within the airline said. Hammami was then assigned to fly on the sensitive route to Tel Aviv, where he flew multiple times. The airline said it wouldnt comment on the investigation while it was ongoing. How Israels security system failed to avert flydubai incident According to a 2023 law passed in Israel, foreign airlines have to submit lists of passengers and crew to the Israeli government ahead of time. A database of these lists are maintained by the countrys Tax Authority, primarily as a measure of preventing terrorism. Although the Shin Bet - Israels internal security service - oversees the domestic carriers, it is the Ministry of Transportation that oversees pilots and crew on flights of foreign airlines to ensure they come from countries Israel considers friendly. As per the law, the Tax Authoritys database can be accessed by authorised bodies such as the Transportation Ministry as well as Israeli security agencies like Shin Bet and Mossad in order to vet people on flights. The ministry, however, said it didnt know that the database was operational - or that it could access it. Since the database was set up in 2023, the ministry has never asked for a passenger or crew list for vetting purposes, sources told WSJ. The ministry also said that while it was indeed responsible for the security of inbound flights, it lacked the intelligence capabilities to stop onboard threats. Foreign carriers were required to make those checks and in this case, it had asked flydubai - the ministry said that the airline agreed in writing to check its pilots backgrounds and nationalities. The final opportunity to stop Hammami from getting onboard FZ1073 was in Israel itself. Notably, Oman doesnt have diplomatic relations with Israel, and pilots from such countries are barred from flying to the country. So, the co-pilot couldve been stopped from boarding the flight merely on the basis of his nationality, but was instead allowed to fly multiple times to Tel Aviv instead. Meanwhile, a classified May 2024 report by Israels comptroller general had flagged the countrys Transportation Ministry for failing to adequately secure foreign carriers flights, WSJ reported. It found that officials in the ministry were failing in their oversight in part due to manpower and budget issues. Although Israeli airlines flying between Dubai and Tel Aviv were subjected to scrutiny and even stopped from flying considering the risks posed by the ongoing war in West Asia, flydubai continued to ply on the same route. October 7 anniversary, elections round the corner What is significant is that the attack happened barely a week ahead of the three-year anniversary of the armed attacks on October 7, 2023, which were carried out by the militant group Hamas and other Palestinian groups. This also comes about a month ahead of Israels parliamentary election, scheduled for October 27. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus office has instructed the head of the National Security Council, Shmuel Ben Ezra, to appoint an examiner to conduct a thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel, a statement from the prime ministers office said. Opposition leader Yair Lapid dismissed Netanyahus announcement, pointing that the chain of failures leading up to the incident couldve led to a disaster of historic proportions. In a reference to the October 7 attacks, he added Just as Netanyahu escaped an investigation into the Oct. 7 massacre, he is now running away again. Even as calls for a serious investigation into the security lapses have been growing in Israel, Transport Minister Miri Regev rejected responsibility for the failure and said that security oversight for flights operated by foreign carriers fell under the remit of security agencies such as Mossad and Shin Bet. Keren Terner, a former director-general of the transport ministry who is now an opposition candidate in the upcoming Israeli parliamentary elections, blamed Regev for the security failure, noting that the Civil Aviation Authority was under the direct subordination of her ministry. Gadi Eisenkot, a leading challenger to Netanyahu in the upcoming election, wrote on X that in a proper and functioning government, the minister of transportation would have submitted a letter of resignation.

articleTitle: Ireland Head coach on spitting incident during game against Israel: ‘…not going to comment’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ireland
description: Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had already left the sideline and did not see what happened
body_raw: Israel faced Ireland in the UEFA Nations League, and tempers ran high between the two sides yet again. This is the second time both teams have faced each other in a fortnight. The Irish media reported that one of the Israeli players spat on the Ireland coach, Damien Doyle, during the half-time whistle. Asked about the spitting incident at the post-match news conference, Icelandic football manager Heimir Hallgrimsson declined to provide details. I was there. Im not going to comment. Its something a disciplinary committee will look at, he told reporters. Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had already left the sideline and did not see what happened. Halftime, I was in the dressing room, in my room with my staff I didnt see anything. When Im going to see and check, I will get back to you with the answer, he told reporters. Ireland had faced calls from some supporters and politicians to boycott the fixtures before beating Israel 3-0 behind closed doors in Hungary in their first meeting a week ago. Im absolutely delighted this is finished, Irelands Hallgrimsson told reporters. Its taken a toll out of us all. Ive given so much credit to the players. They have been absolutely amazing in tough times, and I wish no national team to go through what we have gone through for the last two weeks. Ireland is one of Europes most outspoken critics of Israels genocidal war on Gaza, and the Football Association of Ireland chose to stage Sundays match behind closed doors in Serbia amid the pressure to withdraw from the fixtures. The absence of supporters, however, did little to ease the tension on the pitch. As in the first meeting, there were no pre-match handshakes or exchange of pennants, while players from each team bowed their heads during the opposing national anthem. Ireland again wore black armbands commemorating all the victims of the conflict in Gaza, with the Israelis sporting black armbands in memory of the victims of the October 7 attack that sparked the war. articleTitle: Haryana, Chhattisgarh CMs seek business investment from Singapore
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Haryana and Chhattisgarh chief ministers seek Singapore business investment (Image: @NayabSainiBJP/X)
description: This is the first time two Indian chief ministers have jointly addressed Singapore investors, citing each state's role in the robustly growing Indian economy, which, at last count, registered 7.8 per cent GDP growth.
body_raw: The chief ministers of Haryana and Chhattisgarh held a series of back-to-back meetings with Singapore investors on Monday, highlighting investment opportunities in mineral resources and their states planned shift from an agri-economy to technology-driven industries. Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai and Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini arrived in the city-state on Sunday. On Monday, both chief ministers and their high-level delegations addressed the Singapore-India Network for Growth Forum 2026, attended by around 300 Singapore-based investors with a focus on Indian industrialisation programmes. The forum was organised by the Singapore Business Federation. Speaking to PTI after addressing the forum, Saini said his administration is focused on semiconductors, electronics, AI, data centres, medical devices, automobiles, electric vehicles, agri-business and global capability centres. We have issued specific incentives and policies for these industries for which 100 MoUs have been signed, said Saini. He highlighted the success of Singapore companies in Haryana and NCR and said, Singapore brings global expertise Haryana offers the scale of Indias growth. Singapore has shown the world how, despite limited resources, it is possible to build world-class infrastructure, efficient cities, robust logistics and thriving business ecosystems. He invited Singapore investors to participate in the development of Haryana, including in logistics and urban infrastructure. Chhattisgarh chief minister Sai invited investors to become long-term partners and highlighted the potential in the states large mineral resource reserves. This is the first time two Indian chief ministers have jointly addressed Singapore investors, citing each states role in the robustly growing Indian economy, which, at last count, registered 7.8 per cent GDP growth. We have rich mineral resources. Minerals such as iron ore, coal, limestone, and bauxite are available in large quantities. This creates a strong foundation for mineral-based as well as downstream industries, Sai said. He also highlighted strong trade relations between Chhattisgarh and Singapore, including the export of rice, spices, pharmaceuticals, speciality industrial materials, engineering products, electronic components and steel-related products. We now wish to take this relationship beyond trade and transform it into a long-term partnership. On Tuesday, the two chief ministers and their delegations will visit Singapore industrial sites, including the technical education centre, and are scheduled to separately hold round-tables with CEOs.

articleTitle: The Cornell case made me ask my sons — what would you have done?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Cornell fraternity case, Cornell sexual assault case, Cornell Chi Phi fraternity, Cornell 2024 allegations,
description: As a mother of two boys studying at American universities, I have talked to them about consent, sex, drugs and equality. But I had never asked them what they would do if another man crossed the line
body_raw: By Nalini Sorensen As details surfaced about the reopening of the alleged 2024 gang-rape case at Cornell University, I felt physically ill. I read every horrific detail, and then my thoughts turned to my sons. I have two sons, aged 18 and 21, both studying at universities in America, including an Ivy League one. That made this feel very real for me. I share a close relationship with both of them, and over the years, we have spoken openly and honestly about pretty much everything - relationships, sex, consent, equality, LGBTQ issues, alcohol, drugs, cigarettes and vaping, but I had never asked them what they would do if another man crossed the line. I wondered if Id done enough. What is enough in this world where the rules change daily? Is a mothers work ever truly done with her children? Here I was, thousands of miles away in Mumbai, my head swirling with thoughts, while both my sons were living in university dorms where frat parties happen regularly. There was something I needed to ask my sons. I called my older son first. He didnt pick up. My younger one didnt answer my call either. So, I did the next best thing. I sent each of them a text message This Cornell incident has made me feel sick to my stomach, and it has made me ponder. We have never had this kind of a talk, and so I have to ask. if you were in a text thread with 50 other young men, and they sent violent and explicit messages about a passed-out young woman, what would you do? Because, to me, its not just about those seven boys. Its also very much about the 50 others who were on that chat. Thats what I was calling about. Both my sons called me back. The conversations went very differently, but on reflection, very similarly. I told each of them that it was the silence of those other boys that bothered me. Only a thin line separates silence from complicity. I asked questions When is it okay to keep quiet? When must you call for help? When do you take yourself out of a setting? What kind of situations demand what kind of action? Is consent from someone drunk or high valid? It was interesting to hear their responses and see the difference in their personalities coming through. My younger son was outraged. He could not believe I thought he would keep quiet. It upset him that I had to even ask him what hed do that I didnt just know. Young, brash, fiery, principled. My older son was fuming over what he had read about the case. He wanted consequences that fit the allegations. He hated that Jane Doe had to go through this, that she had had to keep living with it. He wanted justice for her. And yes, he sure as hell wouldnt look the other way. Compassionate, just, action-driven. Both touched on the fact that the other boys on the chat might not have thought this was really happening. That they might have regarded it as someone typing nonsense while high or drunk, or both. It gave all three of us some pause. That led us to discuss which messages we should question, particularly when someones safety is at stake. Who should we believe? Who should we give the benefit of doubt to? They werent easy conversations to have, but I definitely slept better that night. The truth is, as parents, we are never really done. Our children may grow up and leave home, but the conversations dont have to end. We keep asking the difficult, uncomfortable questions. We keep reminding our sons that masculinity doesnt require hardness. We keep teaching them not just how to avoid doing the wrong thing, but how to recognise when something is wrong, and find the courage to do something about it. We keep hoping that we have raised boys who will know when to speak up, when to step in, when to ask for help, and when to understand that silence is a choice too. We owe that to our sons. And we owe it to every girl in the world. Sorensen is a Mumbai-based childrens author

articleTitle: Delhi waste dumped in Gurugram: 10 arrested, interstate syndicate under scanner
articleFeaturedImageAlt: waste pickup
description: The action comes as the city grapples with 1,200 tonnes of municipal waste a day and millions of tonnes of legacy waste. Police said so far, no link with any Delhi civic body has been found.
body_raw: A waste trail from Delhi to Gurugram has led to 10 arrests and the seizure of seven vehicles, with police alleging that an interstate network was bringing in municipal and plastic waste to dump, segregate and sell in the state. As of now, we have found that the dumping work was operating like a syndicate, where they would also segregate useful items theyd find and sell those, a senior police officer said. Senior officers said the enforcement drive on Sunday evening was launched following a Friday review meeting chaired by Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, who directed authorities to ensure the city is not turned into a dumping ground and ordered strict action against vehicles bringing in garbage from outside. Following the directives, police initiated suo motu action rather than waiting for formal complaints, officials said. Four FIRs have been registered across three border-adjacent police stations two at Bajghera, and one each at Udyog Vihar and Rajendra Park. This is the first of its kind police operation earlier we would only get complaints of it happening on a small scale, said an officer. Inside the op Gurugram Police spokesperson, Assistant Sub-Inspector ASI Sandeep Kumar, said the drive was carried out under the directions of the Commissioner of Police and the supervision of the Deputy Commissioner of Police West. Police teams conducted checking and naka-bandi at several locations. Vehicles bringing garbage and plastic waste from Delhi were intercepted, leading to the arrest of 10 accused and the recovery of seven vehicles, including canters and tractor-trolleys, Kumar said. Questioning revealed that the waste was being transported into Gurugram through a coordinated network linked to Delhi, ASI Kumar. Once brought across the border, the plastic waste was separated from the general refuse and segregated before being dispatched to buyers elsewhere, he added. ASI Kumar said that investigators are scrutinising ownership records of the seized fleet. Police teams are gathering information regarding the arrested accused and vehicle owners. If the involvement or role of any vehicle owner is established during the probe, strict legal action will be taken against them as per law. Strict action for environmental protection will continue, he said. A senior police officer said notices have been sent to truck owners to join the investigation. We will check if the vehicles belong or are under any government or private body from Delhi, he said. So far, no prima facie link with any Delhi civic body has been found, officers said. Police said further investigation is underway to track the waste supply chain back to its collection points in the national capital and identify all intermediaries involved in the transport and recycling network. Gurugrams waste problem The operation assumes importance given the scale of the citys garbage problem. Millennium City generates roughly 1,200 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily, as per civic body data, while struggling to fully clear millions of tonnes of legacy trash at the oversaturated Bandhwari landfill. The landfill site is under persistent National Green Tribunal NGT scrutiny over alleged groundwater contamination, toxic leachate, and frequent fires. Garbage is currently not segregated at the time of collection from most residents. The citys garbage collection and processing has been addressed only through stopgap arrangements and short-term tenders for over two years, when the work order of the previous contractor was scrapped due to poor performance.

articleTitle: ‘Completely false’: Makers deny ticket price hike in AP for Vijay-Rashmika’s Ranabaali
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna in Ranabaali
description: Production house Mythri Movie Makers has issued an official statement on X denying reports that it has applied for ticket price hike in Andhra Pradesh for Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna's Ranabaali.
body_raw: Production house Mythri Movie Makers has denied reports that it has applied for a ticket price hike in Andhra Pradesh for Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandannas upcoming period action drama Ranabaali, calling the reports completely false in an official statement posted on X on Sunday. There have been reports that we have applied for ticket price hikes in Andhra Pradesh for Ranabaali. We would like to clarify that these reports are completely false. We have not applied for any ticket price hikes in either of the Telugu states, the statement read. The statement confirmed that Ranabaali will release at standard ticket prices when it arrives in theatres on October 16 during the Dussehra festival window. Ranabaali will release at standard ticket prices, and we are confident that audiences will have a great cinematic experience this festive season, the statement added. Also Read Ranabaali director on how Vijay Devarakonda and Rashmika Mandannas marriage helps his film The clarification comes at a sensitive time for ticket pricing in the Telugu states. Andhra Pradesh has maintained strict controls on theatrical ticket prices, with any increase requiring government approval. The issue has been one of the most contentious subjects in the Telugu film industry over the past two years, with producers and exhibitors arguing that fixed pricing caps limit their ability to recover rising production costs. Telangana operates under a similar but slightly different pricing framework, with the state government retaining authority over ticket price approvals. About Ranabaali Ranabaali is directed by Rahul Sankrityan and stars Vijay Deverakonda as Singanamala Bobbili Ranabaali, a Rayalaseema warrior who rises against British colonial forces during the Madras Famine of 1876-78. The film also stars Rashmika Mandanna as Jayamma and South African actor Arnold Vosloo as the British antagonist Sir Theodore Hector. The film is produced by Naveen Yerneni and Y. Ravi Shankar under Mythri Movie Makers banner and presented by T-Series. It releases worldwide on October 16, where it will compete with Rajinikanths Jailer 2, which releases a day earlier on October 15, for screens across the Telugu and Tamil markets.

articleTitle: Ola, Uber, bike taxis in Maharashtra get 9 months to switch to 100% EV fleets
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ola uber 100 percent EV fleets maharashtra
description: The 100 percent EV fleets directive comes amid concerns raised by bike taxi associations and riders over the mandatory transition to electric vehicles.
body_raw: The Maharashtra government has set July 2027 as the deadline for bike taxi aggregators, including Ola, Uber, Rapido and other bike taxis to transition to a 100 per cent electric fleet. In October, the State Transport Department wrote to ride-hailing aggregators and Regional Transport Offices RTOs across Maharashtra, granting a nine-month phased transition period to operators to switch to 100 percent EV fleets, following directions from Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. Under the 100 percent EV transition plan, aggregators currently operating petrol-powered bike taxis will be given six months in the first phase to comply with the EV mandate. Operators that have applied for provisional or temporary licences under the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Rules, 2025, will receive an additional three months to meet the requirement. The directive comes amid concerns raised by bike taxi associations and riders over the mandatory transition to electric vehicles. What did the bike taxi aggregators seek? In September, the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Welfare Association had written to CM Fadnavis and other officials, including the State Transport Minister and Transport Commissioner, requesting one-and-a-half years to fully switch to EVs given several considerations. Most bike taxi riders hail from middle or lower-middle-class backgrounds, making it difficult for them to undertake a significant investment to purchase an EV bike at once. The lack of EV charging infrastructure and the smaller life of an electric vehicle also makes this decision more difficult, Amit Gawde, President of the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Welfare Association, said. Aggregators had also sought an extension until 2030, citing the Maharashtra Electric Vehicle Policy and the need for more time to transition their fleets, according to a state government official. The government has, however, granted them only nine months to switch to 100 percent EV fleets. Aggregators had also sought an extension until 2030, citing the Maharashtra Electric Vehicle Policy and the need for more time to transition their fleets, according to a state government official. The government, however, has granted only a nine-month transition period. The move comes as the state has stepped up enforcement against unauthorised and non-compliant bike taxi operations. State Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik had earlier told The Indian Express that the government had initially considered allowing a 5050 mix of petrol and electric motorcycles. However, the Cabinet rejected the proposal amid concerns that companies could choose not to procure electric vehicles despite having the capacity to do so, as they are more expensive.

articleTitle: Minimum 10% water cut in Maharashtra from October 16 amid drought, El Nino concerns
articleFeaturedImageAlt: maharashtra drought water cut
description: Amid drought-like conditions, the Maharashtra government has ordered a minimum of 10 percent water cut.
body_raw: The Maharashtra government has directed all municipal corporations, municipalities, and gram panchayats to impose a minimum 10 percent water cut from October 16, citing water storage, drought-like conditions, and the possibility of El Nino-related water stress extending into next year. Local bodies have also been asked to undertake special drives to identify and stop water leakage. Besides, sewage treatment plants have to be operated at full capacity. The government has local bodies to ensure that instead of fresh water, treated wastewater should be used for gardening, construction and washing. Water Resources Minister Girish Mahajan said the department had prepared a reservoir-wise and use-wise water management plan up to August 31, 2027, with drinking water given the highest priority. The government has asked all agencies to use water carefully and take measures to conserve available supplies. Under the plan, water needed for drinking purposes will first be reserved in dams and reservoirs up to August 31 next year. The department said it would take into account evaporation, siltation and unauthorised water extraction while calculating the available supply. A 10 percent emergency buffer stock will be maintained in every reservoir to deal with uncertain rainfall and water situation. In an extreme situation, water from the dead storage of a reservoir may also be used after a technical assessment, the government said. Irrigation only after drinking water, livestock needs The department has also laid down a priority order for agricultural use. Water will be released for agriculture only after meeting the drinking water, livestock and fodder requirements. For irrigation, the priority will be rabi foodgrain and fodder crops, followed by other rabi crops. Water will be made available to perennial crops only if supplies remain after meeting these requirements. The government has also said it will encourage water-saving irrigation methods. Industries must reuse 30 of water For the industrial sector, the government has made reuse or recycling of at least 30 per cent of the consumed water mandatory. The move is part of the departments efforts to reduce freshwater demand as reservoir levels remain limited, according to the government. Illegal extraction under scanner As two-thirds of Maharashtra is reeling under drought-like conditions, the government will form joint squads to patrol dams, rivers and canals and prevent unauthorised water extraction. The squads will take action against those drawing water illegally. The water availability will be reviewed regularly through guardian ministers and canal advisory committees, Girish Mahajan said. Every department and citizen must use every drop of water carefully to avoid a water crisis in the coming year, Mahajan said. The government also referred to 265 talukas where drought had been declared, saying that the possibility of El Nino conditions continuing into the following year had prompted the detailed planning.

articleTitle: Suvendu Adhikari signs UDAN airport pact, blames delay on TMC ‘attitude’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UDAN scheme West Bengal Suvendu Adhikari
description: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari said land had become the main obstacle for aviation infrastructure development under Trinamool Congress rule.
body_raw: The West Bengal government has finally joined the Union civil aviation ministrys UDAN scheme by signing a memorandum of understanding to set up four new airports in the state-at Chharra in Purulia, Balurghat, Hasimara, and Kalaikunda. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, Union Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu, and senior officials from both the state and the Centre attended the event at Nabanna where the agreement under the Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik UDAN scheme was signed on Monday. At a press conference held afterwards, Adhikari sharply criticised the previous Trinamool Congress government, accusing it of delaying the states airport and infrastructure development. Even though the central government asked for land, the previous government did not provide it. The signing of the agreement was stalled for so long because of this negative attitude. The previous government had refused to provide land for a second airport in Kolkata. Not only the airport, but due to the failure to provide land, several important national highway and railway projects remained stuck for years, the chief minister said. Adhikari further said, Land had become the main obstacle in the path of development. Once the new airports are built, trade and economic activity in the state will surge. As per the MoU, the state government will provide required land and basic infrastructure, while the Centre and the Airports Authority of India will oversee the airport development. The chief minister said the government planned to set up a modern pilot training centre at Behala in southwestern Kolkata. The four new airports are expected not only to reduce pressure on Kolkata airport but also to create direct air connectivity between the states districts and other parts of the country.

articleTitle: NCERT launches 40-week online science teaching diploma; register from October 12
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ncert course
description: Registration for the fresh batch will begin on October 12, 2026, and candidates can enrol until November 12, 2026 through the NCERTX learning platform at ncertx.in.
body_raw: NCERT has announced a 40-week online Diploma Course in Teaching of Science at Middle Stage Classes 6-8 for the 2026-27 session. The programme is aimed at in-service and pre-service teachers and others involved in science education, with a focus on improving subject knowledge as well as pedagogical skills needed to teach Science at the middle stage. Registration for the new batch will begin on October 12, 2026, and candidates can enrol until November 12, 2026 through the NCERTX learning platform at ncertx.in. The course is designed as a MOOC for Science teachers dealing with Classes 6 to 8. It uses multimedia-based interactive learning material and is structured to take learners from basic concepts to greater conceptual depth. NCERT says the material can also support classroom teaching, including lesson planning and explaining concepts to students. Also Read Ram Rajya, NEP, Sengol What students will learn in NCERT in Governance and Public Policy chapter The programme is intended for professional development and is available online, allowing enrolled participants to access the course through their registered accounts. Who can enrol? Candidates with a Bachelor of Science BSc degree, in-service teachers teaching Science in Classes 6 to 8, candidates with a diploma or degree in education, and pre-service teachers pursuing a diploma or degree in education can apply. Other individuals directly involved in Science education can also enrol. The course is not, however, a teacher-appointment qualification. NCERT specifically states that it is an academic course and cannot be treated as equivalent to another qualification required for teacher appointment or claimed for exemption. The programme carries a one-time enrolment fee of Rs 2,000, with no other fee specified. Payment has to be made online. After making the payment, candidates will receive an invitation email from NCERTX, generally within a week, with instructions to complete enrolment. Candidates have been advised to use the same email ID throughout the payment and enrolment process. Also Read Resisting invaders to swords of goddesses NCERT revises book on medieval history for Class 9 The course is scheduled to begin on November 16, 2026, and tentatively conclude on August 31, 2027. It will have 40 modules, with a new module opening every Monday and each module expected to require around six to eight hours. What after the course Assessment and certification Each of the 40 modules will have an objective end-of-module test. The tests will remain open for 15 days, allowing learners to complete them at their convenience. Participants who complete all modules and appear for all 40 tests will be eligible for the final examination, which will be a timed test with its date announced separately. Also Read No topics dropped from class 9 math syllabus NCERT On successful completion, NCERT will award an e-certificate for Teaching of Science at Middle Stage. The course can be accessed online throughout the course period using a laptop or desktop with an internet connection.

articleTitle: Do we really need affidavits?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: affidavit
description: If identity can be authenticated, false statements can be punished and facts can be verified, what does the act of swearing actually add?
body_raw: By Preeti Kumari The Act XIV of 1848 empowered the Supreme Court at Fort William to commission persons to take affidavits and solemn affirmations. An affidavit so taken was deemed to have been taken in Court. The purpose was practical It let a sworn statement be treated as made in court without the maker appearing in person. Nearly two centuries later, we must ask whether a device intended to save a journey has itself become the reason for another journey? Affidavits are routinely used for caste, income declaration, residence, and eligibility for benefits, etc. But this does not answer a fundamental question Why must the statement be sworn at all? Suppose an applicant states in an affidavit that her annual family income is below Rs 2 lakh. The notary neither verifies ITRs, employment records or bank accounts nor bears responsibility if the statement later proves false. The affidavit establishes the makers belief in its truth under oath, not the truth of the assertion. The government may still require documentary evidence or administrative enquiry before deciding the claim. We are dealing with four separate questions Who made the statement? Can the authority or court legally receive it? What happens if the maker deliberately lies? Is the underlying fact true? If identity, admissibility and consequences for deliberate falsehood can all be provided by law, why must I go before another person and swear that I am telling the truth? During my time in public administration, I have seen the huge cost that the procedural requirement of affidavit imposes on citizens, particularly in smaller towns and remote areas. The line Affidavit to be enclosed creates an entire journey. She finds the format, gets it drafted, procures stamp paper, locates a notary or magistrate, pays, and returns to the government office or court carrying substantially the same statement she could have made directly. A few thousand rupees fee, and a days lost work mean something very different to a poor person seeking a caste certificate or welfare benefit than they do to the system imposing the requirement. But the argument cannot stop at the government counter. There is another citizen whom affidavit reform often forgets The person caught in a legal proceeding - a witness, an accident victim, a maintenance claimant, a spouse in a matrimonial dispute or a person defending her home in a property case too is a citizen. Some inconvenience is unavoidable in administering justice but inconvenience should serve a clear purpose. If the statement needs to be challenged, challenge it. If the maker needs to be cross-examined, summon her. If records contradict her, examine the records. If the underlying fact needs verification, verify it. If she deliberately lies, punish her. Which of those protections disappear merely because she did not submit a sworn affidavit? To dispense with affidavit is not an untested idea. In the United States, 28 U.S.C. 1746, Unsworn declarations under penalty of perjury, separates truthfulness and legal liability from the necessity of swearing. Irelands Civil Law and Criminal Law Act 2020 has removed the need for making statements through sworn affidavits with electronically signed self-declarations - Statement of truth. Crucially, it has replaced, in the proceedings covered by the reform, the sworn form with a statement carrying direct legal responsibility. Affidavit reform in India has generally asked In which cases can we dispense with the affidavit and accept a self-declaration?. That is, it starts with the affidavit as the default and the declaration as an exception. Perhaps the presumption should now be reversed. The reform can begin with the principle Preserve the legal consequence, dispense with the ritual. For government services, an authenticated self-declaration carrying clear legal consequences for deliberate falsehood should suffice. The courts could recognise an electronically authenticated statement of truth, with Aadhaar-based authentication as one possible means of establishing identity, give it the evidentiary status by law, preserve the ability to challenge it and cross-examine its maker, and attach serious consequences to deliberate falsehood. In Swear Not At All 1817, Jeremy Bentham asks If these safeguards can be built into the process, and falsehood punished, what does swearing add? Perhaps it is time the affidavit itself proved its necessity. The writer is district commissioner, West Karbi Anglong, Assam

articleTitle: Jailer 2 trailer: Rajinikanth returns with a bigger cast and an even bigger battle. Watch
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajinikanth movie Jailer 2 trailer
description: Jailer 2 trailer: Jailer 2 brings back Rajinikanth as the retired jailer Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, alongside an expanded ensemble featuring SJ Suryah, Vidya Balan, Mithun Chakraborty and Suraj Venjaramoodu.
body_raw: Jailer 2 trailer Sun Pictures released trailer for Jailer 2 on Monday, October 5, offering audiences their first detailed glimpse of the sequel to the 2023 blockbuster Jailer. The trailer arrives ten days before the release, following a promotional campaign that has included four singles from Anirudh Ravichanders 12-track album, including the Nora Fatehi special number Bindaas. What the Jailer 2 trailer shows The Jailer 2 trailer picks up from where Jailer left off. Rajinikanth reprises his role as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, the retired jailer who dismantled an idol smuggling network in the first film. The sequel finds the entire racketeering network turning against him, with former allies and new enemies converging on the retired officer who thought his fight was over. While his enemies try to track him, Tiger is seen working as a driver in a remote village. The trailer establishes a darker, more expansive conflict than the first film. While Jailer was primarily a cat-and-mouse game between Tiger and Vinayakans idol smuggler, Jailer 2 appears to involve multiple antagonists and a broader criminal conspiracy. SJ Suryah features prominently in the trailer in what appears to be a pivotal antagonist role, bringing his trademark unpredictability to a character whose motives are deliberately kept under wraps. Vidya Balan makes her Tamil cinema debut in a role whose details have been kept under wraps. The trailer also shows glimpses of Jackie Shroff, Mohanlal and Shiva Rajkumar. Vijay Sethupathi, who had earlier confirmed his involvement in the film, is not seen in the trailer. The trailer showcases action sequences that appear to be significantly larger in scale than the first film. Nelson Dilipkumar, who established a distinctive visual style in Jailer that blended dark comedy with bursts of violence, appears to have amplified both elements for the sequel.
