articleTitle: Family member held for murder of two elderly women in Baramati, robbing gold jewellery
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police detained Vikas Ladkat after finding his movements suspicious.
description: Pune rural police Superintendent Sandeep Singh Gill formed eight teams to crack the murders.
body_raw: Pune rural police have arrested a family member in connection with the murder of two elderly women at their house in Baramati. Police identified the accused as Vikas alias Appa Rajendra Ladkat 25, a resident of Sherechiwadi village in Baramati taluka of Pune district. Indumati Maruti Ladkat 75 and Krushnabai Kundalik Ladkat 60 were found dead, with their throats slit, in an open space near their house in Sherechiwadi on September 29. About 50 grams of gold ornaments on their bodies were missing. Indumatis son Ganesh Ladkat 45 lodged the FIR at the Supa police station in Pune rural. Initial probe revealed that the two elderly women were murdered while they were sleeping, robbery being the motive. Pune rural police Superintendent Sandeep Singh Gill formed eight teams to crack the murders. Police teams checked about 200 history sheeters in Ahilyanagar, Solapur, Satara, Kolhapur, Pune and Beed districts in Maharashtra and Nipani in Karnataka. Police also checked CCTV cameras installed at various locations for leads. Simultaneously, the police also kept watch on the movements of people in Sherechiwadi village, especially those residing near the deceased women. Police detained Vikas Ladkat after finding his movements suspicious. During interrogation, Vikas admitted that he murdered the two women, who were his relatives, by attacking them with an axe and then looted their gold ornaments, a press release issued on Monday stated. Police arrested Vikas under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS sections 103 1 murder, 309 4, 332 c, on October 4. Police also recovered the robbed ornaments from his possession. Assistant police inspector Shashikant Shelke of Supa police station said, A court has remanded the accused in police custody for five days. He is a distant family member of the deceased woman. Probe so far has revealed that he was debt-ridden. So he killed the elderly women when they were alone and robbed their gold jewellery. In the past he was booked in a criminal case when he was a minor. Further investigation is on.

articleTitle: In Nobel Prize for medicine, a single cell, a flash of light, a breakthrough
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A single cell, a flash of light, a breakthrough
description: In awarding the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Hegemann, American neuroscientist Karl Deisseroth and German biophysicist Georg Nagel, the Nobel Assembly has recognised what is effectively a new era in neuroscience.
body_raw: In the beginning was a single cell, instinctively moving towards light so that the business of living may continue. For German photobiologist Peter Hegemann, studying the microscopic alga known as Chlamydomonas in the 1990s, the question was straightforward How did this simple organism respond to light in one-twentieth of the time that it took the human eye to see? The simplicity of the algas biology, it turned out, was the key needed to unlock the complexities of the human brain, from how different organs are controlled to where feelings, memory, even consciousness itself, reside. In awarding the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Hegemann, American neuroscientist Karl Deisseroth and German biophysicist Georg Nagel, the Nobel Assembly has recognised what is effectively a new era in neuroscience. Hegemann, along with Nagel, discovered channelrhodopsin, a protein that enables Chlamydomonas to react to light in half a millisecond - compared to the 10 milliseconds that it takes the human eye to process information. Deisseroth then used it to develop a light switch that can control nerve cells, thus inaugurating the field of optogenetics. The pinprick of illumination that was made by Hegemanns curiosity has since expanded to shed light on neural pathways that could once only be guessed at. Researchers have been able to identify the precise circuits that control functions and behaviours, from why some people develop a greater preference for sugar to how the rhythms of the heart can affect emotions and how the brain stores information about fear, anxiety and depression. It offers hope for a greater understanding of psychiatric and neurological disorders - areas of darkness that could soon become less intimidating.

articleTitle: Campus polls return in Odisha after 8 years. Why all 3 parties are hopeful
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Campus polls return in Odisha after 8 years. Why all 3 parties are hopeful
description: The Mohan Majhi government announced the revival of student body polls in the state’s universities and colleges, signalling the return of student politics after an eight-year hiatus.
body_raw: Campuses across Odisha are bracing for a fresh bout of political activities after the state government announced the return of students union polls in degree colleges and universities after an eight-year gap on Monday. Student wings of major political parties such as the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ABVP, Biju Chhatra Janata Dal BCJD and National Students Union of India NSUI swung into action, reviving their campus networks and stepping up outreach activities. The students union polls are also being closely watched by all three major political parties, which see the event as an opportunity to connect with the Gen Z voters, understand their concerns and cultivate their support. For political parties, success in the campus polls could also be viewed as a measure of their acceptance among young voters and an indication of the extent of support they enjoy among the student community. According to a notification issued by the state higher education department on Monday, students union elections will be held in all colleges on October 15. The states higher education minister, Suryabanshi Suraj, announced the decision following a meeting with chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi. The decision to hold campus polls is a key step towards nurturing youth leadership in our state. Reviving campus polls was also one of our major promises in the election manifesto. After our party formed the government, it took us some time to review the situation on campuses. This year, the poll will be held across campuses, said the higher education minister. The decision to complete the entire process within 10 days has been taken to prevent violence on the campuses, said officials. Campus polls in Odisha were last held in 2017. The students wings of various political parties were also demanding the revival of student body polls, with the National Student Union of India - the students wing of the Congress-meeting the higher education minister to demand student body polls. Euphoria swept campuses following the announcement of the students union polls the ABVP, the student wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh RSS, launched marches across campuses to thank the state government for the decision. The decision has also triggered a political slugfest, with BJP spokesperson Anil Biswal criticising the former BJD government for not holding campus polls for a long period. He said the previous BJD government didnt want to encourage youth leadership. BCJD president Ipsita Sahoo said the campus poll was suspended during the BJD regime due to various reasons such as COVID-19 and that it had always supported student body polls.

articleTitle: ‘No land for burial’: Chhattisgarh village resolution raises concerns for Christians
articleFeaturedImageAlt: 'No land for Christian burials': In Chhattisgarh, gram sabha resolution raises concerns
description: Of 2,000 residents of this village in Sukma district, only 21 families with 75 members in total follow Christianity. Community members say some groups have been misusing the split verdict by the Supreme Court in a burial rights case earlier this year to trouble them
body_raw: At Punpalli, a village in Chhattisgarhs Sukma district, a new banner has come up prohibiting the entry of pastors for religious activities. The notice further states that the village will not allow any event being held for the purpose of conversions or any other religious activity. The development follows a list of 12 resolutions taken recently by the village panchayat. However, it is the resolution not written in the banner that has become a source of greater worry for people from the Christian community in this village of 2,000 residents. It one of the resolutions says that the village will not give any land for burials to tribals, who follow Christianity, Madkam Bhima, a Janpat member elected from Punpalli village, said. Bhima said that till now, a total of four villages have made such resolutions in Sukma, including Punpalli. It started from Errabore a few months ago followed by my village Polampalli. It will be done gradually in all villages, he said. This village has only 21 families with 75 members in total who follow Christianity. If the resolution holds, the families will have to travel over 13 kilometers to Dhornapal for burials or to Sukma headquarters, which is over 40 kilometers away. When asked if the diktat had a legal basis, Bhima said, Yes, we are adhering to the PESA law. We are not violating any law. During the October 2 meeting, the Punpalli Gram Sabha cited the Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas Act, 1996 PESA, as the village is covered under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India, as it passed the resolution. The board that was put up soon after read According to PESA, the Gram Sabha has the right to protect its cultural identity, traditions, customs and social heritage. The villagers believe that activities related to religious conversion through inducement, pressure or any other means affect our traditional tribal culture, social unity and cultural identity. Therefore, it has been decided that any event related to religious conversion by outsiders, religious preaching whose objective is to convert people to another religion will not be acceptable. However, advocate Sudeep Shrivastava, who has been raising such issues in the region, said, The entry of any Indian citizen in a village cannot be prohibited. A person can profess his religion in any village. As far as others joining his prayers is concerned, the villagers have the right to voluntarily do so. If there is a resolution that says land will not be given for any person living in the village, who professes Christianity, for burials, it is unconstitutional. Nukesh Baghel, vice president of Bastar District Rural Christian Service Committee, said, This is at least the 10th village in Bastar region which is doing this. Top courts split verdict being misused Nukesh said some groups have been misusing the split verdict by the Supreme Court in a burial rights case earlier this year. The Supreme Court, in February, had ordered an interim stay on forcible exhumation of tribal Christians. Following this, villagers are not allowing us to bury the bodies in the first place, Nukesh added. In January 2025, a two-bench judge was deciding a case wherein Ramesh Baghel, son of a deceased Christian pastor from Chhattisgarh, was seeking to bury his fathers body in his native village in Bastar district. While Justice B V Nagarathna pulled up the gram panchayat authorities for denying the man a burial in the tribal-majority village, and allowed Ramesh to do so in his private agricultural land, Justice S C Sharma was of the view that the statutory rules did not permit this and said the burial should be conducted at a common designated burial ground designated for Christians of three-four villages in Karkapal. Baghel had to carry out the burial rites in Karkapal under heavy security. The right-wing workers have made a team, which is going to villages where tribes and tribal Christians are living in peace. They provoke the tribals and get them to pass such resolutions, misusing the split verdict, said Nukesh. Soon after the SCs interim relief in February, we wrote to the Chhattisgarh DGP, requesting implementation of the top court order that forcible exhumation of bodies should not happen but it still takes place. We are documenting all these instances and will approach the court in the matter again, said advocate Degree Prasad Chouhan, convenor of Chhattisgarh Association for Justice and Equality. When contacted about the resolution, Mukund Thakur, CEO Zilla Panchayat, Sukma District, said, It was not in the agenda. If I receive a written complaint, I will take appropriate action after checking the legality of the matter as per the applicable rule.

articleTitle: Who modified what?: Supreme Court seeks ECI records on Form 6 change
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Will like to see who has modified what in records: Top court
description: The court’s observation comes after the ECI issued a statement on September 26 that the Form 6 would revert to the original version as per Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
body_raw: The Supreme Court said on Monday that it had not approved any modified version of Form 6, which is used to enroll new voters, and will examine Election Commission of India ECI records to know whether any change had been made and, if so, by who. The apex court was responding to a petition, which argued that a modified Form 6 was used for the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. The matter is being heard by a three-judge bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, and also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. The courts observation comes after the ECI issued a statement on September 26 that the Form 6 would revert to the original version as per Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used, the ECI had said in its statement. The ECI was responding to the findings of an investigation by The Indian Express published on September 23 that two Election Commissioners in the three-member ECI objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps taken by the Commission under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar - from keeping them in the dark to adding new voters and deleting names. The Indian Express had first reported in July that the online Form 6 on the ECIs ECINet portal has started asking applicants whether they, or their parents or grandparents, were on the electoral roll of the last SIR - and that the form could not be submitted without an answer. On September 23, this newspaper reported that Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi had recorded on May 16 that the form cannot be altered without making amendments in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and his colleague Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred on May 19 - the change in the portal went ahead regardless. On Monday, appearing for petitioner Shailendra Mani Tripathi, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy told the bench Let me give you an illustration.since it pertains to most recently, for instance, Delhi. Let us see how the SIR was conducted in Delhi. Form 6 has two new conditions added. Those Forms 6 were circulated. Neither the petitioner is now allowed to be on the roll. I got a notice also.based on this new Form 6, which cannot, under the schedule, be modified. The CJI said Lets be very clear. The modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let us also be clear that when the record will be produced, we will like to see who has modified what. The reference was to a related plea by Patna-resident Rakesh Kumar Singh who sought the summoning of original records of the ECI in this regard. Referring to The Indian Express investigation, Tripathis plea raised unprecedented Constitutional fractures and illegalities committed within the Election Commission of India under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as exposed by documentary records published. The plea sought probe by an independent, high-powered judicial inquiry commission or a special investigation team headed by a retired judge of the Supreme Court into the CECs actions. These illegal acts include Unilateral Illegal Alteration of Statutory Form 6. Centralisation and Usurpation of Statutory Powers Depriving decentralised Electoral Registration Officers EROs of their statutory authority under Section 13B, 22, and 23 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and centralizing electoral roll management under the Director General of IT DG-IT in Delhi, the petition said. The plea also listed disenfranchisement due to software failures unauthorised subversion in West Bengal by filing over 16.10 lakh unauthorised appeals in the name of the ECI to purge citizens restored by 700 Judicial Officers, without the knowledge, authorization, or sanction of the other two Election Commissioners or the Chief Electoral Officer CEO of West Bengal. It raised the issues of bureaucratic usurpation and subversion of oversight and subversion of multi-member decision making. The plea contended that defying this binding majority, respondent number 3 CEC Gyanesh Kumar, acting in concert with respondent number 6 DG-IT, altered Form 6 digitally on the ECINet portal in July 2026. Referencing The Indian Express investigation, the plea said that on August 13, 2026, Commissioner Sandhu formally recorded that this alteration was unauthorised and illegal and was causing arbitrary harassment to young, eligible first-time electors, ordering its immediate withdrawal. Despite this, the unauthorised form was kept live on the portal. In May, in its judgement upholding the Bihar SIR, the Supreme Court had said that the ECI had residual powers to formulate appropriate documentation work regarding Form 6 to meet the needs of a special revision of electoral rolls, provided it was not arbitrary. Such authority, however, is not unbounded, the court had said then.

articleTitle: Did not clear Form 6 change… can annul unilateral decisions: Supreme Court sends notice to Election Commission
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Did not clear Form 6 change... can annul unilateral decisions: SC sends notice to EC
description: The CJI assured that the court would examine the records and ensure that any decision taken without unanimity will have to go. “We can always annul any decision,” the CJI said.
body_raw: The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India ECI on a petition accusing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of acting in violation of the law that governs his terms of office by functioning in a unilateral manner and seeking his removal. The notice issued by a three-judge bench, presided by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, was also directed at the CEC, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg and ECI Director General Information Technology Seema Khanna. The petition, filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh, is based on the findings of an investigation by The Indian Express published on September 23 that Sandhu and Joshi had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps taken by the Commission under the CEC - from keeping them in the dark to adding new voters and deleting names. The plea urged the bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, to seek the complete original and primary records relating to the matter from the Election Commission. It also prayed that the ongoing exercise be declared illegal. The CJI assured that the court would examine the records and ensure that any decision taken without unanimity will have to go. We can always annul any decision, the CJI said. Justice Bagchi said that after examining the records, if the court finds that some decisions were taken neither by unanimity nor by majority, we will injunct those decisions.we will say these decisions are ultra vires.. The bench, however, declined to pass any interim order to suspend CEC Kumar or direct that the poll body should take decisions unanimously till it finally decided the matter. Appearing for the petitioner, Senior Advocate Vikas Singh said some interim directions are necessary. I am wanting an interim order today to suspend the CEC immediately.Today there are elections happening.or divest him of the authority to act as CEC, he said. Justice Bagchi, however, asked who will conduct the election in such a scenario. Singh responded that the two Election Commissioners can, and added that in the interim, the court should also restore the position of the ECI as it had made the CJI a member of the selection committee for CEC. We are dealing with a very grave situation today. A grave situation which can undermine the very basis of our democracy. Today, our democracy is vibrant and known all over the world because of the way we are able to conduct the elections. This election.. has been conducted for 76 years, with the ECI having a certain amount of respect, Singh said. He said that while there have been earlier occasions where one or two decisions of the ECI may be questioned, today we are having a situation where the very CEC as a constitutional body is acting in a manner which is completely contrary to the statute under which he is appointed. Pressing for interim relief, Singh said .today Your Lordships will pass some orders. Otherwise this country will burn today. The elections were conducted with the ECI having some respect. But today we are having a situation where the CEC is acting in a manner which is completely contrary to the statutory framework. Your Lordships have to take some interim measures here. Because otherwise the very credibility of the electoral process is so undermined that every citizen of this country is feeling unsafe. When the court expressed its disinclination to issue any order to suspend the CEC, Singh sought a direction that the ECI will decide things unanimously till the court hears the matter next. Referring to The Indian Express investigation, Singh pointed out that the ECI had not denied the report. There is a press release on September 26 by the Election Commission, which has not denied the newspaper report. The press release is in the vaguest of language. The CJI said The newspaper report may be 100 percent correct, it may be partially correct, it may be partially incorrect. We cannot really pass an order today on that basis. But we would definitely like to have their response. And then whatever correctional requirements are needed, will issue them. When Singh insisted that the court pass an interim order directing that the ECI act unanimously till the next date of hearing, the CJI said .going by the law, they are expected to take firstly a decision by unanimity and if there is no unanimity, by majority. Now if there is a decision which is neither unanimous nor by majority, then that is subject matter of challenge.. The CJI said, There is a mandatory law. We will accept that they follow it. And if ultimately we find there are instances it has not been followed, you know the consequences. Accusing the CEC of violating the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office Act, 2023, the petition said If the power constitutionally vested in the Election Commission as a multi-member body can, in fact or in substance, be exercised by one office within it without the participation the Constitution and the 2023 Act. then decisions that determine who is on the electoral roll, and therefore who may vote, raise a serious constitutional question as to whether such decisions are being taken by the constitutional authority the Constitution created for that purpose.

articleTitle: Plaque in tribute to Indian Express group founder Ramnath Goenka unveiled at Nariman Point in Mumbai
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Plaque in tribute to Express group founder Ramnath Goenka unveiled at Nariman Point in Mumbai
description: The plaque commemorates the memory of Ramnath Goenka who launched The Indian Express in 1932 and ensured it became a fearless, credible and fiercely independent newspaper.
body_raw: A marble plaque built in tribute to the founder of The Indian Express Group of newspapers, Ramnath Goenka, was inaugurated on Monday by Bombay High Court judge Somasekhar Sundaresan at Mumbais Nariman Point, where the newspapers office is located. The plaque commemorates the memory of Ramnath Goenka who ensured that The Indian Express, founded in 1932, became a fearless, credible and fiercely independent newspaper. The Executive Director of The Indian Express Group, Anant Goenka, was present at the event organised on the founders 35th death anniversary. Built in Makrana marble, the plaque is installed on Ramnath Goenka Marg, a street that links Maharashtra Vidhan Bhavan to the Vinay K Shah Road in Nariman Point. The road was named after The Indian Express founder after former Mumbai mayor and senior Congress leader from Mulund, Ramcharitra Rambhajan Singh, on September 13, 1993, cleared a request submitted by former corporator Vijaya Kanti Dhulla. Two years after the BMCs decision, the road was officially named as Freedom Fighter Ramnath Goenka Marg on November 25, 1995. It was inaugurated by then Vice-President K R Narayanan, with then Chief Minister Manohar Joshi and municipal commissioner JD Jadhav. The name of the lane has now been engraved upon the new plaque along with Goenkas portrait and his words that define the newspapers motto of Journalism of Courage. Remembering our founder Ramnath Goenka On his 35th death anniversary, a plaque was unveiled on the corner of Ramnath Goenka Marg, Nariman Point, Mumbai in the presence of Justice Somasekhar Sundaresan of the Bombay High Court and Anant Goenka, Executive Director, Indian Express Group. Express Photo by Sankhadeep Banerjee - The Indian Express IndianExpress October 5, 2026 The plaque of 8.5 feet width and 12.5 feet height, was constructed over four months. While the plaque was constructed in four months, the intricate engravings were executed over a period of 25 days. The plaque rests on a platform, which takes the total height of the structure to 14 feet, said urban planner Hardik Sankhe, who worked on its design. The project work was executed by the contractor, Aditya Interiors. The final nod for constructing the commemorative plaque was granted by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporations A ward office in July 2025, following which permissions from traffic police, BEST and the Mumbai Heritage Conservation Committee were obtained.

In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1iii, ECI has stated that, the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court, the ECI said on X. Congress general secretary organisation K C Venugopal said it was yet another instance where Gyanesh Kumar overruled other ECs to perpetuate illegality for the BJP. During the Modi-Shah regime, the Election Commission has truly become a cheating commission which deprives the ordinary citizen of their inalienable right of franchise. These contradictions go to the heart of our democracy. If the institutions meant to protect our vote contradict each other, who protects the voter? This is how elections are stolen, he wrote on X. Samajwadi Party MP Rajeev Rai told The Indian Express that the top court is now realising the seriousness of the issue of SIR. The people of the country are hitting the streets. The courts are realising the seriousness now, even though it is late. CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar said the SC categorically stated that it never approved the modified Form 6. CPIM MP John Brittas said I had written to the EC months ago pointing out that the modifications to Form 6 are illegal and unconstitutional. articleTitle: Trump approves firing squad execution for 2009 Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Donald Trump, firing Squad, Nidal Hasan
description: Nidal Hasan had opened fire on unarmed troops at Fort Hood, Texas, while shouting "Allahu Akbar", resulting in 13 deaths and 32 injuries
body_raw: The Pentagon announced late on Monday that President Donald Trump has approved death by firing squad for Nidal Hasan, who was convicted for his role in the fatal 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood in Texas. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell posted on X that the recommendation came directly from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who will set the timeline and venue for the execution. Recalling the event, Parnell noted that Hasan opened fire on unarmed troops while shouting Allahu Akbar, resulting in 13 deaths and 32 injuries. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come, Parnell stated. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has recommended - and President Donald J. Trump has approved - death by U.S. Army firing squad for convicted terrorist Nidal Malik Hasan, the jihadist who opened fire on unarmed American soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009. He killed 13 people and wounded 32 others while shouting Allahu Akbar during the attack. The Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come. - Sean Parnell SeanParnellASW October 5, 2026 In a follow-up post, Hegseth echoed the sentiment, writing Justice. FROM THE ARCHIVES Fort Hood Muslims voice outrage at rampage Is firing squad legal in the US? Execution by firing squad is authorised in five US states - Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Utah. Three executions by firing squad were carried out by South Carolina after the inmates chose the method in 2025. Before that, a firing squad execution was carried out in 2010 in Utah. In the United States, a firing squad execution involves strapping the condemned inmate to a specialised chair with protective restraints and placing a dark hood over their head. A medical examiner or official locates the inmates heart and pins a target often a white cloth target with a red bullseye directly over it. The execution takes place behind a wall equipped with small ports or a black curtain, says the Death Penalty Information Center in the US. A team of designated executioners - typically five trained law enforcement or correctional officers - stand roughly 20 feet away armed with identical high-powered rifles. To spare the officers from individual guilt, one of the rifles is randomly loaded with a blank or dummy cartridge so no shooter knows who fired the lethal rounds. Upon command, the shooters fire simultaneously at the chest target, causing rapid fatal internal injuries. Apart from the US, execution by firing squad remains legally authorised as a primary or secondary form of capital punishment in several nations, including Indonesia, North Korea, Taiwan, Cuba, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Yemen, Somalia, and Saudi Arabia. Some countries, like Brazil and El Salvador, authorise firing squad executions during times of military conflict. Firing squad executions in the five states require the Presidents authorisation, as in the Nidal Hasan case. From the archives OPINION What should we make of Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan,who apparently killed 13 innocent people at Fort Hood? The Nidal Hasan Case On November 5, 2009, US. Army Major Nidal Hasan, an American citizen of Jordanian descent, carried out a deadly mass shooting at the Soldier Readiness Processing Center inside the Fort Hood military post near Killeen, Texas. Hasan was a military psychiatrist there. Armed with an FN Five-seven semi-automatic handgun, Hasan opened fire on unarmed troops preparing for deployment, killing 13 people-including a pregnant soldier-and wounding 32 others while shouting Allahu Akbar. The rampage ended when civilian responders engaged him in a gunfight, shooting him multiple times and leaving him paralysed from the waist down. Prior investigations revealed Hasan had been radicalised after getting in touch with extremist Islamic figures, including radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki. Hasan was charged under the Uniform Code of Military Justice and faced a court-martial in August 2013, where he represented himself and admitted to have carried out the attack. He claimed his motive was to protect Taliban leaders abroad. A military jury convicted him on 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 counts of attempted premeditated murder, subsequently sentencing him to death. Since his conviction, Hasan has remained incarcerated on military death row at the United States Disciplinary Barracks in Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

articleTitle: Extreme heat puts pregnant women, newborns at greater risk: Survey
articleFeaturedImageAlt: heat, pregnant women
description: Global survey includes 200 Indian maternal healthcare professionals; separate India research examines heat exposure and pregnancy outcomes
body_raw: Extreme heat is increasingly affecting pregnant women and newborns, with maternal healthcare professionals reporting a rise in heat-related complications and growing concerns over health-system preparedness, according to a new international survey commissioned by Wellcome, a global charitable foundation that funds health and scientific research. The survey of 1,000 healthcare professionals across India, Australia, Brazil, the UK and Zimbabwe found that 73 per cent reported an increase in heat-related cases or complications affecting pregnant women over the past five years, while 76 per cent reported an increase affecting foetal or newborn health. Nearly all respondents said they had personally cared for a pregnant woman 98 per cent or baby 99 per cent whose health they believed had been affected by extreme heat. India accounted for 200 respondents in the survey, which included obstetricians, gynaecologists, doctors, midwives, nurses and other frontline healthcare workers involved in pregnancy, childbirth, postnatal or newborn care. The survey was conducted online between September 17 and October 1. Separate India-specific research has highlighted the potential consequences of heat exposure during pregnancy. In a July 2026 overview of heat and maternal health, researchers in India had found that working in high heat can double the risk of miscarriage and stillbirth. A separate research is examining the effects of extreme heat on maternal, placental, foetal and newborn health across different climatic regions of India. The study is examining heat exposure during pregnancy and its potential impact on outcomes for mothers and babies, including through research involving 600 pregnant women across three climate zones. Pregnant and postpartum women face particular risks from extreme heat. The study has linked heat exposure with preterm birth, low birth weight, stillbirth and maternal complications. For every 1C rise in heat exposure, the odds of preterm birth increase by around 5 per cent, while exposure to heatwaves has been associated with a 25 per cent higher risk of obstetric complications. Among healthcare professionals surveyed, 23 per cent said they had seen pregnancy complications requiring additional monitoring or treatment that they believed were linked to extreme heat. They also reported low birth weight or restricted growth 34 per cent, dehydration and heat-related illness in newborns 36 per cent, and difficulties with feeding, breathing and temperature regulation 33 per cent. Heat is also affecting access to healthcare. Twenty-seven per cent of respondents said extreme heat was making it harder for pregnant women and families to travel to or access care, while 29 per cent reported an increase in urgent or emergency presentations. Midwives and doctors from countries across five continents are telling us that extreme heat is affecting the health of pregnant women and newborn babies, said Julia Gillard, Chair of Wellcome and former Prime Minister of Australia. As the planet continues to heat-up because of anthropogenic climate change more mothers and babies will be put at risk. More than four in five respondents 81 per cent were concerned that extreme heat would pose a growing risk to maternal, foetal and newborn health over the next five years unless further action is taken. Another 82 per cent said policymakers and health-system leaders should give greater priority to protecting pregnant women and babies from extreme heat. The survey also highlighted a preparedness gap among health workers. Ninety-two per cent of respondents said they wanted more training and resources to protect pregnant women during extreme heat, while 55 per cent said clearer national or international guidance would help them provide better care. Extreme heat, fuelled by climate change is impacting our way of life and our health - and yet many countries are not prepared, said Dr Madeleine Thomson, Head of Climate Impacts and Adaptation at Wellcome. She said measures such as early warning systems and cooler buildings could help protect vulnerable groups, including pregnant women and newborns. The researchers called for pregnant women, new mothers and babies to be specifically included in national climate and health plans, along with clinical guidance on heat during pregnancy and the postpartum period. They have also called for stronger surveillance systems to track the impact of heat exposure on maternal and newborn health. The survey has been released ahead of COP31, as climate and health researchers push for maternal and newborn health to be given greater prominence in climate adaptation and health planning.

articleTitle: 5 injured in accident on Pune-Mumbai Expressway’s Missing Link; traffic diverted briefly
articleFeaturedImageAlt: pune mumbai accident
description: According to the State Highway Police, the injured have been provided with necessary medical assistance.
body_raw: At least five people were injured after a private bus collided with a container on the Pune-Mumbai Expressways Missing Link Connecting Link on Tuesday morning. The injured have been provided with necessary medical assistance, State Highway Police said. The incident led to the closure of the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway, with traffic being briefly diverted through the Ghat section of the expressway. Traffic movement towards Mumbai remained closed on the carriageway for four to five hours before being restored by afternoon as the damaged vehicles were removed from the spot. The State Highway Police confirmed that the situation was under control. The accident also brought into focus the restrictions on and violations by the vehicles on the Connecting Link. Containers are not permitted on the Missing Link, while buses are allowed to use the corridor. The container involved in the accident was therefore in violation of the restrictions applicable to the route. The Highway Police said official, detailed information about the circumstances of the accident will be shared after an initial probe. Motorists travelling from Pune towards Mumbai have been advised to follow the directions of the traffic police and use the Ghat section until the affected carriageway is cleared and reopened.

articleTitle: Lucknow flooded, 40,000 homes hit: Trouble began hundreds of kilometres upstream
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Residents at flood-hit areas of Lucknow.
description: The rising level of the Gomti river is being attributed to a chain of weather events in UP
body_raw: For the past few days, Lucknow has received no significant rainfall. Yet large parts of the state Capital are flooded in the month of October. Faizullaganj, on the citys northern fringes, is worst hit, and the situation has been deteriorating with each passing day. At least 40,000 homes are estimated to be affected. The reasons for the flood-like situation, affecting areas from Bakshi Ka Talab and Lucknow North through Faizullaganj towards Naimish, are the result of a chain of events. Officials said the water inundating low-lying areas is largely the result of heavy rainfall in the upper catchment of the Gomti in the last week of September, with the river now carrying the water downstream to Lucknow. The Gomti rivers catchment areas are spread over Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur, Lakhimpur Kheri and Sitapur districts that witnessed exceptionally heavy rainfall between September 22 and 27. Normally, the rainfall over five days would be around 15 mm. This time it was around 150 mm, with some places receiving nearly 257 mm, Principal Secretary Irrigation Anil Garg said, describing the spell as extreme rainfall. The Gomti originates near Madhotanda in Pilibhit and flows through the upstream districts before reaching Lucknow. The extreme rainfall in the last week of September also flooded smaller rivulets and streams feeding the Gomti, resulting in a large volume of water entering the Gomti system. How did this happen? The water in a river system does not move instantaneously, Garg explained. Under normal conditions, it takes about 10-12 days for water to travel from the Pilibhit region to Lucknow, he added. This time, however, several days of exceptionally heavy rainfall meant that large volumes accumulated across the catchment and in the smaller streams before moving downstream. So, even after the skies over Lucknow cleared, the city continued to receive water generated much earlier and much farther upstream, the official said. The high flow also takes time to move through the river. Since it takes 10-12 days for water from upstream to reach Lucknow, experts expect the water level to start receding after two days, as the peak inflow moves downstream. With the upstream areas of the Gomti receiving 25 per cent of the annual rainfall in just three days time till September 27, and with water travelling at the speed of 1 km per hour, it took several days for the water to reach Lucknow, which is about 240 km from the point of origin, said District Magistrate Vishak G. Garg said the water generated after the September 22-27 spell continued moving downstream for several days, eventually heading towards areas such as Sultanpur. Lucknows own share of record rainfall Lucknow itself received around 150 mm of rainfall during the September-end brief spell, adding to the water flowing through the Gomti. The combined effect of local rainfall and upstream inflow pushed the rivers discharge to around 1,100 cusecs, said Garg. To allow the excess water to pass downstream, all 10 gates of the Gomti barrage were opened, as holding back the water would have led to more problems, according to officials of the Irrigation Department. Also, as the river passes through Lucknow, its flow is affected by multiple bridges and structures along the river, meaning the water does not move through the city as one uniform surge. Why Faizullaganj is worst hit Faizullaganj lies in the floodplain of the Gomti river, an area naturally prone to inundation when the water level in the river rises. Concrete houses have come up in the area over the past two decades. This has increased the vulnerability of the settlement when the river receives an unusually large volume of water, said an official. Sources said that since there was no such flooding in the past two decades, settlements developed on this floodplain. Whats next The state government is now looking at building embankments from Faizullaganj to Naimish as a measure to protect vulnerable areas from future flooding. According to officials, the Lucknow Development Authority LDA was already in the process of laying embankments in Faizullaganj. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who on Monday did an aerial survey of the affected areas, ordered building embankments along the river. The Irrigation Department is expected to conduct the survey from Faizullaganj to Naimish in Sitapur.

articleTitle: ‘Left doesn’t fear or sell out’: Neha Bora says right-wing outfits threatening secular views at educational institutes

Addressing an event organised by the Left-wing student organisations at Jadavpur University, Bora said, The BJP and RSS are out to destroy Bengal. She also alleged that an atmosphere of terror has been created ever since the current dispensation came to power in Bengal.bulldozers are being run on houses one after another. Hitting out at the Centre, Bora said, They think that they have either scared people away or bought them off. But what they dont know is that there is a community that neither fears nor sells out, and that is the Left. As long as even a single voice remains alive against oppression in this country, in Bengal, and across the world, the Left will remain alive. Bora also raised questions about the role of the Election Commission, the police, and the media. The media, Election Commission, and police all are under the control of those in power. Voting is peoples democratic right, and that very right is being repeatedly attacked. The Constitution is also being insulted, she said. She also brought up the ongoing agitation at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi and the recent protests at SRFTI. Protesters cannot be suppressed by attacking them. Even if they face violence, the protesters will not step back. Wherever there is oppression and violence, Leftists will protest. If blood is spilled in Delhi, protests will echo in Kolkata similarly, if violence takes place in Kolkata, Leftists will reach there, she said. SFI leader Srijan Bhattacharya also addressed the convention, raising questions about the right to speak and freedom of expression. How was Rabindranath Tagores poem removed from the syllabus and replaced with the biography of Syama Prasad Mookerjee? When blood flows in Delhi, Kolkata feels the pain and when blood flows in Kolkata, Delhi will surely stand up. This is a promise, a commitment to one another that we will keep making time and again. And on the foundation of this solidarity and this promise, a new India, a new Bengal will surely rise. These are just four more days of sorrow, four more days of oppression these days too shall pass, he said. After being detained by Delhi Police, AISA leader Neha Bora was released on Sunday night. Upon reaching Kolkata on Monday, she attended the JU convention. Fearing protests from right-wing groups, CPIM workers and supporters cautiously escorted her from the airport to Jadavpur. As the crowd swelled, the venue had to be changed mid-way. Ultimately, the convention was held at the K.P. Basu Memorial Hall of JU.

articleTitle: ‘No malafide intention’: Gurugram police chief concedes ‘lapses’ before SC in Delhi man’s cremation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gurugram
description: While the Gurugram police chief claimed that all records were handed over on September 15, Delhi Police documented that inquest papers and the post-mortem report were produced at Lajpat Nagar police station only on September 21.
body_raw: Gurugram Commissioner of Police CP Sibash Kabiraj has conceded that the local police committed procedural lapses while handling the unidentified body of Delhi-based real estate professional Yuvraj Manchanda who was allegedly killed by his former colleague and her partner last month, The Indian Express has learnt. A compliance affidavit, filed in the Supreme Court on October 1, has the Gurugram CP tendering an unqualified apology for the lapses. The affidavit acknowledged that supervisory reviews had found that information regarding the unidentified body was not entered promptly in CCTNS form IIF-10, that intimation was not given to the Executive Magistrate within 24 hours and that the control room in-charge was negligent in performance of her duties for having relayed the information with regards to the discovery of the dead body only to local police stations and not to adjoining states. The police chief, however, maintained that there was no malafide intention involved on the part of the local police. Sequence of events per affidavit Police said a PCR call was received around 405 pm on September 10 regarding a body lying in a waterlogged open field near a drain in Sector 70. According to the police, a team of officers reached the spot to find that the body was bloated and decomposed, rendering fingerprint collection impossible and detailed on-site examination for external injuries infeasible. The body was shifted to a mortuary, and following an autopsy on September 14, it was cremated as an unidentified individual at Ram Bagh Crematorium, police said. According to the affidavit, officers at Badshahpur police station uploaded a recovery entry on the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network Systems CCTNS form, IIF-10, only on September 15, a day after the cremation. An order dated September 17, issued by Deputy Commissioner of Police Headquarters Dr Anshu Singla, placed investigating officer ASI Sahun Khan under immediate suspension and ordered a joint regular departmental enquiry against him and Badshahpur police station SHO Rajesh Kumar. The order observed that ASI Khan made no effective efforts to establish the identity of the deceased, failed to publish an advertisement in local newspapers, omitted uploading details onto the Zonal Integrated Police Network ZIPNET portal, and failed to record complete particulars in CCTNS Forms IIF-10 and IIF-11, police said. The DCP Headquarters noted that an abduction case had already been registered at Lajpat Nagar police station, Delhi, remarking that had the information regarding the unidentified dead body been uploaded on the ZIPNET portal in accordance with the prescribed procedure, there was a possibility of establishing the identity of the deceased. Inspector Kumar was deemed prima facie liable for gross negligence for failing to visit the spot, inspect the body and supervise formalities. ASI Khan was directed to deposit arms and ammunition with him and restricted to subsistence allowance. A second departmental enquiry against both officers was initiated via an order dated September 30, also issued by Dr Singla. This order cited a report by the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Badshahpur, that had found that both the SHO and the IO failed to callseek the presence of the Executive Magistrate at the spot, in direct violation of BNSS Section 194 as well as the police commissionerates Standard Operating Procedure. Through a communication dated September 18, the DCP Headquarters recommended departmental action to the Superintendent of Police, Telecommunication H, against ESI Hasina, who was on duty as Control Room In-charge on September 10. It recorded that she failed to convey the said information regarding the recovery of the unidentified dead body to the concernednearest districts and neighbouring States. Following these lapses, the Gurugram Police Commissioner issued fresh instructions on September 28, mandating that control room personnel must immediately flash particulars of every unidentified body to adjoining districts and neighbouring states. Differences between affidavits Meanwhile, a comparative analysis of affidavits filed by Delhi CP Anurag Kumar dated October 3 and his Gurugram counterpart reveals some differences in the accounts. CP Kabiraj asserted that on September 15, the Delhi Police approached the district police regarding the FIR concerned, and on their request, the entire case property and the documentation was handed over to them. The Delhi Police affidavit, however, stated that its officers were tracking the suspects in Uttarakhand during September 15-16, arrested them on September 17, and only discovered the recovery and cremation of the body on September 18 while inspecting the drain in Gurugram. While the Gurugram police chief claimed that all records were handed over on September 15, Delhi Police documented that inquest papers and the post-mortem report were produced at Lajpat Nagar police station only on September 21. Emphasising the operational fallout of Gurugrams omissions, the Delhi CP Anurag Kumar submitted that the efficacy of ZIPNet and CCTNS in matching missing persons with unidentified dead bodies depends upon the contemporaneous uploading of both by every participating police unit, and upon a cross-search of these databases before an unidentified dead body is disposed of.

articleTitle: Nvidia-backed Reflection unveils first AI model to take on Chinese open models
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The latest letter, signed by 25 companies, comes at a time when Chinese AI models are rapidly proliferating. (AI Image via OpenAI)
description: Founded ​in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis ​Antonoglou, Reflection develops tools that automate ⁠software development, a fast-growing use case for AI.
body_raw: Nvidia-backed Reflection AI debuted its first open-weight model named Beam on Monday, as the startup aims to compete with lower-cost Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Kimi in coding and agentic tasks. Reflection said Beam is competitive with Chinese AI startup Z.ais GLM-5.2 and is closing in on Qwen3.8-Max on coding and agentic tasks. Here are some details The startup said that Beam contains 501 billion total parameters, or variables that determine how an AI system processes information, but activates only 23 billion for each task to make the model faster and cheaper to run by using only part of its network for each task. Comparatively, Z.ais GLM-5.2 has about 744 billion total parameters with 40 billion active parameters. The launch comes as US tech firms are trying to fend off competition from Chinese open-weight models that are cheaper, more customizable and capable of generating code nearly as well as leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic. Founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, Reflection develops tools that automate software development, a fast-growing use case for AI. Earlier this year, Reflection signed a deal with SpaceX for additional computing capacity at the Elon Musk-led companys Colossus 2 data center.

articleTitle: A thick heart? When my patient’s perfect lifestyle wasn’t the whole story
articleFeaturedImageAlt: heart disease
description: She was 36, fit and health-conscious, yet breathlessness, dizziness and fainting revealed a heart condition she never knew she had. Here’s what everyone should know about hypertrophic cardiomyopathy — and the myths that surround it
body_raw: Tanvee, a 36-year-old woman, had always considered herself playing by the book. She exercised regularly, enjoyed yoga and strength training at the gym and maintained a balanced diet. Over the past year, however, she began experiencing breathlessness while climbing stairs, occasional chest discomfort, dizziness, and a racing heartbeat after mild physical activity. She initially dismissed these symptoms as stress, lack of fitness, or fatigue from balancing work and family responsibilities. But when she briefly lost consciousness after walking uphill and sought medical attention, the diagnosis surprised her. Imaging tests revealed she had obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy oHCM, an inherited condition in which the heart muscle becomes abnormally thick, making it harder for blood to leave the heart. Although the diagnosis initially caused anxiety, she was reassured that with appropriate treatment, regular follow-up, and lifestyle guidance, she could continue to lead an active and fulfilling life. Her story is not unique. OHCM remains one of the most misunderstood cardiac conditions, despite being the most common inherited condition. Misconceptions around the disease can lead to fear, delayed diagnosis, and hesitation in seeking appropriate medical care. While oHCM has historically been associated with sudden cardiac death, particularly in young athletes, advances in diagnosis and treatment have significantly transformed its management. Today, with early diagnosis and appropriate treatment, many patients can lead active and fulfilling lives. Understanding oHCM Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a form of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy HCM - an inherited heart muscle disorder caused by genetic mutations that affect the structure and function of the heart muscle. These changes cause the heart muscle to become abnormally thick, most commonly affecting the wall, or septum, between the two lower chambers of the heart. In nearly two-thirds of patients with HCM, the thickened heart muscle can block the flow of blood leaving the heart, a condition known as obstructive HCM oHCM. As a result, the heart must work harder to pump blood throughout the body, often leading to breathlessness, chest pain, fatigue, palpitations, dizziness, or fainting during physical activity. Myth 1 A diagnosis of oHCM inevitably leads to sudden death. Fact While oHCM was once primarily recognised for its association with sudden cardiac death, advances in medical science have significantly improved patient outcomes. With timely diagnosis, appropriate medical care, and ongoing monitoring, many people with oHCM can experience a good quality of life and a near-normal life expectancy. Regular follow-up helps assess disease progression and guides individualised care. Myth 2 People with oHCM need to avoid physical activities. Fact Complete avoidance of physical activity is no longer recommended for most patients. Although high-intensity competitive sports may not be suitable for everyone with oHCM, mild-to-moderate exercise is generally encouraged and offers important cardiovascular benefits. Exercise recommendations should always be individualised after a comprehensive assessment by a cardiologist, taking into account symptoms, severity of obstruction, and overall risk profile. Myth 3 Diet and lifestyle are the primary causes of oHCM. Fact Unlike heart conditions caused by high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol, oHCM develops because of inherited genetic mutations affecting heart muscle proteins. Since the disease often runs in families, screening of close relatives may also be recommended. Myth 4 Every patient with oHCM will require surgical treatment Fact Surgery is only one of several available treatment options. Care is individualised, and the most appropriate approach depends on each patients symptoms and clinical condition. Myth 5 oHCM cannot go unnoticed. Fact The condition can remain silent for years. Symptoms can be subtle and easily mistaken for stress, poor fitness, or other illnesses. Some individuals carrying the genetic mutation never develop symptoms, while others experience mild or intermittent symptoms. Typical symptoms include Shortness of breath Chest pain Fatigue Palpitations Dizziness or light-headedness Fainting, particularly during or after exercise Given this variability, individuals with persistent symptoms or a family history of cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death should undergo appropriate cardiac evaluation. Myth 6 Medication can cure the condition. Fact Advances in treatment have significantly improved disease management, helping many patients lead healthier and more active lives. While current therapies focus on controlling symptoms and reducing complications, ongoing research continues to expand treatment possibilities. Treatment aims to reduce symptoms, improve blood flow, minimise obstruction, and lower the risk of complications such as abnormal heart rhythms and heart failure. Long-term follow-up remains an important part of care, allowing treatment to be adjusted as the condition evolves. Timely evaluation is particularly important for those with a family history of the disease. Early detection can also help identify family members who may be at risk and require screening. Although oHCM remains a lifelong condition, it is no longer viewed through the lens of fear alone. The author is cardiac electrophysiologist at AIG Hospitals, Hyderabad

articleTitle: BJP, JD(S) defend bulk Form 7 filings, allege ‘false FIRs’ in Karnataka
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka SIR voter deletion Form 7
description: A delegation of BJP and JD(S) leaders submitted a petition to Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukumar, seeking that election officials be instructed to 'safeguard the interests of individuals filing Form 7 objections'.
body_raw: A delegation of BJP and Janata Dal Secular leaders on Monday submitted a petition to the Karnataka chief electoral officer CEO, urging him to direct the state police not to register false or unwarranted FIRs against individuals, including BJP workers for allegedly filing Form 7s in bulk to disenfranchise eligible voters during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. The National Democratic Alliance NDA partners also sought that CEO V Anbukumar instruct the electoral registration officers ERO and assistant EROs to safeguard the interests of individuals filing Form 7 objections as there was no bar on filing bulk objections through Form 7. Form 7 allows an elector to object to the inclusion of a name or seek deletion of an existing entry from the electoral roll. The delegations memorandum also accused the Congress government in Karnataka of unduly influencing and interfering in the SIR process. The members of the ruling government, along with their party workers are also misusing the state police machinery by filing false and serious criminal charges against individuals who have been filing objections through Form 7, thereby creating a sense of fear and apprehension in the minds of objectors and diluting the entire exercise of SIR, the NDA partners said in the petition. Karnataka voter row Protests escalate Last week, a Karnataka BJP delegation had met Director General and Inspector General of Police M A Saleem, alleging that criminal cases were being registered against BJP workers and political activists for submitting Form 7 objections. The development came amid multiple FIRs being filed across the state based on complaints by voters who discovered that Form 7s were submitted against their names despite them being genuine voters. A protest by Congress leaders, led by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, saw Anbukumar agreeing to initiate legal action against those responsible for filing bulk Form 7 applications to remove eligible voters. No bar on bulk objections BJP, JDS There exists a provision to file applications in bulk for identifying corrections to be carried out in the draft electoral rolls. Hence, there is no bar on filing bulk objections through Form-7 as per the communique issued by the Honble Election Commission of India dated 16.01.2026. There are no restrictions on the number of Form-7 applications that may be submitted to the ERO Hence, no illegality is committed while submitting Form-7, the BJP-JDS petition said. The two parties also raised questions about the protest staged by Shivakumar and other ministers in front of the CEOs office. We express our serious concern and disapproval regarding the undue influence exerted by the state government on the constitutional process of SIR. It is also distressing to note that the chief electoral officer appears to have succumbed to such pressure, it added.

articleTitle: Karnataka High Court stays drug licence suspension, cancellation orders
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka FSDA, fake medicines
description: The Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration on September 18 cancelled the licences of 16 retail and wholesale pharmaceutical firms across Bengaluru. It suspended the licences of eight others, including pharma major Pfizer’s depot.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court on Monday stayed the Food Safety and Drug Administration FSDA order cancelling Fortune Medical Solutions licence and suspending Vivanta Pharmaceuticals licence for allegedly selling spurious products. The Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration FSDA on September 18, cancelled the licences of 16 retail and wholesale pharmaceutical firms across Bengaluru and suspended those of eight others, including global pharma major Pfizers depot, as they violated Rule 66 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945. Rule 66 provides for an opportunity of hearing and explanation to the party against whom action is proposed before suspending or cancelling the licence. Justice C M Poonacha said, The petitioner shall also be permitted to carry on its pharmaceutical distribution business till the next date of hearing in accordance with law. This order will not preclude the respondents from taking such measures as may be permissible under law and petitioner shall cooperate with the authorities in any action that is undertaken in accordance with law, the court said. The court issued notice to FSDA and others and directed them to file their reply to the petitions. The petitions are now posted for hearing on October 9. Additional Government Advocate Rahul Cariappa said the court will hear together all 16 petitions filed by similarly placed pharma companies on October 9. FSDAIs action follows raids at farmhouses in the Bidadi and Dodderi areas of Bengaluru South district on August 18. The agency seized suspected counterfeit medicines worth around Rs 5 crore, along with fake bills, injection-filling equipment and counterfeit labels. Later, a Special Investigation Team SIT was formed to probe the wider racket. According to the FSDA, preliminary investigations revealed that the farmhouse premises were being used to procure low-cost medications from neighbouring states. These cheaper drugs were allegedly refilled into new vials and relabelled to counterfeit expensive life-saving brands of multinational corporations, specifically imitating imported products under the brand name Pfizer. To deceive buyers and maximise illicit profits, the counterfeit labels featured QRscanning codes that the FSDA found completely non-functional upon verification. These counterfeit drugs lack active medicinal ingredients and may contain harmful substances, the agency had noted. In its petition, Vivanta Pharma claimed that the allegations only relate to identified batches of Zavicefta, whereas the impugned order suspended all the drug licences of the petitioner from carrying on its business and violates its fundamental right. Further, the blanket order is excessive, arbitrary, and disproportionate. Firms whose licences were cancelled Avesco Healthcare,Bangalore Speciali Pharma,Patel Medi Trade,Rajarajeshwari Pharma,Surya Speciality Pharma,SWS Pharma,Krupa Healthcare,St Philomena Hospital Drug Centre,Sagar Pharma,Zymus Pharma,Fortune Medical Solutions,Excelcare Pharma,Patel Medicals, and Bangalore Speciality Pharma outlet at Chamarajpet. Firms whose licences were suspended Med Pharma, Surya Speciality Hospital, Sagar Pharma Unit-II, Vivantha Pharmaceuticals, Maruthi Medicals,Viva Pharma Belagavi,Hi-5 Pharma, and Pfizer. Seized materials-5,640 vials of counterfeit Cefiavigent 2.5 injection, falsely branded under Eucratia Healthcare Pvt Ltd, valued at over Rs 3.38 crore, the single largest component of the haul.-1,531 vials of Hizlam injectables, falsely attributed to Welcure Remedies Rs 52.24 lakh.-264 vials of Emblaveo, counterfeiting Pfizer Rs 20.59 lakh.-30 boxes of expired medications, valued at Rs 35 lakh, which officials say were apparently being prepared for reintroduction into the market.-Several other counterfeit injectable batches, including Xavitaz, Zavicefta, Tigynt, Tigvnet, Aztreo, and Trezam, along with packaging components, an injection-filling machine, and bulk quantities of forged labels and stamps.

articleTitle: Noida mall theft video: Woman allegedly caught stealing ghee, refined oil
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Woman stealing Noida mall video
description: A store employee reportedly said staff had been monitoring the woman after noticing similar incidents over the past month.
body_raw: A video showing a woman being stopped by security at a Noida mall after she was allegedly caught with grocery items in her bag has gone viral on social media. According to multiple reports, the incident took place Sunday evening when the woman visited Le Marche at DLF Mall of India in Sector 18 with her husband. After shopping for some time, she reportedly headed towards the exit while her husband remained at the billing counter. When a security guard allegedly stopped her for a routine bag check, the woman reportedly refused, leading to an argument with store staff. Additional security personnel were then called to the spot. Store staff reportedly reviewed CCTV footage and allegedly found the woman placing a 1-kg pack of ghee and a 1-kg bottle of refined oil into her bag. The items were subsequently recovered, according to the reports. Caught on camera Videos of the incident, shared in three parts on X, have gone viral and show the woman being escorted back inside the mall by security guards while covering her face with her phone. A man believed to be associated with the store also appears to confront her in the video. A store employee reportedly claimed that staff had been monitoring the woman after allegedly noticing similar incidents over the past month. The employee further alleged that she had previously taken ghee and other grocery products worth several thousand rupees. However, these earlier allegations have not been independently verified. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Theindianclubs theindianclubs The womans husband was reportedly called from the billing counter after the items were recovered. Store staff allegedly reprimanded the couple in front of other shoppers. The matter was later resolved after the woman reportedly paid for the recovered ghee and refined oil. The two sides subsequently reached an agreement, following which the woman left the mall. It remains unclear whether a police complaint was filed or whether the woman was formally accused of the alleged previous thefts. The claims circulating on social media could not be independently verified based on the information available.

articleTitle: Karnataka plans AI training in government schools from Class 6
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka plans to introduce AI training in govt schools from Class 6
description: Shivakumar also directed officials to identify land for establishing an AI university in the state. Steps are being taken to recruit 956 teachers on an outsourcing basis, it said.
body_raw: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Monday directed officials to explore means to introduce Artificial Intelligence AI training in government schools from Class 6, with support from the Information Technology department and private partners. He issued these directions at a review meeting on the progress of his governments 100-day programmes, recruitments and priority schemes. AI training has already started for Class 9 students in government schools. The officials were asked to work toward extending it to students from Class 6, Shivakumar said. Also Read Karnataka proposes rule to reserve 15 government seats in professional courses for rural students Google expressed interest in providing AI training in schools, and officials were asked to examine the companys initiatives in Telangana as part of this exercise, according to the CMO statement. Shivakumar also directed officials to identify land for establishing an AI university in the state. Steps are being taken to recruit 956 teachers on an outsourcing basis, it said. Reviewing the School Education Department, the chief minister directed officials to organise visits for Class 9 and 11 students from 941 urban schools to progressive farmers fields. The students should be provided facilities to stay overnight in villages, including community halls and hostels, and private schools should also mandatorily implement the programme, he said. The programme should be completed by December. The implementation process has been simplified by authorising deputy commissioners to approve detailed project reports and tenders for KPS, he said.
