articleTitle: Nearly 1/3rd of electors in Delhi issued SIR notices now verified
articleFeaturedImageAlt: sir delhi
description: This is a sharp uptick in the number of notices disposed of compared to a week back. In the period from August 31 to September 29, only 4.01 lakh notices had been disposed.
body_raw: As the Special Intensive Revision SIR process continues in the Capital, nearly one-third of the electors around 31 who had to prove their eligibility to stay on the electoral rolls have been verified, data from the office of the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer CEO showed on Monday, with over 55 days left to dispose of the rest of notices and objections. This is a sharp uptick in the number of notices disposed of compared to a week back. In the period from August 31 to September 29, only 4.01 lakh notices had been disposed. Over the next one week, more than six lakh notices were disposed of, with the total figure reaching 10.28 lakh on Tuesday. Election officials have attributed this increase to exemptions from in-person hearings for voters who received notices, changes in the portal in which they had to upload documents, additional deployment of officials and special camps. Delhi had around 1.45 crore electors before the SIR process of voter rolls began in the Capital. Among them, 97.5 lakh were included in the draft electoral roll, while around 47.5 lakh electors were classified as uncollectible-after the Booth-level officers BLOs found them absent, shifted, dead or having duplicate entries, among other reasons-and were struck off the roll. Among the 97.5 lakh who did make it to the draft roll, one-third or around 33.1 lakh electors were issued notices to prove that they are eligible to be on the final roll. While 13.79 lakh electors got notices because they could not link themselves to the electoral roll of the last SIR, 19.33 lakh were flagged for logical discrepancies in their enumeration forms. On the new changes, an Electoral Registration Officer ERO said, Now, I dont need to call hundreds of people to my office everyday for hearings, right? BLOs are going house to house and where needed, electors can also forward their documents to the BLO on Whatsapp also. After its first meeting since The Indian Express reported on the rupture within the Election Commission, the poll panel had said last week that electors who were issued notices will not be required to attend hearings to prove their eligibility. BLOs will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them on the ECINet, for decision by the ERO. Such persons need not be called for hearing to EROAERO office, a statement from the ECI said. Some BLOs, however, expressed disappointment with the deadline for disposal of notices, claims and objections getting extended to November 30. I am also working in the school for 5-6 hours, after which now I have to again go door-to-door to collect documents. The deadline has also been increased by another month. It was supposed to be a three month exercise, but now it will last five months. Should we leave school work and do this full time only? a BLO said. Another BLO said that in some areas it is easier to conduct hearings at a central location instead of going house to house due to often confusing and wrong addresses. The number of Assistant EROs, who are often school principals and can also dispose of notices like EROs, was also increased in Delhi. On September 24, the number of AEROs was increased from 297 to 902, an increase of 605. An official said that BLOs have been given a target of conducting at least 10 hearings every day. An ERO pointed out that the change in the ECINET portal which lets EROs dispose of notices without conducting a hearing is one reason behind the uptick in notices being disposed of. Especially for notices for very minor logical discrepancies, if a BLO has verified the elector and is satisfied, we dont need to trouble the electors for documents. I cleared hundreds of notices in one night after this became available, an ERO said.

articleTitle: FIR against 2 ‘BJP agents’ over Form 7s to delete 5,698 Bengaluru voters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka SIR Form 7 mass voter deletion
description: As per Karnataka Pradesh Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy’s complaint, the Form 7 applications claimed that 5,698 voters had permanently shifted from Jayanagar constituency.
body_raw: An FIR was registered in Bengaluru against two alleged BJP booth level agents BLAs and others for submitting fraudulent Form 7 applications seeking the deletion of 5,698 voters from the electoral rolls in Jayanagar Assembly constituency. The FIR registered on October 5, based on a complaint by former Jayanagar MLA and Karnataka Pradesh Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy, names BLAs Ramakrishna and Yogesh as accused, alleging that they are affiliated with the BJP. The move comes amid a growing row over bulk Form 7 filings in Karnataka, with the Congress alleging a conspiracy to delete lakhs of eligible voters from the electoral rolls amid the Special Intensive Revision exercise, and the BJP and Janata Dal Secular seeking protection from what they term false or unwarranted cases against party workers. Form 7 allows an elector to object to the inclusion of a name or seek deletion of an existing entry from the electoral roll. 5,698 voters permanently shifted What the Form 7s said According to the October 5 complaint, the alleged irregularities took place between June 16 and October 5 during the electoral roll revision process. Form 7 applications were allegedly submitted claiming that 5,698 voters had permanently shifted from the constituency. As per the complaint, the applications sought deletion of 54 voters in Pattabhiramanagar Ward 165, 525 in Byrasandra Ward 169, 719 in Jayanagar East Ward 170, 4,327 in Gurappanapalya Ward 171, and 82 voters across J P Nagar, Sarakki and Shakambarinagar Wards 177, 178 and 179. Reddy alleged in her complaint that the applications disproportionately targeted voters from minority communities and other sections perceived to be politically opposed to the BJP and its allies. The complaint also alleged that the identity details and voter IDs of two citizens or voters identified as C Ramesh and his wife Roopa were used to file the Form 7 applications without their knowledge or consent. Some of the applications allegedly carried forged signatures and were submitted to Booth Level Officer Lokesh at the election office in Jayanagar 4th Block. The police are investigating the allegations. Similar complaints across Karnataka In Bengaluru, the Vyalikaval police on October 2 registered an FIR after Congress leader Anoop Iyengar alleged that 778 Form 7 applications had been filed seeking deletion of voters in eight polling parts of Ward 64 in the Malleswaram Assembly constituency. The complaint alleged that several voters were still residing at the addresses mentioned in the electoral rolls and that some applications contained false information or suspected forged signatures. G S Vasanthalakshmi, identified in the FIR as a BJP member, was named as an accused. The allegations are under investigation. Similar complaints have been reported from other parts of Karnataka. Police have registered cases in Bidar, Mysuru and Belagavi over Form 7 applications seeking deletion of voters, with the complaints alleging false information and forged documents.

articleTitle: Israel nearly shot down flydubai flight 1073 after cockpit attack on Indian pilot Smit Machchhar: Report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: FlyDubai
description: Israel was prepared to shoot down a FlyDubai plane after its captain was attacked in the cockpit.
body_raw: Israel was prepared to shoot down flydubai Flight 1073 with all passengers on board after Indian captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami in the cockpit, CBS News reported, citing two Israeli sources with direct knowledge of the matter. The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, with 182 people on board, most of them Israelis, was flying along the Saudi-Jordanian border when Captain Machchhar was stabbed by his co-pilot in an attempt to crash the aircraft. The report said that after the plane plunged 14,000 feet, the Israeli Air Force tried contacting the cockpit but got no response. It then activated its long-practised procedure for a potential 911-style incident, swiftly convened a pre-established emergency committee, set up a command centre, scrambled fighter jets and closed its airspace. Israel recalled fighter jets Israel, however, called back its fighter jets after authorities realised the aircraft was turning towards Saudi Arabia, which had also scrambled its own fighter jets, according to the report. The flight then made an emergency landing in Tabuk, after Captain Machchhar opened the cockpit door and passengers subdued the Omani co-pilot. The report, citing sources, further stated that Israel would have dispatched fighter jets into Jordanian airspace to investigate if the FlyDubai flight had moved closer to Israeli territory. The Israeli Air Force pilots would have then attempted to approach the aircraft closely enough to establish visual contact with the cockpit and assess the situation, before checking the cabin for signs of panic. After checking in on the aircraft, the IAF would have updated the emergency committee, which, according to the report, would in turn alert the defence minister and prime minister if a hijacking was confirmed and there was no response from terrorists. Ultimately, the final decision to shoot down the aircraft would have fallen to the prime minister, a course of action CBS News sources described as far preferable to letting the plane crash into Ben Gurion Airport, the Azrieli Center in Tel Aviv or another high-value target.

articleTitle: ‘Focus on 403, not 3’: Akhilesh rules out Samajwadi Party’s third Rajya Sabha candidate
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has said the party will not field a third candidate for the upcoming Rajya Sabha polls (File photo).
description: The SP has already fielded party veteran Ram Gopal Yadav and Reliance Industries executive Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, who filed their nominations in Lucknow last week.
body_raw: After a week of suspense, Samajwadi Party SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday announced that the party is not fielding a third candidate for the upcoming Rajya Sabha polls, stating that the partys focus is not on three seats but on the 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. The state goes to polls next year. Yadav had earlier stated that his party would field a third candidate once the required numbers are secured. However, in a post on X this morning, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said, Now, our focus is not on three, but on 403. Tuesday is the last day for filing nominations for the biennial polls, followed by scrutiny of papers on October 7. Names can be withdrawn till October 9, while polling will be conducted on October 16. ALSO READ Why Samajwadi Party fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani in Rajya Sabha polls Rajya Sabha math The SP has already fielded party veteran Ram Gopal Yadav and Reliance Industries executive Dhanraj Nathwani for the Rajya Sabha polls, who filed their nominations in Lucknow last week. The BJP on Monday had announced eight candidates, including Dalits and Brahmins, leaving out Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma, whose terms in the Upper House are set to end next month. They comprise state minister Dharampal Singh, Shruti Gangwar Prakash Pal, Vidya Sagar Sonkar, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Radhakant Ojha and Gopi Krishna Pandey and Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan. The SP and the Congress together effectively have 102 MLAs on their side, with the numbers enough to elect two MPs 37 first-preference votes are required. They are, however, nine first-preference votes short of getting a third candidate elected In the 403-member Assembly, the ruling NDA has 291 MLAs, including the BJPs 255. With support of Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, which has two MLAs, the alliances effective strength is 293. The main opposition, Samajwadi Party, has 101 MLAs, and its ally, Congress, has two.

articleTitle: ‘You are licking an ice cube’: Vijay Deverakonda recalls cutting water intake for Liger
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay Deverakonda
description: Vijay Deverakonda’s candid account of his Liger prep reveals just how far actors can go for a shredded look
body_raw: Vijay Deverakonda recently opened up about cutting his water intake for the film Liger. I did it during Liger.where the water was cut down to make my body look shredded. It is not healthy or good at all. It starts with four or six litres of water and slowly cuts it down to 300 ml to 100 ml. 10 hours before the shoot, you dont drink water. You are licking an ice cube. Its a random t, the Ranabaali actor told Sudhir Srinivasan on his YouTube podcast. Bodybuilders and all do it. Every second from the time I was drinking 300 ml of water a day.every minute.you are like..water.water.water. When I was licking that ice cube and was not allowed water, I was sleeping thinking of water. I knew I had to go four hours without water, and then I could drink. I asked my team for coconut water and to get four litres of it. I didnt want food or anything, the 37-year-old added. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. During the conversation, he also mentioned that he has tried fasting but failed many times. Intermittent is easy. Some people fast for 48 or 72 hours. I have managed just about 24 hours fast once. I have tried six times and given up five times. Taking a leaf out of his candid admission, we asked experts about cutting water intake and how it impacts the body. From a nutrition and sports-health perspective, consultant dietitian and fitness expert Garima Goyal noted that this is not a healthy fat-loss strategy. Athletes and bodybuilders sometimes use short-term dehydration protocols before competitions or photoshoots to alter appearance, but these practices are highly context-dependent and can carry risks. The general public should not copy them as a weight-loss method. Severe water restriction causes dehydration, not meaningful fat loss. The temporary shredded appearance happens because reduced body water can make muscles and skin appear tighter and more defined, said Goyal. But the risks can be significant. Severe dehydration can lead to dizziness, weakness, headaches, low blood pressure, impaired concentration, reduced exercise performance and electrolyte disturbances. In more extreme situations, dehydration and electrolyte imbalance can affect kidney function and cardiovascular health, Goyal told indianexpress.com. What is particularly concerning for general people is that dehydration can be mistaken for successful weight loss. The number on the weighing scale may fall rapidly because water is being lost, but that does not mean the person has suddenly lost the same amount of body fat. Once normal hydration resumes, much of that weight returns, clarified Goyal. Can drinking only 100300 ml of water a day be dangerous? For most adults, that is far below normal fluid requirements, although individual needs vary. Such extreme restriction can result in significant dehydration, particularly if the person is exercising, sweating or working in a hot environment. It can also disturb the bodys electrolyte balance, which in severe cases can affect the heart and nervous system, said Dr Amit Sara, director, internal medicine, Jupiter Hospital Thane. Is licking ice or drinking coconut water enough to prevent dehydration? No, noted Dr Sarf. Licking an ice cube provides very little fluid and does not compensate for severe water restriction. Coconut water contains fluids and electrolytes, but it should not be considered a substitute for adequate hydration, particularly when someone has deliberately restricted fluids for several hours, said Dr Saraf. Extreme thirst, very little or dark-coloured urine, dizziness, confusion, unusual weakness, fainting, rapid heartbeat or inability to keep fluids down are warning signs that should not be ignored. Severe dehydration can become a medical emergency and may require prompt fluid and electrolyte replacement, said Dr Saraf. Vijays experience also highlights an important distinction looking extremely lean for a few hours is very different from being healthy and maintaining a sustainable body composition. For fat loss, the focus should remain on an appropriate calorie deficit, adequate protein, resistance training, recovery and proper hydration rather than manipulating body water. A shredded look is temporary. Dehydration is not a shortcut to sustainable fat loss, said Goyal. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood ‘bunch of thieves’ for stealing his bestseller plots
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jeffrey Archer once accused Ladies Vs Ricky Bahl for stealing the plot of his book.
description: British author Jeffrey Archer, who died at 86 on Monday, once accused Bollywood films Ladies vs Ricky Bahl and Khudgarz of stealing the plots of his bestsellers.
body_raw: British author Jeffrey Archer, who wrote several bestselling novels, died at 86 on Monday. He died suddenly and peacefully at his home between writing sessions, as per his publisher HarperCollins. Hes already completed Adam and Eve, touted as his final novel after a publishing career of 50 years. A fan of Indian author RK Narayan, he had a rather love-hate relationship with India, particularly the Hindi film industry. When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood a bunch of thieves Just look at your Bollywood These bunch of thieves have stolen several of my books without so much as a by your leave. Ladies Vs Ricky Bahl and Khudgarz, and several others, alleged Archer in an interview back in 2015. He was in the process of pitching his 2011 bestseller Only Time Will Tell to Hollywood and Bollywood production houses for a film adaptation. While he claimed several Hollywood companies wanted the rights of the book, he had also been looking for an Indian partner. And that does not mean some second-rate Bollywood idiot who goes around saying hes a Bollywood star producer and then he is not Its true What can I say? Such has been my Indian experience many times, he told DNA, laughing. Archer claimed that Manish Sharmas 2011 crime comedy Ladies vs Ricky Bahl was based on his 1976 bestseller Not A Penny More, Not A Penny Less, which also revolved around three people whove been conned trying to frame and get back at the conman. While Ranveer Singh played the titular character of the conman, the three peoples genders were switched to women hed wooed in order to scam them. Anushka Sharma, Dipannita Sharma, and Parineeti Chopra played the three women in Ladies vs Ricky Bahl, with the film being Parineetis acting debut. It was produced by Yash Chopras production house Yash Raj Films, and marked the reunion of Ranveer and Anushka after his 2010 acting debut, Manish Sharmas hit romantic comedy Band Baaja Baaraat. Archer also claimed that Rakesh Roshans 1987 directorial debut Khudgarz was based on his 1979 bestseller Kane and Abel. Like the book, it revolved around two feuding brothers, played by Shatrughan Sinha and Jeetendra. Co-written by Mohan Kaul and Ravi Kapoor, it was also produced by Roshan. The cast of the action film also includes Amrita Singh, Govinda, and Neelam among others. Jeffrey Archer on his official collaborations with Bollywood Despite his unpleasant encounters with Bollywood, Archer remained endlessly fascinated with India. He began selling the adaptation rights of his book officially. Producer Sheetal Talwar bought the rights to his 1984 bestseller First Among Equals and short story A La Carte from the 1988 collection A Twist in the Tale for a reported sum of Rs 1.5 crore, as per a Mumbai Mirror report. While he planned to adapt the former into a high-budget television series, that never saw light of the day. Kussh Sinha, son of Shatrughan Sinha and brother of actor Sonakshi Sinha, was supposed to make his directorial debut with that show. He ended up directing his first feature only as recently as last year with horror film Nikita Roy, starring Sonakshi in the titular role. Filmmaker Hansal Mehta was also in talks with Archer to buy the adaptation rights of Kane and Abel. However, while that never materialized either, Mehta had already directed a TV show loosely based on the book. Lakshya 1999 starred Kay Kay Menon and Sachin Khedekar among others. He wanted to remake the show into a film, starring longtime collaborator Rajkummar Rao, back in 2014. Also Read Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Back in 2015, Archer was even planning a book set in India, and particularly Bollywood. Consisting of eight chapters, the novel was supposed to have a Bollywood heroine at the centre. However, that book never saw light of the day either. However, Archer enjoyed massive popularity in the country, partly thanks to widespread piracy, which gave him the moniker, The Lord of the Paperbacks.

articleTitle: GST process reforms pin hope on data, tech to ensure compliance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: GST
description: Ease of doing business in focus: from no arrest, minimum sentencing removal to Rs 10,000-threshold for notices
body_raw: The GST Councils meeting on Wednesday will take up the second half of the reform exercise that was kicked off by the Goods and Services Tax GST rate cuts announced in September 2025, with officials saying the process reforms on the agenda will cement the indirect tax regime for the next half a decade or so. Officials are also of the view that systems built on technology and good quality data can help ensure correct behaviour from businesses without onerous compliance. GST rates were cleaned up last year. Now, the focus is on moving towards a stable tax system with predictability, as was the demand from the industry. It may take a year or two to stabilise and then the GST regime will only require minor tweaks for the next 5-6 years, an official said. If the proposals are approved by the Council, then the framework will be set, the official added. No arrest, notices threshold A key proposal in the process reforms that will be discussed in the Council meeting on October 8 is going to be the removal of the power to arrest by GST officers, as reported by The Indian Express on Sunday. This power, officials said, has led to the creation of unnecessary leverage over businesses even before the actual arrest stage is reached. Tax disputes will be resolved through civil consequences, namely recovery of the tax, interest for the delay, and penalty, the official said. However, prosecution will remain available, with the GST Council expected to discuss some tweaks. Additionally, the threshold for prosecution is likely to be increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore. The sentencing provisions are also proposed to be softened, with the minimum sentence likely to be removed altogether. This, officials said, means courts wont be bound to impose a term of imprisonment regardless of circumstances. Also, a fine will be available as an option in every case. Furthermore, it is proposed that no notice will be issued at all where the amount involved is below Rs 10,000. Crucially, this change is expected to apply to new cases as well as those pending, whether in adjudication or in the appeal phase. Such cases are about a fifth of all cases by number and a negligible part of the money. For a small business, a notice of this size costs more to answer in fees and time than the amount in dispute. Removing that category will be a real relief, and will free up officers for matters of substance, the official said. Redesign of processes The GST Council will deliberate on a wide variety of issues on October 7 that encompass all the tax dealings of an entity during its lifecycle - getting registered, filing returns and correcting them, claiming refunds, and answering demands. All four processes are proposed to be redesigned on a single principle, namely that the system should do what can be done from data and the officer should be left with what needs judgement, an official said. One major process change is set to be for the export of services, which will help align GST laws with the practice on ground. Citing the example of a testing laboratory which receives a prototype from a foreign client, tests it, sends back the report, and is paid in foreign exchange, the official explained that the place of supply followed where the work was performed. It will now follow the location of the customer, and such work therefore qualifies as an export. This opens the whole field of testing, certification, repair, calibration, research, and analysis to export treatment, and India has substantial capacity in all of them. Wednesdays GST Council meeting comes over 13 months after the last one in September 2025 which announced the major rate overhaul that saw the number of tax slabs being reduced to 5 and 18, with a 40 rate for demerit goods. There have been no meetings of the GST Council in the interim, but discussions have been ongoing to bring all stakeholders on the same page, and that takes time. What has helped is that there have not been any major concerns about revenues being adversely impacted by the rate rationalisation exercise of September 2025. This has made it easier to go ahead with the process reforms discussions at this weeks meeting.

articleTitle: Vidyut Jammwal sits still for 16 minutes as tears roll down his face: ‘You need to stop’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vidyut Jammwal
description: Vidyut Jammwal’s unusual meditation has expert looking at what happens when we simply stop
body_raw: Actor Vidyut Jammwal is receivingwidespread online love formeditating for 16 minutes without blinking, holding his breath, and remaining remarkably still even as tears rolled down his eyes at theStreet Fighter trailer launch event.He also had a message to share for the younger generation, urging them to pause and take a breather. You need to stop. Stay still. It will take you places, said Jammwal. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. That statement is worth examining, especially at a time when almost every aspect of modern life encourages the opposite. We are taught to move faster, achieve more, consume more information, respond immediately and remain constantly available. Even our empty moments have almost disappeared. A lift ride, a traffic signal, a waiting room or two quiet minutes before a meeting are quickly occupied by a screen. Yet there is an important distinction we rarely discuss meditation and stillness are not necessarily the same practice, and each can teach us something different about ourselves, reflected Delnna Rrajesh, psychotherapist and relationship breakthrough coach. Delnna noted that meditation itself is a vast field, and many traditions include open-eyed, walking and movement-based practices, so it would be inaccurate to define meditation simply as sitting with ones eyes closed. It sounds easy until we try it. Within minutes, the body begins issuing instructions. Shift your leg. Move your hand. Look over there. Scratch that itch. Check the time. Pick up the phone. Speak. Do something. The mind joins in How much longer? What is the point of this? I am bored. I cannot do this. Suddenly, what seemed like an exercise in doing nothing becomes an extraordinary opportunity to observe how continuously we are pulled by sensation, thought, and impulse. Stillness makes restlessness visible, described Delnna. To the expert, that is one of its greatest values. We often assume that because we are constantly moving, the movement is voluntary. Stillness lets us see how much of our behaviour may actually be automatic. A sound occurs, and our attention follows it. Something moves, and our eyes chase it. A notification appears, and the hand reaches for the phone almost before a conscious decision has been made. An uncomfortable thought arises, and we immediately look for distraction. Stillness introduces a tiny but psychologically important possibility I can notice an impulse without immediately obeying it. Meditation can therefore help us observe what is happening within us stillness can help us discover that not everything happening within us requires an immediate response. The two practices can meet beautifully, but their emphasis can be different, expressed Delnna. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Varinder Chawla varindertchawla For most people, the experiment can be much simpler. Sit comfortably for a few minutes. Keep the eyes naturally open and blink normally. Allow the gaze to remain soft. Put the phone away. Minimise unnecessary movement without turning discomfort into punishment. Then observe what happens. Notice the urge to move, look, check, speak, plan or escape. Instead of judging the impulse, become curious about it, said Delnna. Meditation can then be practised separately and intentionally perhaps closing the eyes, depending on the method, settling attention and allowing yourself to go inward. We do not need to choose between meditation and stillness. We can train both. One can deepen our relationship with our inner world the other can strengthen our ability to stay steady while the outer world continues around us. The real test of either practice, however, begins when we leave the meditation room. A person can sit peacefully for an hour and still become completely reactive during an argument. We can have profound experiences with our eyes closed and still lose access to that awareness when somebody criticises us, our child refuses to listen, our partner touches an old wound, or anxiety begins constructing frightening possibilities. The deeper question is whether practice gradually changes what happens in those moments. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: How Kane and Abel made Jeffrey Archer a household name in India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A portrait photograph of Jeffrey
description: Britain’s bestselling storyteller and an Indian bookshelf staple, Jeffrey Archer died suddenly and peacefully at 86, hours before his final novel, Adam and Eve, was released
body_raw: Jeffrey Archer, one of Britains most commercially successful novelists, whose page-turners remain fixtures on Indian bookshelves, died on Monday at his home in England, a day before his final novel was published. His publisher, HarperCollins, said the 86-year-old writer died suddenly and peacefully. From Kane and Abel to Adam and Eve Published in 1979, Kane and Abel-the sprawling saga of two men born on the same day in 1906, William Lowell Kane, the son of a wealthy Boston banking family, and Abel Rosnovski, a Polish immigrant who escapes a Siberian labour camp and builds a hotel empire-made Archer a household name around the world, especially in India, where the novel was, for many, their first introduction to adult fiction. His final book, Adam and Eve, out today, returns to the idea of two lives beginning on the same day at opposite ends of society a shepherds son and an earls daughter, both born on Armistice Day 1918. As the only son of an ailing journalist in Weston-super-Mare who became Baron Archer of Weston-super-Mare, Archer had lived on both ends of the spectrum. He was one of the few novelists who could claim that his life was almost as eventful as the plot of his books. He was a member of Parliament at 29, nearly bankrupt at 34, a millionaire novelist by 40 and a prisoner at 61. Everyone goes through several highs and lows in their lives, he told The Indian Express in Pune in 2016. Mine are just more public. Archer and India His books have sold more than 300 million copies and have been published in 114 countries, according to his official website, but he himself admitted that no country quite embraced him like India. From 2008 he toured almost every year, often launching books here before their British release. In 2011 he began the world tour for Only Time Will Tell in Bangalore, and Nielsen BookScan figures showed it as the fifth-bestselling novel in India that year, with more than 48,000 copies sold. Fifty million Indians have read Kane and Abel, he liked to say. In America, two to three hundred might turn up for a talk and book-signing in India its two to three thousand. He was struck by how young those crowds were. Of the 1,000 people who came to hear him in Bangalore in 2013, he said, 80 per cent were under 20. After travelling through the country and reading writers such as R K Narayan and Vikram Seth, eventually, India worked its way into his fiction. Six chapters of Cometh the Hour 2016 are set in Bombay. Indian readers were stoked to get their own cover featuring the Gateway of India. His 2010 anthology, Thereby Hangs a Tale, includes a story about a Delhi couple who fall in love at a traffic signal. Fans were hoping that Archer would also write a sprawling novel set in India, but Archer dashed down the possibility. I just dont have the knowledge, he said in 2013. I will be foolish to write about something I do not understand. While he enjoyed India and its people, he also had his moments of frustration, piracy being a sore point. In 2016, he said he found a street vendor selling a copy of Agatha Christies Passenger to Frankfurt under his name. He also accused Bollywood producers of stealing his plots, saying Rakesh Roshans Khudgarz borrowed from Kane and Abel, and Yash Raj Films Ladies vs Ricky Bahl from Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less. They should, of course, contact my agent, he said. A life stranger than fiction Jeffrey Howard Archer was born in London on April 15, 1940. His father, William, was 64 at his birth and died when Jeffrey was a teenager. Archer later claimed his father had been a colonel in the Somerset Light Infantry. In a 1988 unauthorised biography, In for a Penny, Jonathan Mantle writes that the regiment found no connection. Archer went to Wellington School in Somerset and then to Oxford for a one-year diploma in education where he won an athletics Blue, running the 100 yards in 9.6 seconds for Britain in 1966. Archers political career began in 1966 when he was elected to the Greater London Council. In 1969, at the age of 29, he became the Conservative member of Parliament for Louth. However, in a rags-to-riches-and-back-to-rags story, a disastrous investment in a Canadian company, Aquablast, left him deep in debt, and he left the Commons in 1974. To pay what he owed, he wrote Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less 1976, about four men swindled in a share scam who set out to win their money back. Kane and Abel followed in 1979, and there was no looking back. His newfound popularity reopened doors and brought him back into politics. Margaret Thatcher made him deputy chairman of the Conservative Party in 1985. However, he resigned in 1986 after a newspaper reported that an associate had paid money to a sex worker. Later,he sued the Daily Star over the allegations and won 500,000 in damages. He was made a life peer in 1992, and in 1999 he became the Conservative candidate for Mayor of London. However, again, he had to withdraw after a former friend revealed that Archer had asked him to provide a false alibi for the 1987 trial. He was convicted of perjury and, in 2001, sentenced to four years. His Prison Diaries He spent less than a month in Belmarsh, a high-security prison in London, before moving to Wayland in Norfolk and then North Sea Camp in Lincolnshire, before beingreleased in 2003. Writing 2,000 to 3,000 words a day in his cell, he produced A Prison Diary in three volumes Hell, Purgatory and Heaven. His first night at Wayland left him, he wrote, as low as I did during my first night at Belmarsh. I thought I had escaped from hell. So much for purgatory. After being released, he was as prolific as ever. The seven-volume Clifton Chronicles 201116 was, he said, pretty autobiographical A lot of me in Harry, my wife is Emma, my mother is Maisie. The William Warwick detective series came next. He retired from the House of Lords in 2024. Adam and Eve, about an earls daughter and a shepherds son both born on Armistice Day 1918, was always meant to be his last novel. He was signing copies for readers in London the day before he died. His detractors dismissed his prose as workmanlike, and Archer never claimed otherwise. I am not a writer, he said in Pune. I am a storyteller. I try to make people turn pages about what will happen next. Asked in 2013 what kept him going, he said The fear of stopping. I cant stop. He is survived by his wife of 60 years, Dame Mary Archer, a chemist who chaired Cambridge University Hospitals and the Science Museum Group their sons, William and James and five grandchildren. On one visit to Mumbai, a boy selling pirated books on the street asked him whether he wanted the latest Jeffrey Archer. Archer told him he was the latest Jeffrey Archer.

articleTitle: Green coffee sold with unproven weight-loss claims, CCPA imposes Rs 1 lakh penalty
articleFeaturedImageAlt: green coffee weight loss benefits CCPA
description: The CCPA found a company guilty of misleading advertising after it failed to provide conclusive scientific evidence supporting its green coffee extract’s weight-loss and health claims.
body_raw: The Central Consumer Protection Authority CCPA recently ordered a health and wellness company to pay Rs 1 lakh penalty for falsely advertising and claiming that its green coffee extract products help with weight loss, blood sugar management, and detoxification. The ruling further directed the company to immediately remove the advertisement from all electronic and print media. Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra were hearing a complaint filed by a consumer group alleging that certain green coffee extract products were being sold by the company as scientifically unproven weight-loss dietary supplements, which were available in many forms, such as capsules and powder. By marketing catchphrases such as helps improve insulin function which assists in blood sugar management and detoxification, the opposite party the company has falsely described the products natural attributes and intentionally exaggerated its material characteristics. This deceptive marketing strategy was engineered to exploit consumer vulnerabilities, lure undiscerning buyers through misleading representations, and distort market choices under the false pretense of wellness, the October 5 order read. In the complaint, the complainant alleged that the markets were flooded with green coffee extract products both online and offline with misleading advertisements promising weight loss. Further, it also claimed that the research carried out so far did not give any evidence-based conclusion on the positive correlation between green coffee extract and weight reduction. The CCPA sought views of the Ministry of AYUSH in the case. According to the ministry, green coffee extract products were not mentioned in any of the authoritative books of Ayurveda, Siddha, and Unani as listed in the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The CCPA also noted that the advertisements published by the company on e-commerce platforms claimed without any proof that their products help improve insulin function, which assists in blood sugar management and detoxification. After conducting an initial inquiry into the case, the CCPA noted that the company was selling the green coffee product as a scientifically unproven weight loss dietary supplement in the form of capsules, powder, etc. However, no essence or quality of coffee was mentioned, but just weight-loss management under the name of green was advertised. Subsequently, the consumer authority came to the conclusion that a prima facie case was made out for a show cause notice to be sent to the company. In the reply to the show cause notice, the company contended that there were scientific studies conducted by research organisations where it has been proved that green coffee beans helped in weight loss, blood sugar management, and improved metabolic functions and that they had established an internal ethics and compliance committee to ensure that their advertising practices met the highest standards of ethics and compliance. Investigation The CCPA then referred the case for detailed investigation, as per which it was found that the company, which was earlier selling green coffee bean powder with misleading and exaggerated claims, continues to sell the product with identical claims on various e-commerce platforms. The report stated that the claims of the company were misleading, for which the company had not provided any independent scientific studies or clinical trial data conducted as evidence. The report observed that the research papers submitted by the company were not directly comparable to the product, as the conclusions drawn from those studies were inconclusive in nature and did not establish a clear correlation with the specific dosage or intended use of the product. The report concluded that the company was violating the Consumer Protection Act because its advertisements falsely described the product and exaggerated its characteristics to mislead and lure consumers under the labels of green, healthy, and weight loss supplements. On inquiry, the company also informed the authority that a total of 3,318 units of the product had been sold to date, and the total sale value of the product was Rs 6.54 lakh. Valid license Advocate Pratyush Kumar Yadav, appearing for the company, submitted that the company held a valid license issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India FSSAI for the manufacturesale of the product and that the ingredients used in the product were covered under the Nutraceutical Regulations. The counsel contended that the product was a nutraceutical supplement which provided nutritional and health benefits and was available in tablet form. The CCPA was further informed that the recommended dosage of the product was one tablet per day. The counsel urged that the production of the product was stopped in 2025 and the company had already begun communication with e-commerce websites for delisting of the said product. Notify me The CCPA observed that the research papers relied upon by the company cannot be seen as conclusive scientific evidence that supports the alleged weight-management benefits of the product because the studies themselves acknowledge that, owing to the limited number of available studies and the small sample sizes, the efficacy of green coffee extract could not be conclusively established. According to the authority, despite discontinuing the manufacturing of the product in 2025, the company persists in profiteering by maintaining active digital listings on e-commerce platforms and utilised the interactive notify me interfaces to sustain consumer engagement and indulged in unfair trade practice.

articleTitle: CBI probe order against Mann’s aide: Punjab takes fight to Supreme Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjab CBI probe HC order Bhagwant Mann OSD
description: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the CBI to probe Enforcement Directorate allegations against people linked to Bhagwant Mann’s office.
body_raw: The Punjab government has moved the Supreme Court challenging the Punjab and Haryana High Courts October 5 order directing the CBI to register a case and investigate allegations made by the Enforcement Directorate ED against people linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns office. The state filed a special leave petition SLP against the high court order at 1.42 am on Tuesday. The matter is now expected to come up before the Supreme Court. We are waiting for the petition to be admitted, a government functionary said, confirming the development. The high court had on Monday directed the CBI to conduct a fair and transparent investigation into allegations contained in an ED communication to the Punjab director general of police DGP and submit its report within two months. The case is scheduled to come up before the high court on December 7. The ED had sought registration of a case against Manns Officer on Special Duty Rajbir Singh Ghuman and his alleged associates Nitin Gohal and Bir Devinder. What the ED alleged In its communication to the DGP under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act on July 30, the ED sought registration of a criminal case on the basis of material allegedly indicating cash-for-transfers and postings, influence over government policies and tenders, leakage of confidential government documents and other favours. According to the allegations cited by the ED, Ghuman, Gohal and Devinder had allegedly interfered in transfers and postings of government officials, government work and tender processes. The agency had also referred to material purportedly indicating attempts to influence postings, access confidential government documents, and interfere in administrative approvals and other official processes. What the high court said The high court order came on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, based on the ED communication sent to the DGP. The court noted that the communication was received in the DGPs office on August 3 and was marked to the Punjab Bureau of Investigation, but no FIR had been registered even after two months. While directing the CBI to register a case, the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor said the allegations would have to be tested during investigation and trial. Prima facie allegations with regard to scams including cash for transfers cash for getting favourable policies cash for tenders, and such other illegal activities corruption in high public offices have been substantiated by the ED with reference to various WhatsApp chats and other information, the bench had observed. The court, however, made it clear that it was not expressing any final view on the allegations. Merits of the allegation can only be gone into at the stage of investigationtrial and we are not required to express any definite opinion on it, it said. The bench had further held that the material supplied by the ED was not merely an expression of its opinion but was supported by material on the basis of which the agency had formed its view about possible violations of law.

articleTitle: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026: How Uruguay beat Spain and Portugal to top spot
articleFeaturedImageAlt: travel
description: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026 list: Know more about the world's 10 best countries for retirees seeking financial security, superior healthcare, and an exceptional lifestyle.
body_raw: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026 Uruguay has been named the best country in the world for retirees, taking the No. 1 spot in the annual Global Retirement Report and Index 2026 published by Global Citizen Solutions. The overall rankings are derived from a composite score calculated across five weighted pillars quality of life, mobility and citizenship, tax, cost and investment, and administrative procedure, including processing speed and family inclusion. With a near-perfect score of 99.90, Uruguay emerged as the worlds premier retirement destination and was one of only two top-10 nations to score at least 75 in every evaluation category. Mauritius, Spain, and Costa Rica were ranked at No. 2, 3, and 4, respectively. Portugal, Paraguay, and Latvia were ranked at No. 5, 6, and 7, respectively. Andorra and Italy were ranked 8th and 9th, respectively, while Greece closed out the top 10 list. A primary driver behind Uruguays top ranking is its streamlined immigration and naturalisation pathway. Eligible applicants can apply directly for citizenship without completing a prior temporary residency period. The index also highlights Uruguays manageable monthly income requirement of 1,700, along with short routes to naturalisation three years for married applicants and five years for single applicants. According to the report, the modern concept of retirement has shifted away from simply withdrawing from active life. Patricia Casaburi, CEO of Global Citizen Solutions, noted that the concept of retirement has changed over the years. Earlier, retirement was closely tied to withdrawing from active life. But lately, retirement has become a deliberate new chapter. Casaburi added that retirement involves more than safety. Quality of life after retirement also has to be healthier, lighter in taxes, and richer in possibility than the life left behind, Casaburi said. Rank Country 1. Uruguay 2. Mauritius 3. Spain 4. articleTitle: Harmanpreet Kaur’s real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur's last act as India captain was leading the side to their second consecutive Asian Games gold medal. (BCCI Photo)
description: Before her, India reached two ODI World Cup finals. Under her, semifinals and finals became regular, and the 2025 title came at home
body_raw: Harmanpreet Kaur ran back to complete the catch that sealed Indias 2025 ODI World Cup triumph. The captain who had carried Indian womens cricket through expectation was there at the finish. But her legacy is bigger than that trophy. Harmanpreet leaves captaincy having changed what India expects from itself. Before her, India had reached the ODI World Cup final in 2005 and 2017 under Mithali Raj. Under Harmanpreet, India became regulars at the business end of tournaments the 2018 T20 World Cup semifinal, the 2020 T20 World Cup final, the 2023 T20 World Cup semifinal and, eventually, the 2025 ODI World Cup title at home. Her biggest contribution was renewed belief. Semifinals and finals were no longer a flash-in-the-pan moment. India started to feel like they belonged there. She took over when Indian womens cricket was growing, but was still searching for consistency and belief. At the 2018 T20 World Cup, her first major tournament as captain, she announced herself with a 103 against New Zealand. It was a statement of the captain she would be aggressive, unafraid of the big stage. That intensity stayed with her. Harmanpreet was emotional, vocal and sometimes combative. Players were coming in with bigger ambitions, and her job was to build a team that believed it could compete at the highest level. Her batting, however, became less consistent as the years went by. Her strike rate was a concern. The Harmanpreet who could win a match from anywhere showed up less often. But she still produced when India needed her. In the 2025 World Cup semifinal against Australia, with India chasing a record total, Harmanpreet made 89 and helped keep the chase alive alongside Jemimah Rodrigues. A year later, in a must-win T20 World Cup game against Australia, she made 56 off 27, hitting three sixes in the final over to take India to a competitive total. Those innings offered reminders of the player India will want to see more often. In her farewell post, Harmanpreet acknowledged the cost of captaincy herself. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first, she wrote. There were difficult days too defeats, criticism, questions over her decisions. She faced them as openly as she celebrated the wins. I gave this team everything I had, she wrote. I carried the responsibility with pride. She said every difficult decision was made with one intention to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves. She leaves behind a team in which Smriti Mandhana has become the batting leader, Deepti Sharma a central figure, and younger players such as N Sree Charani have emerged with confidence. It is a team that has won a World Cup and now knows what it feels like to be there. Harmanpreet wrote that she leaves captaincy with a heart full of emotions, but also with PEACE because she believes the team is in a good place. It is a team with talent, character, belief and a future that she is excited to be part of. Her post ends Now, Im ready to play for the love of the game again. That is what Indian cricket will hope for. Without the burden of captaincy, Harmanpreet can focus on being the batter who can change a game. At 37, the hope is that giving up the captaincy brings back more of her best batting. India have a home global event, the Womens Champions Trophy, in February next year, before bigger challenges in 2028 and 2029. She says she has done her duty. She leaves the next captain with more than a World Cup trophy a team that believes it can compete on the biggest stages. Captaincy ends. The journey continues, Harmanpreet wrote. For Indian cricket, the hope is that the next chapter brings back the player who made everyone believe.

articleTitle: Ban defied: Karnataka IAS officer seeks police explanation over idol immersion
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka Hassan Ganesh idol immersion row
description: Hassan Deputy Commissioner K S Lathakumari issued a notice to SP Shubhanwita for failing to prevent Ganesh idol immersions in Devigere Tank despite prohibitory orders.
body_raw: The deputy commissioner of Hassan district in Karnataka issued a notice to the superintendent of police Sunday, seeking an explanation for why Ganesh and Gowri idols were allowed to be immersed in Devigere Tank, a prominent water body, despite a district administration ban. Acting on requests from the Hassan Municipal Corporation commissioner and the tahsildar, Deputy Commissioner K S Lathakumari, an IAS officer, Saturday banned immersions in the tank, which falls under the Muzrai Department that manages temples in the state, to prevent water contamination from chemical paints, flowers, fruits, and puja materials. The prohibition order was issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS and Section 24 of the Water Prevention and Control of Pollution Act. Despite the ban, major public Ganesh festival organisers held massive processions led by the main town pandal. They immersed the idols in Devigere Tank near the Neerubagilu Anjaneya temple Saturday. DC Lathakumari asked SP Shubhanwita why the matter should not be referred to the competent authority for disciplinary action over alleged dereliction of duty and negligence unbecoming of a government servant. The notice highlighted that although police were empowered to book violators, no FIRs were registered and no action was taken against the organisers. The notice asked SP Shubhanwita to respond in writing immediately, failing which it will be presumed she has no explanation to offer. Copies of the notice were forwarded to the minister-in-charge of the district, the chief secretary, the regional commissioner Mysuru, and the inspector general of police southern range. Addressing the issue on Tuesday, DC Lathakumari said, There is nothing personal in the issue. Since Devigere Tank was polluted, such prohibitory orders were issued after consulting the SP as well. If some untoward incident had taken place, the district administration would have been held responsible. I was also unhappy that plaster of Paris PoP and non-eco-friendly Ganesh idols were also immersed in Devigere. JDS MLA back police officer While SP Shubhanwita was unavailable for comment, a police officer attributed the lapse to the last-minute arrival of the prohibition order. The orders were issued on Saturday morning when the massive procession had already begun. The organisers had obtained permission providing their route map and immersion place. At the last minute, it was impossible to change it, the police officer said. Hassan MLA H P Swaroop Prakash of the Janata Dal Secular backed the SP, pointing out that the pandal committee has immersed its idols in Devigere Tank for six to seven decades. The DC has threatened to initiate legal action against those who have immersed Ganesh idols in Devigere. We will have to stage a protest against the DC. We learned of the order only after the procession had begun. If the district administration is not coordinating with district agencies properly, it will be a problem, Prakash told reporters. The dispute comes weeks before the annual Hasanamba temple fair, scheduled between October 30 and November 10, which is expected to draw at least 20 lakh devotees to the district.

articleTitle: 25 years, three times the cost: Versova-Yari Road bridge gets a December 2027 deadline
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Versova-Yari Road bridge
description: The 206-metre bridge over Kavthe creek, conceptualised in 2002 at Rs 16 crore and now pegged at Rs 48 crore, will cut a 30-minute detour between Lokhandwala and Andheri back road to under 10
body_raw: The Versova-Yari road bridge - one of suburban Mumbais much-awaited infrastructure projects is set to see the light of day in December 2027, 25 years after it was conceptualized. The 206-meter-long bridge is set to connect Lokhandwala with Andheri back road, passing over the Kavthe creek at Andheri West. At present, there is no direct connectivity between these two places, and the travel time between these two places takes 30 minutes. Meanwhile, once operational, the travel time is set to drop below 10 mins. Earlier on Monday, a team of Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation BMC officials led by Abhijit Bangar - additional municipal commissioner Projects carried out a site inspection. Following this, the private agency executing the work was told to complete the work by December next year. At present the work of erecting the pillars and columns is underway. The bridge will pass above the creek establishing a direct east-west connection between Yari Road, Panch Marg and Versova in Andheri West, an official told the Indian Express. The bridge will be Y-shaped, while the main structure will feature a 110-metre-long single-span steel basket handle arch structure. Tension rods will connect the steel arch to the bridge deck slab. The cost of this bridge has been pegged at Rs 48 crore. Initially the cost of this project was pegged at round Rs 16 crore. However, with the delay, the project saw a massive cost escalation. In 2019, members from a local housing society filed a petition with the Supreme Court stating that this project would affect mangroves therefore, it needs to be scrapped. They have also stated that the proposed alignment of this bridge was flawed. Later in August 2022, the SC quashed the stay. Following this, the project came back on track. Civic officials said that they had to acquire a slew of permissions from the forest and mangrove departments before they could go ahead with the work. As a result, the issuance of permission took more than three years, and the work could have begun last year.

articleTitle: C Raja Mohan: In Iran war, US midterm elections are the new front
articleFeaturedImageAlt: iran war, us midterms
description: For both Tehran and the White House, managing the home front can matter as much as gaining on the battlefield
body_raw: Irans Revolutionary Guards have found a new audience for their war with Donald Trump The American voter. The history of warfare tells us that weakening the adversarys domestic support can be as important as defeating its armed forces on the battlefield. In a 25-page letter last week, the Guards appealed to the honourable people of the United States to reject Trumps policies and consider peaceful coexistence with Iran. Trump, in turn, hopes that escalating military and economic pressure will force the Islamic Republic to fall in line. Coming just weeks before the midterm elections, the letter brings Tehran directly into Americas domestic political contest. With Republicans vulnerable in November, the political consequences of the Iran war are becoming harder to separate from its military course. In Tehran, too, internal struggles between advocates of negotiation and hardliners favouring confrontation are shaping the wars conduct. That brings us to the idea of the October surprise in American politics - a major event or political move that changes the national mood before the traditional voting in the first week of November. Iran helped make the phrase part of American political language during the 1980 presidential election. The Iranian Revolution of February 1979 overthrew the Shah, a close American ally. In November, militants seized the US embassy in Tehran and took its staff hostage. The crisis haunted President Jimmy Carters re-election campaign. His Republican challenger, Ronald Reagan, feared that freeing the hostages before November would rescue Carters political fortunes. Allegations that Reagans team secretly worked to delay the release remain disputed. The hostages came home as Reagan took office in January 1981. Irans upheaval had become entangled with the struggle for power in Washington. Today, Tehran hopes to exploit another American electoral moment. Trump insists the midterms do not determine his Iran policy. But the electoral calendar is now visibly intertwined with the military debate. In an interview last week, Trump said it was possible that US bombing of Iran could intensify after the November 3 elections. He has also said the war could be won right after the election - or perhaps before it. The military preparations reinforce the message. The unfolding deployment gives Trump more options if diplomacy fails - and gives Tehran reason to take his threats seriously. Setting aside the Islamic Revolutions enduring slogan, Death to America, the IRGC letter claims to have no quarrel with ordinary Americans. Its immediate target is Trump. It hopes public anxiety over the war and rising prices will weaken Republicans and create space for a more accommodating policy in Washington. The appeal could easily backfire as Republicans accuse Democrats of serving Tehrans interests. Iran is not alone in trying to exploit domestic divisions. Trump has hoped that military and economic pressure would encourage Iranians to challenge their rulers. That expectation has produced little so far. Tehrans appeal to American voters may prove equally ineffective. Both sides nevertheless see the adversarys home front as a battlefield. Meanwhile, Trump has secured an important gain at Hormuz. The recovery in Gulf oil flows has accelerated. New data show Gulf crude exports averaged about 16.3 million barrels a day in September - roughly 91 per cent of pre-war levels. This does not establish Trumps claim of total control. Iran never enjoyed uncontested sovereignty over the international waterway. Its leverage lay in making passage dangerous and expensive. Tanker attacks, higher insurance costs and uncertainty forced its adversaries to spend heavily on keeping commerce moving. Nor has the energy crisis disappeared. The problem has shifted from crude supply towards logistics and refining. Refined-product exports from the Gulf recovered to only about 60 per cent of pre-war levels in September. That distinction matters politically. More crude moving through Hormuz does not automatically mean cheaper diesel at American pumps. Crude must be transported, refined and distributed. Diesel prices have a direct effect on inflation and cost of living, a major issue in US domestic politics right now. The G7s decision, under Trumps pressure, to release 100 million barrels of crude and fuel products from emergency reserves is meant to ease this pressure. But Trumps dilemma remains. Convincing Tehran that it cannot wait him out requires a credible threat of escalation. Reassuring American voters requires avoiding an escalation that sends fuel prices soaring again. Irans letter seeks to exploit precisely that tension. Tehran faces pressures of its own. Washingtons Operation Economic Outcast is tightening the financial noose. The US has expanded sanctions from military procurement networks to Irans automotive, rail, manufacturing and steel sectors. Washington has now warned foreign financial institutions that doing business with Iran could bring sanctions without prior notice. Neither side can assume the other will crack first. The October surprise could be another military blow, a diplomatic opening, or another fuel-price shock. For India, there is a larger lesson from the US and Iranian efforts to influence each others domestic politics. Americas hopes of political change in Iran and Tehrans appeal to American voters underline an old truth Wars are fought within societies as much as between states. Managing the home front can matter as much as gaining military ground on the battlefield. The principle applies in peacetime too, especially to democracies such as India. Effective engagement with a turbulent world demands cohesion at home. Political differences are inevitable in a democracy. But a politics of winner takes all can turn those differences into debilitating domestic conflicts. That inevitably weakens the nations capacity to deal with mounting challenges abroad and the growing prospects for external meddling in its domestic affairs. The writer is contributing editor on international affairs for The Indian Express. He is professor and director at the Motwani Jadeja Institute of American Studies, Jindal Global University, Delhi

articleTitle: More wait for Sewri-Worli connector as deadline pushed to May 2027

description: The Sewri Worli is a 4.5km connector between the Coastal Road at Worli and the Atal Setu at Sewri, improving east-west connectivity in the city
body_raw: The wait for the east-west Sewri-Worli connector, linking Coastal Road and Atal Setu, is getting longer as the Maharashtra government has pushed the completion deadline to May 31, 2027, informed Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis during a meeting on various infrastructure projects. An MMRDA senior official confirmed the development, adding that the height of the bridge piers and the double-decker corridor have added to the construction challenges in launching girders, with traffic flowing on the road below. The Sewri Worli is a 4.5km connector between the Coastal Road at Worli and the Atal Setu at Sewri, improving east-west connectivity in the city. Over the railway tracks at Prabhadevi and Parel stations, the bridge doubles to replace the local Elphinstone bridge for traffic going over the railway tracks. Shut since September 2025, the project was supposed to be completed by September 2026. But the deadline was extended because a lot of work on the connector still remains. Currently, officials of MahaRail - which is constructing the portion of the bridge over the railway tracks - are preparing for the launch of girders over the tracks in November. This involves the assembly of the prefabricated girders on site before they can fit into place. Each of the xx girders is 132 meters long. MRIDC dismantled the 112-year-old bridge in April, a month later than scheduled. articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | How should you read Maharashtra’s drought?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | How should you read Maharashtra's drought UPSC IAS, UPSC CSE, UPSC 2027
description: Maharashtra has declared drought in 265 of its 358 talukas amid an 18% rainfall deficit and prolonged dry spells across large parts of the state. What is drought, and how is it classified in India? Which parts of Maharashtra are most drought prone? Also go beyond the nugget to understand how a drought is declared in India.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on Drought. Knowledge Nugget Drought Subject Geography, Disaster Management Why in the news? On September 26, the Maharashtra government declared a drought in 265 out of the states 358 talukas, across its 36 districts, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis terming the crisis the worst the state has endured since 1972. Key takeaways 1. With no rainfall in over 20 days during the crucial kharif crop season and the Southwest monsoon receding, the crisis is expected to worsen in the summer months next year. 2. The Maharashtra government has directed all municipal corporations, municipalities, and gram panchayats to impose a minimum 10 percent water cut from October 16, citing water storage, drought-like conditions, and the possibility of El Nino-related water stress extending into next year. 3. From June 1 to September 26, Maharashtra has received 798.2 mm of rainfall against a normal 970.9 mm, a deficit of 18. 4. According to the India Meteorological Department IMD, 31 of 36 districts in Maharashtra are rain-deficient, with 20 of these facing a deficit of 25 to 58 per cent. 5. Beyond the deficit, shifting rain patterns have added to the damage in more than 100 of the states 355 drought-hit talukas, gaps between rain spells have stretched to 4060 days. 6. As a result, the main kharif crop, sown across 147 lakh hectares, has withered. Maharashtras agriculture is largely rain-fed its irrigation potential, at under 20 per cent, is much lower than in states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. What is drought? -Drought is a rainfall scarce period, affecting the availability of water for irrigation, drinking etc. -Ministry of Agriculture is the nodal Ministry in respect of monitoring and managing drought conditions. It classifies droughts into meteorological droughts, hydrological droughts and agricultural droughts. -Meteorological drought is classified based on rainfall deficiency w.r.t. long term average-25 or less is normal, 26-50 is moderate and more than 50 is severe. It is usually the starting point of drought conditions, indicated by prolonged dry spells. -Hydrological drought is best defined as deficiencies in surface and sub-surface water supplies leading to a lack of water for normal and specific needs. -Such conditions arise even in times of average or above average precipitation when increased usage of water diminishes the reserves. It can develop after prolonged rainfall deficiency or excessive withdrawals. -Agricultural drought is identified by 4 consecutive weeks of meteorological drought. Scarcity of water and inadequate soil moisture for normal crop growth starts affecting agricultural production. Which regions in Maharashtra are prone to drought and why? 7. Marathwada and Vidarbha, the two rain-shadow regions of the state which traditionally are drought-prone, have received very little rainfall. 8. Marathwada is particularly affected, having received 38 less rainfall than normal, while Vidarbha has a 27 deficiency. 9. The big deficit is in seven districts - Solapur, Dharashiv, Latur, Hingoli, Jalna, Beed and parts of Nanded, which are away from Godavari river - where rainfall has been just around 50 of normal. Except Solapur, all these districts fall in Marathwada region. 10. Vidarbha region is a little less affected, while western Maharashtra, which is the sugarcane and onion producing zone, is in a relatively comfortable position. Nashik district, known for onion production, has received 37 excess rainfall till now. 11. In Vidarbha, the average deficit across 11 districts is 27, with the shortfall ranging from 26 in Yavatmal to 42 in Amravati. Did you know? - A drought year is especially hard on the women. While most of them work on fields along with the men of the household, their days start much before daybreak, usually around 4 am - a relentless cycle of cooking, cleaning, tending to the children and livestock, besides spending backbreaking hours on the land they till but dont own. What are the relief measures undertaken by the Maharashtra government? 12. The declaration, under the Drought Management Code, 2016, will trigger crop-loss surveys and a package of immediate concessions, including waiver of land revenue, restructuring of crop loans, a stay on recovery of agriculture-related loans and relaxation of Viksit BharatGuarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin VBG RAM G norms. 13. The government has also provided for concessions on electricity bills for agricultural pumps, with bills for pumps up to 7.5 HP already waived and concessions to apply to pumps above that capacity. 14. Financial assistance for crop losses will be decided separately after the assessment is completed, government officials said. 15. For farmers and rural households, the immediate relief measures announced with the drought declaration include a waiver of land revenue, restructuring of crop loans and a stay on recovery of agriculture-related loans. 16. Other measures include a waiver of examination fees for school and college students, deployment of tankers for drinking water wherever required, no disconnection of electricity supply to agricultural pumps in villages declared to be facing shortages, and arrangements for foodgrains and fodder. 17. The government has also directed authorities to plan drinking water and livestock water supply and undertake water conservation works in affected areas. The measures are intended to provide immediate relief while the crop-loss assessment is carried out. 18. The extent of compensation to individual farmers will depend on the findings of the surveys and the separate government order to be issued on crop damage assistance. BEYOND THE NUGGET How is a drought declared? 1. Under the National Disaster Response Fund NDRF rules, drought declaration for kharif the monsoon cropping season, which runs from June to October requires an assessment that can begin from October 5, once the monsoon starts to withdraw. 2. For rabi, the winter cropping season from October to April, assessment can be held in March 2027. 3. There is no single definition of drought accepted across India. States have the authority to declare a drought based on local conditions. 4. But the state governments report should conform to parameters specified under NDRF norms, and disaster relief funds can be unlocked by the Centre. 5. Under NDRF rules, drought declaration is based on crop loss, the moisture adequacy index used to assess soil health, and rainfall deficit, along with decline in food production and labour migration in search of work. 6. Sowing must fall below 50 per cent of total cultivable kharifrabi area, drinking water shortage must be severe, groundwater tables must be shrinking, there must be fodder shortage, and rainfall deficit must be up to 70 per cent. Rainfall deficiency is the sole criterion for declaring drought. 3. Crop conditions, soil moisture and socio-economic indicators can also be considered in drought assessment. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 and 3 only b 1 only c 2 and 3 only d 1, 2 and 3 Answer a Sources Maharashtra is parched, but heres why drought cant be declared before October, Maharashtra declares drought in 75 of state amid rainfall deficit,Three kinds of drought, Behind Maharashtra drought crisis, sharp regional variation in rainfall Click here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026.
