articleTitle: Rahul’s impromptu move, Priyanka’s negotiation skills: The INDIA march twist
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi climbs atop the barricades during the INDIA bloc MPs' march from Parliament to the ECI, demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha)
description: Congress leaders have credited the Gandhis with derailing the police plan to end the protest.
body_raw: The INDIA bloc protest against the Election Commission took a surprise turn on Tuesday, thanks to Rahul Gandhi and his sister and Wayanad MP, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.Opposition MPs were detained and pushed into buses to different police stations in Delhi. The protest was all but over when the siblings pulled off an impromptu move that even left Congress leaders confused. India News Live UpdatesRahul Gandhi, Priyankas sit-in at Doordarshan office in face-off with cops Priyanka was already seated in one of the buses, parked outside the Akashvani Bhavan, the headquarters of All India Radio, and Rahul was about to get in. Suddenly, the siblings looked at each other, and then walked past the cops and into the Akashvani Bhavan premises. The move was off the script and the police personnel initially did not know how to react. Once the Gandhis went inside, Congress leaders KC Venugopal and Pawan Khera climbed the boundary wall of Akashvani Bhavan and started raising slogans. Congress leaders Imran Pratapgarhi and Srinivas BV joined them. Most Congress leaders said they had thought the protest was over. We dont know what happened. This was not part of the plan, one of them said. According to sources in the Congress, Rahul Gandhi planned to enter the Akashvani Bhavan premises and then exit through the back gate, located opposite the Election Commission. All the other routes to the poll panels office were blocked for the rally, so the Leader of the Opposition made this plan on the go, the sources said. Once he entered the Akashvani Bhavan premises, police officers shut the back gate. So he sat here in protest, said a source. Only the two of them know what they had in mind when they walked in, said a Congress MP outside Akashvani Bhawan. At this point, the Congress leaders are still camping on the premises as top security officers talk to them. Personnel from Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force are now stationed outside the Akashvani Bhavan. A police officer said the force inside the premises was to ensure the leaders safety. Congress leaders have credited the Gandhis with derailing the police plan to end the protest. The protest would have been over if they didnt do this. Senior Congress leader Pawan Khera said in a post on X, In the morning, the India Alliance attempted to walk towards the election commission. The police forcibly stopped the MPs. Currently, Leader of Opposition Shri Rahul Gandhi and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra along with several leaders, are sitting on a dharna inside the All India Radio premises which is next to ECI office. The Congress leaders are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of disenfranchising voters through the Special Intensive Revision exercise to give advantage to the ruling BJP. According to highly placed sources in the Congress, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is leading negotiations with the top police officers. Following The Indian Express investigation on the rift within the poll panel, underlining how two Election Commissioners objected on record at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken without their knowledge, the Election Commission acknowledged these notes, but described them as part of the panels decision-making process. However, it did not respond to any of the concerns raised by the two Commissioners, nor did it state whether or how these concerns had been addressed. Opposition leaders detained Earlier, top Opposition leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Trinamool Congress MPs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, were detained as police stopped the march to the Election Commission office. The protesting MPs were taken away in buses. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge said the opposition would continue its protest to protect voting rights and democracy. This protest will continue. We are doing this to protect your vote and your freedom. The people of the country are saying that many of their votes have been deleted and vote theft is taking place, and we are fighting and will continue to fight for their protection, he said. BJP takes a swipe Criticising the Opposition march to the Election Commission to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation, the BJP said this was yet another attempt by the Congress and its allies to create anarchy and relaunch Rahul Gandhi. Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the Opposition leaders are venting their frustration over electoral defeats by levelling baseless allegations. Friends in the opposition, the very system you are questioning is the one under which you won in Kerala. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Karnataka. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Himachal. Was that victory illegitimate? Opposition governments were formed in Punjab and Jharkhand were those victories illegitimate? the senior BJP leader asked. If you question constitutional institutions, you will commit the sin of plunging the country into the fires of anarchy. Do not commit the sin of plunging the nation into unrest and anarchy. The country and its people will never forgive you, he added. Addressing the media at the BJP headquarters, party spokesperson Sambit Patra said, The Congress has been repeatedly trying to launch and re-launch Rahul Gandhi by any means necessary. When, despite numerous attempts, he failed to gain traction, the Congress and some of its allies decided that even if it meant resorting to anarchy and undermining the nations democracy, they would launch Rahul Gandhi politically at any cost. As part of these efforts, they attacked the Indian army from time to time, the Supreme Court, Hindus, and EVMs Electronic Voting Machines. And for the last few weeks, they have been attacking the Election Commission, Patra said.

articleTitle: IIT Ropar launches app to help children learn about plants, crops and agriculture
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The app is designed to introduce agricultural knowledge before children formally study agriculture as a subject
description: The platform is described as free, ad-free and privacy-focused, with a child-focused design aimed at keeping the digital learning environment safe and age-appropriate.
body_raw: IIT Ropars Centre of Excellence in AI for Digital Agriculture, ANNAM.AI, has launched AVNI-Grow with Nature digital learning platform designed to help children learn about plants, crops, food and agriculture through their surroundings. The web and mobile app uses artificial intelligence AI along with hands-on activities to help children identify and understand what they see around them. The platform allows children to explore crops, fruits, vegetables, spices, cereals and millets. For example, a child can use the app while looking at a plant, fruit or crop and learn more about it through AI-powered identification. The idea is to connect what children see in everyday life with basic knowledge about agriculture and food. AVNI developed by the team at IIT Ropar, is available in Hindi and English and also provides audio content for younger children. It includes daily challenges, a digital Nature Book, a Nature Gallery and a Crop Compare feature. These tools allow children to record what they learn, explore different plants and compare crops as part of their learning. The app is designed to introduce agricultural knowledge before children formally study agriculture as a subject, IIT-R said in a statement. A plant in a school garden, a fruit at home or a crop in a nearby field can become a starting point for learning about how food is grown and where it comes from. Also Read IIT Ropar announces scholarship for underprivileged students, lays foundation stone of yogic sciences centre The platform also places emphasis on learning through observation rather than only reading information. Children can explore their surroundings, identify plants and crops and gradually build a basic understanding of agriculture and nature. AVNI has been developed by Dr Mukesh Saini, Co-project Director of ANNAM.AI, IIT Ropar. The initiative is part of ANNAM.AIs work on the use of AI in agriculture and education. The platform, as per the institute is free to access, ad-free and privacy-focused, with a child-focused design aimed at keeping the digital learning environment safe and age-appropriate. ANNAM.AI is working on AI-based digital public infrastructure for Indian agriculture. AVNI extends this work into education by using AI not just to provide information but to help children learn about agriculture through direct observation and exploration. The initiative is aimed at building agricultural awareness among children at an early age, including an understanding of the plants they see, the food they eat and the role agriculture plays in producing it.

articleTitle: Swatantra Bhardwaj gets regular bail in Jantar Mantar assault case

body_raw: A Delhi court Tuesday granted self-styled influencer Swatantra Bharadwaj regular bail in a case where he allegedly attacked the father of a student protester who had participated in the Cockroach Janta Party CJP protest in July. Additional Sessions Judge ASJ Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler of the Patiala House Court had earlier granted Bharadwaj interim bail for three weeks. ASJ Laler had then said that it would observe his conduct before considering his plea for regular bail. A detailed regular bail order is awaited. In its order granting Bharadwaj interim bail, ASJ Laler had said, Weighing all circumstances, the Court takes into account that the applicant has been in custody for a little over 10 days. a period that should have afforded him time for reflection. The case Bharadwaj had purportedly admitted to attacking the father of the student protester at Jantar Mantar in a video. He was picked up by the Crime Branch officers from his house in Bulandshahr on September 4 and brought to Delhi after securing a transit remand. On September 4, relevant sections pertaining to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989 SCST Act, were added to an earlier FIR registered against Bharadwaj over the alleged attack, amid a protest by CJP supporters and the Indian Youth Congress, as well as Lok Sabha MPs Chandra Shekhar alias Azad and Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav. The same day, another FIR was also registered under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences POCSO Act, 2012, and for criminal intimidation based on the protesters complaint alleging she had received rape threats from Bhardwajs supporters. Bharadwaj had been in judicial custody since September 5 till he was granted interim bail on September 15. While granting interim bail to the accused, the court had also pulled up the police for leaving significant ground uncovered in the investigation. The investigation, as disclosed in the reply, leaves significant ground uncovered. The podcast forms the central basis of the States opposition, and its authenticity is disputed. Yet the reply does not state whether the person who manages the channel has been examined, whether the original footage has been requisitioned, or whether the electronic material has been sent for forensic examination, ASJ Laler had said in the interim bail order.

articleTitle: Allies turned foes? Bombay HC steps into BJP vs Shiv Sena in Ulhasnagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bombay HC ulhasnagar BJP vs Shiv Sena
description: The Mayor, a Sena Corporator, allegedly altered the UMC Commissioner's recommendations, excluding the names of S B Singh and Pradeep Ramchandani – the other BJP nominees.
body_raw: In a setback for the ruling Shiv Sena in the Ulhasnagar Municipal Corporation UMC in Thane district, the Bombay High Court on Monday halted further steps on Mayor Ashwini Kamlesh Nikams decision to recommend only two of four BJP candidates as co-opted or nominated corporators. The Mayor, a Sena Corporator, allegedly altered the UMC Commissioners recommendations, excluding the names of S B Singh and Pradeep Ramchandani-the other BJP nominees. Ramchandani, along with BJP district president Rajesh Vadhrya, had approached the court with pleas challenging the proposed nomination of councillors in the Special General Body Meeting SGBM of the UMC held on October 1, which recommended the names of only two of four BJP candidates while recommending five candidates of the Ulhasnagar Shahar Vikas Aghadi USVA - alliance dominated by the Shiv Sena. Prima facie, there appears to be substance in the contentions of the counsel for the Petitioners on whether the Mayor at all had any authorityjurisdiction under the Maharashtra Municipal Corporations Qualifications and Appointment of Nominated Councillors Rules, 2012, to reject the nominations as made, and place the names of only two candidates out of four as recommended by the Commissioner, a bench of Justices Girish S Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale noted. In the meantime, till the adjourned date of hearing, the Municipal Secretary is restrained from taking any steps to notify andor undertake any publication of the nominated councillors as per the provisions of Rule 6 of the 2012 Rules, the HC noted. Senior advocates Birendra Saraf and Anil Y Sakhare, appearing for the petitioners, argued that while the Municipal Commissioner, under Rule 5 1 of the 2012 Rules, had recommended three USVA candidates, the Mayor placed the names of five USVA candidates before the house and thereafter, hurriedly closed the meeting with the national anthem. The long-standing BJP-Shiv Sena dispute over UMC-nominated corporators had earlier reached the High Court and Supreme Court, which ordered the convening of SGBM for the issue by October 1, after which the Mayor took a decision in question in the present pleas. It should be noted that BJP and Shiv Sena are allies in the state, but not the civic body. On October 5, the petitioners sought urgent ad-interim relief and argued that as per 2012 rules, the Mayor had no power to reject the Commissioners recommended candidates. Finding prima facie substance in petitioners contentions, the bench issued notices to the respondents, directing them to file reply affidavits by October 12.

articleTitle: Gift coupon fraud: Police bust suspected Dubai-linked fake BPO in Bengaluru
articleFeaturedImageAlt: gift coupon fraud
description: The Bengaluru police initially suspected that employees were being trained to commit fraud and that SIM cards registered in other persons’ names were being used to contact and threaten potential victims.
body_raw: The Bengaluru police have detained and questioned six people after a suspected gift coupon fraud operation targeting overseas victims was uncovered on Hennur Main Road, officials said on Tuesday. The police have not identified any victims in India so far. Investigators suspect that the operation was linked to a network being run from Dubai, though the alleged Dubai connection is yet to be established. The Central Crime Branch CCB registered a case on September 26 following a tip-off that an alleged fraudulent operation was being run from a building. The police initially suspected that employees were being trained to commit fraud and that SIM cards registered in other persons names were being used to contact and threaten potential victims. Around 60 to 70 young men and women were working from the premises, which initially led investigators to suspect that it was being used as a call centre to facilitate online fraud. However, the subsequent investigation indicated that the suspected operation was linked to a gift coupon fraud targeting people outside India, the police said. Not everyone was involved. As per our interrogation, only a few people appear to have known about the activity. We have served notices to everyone and are questioning them to ascertain their roles, a senior CCB officer said. The police have also served notices on more than 60 employees who were working at the premises. Investigators have seized laptops and mobile phones and are examining the devices to determine how the suspected operation functioned and which employees were aware of the alleged fraud. The CCB is yet to establish a financial trail linking the premises to the suspected fraud, as they have not found transaction IDs or other financial details so far. The police said the investigation is continuing to establish the complete modus operandi, the roles played by the employees, and the alleged link to the Dubai-based operation.

articleTitle: Colonial legacy of India’s policing system must end: Andhra Pradesh High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Andhra Pradesh High Court police policing colonial
description: Hearing six pleas alleging police interference in land or property disputes, the Andhra Pradesh High Court barred the police from adjudicating civil rights.
body_raw: The Andhra Pradesh High Court has invoked the colonial legacy of Indias policing system while calling for a shift towards people-centric and democratic policing. Referring to legal scholar Upendra Baxis observation that the colonial police survived decolonization it simply changed masters, the court said the police structure, methods and legal framework largely continued to reflect the colonial model even after Independence. Justice Maheswara Rao Kuncheam was hearing a batch of six petitions alleging police interference in civil disputes involving land, houses and other properties. The petitioners alleged that police personnel had called them to police stations, pressured them to settle disputes and interfered in matters pending before competent courts or legal forums. The common order in the six petitions was passed on October 5,restraining the police from interfering in civil disputes. Police are entrusted with the responsibility of protecting life, liberty, rights and public order, but they are not an authority above the people. Police powers are conferred by law and must be exercised fairly, reasonably and proportionately. Thus, the police must act as guardians of the constitutional principles, rather than as rulers exercising unchecked authority over citizens., the court said. The police structure, methods and legal framework largely continued to reflect the colonial model, mainly based on the Police Act, 1861, which was primarily designed to maintain order, control the population and protect the interests of the ruling authority, rather than to function as a citizen-oriented service, it added. The court said that though the British rulers were replaced by an elected Indian government, the basic institutional character of the police remained substantially unchanged. Hence, all the stakeholders contribute their respective support to change the overall existing police structures from the colonial phase to people-centric policing in the larger interest of modern Indian and turns into Democratic policing, which means a system of policing in which the police exercise their powers within the limits of law, remain accountable to constitutional and democratic institutions, and respond to the legitimate needs and rights of the people, it added. 6 pleas raised common concern The six petitions involved different disputes but raised the common issue of police allegedly interfering in civil matters already pending before competent forums. In one petition, the petitioner alleged police interference in a dispute concerning his house and pressure to vacate it. Another alleged that police had locked her house and prevented her from entering. Other petitions involved allegations that police repeatedly called parties to stations to settle disputes concerning land or property. One petitioner alleged that police threatened her to withdraw a civil suit, while another alleged that he was detained for hours and pressured to compromise in a property dispute. These were allegations made in the petitions. The State disputed them and told the court that police had not called the petitioners to the respective stations and would not interfere in civil disputes unless a cognizable offence was registered. The high court also highlighted the limited police strength in Andhra Pradesh. It noted that the state has approximately 166.18 police personnel per one lakh population, against the United Nations recommendation of 222 personnel per lakh. The court said that, given these limitations, deploying police resources in areas where they have no jurisdiction could become a futile exercise. It referred to the possibility of unjust enrichment of some police personnel through such intervention and described such conduct as illegal and unconstitutional. Police cant decide civil rights The court made it clear that the police retain their legal duty to maintain law and order, prevent crime, protect life and property, and take lawful preventive measures where there is a threat to public peace. However, those powers do not extend to deciding civil rights between private parties. The court said that once a competent judicial or quasi-judicial forum has seized a dispute, an executive authority without adjudicatory powers cannot assume the role of that forum and determine the rights of the parties. Such action would amount to acting without jurisdiction. The duty to resolve civil disputes is entrusted to the judiciary. No such power is empowered to the Police, the court said, adding that interference in pending or potential civil disputes is not within their province. DGPs guidelines draw the line The court took note of instructions issued by the Andhra Pradesh Director General of Police on October 24, 2025 concerning land disputes. The guidelines say police should not take sides or interfere in civil ownership or title disputes, while providing for preventive action where a dispute threatens public peace. The guidelines also provide for criminal cases where criminal intent or violence is evident, including trespass, cheating, forgery, assault or criminal conspiracy. The high court ultimately held that police have no jurisdiction to adjudicate upon or determine civil rights between parties. It directed the police not to interfere, adjudicate, determine or settle such rights without legal cause and ordered strict compliance with the DGPs guidelines. The parties were left free to pursue remedies before appropriate civil courts or competent forums. The court clarified that if a cognisable offence is made out, police remain free to proceed according to law. There was no order as to costs, and pending interlocutory applications were closed.

articleTitle: Jonathan Bailey as Dracula: Mary Lambert talks casting the ‘Sexiest Man Alive’ as vampire
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jonathan Bailey voices Dracula in Mary Lambert's Audible adaptation.
description: In an exclusive interview with SCREEN, Dracula director Mary Lambert talks about casting Jonathan Bailey as Dracula in Audible's adaptation, and using her experience on Pet Sematary and Madonna's "Like A Prayer" to tell the horror tale.
body_raw: There couldnt have been a more apt name than Mary Lambert to helm the new Audible Original adaptation of Bram Stokers 1897 seminal Gothic novel Dracula. Shes no stranger to horror, having helmed films like Pet Sematary 1989, an adaptation of Stephen Kings 1983 bestseller. Shes also been an aficionado of sound, music, and aural effects, having directed trailblazing music videos of pop stars like Madonna and Janet Jackson. And shes certainly not new to the cocktail of spirituality and sex that is Dracula, having collaborated with Madonna in the highly controversial 1989 video Like A Prayer. Mary Lambert on the cocktail of sex, religion, and horror Why not a Black Jesus?, Lambert recalls suggesting to Madonna when the Grammy winner pitched making out with a Black guy at the altar in the music video of Like A Prayer. It invited the ire of a lot of fundamentalist Christians and other people who want to use religion to control people, instead of connecting people, claims the director in an exclusive interview with SCREEN. She believes that unlike the extremely conservative Americans, Indians have historically been far more open to the idea of embracing sex, a la the Kamasutra. Indians deal with sexuality much better. They acknowledge that sex and sexual desire are religious experiences. Religious ecstasy is very close to what people experience as sexual ecstasy. And I dont mean that in a religious way, but as something like being consumed by desire to a point that youre not limited to your body, argues Lambert. So, when she had Peoples Sexiest Man Alive of last year - Jonathan Bailey - cast as Dracula, she could use his magnetic persona to make the audiences imagination run wild, despite the obvious setback of them not being able to watch Bailey in all his glory as the mythical vampire on screen. Jonathan is an extremely attractive man, and not just physically. Hes so charming. Sexiness is much more than that. It definitely helps to have a gorgeous face, beautiful hair, and lovely skin, but theres something else that makes someone sexy - its their personality and humanity. You really feel theres a lovely, thoughtful, and funny person inside there. He really responds to you in that moment, says Lambert. Beyond not projecting Baileys visual as the sinister, otherworldly aristocrat, directing an audio show was a challenge for Lambert because as a painter, shes also a very visual person. Thats what I enjoy most about movies - making paintings that move, she says, adding, But with sound, you can leave people to their own imagination. When you listen and visualize, the sunlight feels more real and the castle more frightening, instead of watching a movie, where the castle just looks like a hotel On learning horror storytelling from Stephen King Lambert is an advocate for whipping out of imagination than consumption on a platter also because shes a book nerd. Thats also what led to her helming Pet Sematary, which she confesses was difficult to adapt. Stephen King uses the characters voice as the singular point of view, and the readers read their thoughts. For instance, when you read Pet Sematary, you know what Louis Creed is thinking. He wants to kill the cat. He hates his daughter. These are things people dont share. But we understand thats what drives him in order to bring his son back to life, says the filmmaker. Dracula, starring Jonathan Bailey, is now available on Audible - best of jonathan bailey badpostjbailey October 1, 2026 But with Dracula, the job was made slightly easier by multiple characters points of view. They write diaries and letters, and they tear them off sometimes. More often than not, the first letters they write are what they actually think. Its a difficult thing to visualize what someone is saying to themselves. Sometimes, its conveyed through narration, but I feel its best done through performance. Its easier in an audio drama because there are no visuals to distract from it. Sometimes, wed do a sequence over and over again until we were on the same page. Because there are no cameras, sets, hair, and makeup to take care of after every shot, adds Lambert, heaving a sigh of relief. Fallout star Ella Purnell, who voices Mina Murray in Dracula, is not designed as his hapless victim, as has been the trope in several previous iterations. Lambert feels she was able to achieve that because of two key changes in the three decades since Pet Sematary. Studios and financiers realized that women were making up a large percentage of the audience for certain horror movies. Also, more young women began directing horror movies, pointed out the director. Also Read When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood bunch of thieves for stealing his bestseller plots As a result, female characters began to have more agency in the plots of horror films. The female nature - and men can have a female nature - is more in touch with instinct, spirituality, and the invisible world. So, this worked well in movies like The Others 2001, The Ring 2002, Insidious 2010, The Conjuring 2013, A Girl Walks Home Alone At Night, and The Babadook 2014, says Lambert, adding, Women could even be villains Like Amy Madigan, who totally changed the face of horror in Weapons, my favorite movie of 2025, largely because of her performance and its implications.

articleTitle: Denied boarding on Kochi-Abu Dhabi flight, mother and child wins Rs 70,287 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Airlines boarding consumer flight
description: The commission held that the airline's failure to transport the complainants to the destination without any reason amounted to a shortcoming and inadequacy in the service.
body_raw: A Kerala consumer commission has directed an airline to pay Rs 70,287 to a mother and her minor son after they were allegedly denied boarding on a confirmed Kochi-Abu Dhabi flight and had to purchase fresh tickets. President CT Sabu and member Ram Mohan R observed that the complainant had to manage the minor child, rearrange their travel at short notice, undertake an additional journey and were constrained to pay a higher amount for the second ticket. The fact that the 2nd complainant was a child of approximately three years at the time makes the inconvenience and hardship more significant. The 1st complainant had to manage the minor child, rearrange their travel at short notice and undertake an additional journey between Sharjah and Abu Dhabi. Also constrained to pay a higher amount for the second ticket to Sharjah, the order read. Boarding denied The complainant said that she had booked flight tickets to travel from Kochi to Abu Dhabi on 11 February 2021, paying Rs 20,287. It was alleged that they had valid travel documents and were eligible to travel to Abu Dhabi under the travel guidelines applicable at the time, but were denied permission to board the flight. The complainant alleged that they were then compelled to purchase fresh tickets from Kochi to Sharjah for which they paid Rs 29,510. It was further stated that since Abu Dhabi was their intended destination, the mother and child had to undertake an additional journey from Sharjah to Abu Dhabi after landing there. The complainant said that the airline neither provided a satisfactory justification for denying boarding nor refunded the original KochiAbu Dhabi airfare. The airline did not appear before the commission despite being served notice and was proceeded against ex-parte. The commission said that if boarding had been denied because of any lawful restriction, failure to meet mandatory travel requirements or any other valid reason attributable to the complainants, the airline was required to disclose and establish the same. However, no such explanation or evidence was placed before it. The commission held that the airlines failure to transport the complainants to the contracted destination, without establishing a legally sustainable reason, followed by collection of a further amount for travel to a different destination, amounted to a shortcoming and inadequacy in the service. The commission thus directed the airline to refund the original airfare of Rs 20,287. It also awarded Rs 40,000 as compensation for deficiency in service, mental agony, inconvenience and hardship, and Rs 10,000 towards proceedings costs. Takeaway An airline that denies boarding on a confirmed ticket must have a legally sustainable reason and cannot retain the fare for a journey it failed to provide. Passengers can seek a refund and compensation for the resulting hardship. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Kerala 1800-425-1550 or call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 for assistance.

The police team was immediately dispatched, but due to network issues as well as the challenge of identifying the exact location, the two had already taken the extreme step by the time the police reached the spot, a senior officer said. A spontaneous act Karan Panna, Assistant Deputy Superintendent of Police, Limkheda division, told The Indian Express that the circumstances pointed towards family opposition to the relationship. A probe is on. Prima facie, it was a spontaneous act, and the circumstances suggest their families opposed the relationship. We are conducting an investigation after an accidental death case has been lodged. The further steps will be decided accordingly, Panna said. articleTitle: Navratri 2026: Start and End Date, Navratri Colours With Calendar, Significance and Importance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: navratri
description: Navratri 2026 Start and End Date: Know the significance of Navratri 2026, its start and end dates, nine-day colour calendar, and the traditions associated with each day.
body_raw: Sharad Navratri 2026The term Navratri or Navaratri is a combination of two distinct words-nava, which stands for nine, and ratri, which signifies night. When brought together, the name literally translates to nine nights. Spanning nine consecutive nights and ten days, Navratri ranks among the most sacred and widely observed festivals in the Hindu tradition, typically taking place during the autumn months. At its core, the celebration emphasizes devotion to Goddess Durga, also revered as Shakti, the embodiment of universal cosmic power honouring her through her nine distinct manifestations. While four different Navaratris are observed across India over the course of the year specifically Chaitra Navratri, Paush Navratri, Magha Navratri, and Sharad Navratri, it is Maha Navratri, also known as Sharad Navratri, that is held as the most sacred and significant of them all. According to the Hindu calendar, the festival is celebrated in the month of Ashvin, which typically falls in September and October as per the Gregorian calendar. This year, Navratri will be observed from October 11 to October 20, 2026, and the 10th and last day will be celebrated as Dussehra. Importance and Significance of Navratri Regarding the significance of Navratri, it shares the fundamental theme central to all major Indian festivals, the ultimate triumph of good over evil though the underlying legends and mythologies vary significantly. Across Indias diverse regions, the festival manifests in unique ways eastern and northeastern states observe these dates as Durga Puja, whereas communities across the northern and western regions celebrate the nine-night festival to commemorate Lord Ramas victory over the demon king Ravana. According to tradition, Goddess Durga engaged in a fierce battle against the demon Mahishasura, ultimately emerging victorious over him. The festival is observed to honor and worship the Goddess in celebration of this triumph of divine light over darkness. The festivities officially commence on Mahalaya, the first day of the festival, which is dedicated to invoking and remembering Goddess Durga while signifying the conclusion of Pitru Paksha, the sacred fortnight of Shradhh honored by ancestors. On the sixth day of the festival, Goddess Durga is formally welcomed into family homes and elaborate public pandals. These festive observances stretch across the subsequent days until the tenth day, known as Vijayadashami, when the deitys idol is immersed in a body of water. Throughout this period, communities gather to go pandal-hopping, partake in sanctified feast meals called bhog, and distribute food to those in need-an act that celebrates and honors the spirit of goodwill in everyone. Across Northern India, the nine-day occasion centers on commemorating Lord Ramas historic triumph over the demon king Ravana. Over the course of nine nights, theatrical stage plays known as Ramlila perform dramatic adaptations of the ancient Hindu epic Ramayana. On the tenth and concluding day, which depicts Lord Rama slaying Ravana with a bow and arrow, the celebrations culminate in the ceremonial burning of massive effigies representing Ravana alongside his brothers, Meghnad and Kumbhakaran. Observers throughout the region dress in traditional attire, keep ritual fasts, and gather for group prayers. Intricate stage decorations, storytelling recitals, dramatic reenactments of ancient legends, scripture chanting, devotional prayers, and vibrant folk dances like dandiya and garba are performed to embody the energetic spirit of the festivities. Friends and families unite to explore pandals and participate in local gatherings. On the ultimate day, the festivities conclude either with the immersion of the Goddesss idol in water-as practiced during Durga Puja-or through the dramatic burning of effigies during Dussehra. articleTitle: Drishyam 3: Ajay Devgn’s Vijay is like any political leader who uses religion to get his way
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn plays Vijay Salgaonkar in Drishyam 3
description: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 is the representation of the moral decay of our society because here, good does not win over evil, and justice is never served.
body_raw: Drishyam 3 The Conclusion released in the theatres this past weekend and if you, like many others, were waiting for the promised conclusion at the end of Vijay Salgaonkars story, this must have been a disappointment, for the story never really ends. The loose ends still exist, the decade-old crime is still unsolved, and those who committed the accidental killing are still walking around, scot-free. In the first film, back in 2015, the chain of events begins after Vijays daughter Anju and wife Nandini accidentally kill a boy named Sam, who sexually harassed Anju and is now blackmailing her. Vijay then makes it his lifes mission to save his family from getting imprisoned. He forges evidence, coaches the family to lie, and befriends any potential pawn who could help him in his scheme. He succeeds. The film projects Vijay as the family man, the hero, who will do anything for his family, while completely dismissing the fact that, in this attempt, they are villainising those who are trying to seek justice for the dead son. Vijay lies like a sociopath and trains his family like he is running a sleeper cell so no one gets caught for a crime that was indeed committed by them. Of course, the man was killed in an accidental altercation, but he did end up dead, and someone was responsible, but the film is not interested in that conversation. There is no concept of justice in the Drishyam universe. The film only cares about worshipping the family man Vijay Salganokars family values, and not examining how those values come across as completely hollow. Vijay incites religious hatred, and believes its completely okay In many ways, Vijay is the exact representation of the political leaders of our times, which also explains his popularity amongst the masses. He claims to be an uneducated man who has supposedly become street smart from working at a cable TV shop and watching a bunch of movies. This somehow explains his warped idea of morality, as its entirely derived from fictional films, but it also explains why he lives his regular life like a main character where everyone else is just background noise. ALSO READ Is Chris Hansen a hero or villain? Primetime explores his god complex to get to the answer In the new film, Vijay even uses religion as a weapon to save his family because his political smarts tell him that this tactic, if used correctly, cannot fail. This has worked for many political leaders, and it works perfectly for him as well. The authorities watch his plans unfold while being fully aware of how he is manipulating a mob, and just end up being mute spectators. There is even a scene where Prakash Raj lists the qualifications of those trying to put Vijay behind bars. He points out that a chauthi-fail Vijay has left even Harvard graduates scratching their heads but the film fails to acknowledge that a conniving, sly man doesnt really need a degree to fool the world. Fooling the system for ten long years is not a cause for celebration. For over a decade, Vijay has spent hours and days befriending those who are in a weaker position than him so he can take advantage of their situation and save his family. And all this while, the film has never bothered to actually reflect that his morally corrupt practices have turned him into a hate-inciting criminal. Daughters scarred for life but Vijay believes he has saved them Amid all the damage that he has been inflicting on those around him, there has never been even the slightest pause to actually ponder over how deeply he has damaged his own daughters, whom he is supposedly trying to save. In this film, when he pushes his older daughter to get married, he simply talks about moving on, as if she is not still scarred by the act of killing a man with her bare hands. The woman has been living a nightmare that led to seizures, and Vijays solution is just to get an arranged marriage match so she can move on. Its almost as if he truly believes that he saved his family, and did not create a monster that would never be tamed. The family is constantly looking over their shoulder and cant even breathe peacefully without Vijays nod, for they dont know what awaits at the next corner. The younger daughter, who must have been just 7-8 years old when Sam was killed, has lived with the burden of this case all her life. Vijay has coached her into believing that he is her saviour but the poor girl doesnt know that normal families arent hiding bodies and murders for family time. He has created an elaborate scheme for everything, and the family is playing along. Do they think they are saved? Because it definitely doesnt look like they are living a good life. Drishyam 3 is the representation of the moral decay of our society because here, good does not win over evil, and justice is never served. Vijays family faces no consequences for taking the life of a young man but Vijay is celebrated for being a mastermind criminal who can fool the masses by manipulating them.

articleTitle: Centre may look at reviving jet fuel price stabilisation fund scheme amid surge in fuel costs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jet fuel prices for international flights have been reduced by 27%, bringing aviation turbine fuel (ATF) rates closer to domestic levels. (File Photo)
description: However, jet fuel prices have surged again as the conflict drags on, leading to major disruptions in global energy flows.
body_raw: With a surge in jet fuel prices in recent months hitting airlines, the government could consider a revival of the Price Stabilisation Fund PSF scheme to provide stable fuel pricing to airlines amid extreme price volatility in the international market, a senior government official said Tuesday. The Rs 10,000-crore PSF scheme was first announced in June amid soaring jet fuel prices, but lapsed after it failed to attract any airline at the time as prices moderated shortly afterwards on hopes of truce in the West Asia conflict. However, jet fuel prices have surged again as the conflict drags on, leading to major disruptions in global energy flows. Separately, Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu told reporters that the government is in discussion with airlines as well as the public sector oil marketing companies OMCs on jet fuel prices, but didnt elaborate further. The recent hike in jet fuel prices has prompted Indias largest airline IndiGo to hike fuel surcharge on flight tickets after six months, and other airlines might follow suit. Recently, the Federation of International Airlines FIA, which has IndiGo, Air India, and SpiceJet members, also urged the government to review jet fuel pricing in India and implement a cost-plus pricing model instead of the current model of international benchmark pricing. It also said that if timely relief was not made available, the airlines could be forced to withdraw from a number of unsustainable routes. It also said that jet fuel now accounts for 55-60 of airlines operational expenses, versus 30-40 earlier. Under the PSF scheme, which didnt find any takers among airlines at the time, the OMCs were to sell jet fuel to participating Indian airlines for their domestic as well as international flights at a fixed price irrespective of the price fluctuations in the international market. The OMCs were to be compensated from the Rs 10,000-crore price stabilisation fund when they incurred losses on ATF sales. When international prices fell, the OMCs gains were be used to offset the financial support that was provided to them. The government expected this arrangement, which was to be in place for up to three years, to ease the pain for the OMCs as well as Indian airlines, and rein in runaway airfares due to fuel price pressure. It was a voluntary facility only available to Indian airlines, and was to be implemented through an agreement between the airlines and the OMCs, under which the carriers had to commit to procure fuel exclusively from the OMCs for up to three years. The stable jet fuel price level under the scheme was set at Rs 115 per litre in Delhi, with price levels varying at different airports due to differences in state taxes. However, soon after the scheme was announced, prices fell below the fixed price level as global prices eased amid hopes of a resolution in the West Asia conflict. As none of the Indian carriers signed up for the scheme within the prescribed timeline, it was allowed to lapse. But with the revival and escalation of the conflict in subsequent weeks, jet fuel prices again jumped. In the latest revision on October 1, the price of jet fuel was hiked by about Rs 16 per litre to Rs 137 per litre.

articleTitle: Kid in arms, man dangling from window: Tribal students say forcibly being sent home
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tribal students mumbai tilak bhavan
description: The students have alleged that since they refused to leave Mumbai, the police officials tried to push them into the buses and take them to their homes
body_raw: Hundreds of tribal students who marched into Mumbai from Nashik two days ago to press for their demands were allegedly thrown into the police bus-some with a kid in their arms, some dangling from the bus windows, and some with their legs upside down, their clothes torn in the scuffle. Pushing them inside the bus, the cops stood there, smiling. These were the visuals The Indian Express witnessed outside the Tilak Bhavan in Mumbai today on October 6. The tribal students have refused to leave Mumbai without meeting Governor Jishnu Dev Varma. The students have alleged that since they refused to leave Mumbai, the police officials tried to push them into the buses and take them to their homes, prompting an altercation between the students and the police. We have been protesting for so long in Nashik. And we began our journey to Mumbai on September 29. After walking for so many days, we are denied to meet the governor with our demands, one of the protesting students said. The police have denied detaining anyone. A bus was arranged, and the students have been taken back to their hometown. No one was detained, a senior official said. The students had earlier planned to march to the Lok Bhavan, but permission was denied. On Tuesday, there was a heavy police deployment outside the Tilak Bhavan, which is headquarters of the Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee. The students were not allowed to move out of the Tilak Bhavan. On Sunday, October 4, the Congress had alleged that the Mumbai Police entered the Congress headquarters and detained some tribal students, including women. The cops have rejected the allegations. Now the students are planning a protest at a later date. The plan is now to come back to Mumbai for a protest on October 25. All students will go back to their respective home districts in buses arranged by the Congress. Each bus will have a Congress member to ensure safety of all students, said Dhananjay Shinde from Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee.

articleTitle: For India’s ’80s kids, Jeffrey Archer was a window to the grown-up world of power and greed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jeffrey archer
description: Archer’s characters had ambition, greed, villainy, rivalries, deviousness, and love for the good life, with his stories often ending on a satisfying twist
body_raw: Before Hollywood came to our neighbourhoods, before Santa Barbara flummoxed our crammed living rooms, there was Jeffrey Archer. Accessible and dependable, churning out thrillers in book after book, putting us right there next to people in positions of power beyond our budding teenage comprehension. White House to Westminster, FBI to Mossad, within our reach, occupying pride of place on the mats of enthusiastic sellers of pirated books in Connaught Places colonnaded, post-imperialist corridors an irony to please any writers heart held aloft by indefatigable hawkers at traffic lights or jostling for space with Manohar Kahaniyan and Readers Digest at railway platform bookstalls. Pop-up libraries, functioning from crummy, dimly lit garages in DDA colonies, stocked them, friends swapped them, and us of the 80s generation got a new vocabulary that didnt seem handed or drummed down, even as parents beamed in approval at our love for reading English. This was unlike other parent-approved reading material-a big bulk of it Soviet-discounted literature-that one way or the other turned out to be a lesson in abstinence or discipline or being better. Archers characters had ambition, greed, villainy, rivalries, deviousness, and love for the good life, with his stories often ending on a satisfying twist. His women could be politicians and, yes, even the US President, run corporations and rock families, with Archer attributing it to the strong women in his own life. One of them was late British prime minister Margaret Thatcher, who was behind Archers own short-lived political career. It worked, earning Archer 14 years and five months on Britains Sunday Times bestseller lists, over five years on The New York Times bestseller lists, and sales of 300 million books worldwide. When Archer served time for perjury, for lying in a libel case against a tabloid that said he had paid a woman for sex-years after the event-it seemed just the kind of scandal that would animate one of his novels. Unsurprisingly, wife Mary Archer, a scientist in her own right, earned herself some unforgettable lines too, with the judge remarking after her testimony Has she elegance? Has she fragrance? Would she have, without the strain of this trial, radiance? Archer probably would have kept it simpler, not sound as laboured as a judge in a wig. And yet for us non-native-English speakers, he was our introduction to terms such as First Among Equals, Honour Among Thieves, and a personal favourite, A Quiver Full of Arrows. It was a cosy, warm summer when we waited for that one, the quiver holding a promise as much in its title as how our lips and teeth met over the word. And, has there ever been a title that sounded as intimate and as ambitious as Shall We Tell The President? Archer reaffirmed his position as the author whose books we took into beds, and raced through over one night, with his professed love for India. He often came to the country, had friends here, and released books in India before they premiered abroad. One reason for this was to beat the book pirates. But would he have minded the boy hawker peddling the latest Jeffrey Archer, while balancing countless other knockoffs, tapping on his car window at a traffic light? It would be a twist he would enjoy. As much as the fact that death came to him a day before the release of what would be his final book. Its title? Adam Eve. The writer is editor planning and projects, The Indian Express. shalini.langerexpressindia.com

articleTitle: At least 12 Indian sailors injured in attacks in Black Sea, Hormuz; MEA condemns
articleFeaturedImageAlt: MEA: A motorboat travels past commercial vessels appear anchored in the Strait of Hormuz
description: The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, the MEA reiterated, and urged for the earliest restoration of navigation and commerce through international waterways.
body_raw: With Indian seafarers being injured in two separate attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the Black Sea, the Ministry of External Affairs MEA on Tuesday condemned the incidents and expressed deep concern over the targeting of commercial shipping. Eleven Indian crew members were injured after a Panama-flagged vessel was hit by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. In the other incident, at least two foreign crew members were killed and some others, including an Indian, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire on a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea on Monday. We condemn the attack earlier today on a Panama-flagged commercial vessel, MT On Peace, off the coast of Oman, where it was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the MEA said in a statement. Of the total crew of 19, 17 are Indian nationals. It is learnt that 12 crew members have been injured, including 11 Indian nationals, it said. With the assistance of Omani authorities, the injured crew have since been evacuated and are receiving medical treatment in Khasab, Oman. We thank the Omani authorities for their valuable support, it said. The MEA said the continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region remain a cause of deep concern for India. We reiterate our call for an immediate cessation of such attacks in the interests of peace and stability in the region, it said. The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored at the earliest, the MEA said. In the other incident, the Indian Embassy in Romania reported that there were three Indian nationals among the crew members and one of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea. As per preliminary information, there have been 2 casualties foreign nationals while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members, the mission posted on X. It said all three Indians are safe and in good health. We condemn the attack on MV Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea in which two foreign seafarers were killed and some members of the crew, including Indian nationals, injured. The injured have been rescued by Romanian authorities and are receiving medical attention. The three Indian nationals, who were part of the crew, are safe. We thank Romanian authorities for their swift action in this incident, the MEA said. India views these attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers with grave concern, it said. The targeting of traffic in international waterways is severely undermining global commerce and welfare of people across the world. We continue to call for dialogue and diplomacy to bring an end to the ongoing conflicts. Indian seafarers account for almost 12 per cent of the global maritime community. According to sources, at least nine Indian seafarers have died, one is presumed dead, and seven have been injured since the start of the West Asia crisis, until July this year. There have been at least 29 incidents of attacks on vessels carrying Indian seafarers - four involving Indian-flagged vessels and the rest involving foreign-flagged vessels. In the Black Sea, too, Indian seafarers have been victims of attacks from both Russia and Ukraine. In fact, India started actively pushing for Russia-Ukraine peace after Indian seafarers were hit by such attacks. In September 2026, India and Liberia launched a 25-nation Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers during the UN General Assembly to ensure safety and security of merchant crews and commercial shipping against targeted attacks, the MEA said. With PTI, London

articleTitle: ‘Bulli Bai’ auction app case: Engineering student discharged; court says ‘no evidence’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: bulli bai student discharged
description: 'Bulli Bai' was allegedly a mock auction app made to upload photos of Muslim women with objectionable comments.
body_raw: A magistrate court has discharged a 25-year-old engineering student who was arrested in 2022 in connection with the Bulli Bai auction app case. While discharging the student, the court observed that there is no evidence that he was involved in the creation of the Bulli Bai app or shared photographs of the women. Bulli Bai was allegedly a mock auction app made to upload photos of Muslim women with objectionable comments. Vishal Jha, who was then an engineering student at a Bengaluru institute, was the first person to be arrested in the case by the Mumbai Police. It is, however, not known if Jha is still a student. Seeking to be cleared in the case, Jhas lawyer said that the only allegation against him in the chargesheet is that he had shared and followed the app. On this, the court said this in itself is not an offence. .admittedly, the role of the present applicant is that he followed the..App and he was in contact with the co-accused. In the case cited. the Honble Allahabad High Court held that following the page on the website is not an offence. In the present case, the applicant followed.the App. There is no further role attributed by the prosecution against him. So, following the App in view of the above-mentioned judgment is not an offence, Judicial Magistrate Court R T Ingle said. In April, the court had rejected the discharge plea of another accused, Mayank Rawat, noting that prima facie there is proof that he had outraged the modesty of women by downloading the photographs of the Muslim women from their social media accounts and posting them on the app. The cyber cell unit of the Bandra Kurla Complex had filed a complaint under sections including 153 a promoting enmity between two groups, 295 a deliberate acts to outrage religious feelings, 354 d stalking, 500 defamation, and 509 insulting modesty of a woman of the Indian Penal Code and relevant sections of the Information Technology Act. Discharging Jha, the court said that while there is evidence that he was in touch with some of the co-accused, that in itself is not evidence of his involvement. But, in entire charge-sheet, there is no further role of the present applicant which would show that, he either created said App or the help co-accused in creating it. Even there is no allegation that he shared photographs of Muslim women, the court said.

articleTitle: Vidyut Jammwal holds his breath for 15 minutes without blinking, fans call him ‘master’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vidyut Jammwal holds his breath for 15 minutes without blinking
description: At a recent event, actor Vidyut Jammwal held his breath for 15 minutes without blinking his eyes. A video of the act is going viral on social media.
body_raw: Actor Vidyut Jammwal, who is known for his expertise in martial arts, especially kalaripayattu, has impressed fans by showcasing another unusual skill. At a recent event, Vidyut held his breath and entered a meditative state for around 15-16 minutes without blinking, causing his eyes to become visibly teary. A video of the act went viral on social media, leaving netizens impressed. Vidyut Jammwal attended a special Street Fighter event in Mumbai on Monday. The actor, who is set to make his Hollywood debut as the iconic yoga master Dhalsim in the upcoming live-action film, used the occasion to demonstrate the yogic practices that helped him connect with his character. During the event, Vidyut meditated alongside cosplayers dressed as Dhalsim. He remained still on stage for approximately 15 minutes while holding his breath, leaving those in attendance stunned by his discipline and control. After completing the practice, Vidyut explained that he had used a technique from the Patanjali Yoga Sutras. He also revealed that the practice has helped him achieve several milestones in his life and that he teaches the technique to youngsters. articleTitle: He went to Russia to study. Rs 3 lakh visa took him to Ukraine war zone instead
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjab man Russia Ukraine war
description: After losing his parents, Patiala yoga teacher Gagandeep Singh did not want to live alone. He chose to move to Russia, a decision that would land him on the frontlines of the Russia-Ukraine war.
body_raw: For nearly a year, Gagandeep Singh lived by two rules look up for drones, look down for mines. The 35-year-old yoga teacher from Punjabs Patiala had travelled to Russia on a student visa, hoping for a better life. Instead, he found himself on the frontlines of the Russia-Ukraine war, watching fellow soldiers die, and fighting to stay alive. When the danger became extreme, I contacted my sister and sought help, Singh, who returned to India in August, recalled. Singh says he was content working as a yoga teacher at the Government Ayurvedic College and Hospital in Patiala, earning around Rs 26,000 a month. But the death of his parents devastated him. Its then that he decided to move abroad. There was one major constraint he could not afford to go to a European country. Russia, however, was within his means. So, with the help of a Bathinda-based travel agent, Singh says he managed to secure admission to Moscow State Linguistic University, one of Russias largest linguistic universities, and left for Moscow in May 2025 on a one-year student visa. The expenses were about Rs 3 lakh. How Singhs plan fell through His plan was simple learn Russian and work part-time to support himself. He believed knowing the language would help him understand people better and find work in Russia. For around three months in Moscow, he attended classes and worked part-time as a delivery worker. Then a fellow student told him about a job with the Russian Army. Singh says he was offered a good salary and told that the work involved building bunkers and other support duties-not fighting on the battlefield. He agreed. Singh says he, along with around two dozen men from India, signed a contract with the Russian Army and underwent two months of military training. The recruits were made to run, undergo weapons and firing practice, and learn to build bunkers. Their salaries started coming into their Russian accounts, but their phones, Singh says, were taken away. Then the recruits were moved towards Ukraine, bags full of arms and ammunition. On the frontlines of the Ukraine war Around 100 men were left in different groups in different forested areas along the Russia-Ukraine border. We thought it was bunker work, Singh says. He found himself moving through forests with a Russian commander, fellow Indian Inderjit Singh from Kolkata, and two men from other countries. Drones constantly flew overhead, while mines and explosives lay scattered across the ground. It was like walking on our deathbed, he recalls. Food was scarce. He says he was able to bathe only two or three times during the entire period. One by one, the people around him disappeared. Inderjit died. So did the Russian commander and the two other men. Eventually, Singh says, he was alone. He says he spent nearly 11 months in jungles and war-affected areas, eventually reaching close to Kyiv. His right foot and a hand were badly injured during an attack. While under Russian military care, he received some medical aid, but after returning home he underwent an operation. A call for help, an MP steps up Singh kept the truth from his family. They knew he had gone to Russia on a student visa, but not that he had ended up in Ukraine. After he contacted his sister, Singhs family took up the matter with Rajya Sabha MP Baba Balbir Singh Seechewal, who appealed to men not to get trapped by such enticements. The matter was subsequently taken up with the Ministry of External Affairs, which intervened. The Russian authorities were contacted and Singh eventually returned to India on August 26. Back home after surviving a war he never chose to fight, Singh says he only desires the simple things a yoga mat, a classroom, and a normal day.

articleTitle: Cross-voting to 2027 polls: Why Akhilesh dropped plan to put up third RS candidate
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also alleged that poor people were being defrauded of their land in Ayodhya. (File Photo)
description: Samajwadi Party's last-minute move paves way for its two nominees and BJP’s eight candidates to get elected unopposed in October 16 UP Rajya Sabha polls
body_raw: Days after indicating that it would field its third candidate for the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party SP decided against the move Tuesday, the last day of filing nominations, paving the way for the partys two nominees and the ruling BJPs eight candidates to get elected to the Upper House unopposed. The SPs last-minute decision was driven by a combination of factors involved in its attempts to cobble together the numbers needed for a third candidates win, with the high-stakes state Assembly elections just over four months away. SP president and ex-UP chief minister Akhilesh Yadavs rethink on the matter came a day after senior party MLA Ravidas Mehrotra indicated that the party had completed formalities to put up its third candidate for the Upper House polls for 10 vacant seats from UP. On Tuesday morning, however, Akhilesh, in an X post, said, Now our eyes are not on three but on 403 seats, signalling that the party has shifted its focus to the Assembly polls due in February 2027. His move, ending week-long political suspense, made it clear that there would not be any contest between the BJP and the SP for the Rajya Sabha polls now. The BJP and the SP have enough numbers to comfortably win seven and two seats respectively. SPs calculations The SP has already fielded party general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, who is seeking his sixth term in the Rajya Sabha, and Reliance executive Dhananjay Nathwani. Nathwani, 40, is the son of Parimal Nathwani, Director, Corporate Affairs for Reliance Industries Ltd RIL, who was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jharkhand as an NDA-backed Independent in the June 2026 election, securing his fourth consecutive term in the Upper House. Currently, there are 396 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly, with each Rajya Sabha candidate requiring 37 first-preference votes to win. The SP has 101 MLAs. However, its effective strength is 100 as Chail MLA Puja Pal, who continues to figure in the House records as an SP member, has switched to the BJP and is currently its state vice-president. With the support of two Congress MLAs, the SP has 102 votes-nine short of the first-preference votes required to ensure the victory of its third candidate. SP sources said that the partys calculations following the BJPs decision to field its eighth candidate became a key factor in the SPs rethink. Some BJP MLAs were in touch with the SP but showed hesitance to rebel openly months before polls, sources claimed. BJP play The BJP has 255 MLAs with its NDA allies adding another 33 members Apna Dal S 13, RLD 9, SBSP 6, and NISHAD Party 5. With the support of Puja Pal, unaffiliated MLAs Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, and Abhay Singh-who were expelled from the SP in June 2025 for cross-voting in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls-and two MLAs of the Raja Bhaiyya-led Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, the NDAs effective tally stands at 294-just two short of the required 296 37 for each first-preference votes to ensure a win for all its eight candidates. The BJP named its eight candidates Monday, dropping Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma from its list. Its nominees include Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar. Assembly poll factor The BJP appears confident of managing the two additional votes required for its eighth candidate, even as the possibility of cross-voting by some NDA MLAs is not ruled out within the ruling camp too. The presence of the third SP nominee would have led to a contest for the election of 11 candidates for 10 seats. This would have led to cross-voting among the MLAs, which would have favoured the BJP more, said an SP insider. Considering the vindictive nature of the ruling camp, several of its legislators despite being unhappy were hesitant and even fearful to reveal themselves at this stage. We decided to respect their decision and instead aim for the bigger target of the 2027 elections, the party insider said. For the SP, the numbers game was tighter. Its leaders said that in the final analysis, while the party required at least nine additional first-preference votes to push through its third nominee, the BJP needed only two additional votes to secure the victory of its eighth candidate. Thus the arithmetic made the extra-candidate gamble considerably more difficult for the SP than the BJP, especially given the nature of voting in the Rajya Sabha polls. Unlike a conventional secret ballot, the Rajya Sabha elections use an open-ballot system for the MLAs, who are required to show their marked ballots to an authorised party agent. The SP leaders said this made it difficult to rely on cross-voting by even those NDA MLAs who it claimed were in touch with them. With the Assembly elections round the corner, several MLAs were said to be unwilling to risk open defiance of their parties at this stage, when the candidate selection for the 2027 polls has yet to get underway.

The high court order came on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, who sought a CBI probe into issues raised by the ED in a letter sent to Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav.
