articleTitle: Cabinet greenlights new apex body to oversee transport and logistics
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RELIEF scheme exporters India
description: The Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority aims to reduce costs, and meet the government’s Vision 2047 targets
body_raw: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the constitution of an Integrated Transport Logistics Authority ITLA to have a synergy among different transport departments and assess the countrys future requirements in infrastructure development. The authority will be set up in the Ministry of Commerce Industry, serving as the apex body for project planning and appraisal, research, monitoring and evaluation, among other functions. Minister of Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw said that all the major sectors such as the railways, highways, aviation, among others, will have representation under the new authority. Practically, if GDP increases by 7, the logistics requirement increases by 10 in the economy. To meet this heavy requirement, Highways, railway lines, waterways, ports, airports are being built. To have a unified planning of these things, Gati Shakti portal was launched. Now, to meet the future requirements in transportation and have a synergy among different departments, the Integrated transport logistics authority will be set up, said Vaishnaw, as he announced the decision. The fragmented planning across multiple transport-related ministries has been a long-standing challenge in the country. The ITLA is part of the governments Vision 2047 to reduce logistics costs and improve infrastructure efficiency. Apart from the long-term planning of transport projects covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways and coastal shipping, the authority will do the technical appraisal of the projects worth over Rs 500 crore. It will also monitor the transport and infrastructure projects above Rs 500 crore and assess post-completion impact. The authority will create a national transport data repository to integrate GSTN Goods and Services Tax Network e-way bill, FASTag, Vahan, GPS, and urban traffic data and use freight-flow and origin-destination analytics for evidence based project planning. The authority will also advise and assist in reviewing and updating National logistics policy 2022. ITLA will also evaluate short-term sectoral plans five years or so and annual plans of transport ministries to ensure consistency and alignment with the National Transport Master Plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.

articleTitle: Raid before FIR: Karnataka High Court scraps slaughter case despite beef seizure
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court cattle slaughter case beef seizure
description: The court held that taking substantial investigative steps before filing an FIR made the entire process legally unsustainable.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court recently scrapped criminal proceedings against a man accused of illegal cattle slaughter and meat distribution after finding that the police raided his godown and seized beef without registering an FIR first. In an order dated September 28, Justice Rajesh Rai K allowed the petition filed by Zainul Abdeen, challenging the case registered against him under various provisions of the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020. The court held that taking substantial investigative steps before lodging an FIR rendered the entire proceeding legally unsustainable. The failure to register the FIR before proceeding with the raid and seizure, coupled with the fact that substantial investigative steps were undertaken before registration of the FIR, vitiates the proceedings initiated against the petitioner-accused. Consequently, the further proceedings arising out of such FIR cannot be sustained, the bench noted. Pre-FIR search and seizure violates mandatory procedure The case dates back to February 26, 2023, when the police received information at around 9.30 am regarding the illegal sale of beef without a license. Officers subsequently conducted multiple raids on shops and a godown in Shabbeer Nagar, Mysuru. During the search at Abdeens godown, the police allegedly found cattle being slaughtered, meat being processed for transport, and a cattle carcass with two horns. After seizing the meat, the police registered a suo motu complaint against Abdeen. Seeking to scrap the case, the petitioner argued that the police were duty-bound to register an FIR or make an entry in the general diary upon receiving information about a cognisable offence before searching. The petitioner cited the Supreme Courts landmark ruling in Lalita Kumari v. State of Uttar Pradesh 2014, which mandates registering an FIR first upon receiving information about a cognisable offence. The petitioner also noted that the property belonged to his father and that he had no connection to the alleged offence. Court rejects preliminary inquiry argument Opposing the plea, the prosecution argued that the investigation was complete, a chargesheet had been filed, and witness statements pointed to Abdeens involvement. Citing the High Court judgment in Ismail v State of HAL Police Station 2026, the state contended that conducting a preliminary inquiry before an FIR does not invalidate proceedings unless the accused demonstrates prejudice. The court rejected the prosecutions stance, observing that police received information at 9.30 am and had ample opportunity to file an FIR before raiding the premises. In the circumstances, the action of the police cannot be characterised as a mere preliminary enquiry undertaken for the purpose of ascertaining the truth of the information received. The police had already proceeded substantially with the investigation by conducting searches, effecting seizures and recording the statements of panch witnesses before registration of the FIR, the bench stated. Concluding that procedural shortcuts directly impacted the accused, the court held, Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, it cannot be held that no prejudice has been caused to the petitioner on account of the failure to register the FIR before undertaking the raid and seizure.

articleTitle: ‘Tech-savvy’ fighter pilot, who’s flown Mirage and Tejas, set to be next Air Chief
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit
description: A fighter pilot, was involved in Safed Sagar and Operation Sindoor.
body_raw: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is set to become the next Chief of the Air Staff at the end of this month, the Ministry of Defence announced on Tuesday. The announcement comes nearly three weeks before the current Air Chief, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, is due to retire on October 31. Air Marshal Dixit is currently serving as the Vice Chief of the Indian Air Force IAF. Popular among his colleagues, Air Marshal Dixit is described by officers as a thorough professional, soft-spoken, balanced and a grounded individual. An Experimental Test Pilot and Qualified Flying Instructor, he has more than 3,500 hours of flying experience on aircraft including the Mirage 2000, various MiG variants, Kiran, Jaguar, IL-78, Hawk and Tejas. At the same time, he is known to be an avid reader, highly tech-savvy and a visionary leader. His ideas are unique and very different from others. As a leader, he has always been a visionary leader, one of his long-term colleagues told The Indian Express. This is also evident from his public speeches. He has consistently emphasised the need for a balanced mix of traditional and modern weapon systems in the militarys inventory, arguing that conventional aircraft must be complemented by emerging technologies such as drones and missiles to ensure long-term operational effectiveness. In a separate speech, he highlighted the lesson from Operation Sindoor that technology has fundamentally altered the relationship between distance and vulnerability in modern warfare, underscoring the importance of real-time surveillance. Over a distinguished career spanning four decades, the decorated officer has held several critical appointments, including Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee CISC at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff HQ IDS, Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Central Air Command and Deputy Chief of Air Staff. As CISC, he consistently worked to promote jointness and integration among the three services, according to an earlier government statement. As a commanding officer, he re-equipped No. 9 Squadron with Mirage-2000 aircraft and later commanded a frontline fighter base in the Western Sector and a premier fighter training base in the Southern Sector. He has also served as Directing Staff at the Air Force Test Pilots School and as Principal Director, Air Staff Requirements, at Air Headquarters. The Air Marshal has served as Air Defence Commander of Southern Air Command and held the appointments of Assistant Chief of the Air Staff Projects, Assistant Chief of the Air Staff Plans at Air Headquarters, Vayu Bhawan, and Senior Air Staff Officer at Headquarters South Western Air Command. During his four-decade-long service career, he has been actively involved in several operations and exercises, including Operation Safed Sagar, Operation Rakshak and Operation Sindoor. Born on December 9, 1966, he was commissioned into the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force on December 6, 1986. He is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy, the Defence Services Staff College in Bangladesh and the National Defence College.

articleTitle: ‘Don’t sleep…’: How dentist Shota Musaev helped save flydubai captain Smit Machchhar after cockpit attack
articleFeaturedImageAlt: flydubai, smit machchhar, dentist
description: Dentist Musaev said he and other passengers rushed towards the flydubai's FZ1073 plane cockpit after hearing screams. Inside, he saw Machchhar on the floor, bleeding heavily from wounds to his head.
body_raw: Dr Shota Musaev, a Georgian dentist living in Israel, boarded flydubai flight FZ1073 as an ordinary passenger. Minutes later, after the co-pilot attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar in the cockpit, Musaev found himself treating the badly wounded pilot as the aircraft diverted to Saudi Arabia. Speaking to ABC News, Musaev said he and other passengers rushed towards the cockpit after hearing screams. Inside, he saw Machchhar on the floor, bleeding heavily from wounds to his head, neck and hands. How Dr Shota Musaev treated injured Indian pilot Saying that he didnt hesitate to do something, the dentist said, I think, how can I help this situation for all the passengers on the plane? How can I help? And I see one pilot on the floor, with.blood. After passengers subdued the co-pilot, Musaev turned his attention to Machchhar and treated the injured captain for about 45 minutes, according to an interview with The National. He also helped passengers restrain the attacker using headphone cables. The aircraft had been cruising at about 34,000 feet when the cockpit confrontation sent it into a steep descent before it was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Two standby flydubai pilots who had been travelling as passengers then entered the cockpit and helped stabilise the aircraft before it landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. I used T-shirts to press the wounds There was heavy bleeding from his head and left hand. I used T-shirts to press the wounds, but it the bleeding didnt stop, so I asked the stewards for ice, Dr Musaev told The National. Musaev also monitored Machchhars vital signs. At one point, he said, the captains pulse became dangerously low, prompting him to raise Machchhars feet. Later, when he noticed that the pilots lips had turned blue, he told a steward We need to land quickly. He doesnt have much more time. The Israel-based dentist added, He had very, very deep cuts and we needed many ice packets. But every time I opened the T-shirt to check the bleeding, it would bleed more. So I pressed not very hard and used ice. All through the 45 minutes, I kept the pressure on. How Musaev kept captain Machchhar conscious Dr Musaev said that he was trying to keep Captain Machchhar, who was seriously wounded in the attack by the Omani co-pilot, conscious by talking to him as he gave emergency aid to the Indian pilot. I told him, Please dont sleep, we need you. I asked how many children he had and their names. I kept telling him, Dont be afraid you will go back to your family we are landing soon.He was cut badly and would say, Im feeling hot on my hands. I kept telling him that he would be OK, Musaev said. Musaev said Machchhar repeatedly asked for help and told him he wanted to live. The captain also complained of pain in his head and a burning sensation in his hands, according to the dentist. Captain Machchhar wants to meet the dentist In a phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on October 3, Machchhar said he would like to meet Musaev, who had treated him after the attack. Musaev has rejected the idea that he alone was responsible for saving Machchhar, instead crediting the passengers and crew who intervened during the crisis. Everyone in the plane is a hero, he told The National. Smit saved our lives and we saved his life. Musaev, 47, was travelling with his wife, Sigalit, from China via Dubai to Israel when he heard screams and later a call for a doctor. After the emergency landing in Tabuk, Musaev said the experience continued to affect him and his wife. He told The National that they were sleeping only about two hours a night and that he had lost three kilograms in three days.

articleTitle: Visakhapatnam naval base staffer, driver held for ‘sharing information with Pakistan’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Visakhapatnam naval base staffer, driver held for 'sharing information with Pakistan'
description: Andhra Police said the module comprises 18 suspects of which 13 are from the Navy. The arrests are part of “Operation Firewall–2026”, launched by the Counter Intelligence Cell on October 1.
body_raw: Busting a module allegedly involved in sharing sensitive defence information with Pakistan Intelligence Operatives PIOs, the Andhra Pradesh Polices Counter Intelligence Cell has arrested two persons associated with the naval base at Visakhapatnam, officials said. Police said the module comprises 18 suspects of which 13 are from the Navy. The arrested accused include Pradeep Mukharjee, an employee of Visakhapatnam base, who was held in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, for his alleged involvement in sharing an OTP for activation of a WhatsApp account by a PIO, communicating with them, and sharing sensitive information relating to NavalDefence establishments, officials said. He was produced before a court in Vijayawada on Tuesday, which sent him to judicial remand till October 14. The other person to have been arrested is Annam Sai Varaprasad, a civilian contractual driver engaged for naval officers at Visakhapatnam, who was allegedly involved in sharing sensitive information with a PIO in lieu of money, officials said. He was produced in a court in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday, which also sent him to judicial remand till October 14. The arrests are part of a coordinated operation, titled Operation Firewall2026, launched by the Counter Intelligence CI Cell on October 1. As part of this, 12 teams of the CI cell were deployed across 10 states and Union Territories, namely Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Goa, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh and Bihar. A case was registered in this regard at the Counter Intelligence Police Station, Vijayawada, on September 2 under Sections 612, 147 and 148 read with Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS pertaining to charges of criminal conspiracy, waging war, and conspiring to wage war or overawe the government, committed with a shared common intention. Besides, sections of the UAPA and Official Secrets Act have been slapped on the accused. According to the FIR, the CI cell received credible information regarding certain persons in India allegedly maintaining direct contact with PIOs and their suspected involvement in an espionage conspiracy prejudicial to Indias national security. The suspects were allegedly collecting and sharing the sensitiveclassified information relating to defence establishments and strategic locations in Visakhapatnam and other parts of the country through encrypted communication channels, the FIR stated. In coordination with Anti-Terrorist Squads of the respective states, Naval officials and local police, the AP CI Cell investigation teams examined the alleged complicity of the 18 suspects and seized electronic gadgets from them. The two suspects were arrested after prima facie their role was established in this case, said officials. Further investigation is underway for the remaining suspects.

articleTitle: Punjab is among India’s top grain producers. So why is it unable to store it?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The immediate concern is that the backlog is carrying forward: old stocks are not moving out while new paddy continues arriving. (Express photo)
description: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has sought transportation of grain out of Punjab to create storage space, warning of possible law and order issues. Why is this a persistent challenge for the state?
body_raw: With paddy harvesting now underway in Punjab, the states grain storage problems are again in focus. This seasons crop has begun arriving even as stocks from the previous procurement season remain to be fully cleared, leaving the state to potentially manage fresh arrivals alongside a backlog. The procurement chain normally begins with government agencies purchasing paddy, which is stored in rice mills for custom milling to prepare it for sale in the market. Milled rice is then delivered to government agencies and forms part of the central pool. The Centre has extended the deadline for delivery of Custom Milled Rice CMR from the 2025-26 crop season to November 30 - after the 2026-27 procurement season would have ended. Two cycles are thus overlapping 6 lakh tonnes LT of old paddy is still being milled and rice delivered to the government, while fresh paddy is arriving in mandis and being allotted to mills. Recently, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann sought transportation of grain out of Punjab to create storage space, warning of possible law and order issues. The problem could worsen as Punjab targets 180 LT of paddy procurement, against 156 LT last year. So, why does the crisis persist, why might it worsen, and what is the solution? We explain. Why is grain storage in Punjab under pressure? Essentially, a mismatch exists between grain supply and space. Punjab has around 175 LT of covered storage capacity, including what is available with the Food Corporation of India FCI, state procurement agencies and private facilities, besides 75 LT of plinth storage an open-air storage platform primarily used for wheat, where rice cannot be stored similarly. However, rice from previous kharif cycles June to October occupies most covered space. Consequently, 17 LT of wheat from the previous rabi season October to March remains in rice mills and mandi yards due to a lack of storage. Around 6 LT of previous-cycle rice is also pending for delivery by mills. Punjab handles 300320 LT of paddy and wheat annually, making regular movement to other states essential to create space for the next procurement cycle. How much grain needs to move out of Punjab - and how much is actually moving? Rice millers and state procurement agencies traditionally prefer paddy milling to be completed by March 31, as prolonged summer and monsoon storage increase infestation and deterioration risks. The Centres prescribed milling period generally runs from December 1 to June 30, though extensions are given when stocks remain pending. Even by June 30, Punjab would need to deliver about 120.6 LT of rice if it procures the targeted 180 LT of paddy. Over seven months, that means clearing around 17 LT a month. Against this target, officials say that current grain movement out of Punjab averages 1112 LT a month, comprising rice and wheat. The proportion varies, sometimes roughly 5050, while at other times one-third is rice. Could the problem worsen in the coming years? The immediate concern is that the backlog is carrying forward old stocks are not moving out while new paddy continues arriving. Last year, milling went on until September this year, the problem is more visible, with around 6 LT of previous-season rice pending for delivery, while 17 LT of wheat still occupies rice mills and mandi yards. With this trend of no movement, the overlap could double or triple in the coming years. What could be the solution? Both storage capacity and slow movement of grain are to be blamed, according to FCI and state procurement officials. Officials say constructing additional storage in Punjab is expensive because land rates are high. Punjab already has a substantial storage network, but it is not enough to handle the volume of grain procured in the state without regular emptying. When both the Centre and state governments are aware of the amount of grain procured from Punjab, why not create additional storage capacity - if not in Punjab, then outside Punjab? said a senior FCI official. Even if storage capacity is available in any part of the country, wheat can be transported directly from mandis to those locations. In the case of paddy, which is entirely housed by rice mills, the rice can be transported directly from mills to storage facilities elsewhere after milling. Officials point to Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, where land rates are comparatively lower and many storage facilities can be built. They argue that Punjab produces for the nation around 80 of the wheat produced and almost the entire paddy in Punjab goes to the central pool. Therefore, officials say, the storage burden need not be concentrated in Punjab, and suggest faster movement of grain to additional storage capacity outside Punjab.

articleTitle: Anti-EC protest | ‘They have entire career lying ahead’: Delhi court grants bail to 17 protesters arrested
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jantar Mantar protest
description: In four separate orders, Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Animesh Kumar of the Patiala House Court granted bail to the 17 accused.
body_raw: Granting bail to 17 people arrested by the Delhi Police during a protest in the Capital against Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Monday, a Delhi court late in the night sought a report from the DCP New Delhi on allegations that two of those arrested were beaten up at the Parliament Street police station. In four separate orders, Judicial Magistrate First Class JMFC Animesh Kumar of the Patiala House Court granted bail to the 17 accused. The accused persons are of very young age and do not appear to be habitual offenders. They have their entire career lying ahead, JMFC Kumar said. The police had submitted before the court that the protesters were part of an unlawful assembly and had blocked the public space when Section 163 of BNSS was in place, prohibiting public gatherings of five or more people, demonstrations and other activities without prior written permission. httpswww.youtube.comwatch?v-Hjn02Ty0kfeatureyoutu.be After two protesters told the court that they sustained injuries as they were beaten inside the Parliament Street police station after they were detained, JMFC Kumar sought that CCTV camera footage from inside the police station be preserved. Since accused Dharmender and Samarth have levelled allegations regarding custodial torture, let report be called from DCP New Delhi regarding the same. The relevant CCTV footage of PS Parliament Street be also preserved, he said. The Delhi Police submitted that when the accused were being detained to manage the law and order situation, they manhandled and assaulted police officers, during which one woman officer sustained injuries. Seeking 14 days of judicial custody, the police told the court that the protesters broke the glass of a bus in which they were being detained. They alleged that the protesters did not cooperate during the course of the investigation and failed to disclose their complete personal details. JMFC Kumar said, It should be noted that allegations against the accused are serious in nature. One police official has allegedly sustained injuries as per the MLC produced by the IO. While any person has right to protest peacefully, however, assaulting police officials on duty is serious concern which cannot be permitted under the garb of peaceful protest. However, it cannot be ignored that all the offences involved in the present case except offence punishable under Section 132 of BNS are bailable in nature. Even the offence punishable under Section 132 of BNS assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty provides for maximum imprisonment of 2 years only, he added.

articleTitle: Ashok Lavasa: Can the Election Commission untie knots of its own making?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: election commission
description: With high courts questioning some of its decisions, serving judges exhorting against mass disenfranchisement, former ECs/CECs questioning its conduct, the clouds over the ECI become thicker
body_raw: The Election Commission of India ECI is in a bind like never before. That it worked hard to get here is a pity. An organisation that endeared itself by its friendly approach over the years finds itself friendless. Its only friend, the ruling party, pushes it further into a corner each time it comes to its defence. The ECI is under attack from almost all quarters - people, civil society organisations, retired civil servants, former judges, practising lawyers, political parties. The print media has written hard-hitting editorials against the Special Intensive Revision SIR, and YouTubers have ready-made content as the ECI rides through this mire of its own making. The war within the ECI is in the public square with the Indian Express revealing cracks in an organisation in which confidence is crumbling. The 14 letters by the two Election Commissioners EC have pushed the Chief Election Commissioner CEC in the eye of the storm, even if the storm might rock their boats too. Every attempt of the ECI to explain away the controversy drags it deeper into the morass. With high courts questioning some of its decisions, serving judges exhorting against mass disenfranchisement, former ECsCECs questioning its conduct, the clouds over the ECI become thicker. The Shakespearean platitude, when sorrows come, they come not single spies, but in battalions, seems to be playing out, with petitions seeking the suspension of the CEC for his authoritarian ways admitted by the Supreme Court SC. As if this wasnt enough, hearing the petitions on October 5, the Chief Justice of India reportedly observed, No modified Form 6 has been approved by us. It is these modifications in Form 6 that one of the ECs termed illegal and unauthorised in his letter of August 14. The ECIs responses to the Indian Express report added to its miseries. The first response on September 23 was I plead not-guilty, claiming all decisions were unanimous. In its second response of September 26, the ECI climbed down but created confusion by admitting it used two versions of Form 6 for SIR and non-SIR purposes, asserting the SC upheld the changes. Soon, the ECI wilted and withdrew the declaration attached to Form 6 as if it was hiding the weapon used in the crime. The CJIs remark has fuelled the fire, with critics calling it a vindication of their allegations of arbitrary, illegal action of the CEC. However, supporters quickly found a shield in para 152 of the SCs May 27 judgement wherein it observed that Form 6 sets out a framework of documentation however, the same is tailored to the process of revision contemplated under Section 212 of the RP Act and may not, in all situations, be capable of literal application to an exercise of the present nature. The Commission, therefore, retains a degree of residual authority to formulate an appropriate documentation framework suited to the exigencies of a Special Intensive Revision. Such authority, however, is not unbounded. In devising such a framework, the Commission must remain cognisant of the existing statutory scheme, and any departure therefrom must be informed by a rational nexus to the object sought to be achieved. The formulation of the documentation regime must thus reflect a calibrated balance in drawing from the statutory framework, while adapting it, where necessary, to effectively serve the purpose of ensuring the accuracy and integrity of the electoral roll. This is legalese at its ambivalent best. Is the SC merely recognising the ECIs authority to formulate, not approve, an appropriate documentation framework for the SIR? At the same time, is it affirming the guardrails by stating that such authority is not unbounded, reminding it of the existing statutory scheme? If the ECI was deriving legitimacy from this SC order for the Form 6 changes it unilaterally made, why did the EC, nearly three months after the SC order, call them illegal and unauthorised? Did the ECI examine his objections and reaffirm its belief that the SC had legitimised the changes? One must try to untie a few knots the ECI has tied itself in and separate the strands in its most controversial decisions in the 75 years of its existence, namely conducting the SIR. Arguably an abrupt, aggressive and ambitious decision, it was largely perceived as unfair, exclusionary and arbitrary. If the ECI wants the people to believe the decision to conduct SIR was unanimous, it must put the minutes of the relevant ECI meeting in the public domain. The letters revealing the rift within the ECI dont necessarily oppose the SIR. The ECs apparently referred to the illegalities committed in changing Form 6, and denying access to the Electoral Registration Officers to the ECINet, impeding the performance of legally mandated duties. The ECs were already smarting as they felt excluded from the decision-making process, and the ECI neither held meetings for four months, nor circulated the agenda and minutes of meetings for a year. They were understandably perturbed that without their knowledge 16 lakh appeals were filed before the appellate tribunals against inclusion in the purified electoral roll of West Bengal. These made the ECIs functioning questionable. It is difficult to predict how the current drama will end but there is no doubt that it is tragic for Indian democracy. In its withering away, the once-hallowed institution of the ECI resembles Miltons Fallen Angels. It has itself to blame for its sorry plight and the opprobrium heaped upon it. The SC may set aside the ECIs decisions if it finds them illegal but whether that would lead to the CECECs losing their paradise will depend on whether a sin against democracy can be punished by a man-made system. Impeachment is politically fraught the call of the conscience is a far cry. Glory lies not in never falling but rising every time you fall, was a motivational quote inscribed on the walls of my school. I recently learnt it is from Oliver Goldsmiths The Citizen of the World 1762. Now I realise this applies as much to institutions as to individuals. The walls of many constitutional bodies qualify to have this quotation pasted on them. Let Nirvachan Sadan take the lead. The writer is a former election commissioner

articleTitle: On Rentiya Baras, university founded by Gandhi to take charkha to 350 schools
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rentiya Baras 2026
description: The Vidyapith has been celebrating Gandhi’s Hindu calendar birthday as Rentiya Baras for the past 90 years.
body_raw: Gujarat Vidyapith, the university founded by Mahatma Gandhi in Ahmedabad, will celebrate his birthday as per the Hindu calendar on Wednesday October 7. It will mark the celebration by taking charkha to 351 municipal schools to spread Gandhis message of Swadeshi, the university said. As per the Vikram Samvat calendar, Gandhi was born on Bhadarva Vad Baras the 12th day of the sixth month of the Hindu calendar, which is also known as Bhadrapada in 1925. The period corresponds to October 2, 1869, in the Gregorian calendar. The Vidyapith has been celebrating Gandhis Hindu calendar birthday as Rentiya Baras for the past 90 years. Rentiya is Gujarati for spinning wheel, which Gandhi used to spin khadi, turning it into a movement for self-reliance. Gandhi wanted to dedicate the day to charkha Gandhi had wished that his birthday be celebrated as Rentiya Baras. Associate Professor of Social Work at Gujarat Vidyapith Ravindra Pancholi said, When he was alive, Gandhis followers wanted to celebrate his birthday. However, Gandhi said that he did not like the idea of people remembering his birthday. Then, he suggested that the day his birthday as per the Vikram Samvat calendar could be marked as Rentiya Baras. Pancholi 55, who is the grandson of noted Gujarati writer and educationist Manubhai Pancholi Darshak, said Gandhi told his followers that if they loved him, then they should shun foreign clothes and adopt khadi and spin charkha. So, this tradition of celebrating Gandhis birthday, as per the Vikram Samvat calendar, as Rentiya Baras, and not as Mohan Jayanti or Gandhi Jayanti, started around 1929-30, Pancholi said. The celebration this year Around 200 volunteers and over 1,800 students of Gujarat Vidyapith are expected to visit 351 schools in 48 wards of Ahmedabad city. They will demonstrate the spinning wheel and explain its significance to students. Through this, they will talk about Mahatma Gandhis ideas of Swadeshi and self-reliance and reach out to more than 1,35,000 students, according to a statement by Gujarat Vidyapith. Vidyapith Public Relations Officer Advaita Dave said the university had been celebrating Rentiya Baras in different ways every year. Last year, our staff and students spun charkha at Sabarmati Riverfront for around one and a half hours. Apart from Swadeshi, the motive behind the celebration is to spread the message that spinning the charkha is a kind of yoga as well, Dave said. Pancholi said previously, students performed akhand kantan non-stop spinning on Rentiya Baras. They would take turns in batches of 20-25 and spin charkha continuously for 12 hours.

articleTitle: Telangana registers first FIR on ‘illegal’ Form 7s, BJP agent booked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ‘Was doing my duty’: BLO who stopped bulk submission of Form 7
description: The BJP booth level agent filed 30 Form 7s for deletion of names from electoral roll in Musheerabad Assembly constituency, all against Muslim voters.
body_raw: Police in Chikkadpally, Hyderabad, have registered an FIR against a Booth Level Agent BLA of the BJP for filing allegedly fraudulent form 7s against 30 people, all of them Muslim, in the Musheerabad Assembly constituency. The action comes a day ahead of the end of the claims and objections phase of the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral roll in the state. The FIR was filed against the BJPs S Balachander, on a complaint by Musheerabad Electoral Registration Officer ERO T Praveen Kumar Reddy, after a preliminary inquiry reportedly showed that the Form 7s submitted by him were pre-printed with names of the voters concerned. BJP rivals have called this proof that the Form 7s had been centrally generated from the BJP office. Similar forms with pre-printed voter information have also been reported in Bahadurpura and Goshamahal constituencies in Hyderabad. The 30 people against whom Balachander is said to have submitted Form 7s-for the deletion of names from electoral roll-include a Congress BLA. According to the FIR, the BJP BLA brought 30 pre-printed Form-7s and made efforts to submit them to the BLO, Polling Station No. 210, on September 28, 2026, with a mala fide intention for deleting voters not connected to him. The FIR adds that when the BLO and BLO Supervisor collectively refused to receive the forms, in spite of repeated requests from the said BLA of BJP, Balachander left the forms on the BLOs premises and fled. The officials said that a personal field verification by them on October 1 showed that all the 30 people whose names were flagged by the BLA were residents of Hyderabads Musheerabad. Therefore, the form-7s in question cannot be accepted and are liable for rejection, the FIR says. Balachander has been booked under Sections 217 and 3182 of the BNS, pertaining to giving false information to a government officer and cheating, and Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act 1950. On Monday, Telangana Chief Electoral Officer CEO C Sudarshan Reddy issued a memo asking district collectors and District Election Officers of the state to take action against those filing false Form 7s, saying instances of this had come to their notice. AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi claimed that in Goshamahal constituency too, false Form 7s had been filed to delete names of Muslim voters. Our request to the CEO is to not spare anyone who is spreading this hatred against Muslims, Owaisi said. BJP state president N Ramchander Rao has denied any attempts by the party to delete voters, accusing the Congress of misguiding the public against a constitutional institution like the Election Commission. Telangana had 3.39 crore voters before the Special Intensive Revision SIR process started on June 15. In the draft list, 73.39 lakh voters names were deleted and 92 lakh voters were sent notices. The final electoral roll is to be published on November 9.

articleTitle: ‘You need partners for strategic autonomy, you can’t do everything by yourself’: Finland envoy to India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Russia-Ukraine war Finland envoy
description: We are living in quite a turbulent time, when it comes to geopolitics and geoeconomics, said Finland Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski.
body_raw: As he weighs on the global consequences of the Russia-Ukraine war, new Finland Ambassador to India, Mikko Kivikoski, says they appreciate Indias efforts, and it is a situation where everybody else is ready to negotiate to stop the war except the Russians. He says the global community should incentivise Russia to come to the negotiation table and then to have this war ended. In an interview with Divya A, weeks after presenting his credentials to the President Alexander Stubb, Kivikoski weighs in on lessons from global conflicts and the US protectionism, why the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor IMEC is stuck, and the imminent need to reform the UN Security Council. Excerpts With protectionism rising from big powers like the US, what would be Finlands priorities in terms of the India-EU FTA, set to be operationalised in the coming months? The Free Trade Agreement FTA sends a clear and strong message that when it comes to international trade, rules-based trade is still beneficial for all of us. This applies to all the FTAs that both India and the European Union EU are signing with other partners as well. So, there is a strong signal that there are several countries that want to have rules in international trade. The US has imposed steep reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods and even on several EU goods. So, how does Finland assess the impact of all of this on global supply chains and on small, open economies? We are living in quite a turbulent time, when it comes to geopolitics and geoeconomics. Everybody is looking at partners and diversifying things - to make sure you have the freedom of manoeuvre, and also certain amount of predictability. We are all doing that - be it India, the EU or Finland. That is one of the lessons learned. India has been seeking from the EU to ease the CBAM, visa norms for professionals and even data protection. What is Finlands position on this? We are part of the EU, so we have been part of the decision making on the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism CBAM, and the same applies to the EU data protection laws. But we believe it is about level playing field, and sustainability in the long run. Many Indian companies are already adapting something I personally noticed is that sustainability issues are more on the agenda in India. Should India and Finland collaborate more on critical minerals and batteries? Because Finland has large reserves, India has demand. That is also part of the EU-Finland-India partnership. Again, it all comes down to the supply chain and strategic autonomy. And in that context, the EU and India see each other as trusted partners. And you need partners when it comes to strategic autonomy. You cannot do everything by yourself. With navigation disrupted due to war, especially in the Red Sea and the Black Sea, is there a scope for cooperation on alternative routes, maybe IMEC, mooted by India in 2023? Definitely, one of the consequences of the recent geopolitical, geoeconomical changes in the world is that, again, it all comes down to the supply chains and strategic autonomy. All the countries are looking for new logistic routes. They want to cut down dependencies. When it comes to this particular corridor, we all understand that there are several geopolitical issues at the moment. We have been supporting it from the beginning, but one has to be realistic. And when it comes to logistic routes, it must be feasible. For the time being, there are certain geopolitical issues in West Asia that are hindering it at the moment. You have been talking about resilient supply chains and strategic autonomy. Do you think globalisation, as we know, will change forever? I hope not. For a small country like us, we would like to see sort of rules and institutions when it comes to the international order. We would also like to see that world trade would be free. So, we are partnering with countries that have similar views. Finland, India and the EU have similar views when it comes to international order, as well as on multilateralism. India and Finland are definitely natural partners when it comes to multilateralism, the UN charter and the UN-based multilateralism. We would like to see India as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, and we believe that the Council needs to be reformed. India said that it is in touch with Russia and Ukraine to find a solution to the ongoing war, and the Ukrainian Foreign Minister has said they support Indias proposal. Have there been discussions between Kyiv and other EU partners on the proposal? Yeah, sort of two remarks on that. Firstly, all the attempts to bring the war to an end are highly appreciated and needed. As we all know, it has been underway, and it is already the 5th year. The global consequences are clear. Your External Minister has talked about the consequences multiple times, so that is clear. We are in a situation where everybody else is ready to negotiate - to stop the war - except the Russians. So basically, what we need is that the global community incentivises Russia to come to the negotiation table, and then to have the war ended. Incentivise, as in how would that work? To incentivise in terms of sanctions, or trade? Incentivise - that they would understand it is also for their best to stop the war because it is clear that the consequences for the Russian economy and the society are huge. At the end of the day, too many human beings are being lost in the war. You have arrived in New Delhi at a time when the India-EU relations are getting stronger, and the India-EU FTA is in the last leg before being signed. What do you think about the collaboration between New Delhi and Helsinki at this point? We have been witnessing record-high activities this year Finland Prime Minister Petteri Orpo visited India, President Alexander Stubb made a state visit to India, as well as we also had the Nordic-India Summit in Oslo. Then a few weeks ago in Gandhinagar, there was the 10th edition of the World Circular Economy Forum - organised for the first time in South Asia, by the governments of Finland and India. And when you add to that the FTA and the perspective of the agreement to be enforced next year, this creates a great momentum to deepen our collaboration. And therefore, our task here will be to turn this framework into concrete activities.

articleTitle: Union Cabinet hails 25 years of Modi at helm, flags ‘mandate, trust, his governance’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ‘Sir, please fix IRCTC captcha’: Students’ plea prompts Ashwini Vaishnaw to promise new railway ticketing website
description: Vaishnaw said the Prime Minister received a standing ovation from all Cabinet colleagues during the meeting.
body_raw: The Union Cabinet adopted a resolution Tuesday, hailing the enduring trust that the public have reposed in Narendra Modi and his governance achievements over the last 25 years, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat and later as Prime Minister of the country. Briefing reporters on the decisions of the Union Cabinet at its meeting Tuesday, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the resolution covers Modis unbroken public service record, spanning the period from October 7, 2001, when he first assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat, to his continuous tenure as Prime Minister up to October 7, 2026. Vaishnaw said the Prime Minister received a standing ovation from all Cabinet colleagues during the meeting. The resolution congratulated Modi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. An official statement on the resolution stated Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrates the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by the principle of Nation First and Citizen First. Three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive Lok Sabha elections reflect the enduring trust that the public have reposed in PM Narendra Modi. The statement listed ten salient features of his leadership of Gujarat and India. The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarats successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigrams separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarats experience across India. His sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels, it stated. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity, it stated. His determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became Lakhpati Didis, while the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for womens reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded Rs 4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind, it stated. The resolution lays particular emphasis on Modis willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. His appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. Reform emerges as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose, it stated. Under Modis leadership, public capital expenditure rose from Rs 2 lakh crore to over Rs 12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around Rs 2 lakh crore to more than Rs 13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen Indias ability to meet its needs, it stated. Modis faith in technology, it said, emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. Developing Indias own Covid vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moons south pole demonstrated PM Modis vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant Atmanirbhar Bharat. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities. The resolution highlights Modis ability to give India direction through global upheavals. During Covid, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption. His leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times. The resolution cited the 2016 surgical strikes, the 2019 Balakot air strikes and the 2025 Operation Sindoor as national security red lines established under Modi. The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, One Rank One Pension and creation of the Chief of Defence Staffs post. Action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability and public trust, the statement said. The resolution links Indias rising stature with Modis ability to build cooperation across divisions. Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Unions G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how Indias capabilities could serve others. Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and Indias growing influence and contribution to shared solutions, it stated. Modis vision, it said, unites development, cultural confidence and environmental responsibility. Climate action progressed from Gujarats dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships. Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Ram Lallas consecration strengthened Indias connection with its heritage. The resolution culminates in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant and developed India by 2047, it stated. Modis approach to disaster management was also hailed Tuesday. Gujarat was recovering from the devastating Bhuj earthquake that struck just months before Modi became Chief Minister. He set a three-year recovery target and a move towards mitigation. An Institute of Seismological Research was established in 2003. As Prime Minister, he released the countrys first National Disaster Management Plan in 2016. He articulated a 10-point agenda for Disaster Risk Reduction at the Asian Ministerial Conference in New Delhi, calling for technology and mobile-based warnings, wider risk coverage and greater international cooperation. The governments focus also moved to early warnings and zero casualty. A multi-hazard early warning system was launched under Modis tenure and the India Meteorological Department has been providing district-level, impact-based and risk-based warnings while an indigenous multi-hazard decision support system has been operational since 2023. At the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019, India also launched the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, which today has 59 member countries and 13 partner organisations. India has also deployed search and rescue teams at disaster sites, notably in Nepal in 2015 and 2026, in Turkiye and Syria after the 2023 earthquake.

articleTitle: Cabinet clears Rs 10,000 crore fund to support small, medium enterprises
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SME Growth Fund
description: The fund, first announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27, aims to provide enterprises with equity support.
body_raw: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the Small and Medium Enterprise SME Growth Fund SGF with an outlay of Rs 10,000 crore to provide equity support to small and medium enterprises. The fund was first announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27. According to the government, while several existing funds provide equity support to businesses, most of them focus on early-stage enterprises and largely cater to micro enterprises. This has left a structural gap in the availability of growth-stage equity capital for small and medium enterprises. While various initiatives have enhanced access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital required by enterprises seeking to scale, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions, and transform into industry leaders, the government said in a statement. The SME Growth Fund is designed to address this critical financing gap by providing patient growth equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability, it added. Under the initiative, the government will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs 10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund AIF established under the SGF framework. A majority of the funds investments will be directed towards small and medium manufacturing enterprises, with a focus also on SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Investments across industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, will support balanced regional industrial development, reinforce local supply chains and generate high-quality employment opportunities, it said. The Centre expects the fund to help SMEs scale up, improve productivity and strengthen export competitiveness by enabling manufacturing enterprises to expand capacity, adopt advanced technologies and achieve greater scale. India SME Forum in a note said the fund is critical for the MSME as they are facing structural and severe capital gaps. They have been over-dependent on debt financing and have weak integration with the global value chain, the forum said. The SME growth fund could help mobilisation of institutional capital and creation of globally competitive mid-sized champions, it said. Vinod Kumar, President, India SME Forum said the Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund can set in motion a powerful cycle, where stronger manufacturers place larger and more consistent orders with smaller suppliers, enabling those businesses to invest in better machinery, improve quality, build skills and create jobs. As these capabilities deepen across industrial clusters, more MSMEs can meet the standards required by large domestic buyers and global supply chains. The cumulative outcome can be higher domestic value addition, greater export competitiveness and reduced dependence on imported components and finished products, Kumar said. Experts said the fund is critical for the MSME as they are facing structural gaps and severe capital gaps and have been over-dependent on debt financing and have weak integration with the global value chain. Sandeep Jain, an auto-component manufacturer and former President of Federation of Indian Micro and Small Medium Enterprises FISME said the growth fund would give motivation to SMEs to grow and not be overtly concerned with the financing. The route of investment via an AIF is also very innovative. I am sure it will give great dividends,Jain said. The SME growth fund was announced by the Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during the Budget presentation earlier this year, to ensure timely payments to SMEs. I propose to introduce a dedicated Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund, to create future Champions, incentivising enterprises based on select criteria. I also propose to top up the Self-Reliant India Fund set up in 2021, with Rs 2,000 crore to continue support to micro enterprises and maintain their access to risk capital, Sitharaman said while presenting the Budget.

articleTitle: CBI books OSD to Punjab CM for graft, searches Mann’s ‘camp office’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajbir Singh Guman, an OSD to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann
description: Searches come hours after Supreme Court agreed to hear a Punjab govt challenge to HC order directing CBI probe into corruption allegations
body_raw: The CBI on Tuesday registered a corruption case against Rajbir Singh Guman, an OSD to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, and other senior officials and conducted searches at eight locations, including Manns camp office in Chandigarh, officials said. Mann said that the BJP has started preparing for Punjab elections and was now resorting to central agencies to target him and his government. The CBI, in a statement, said that following the orders of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, and receipt of report from the Enforcement Directorate, it has registered an FIR to investigate the allegations of corruption against OSD to Punjab Chief Minister CM and his associates for influencing and manipulating postings of officers including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits. It is also alleged that the accused public servants purportedly accessed and provided drafts of orders and policies to private persons prior to their issuance by the government, the CBI statement said, adding the agency has booked six persons, including two public servants. They include Ghuman, alleged middleman Nitin Gohal, Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder, RS Nagra and unknown public servants and private persons, it added. The central agency carried out raids at House No. 50, the camp office allotted to Mann under the Chief Ministers pool, where Ghuman had been staying. It also conducted searches at Ghumans residence in Gharachon in Sangrur district apart from locations in Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, and Jalandhar connected with the accused persons. Incriminating evidence such as laptops, mobile phones and documents have been seized. These are being scrutinized for evidence of bribery and impropriety. Further investigation in the case is in progress, read the CBI statement. The raids came hours after the Supreme Court agreed to hear a Punjab government plea challenging a Punjab and Haryana High Courts order directing the CBI to investigate Ghuman and others. The high court, in its order on Monday, had held that material shared by the ED with Punjab DGP in the matter prima facie indicated their involvement in acts of corruption, including cash for transfers and cash for favourable orders. The state filed a Special Leave Petition at around 2am in the Supreme Court against the HC order. Reacting to the development, Mann, in a post on X, said, BJP has started preparing for the Punjab elections.CBI raided my camp office. Now, ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab, so that Punjab government and I can be defamed. Seeing the love we are getting from the people, BJP is nervous, Mann said. The high court order came on on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, who had sought an independent probe into the matter raised by the ED with the Punjab Police in its letters to the DGP. The ED had written to the DGP seeking registration of an FIR against an alleged middleman and others, reportedly linked to the Chief Ministers Office, for allegedly influencing transfers and postings of government officials, facilitating arms licence approvals, leaking confidential government documents and securing government approvals in lieu of alleged monetary and other benefits. The EDs letters stem from a money laundering investigation linked to the submission of alleged fake consent letters for obtaining Change of Land Use CLU in a case involving a housing society. The ED had conducted searches on the premises of Nitin Gohal, Ajay Sehgal of Indian Cooperative House Building Society, the Suntec City Project and some others in May. The agency had submitted 200-page affidavit in the high court on the PIL filed by Saraf. The searches took place against the backdrop of an escalating confrontation between the Punjab government and central investigative agencies. The Mann government has repeatedly accused the Centre of using the ED and CBI to target opposition-ruled states, while the BJP has rejected such allegations and maintained that investigative agencies act independently.

articleTitle: Arvind Swamy says wife Aparna is ‘bubbly and energetic’: ‘I am introverted, need my space’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arvind swamy photo with second wife aparna
description: Arvind Swamy opened up about his marriage to Aparna, saying she is extroverted while he is introverted, and explained how they make their differences work.
body_raw: Actor Arvind Swamy has opened up about his marriage, his equation with his wife Aparna Mukerjee and the understanding that keeps their relationship strong. Describing himself as an introvert and his wife as an outgoing, bubbly and energetic person, the Meiyazhagan actor spoke about how they have learnt to respect each others differences, give each other space and trust each others judgement. He also opened up on parenting, saying that children may remember how their parents treated them far more than the sacrifices they made for them. She knows that I need the space In a conversation with Gobinath, Arvind Swamy said Aparna is very different from him when it comes to their personalities. While he considers himself an introvert, he described his wife as someone who is naturally social and comfortable around people. My wife knows me. She talks a lot. She is a very extroverted person. She is friendly with everyone. Everyone likes her. She is a very bubbly and energetic character. I am very introverted. I am extroverted when it comes to my friends otherwise, I am a very quiet person. I dont engage a lot, he said. According to Arvind, understanding this difference has helped them give each other the space they need. He said Aparna does not force him to attend social gatherings when she knows he would rather stay away. She knows that I need the space, so she wont force me to come. This usually happens. There is not much pressure, he said. However, there are times when she tells him that it would be nice if he accompanied her. The actor said he trusts her enough to understand that such a request usually has a reason behind it. At times, she says that it would be nice if I come. I trust her that she has put a lot of thought into it. I trust that it is important to her, so I would go, he said. The actor said he can also recognise when his presence is important at a family function, birthday or another occasion. I have analysed it, and there seems to be an obligation or a requirement behind wanting me to come, either for a function, event or a birthday. If they call me to meet family or anyone, I have that trust. I wont say that I wont come, he said. Arvind said such requests should not become a source of resentment or something partners keep track of. We must not register it like an obligation. If you want to go, you can go. If not, you can tell them. There should not be any issue because of this. Similarly, I would be happy. She can be happy only if I can be happy I can be happy only if she is happy, he said. Arvind Swamy believes that partners need to complement each other and be willing to acknowledge their mistakes. Both must complement each other. When you make a mistake, you must have the courage to admit it. There must be a positive contribution, where you suggest an alternative to the other person. Similarly, they must be understanding of each other as well, he said. ALSO READ Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity Arvind Swamy on parenting The actor also spoke about how stress from work and other responsibilities can affect family relationships. He admitted that there was a point when the pressure he carried would spill over into his interactions with his children. At one point, due to a lot of tension and pressure, when I am with my kids, the tension and pressure gets translated into the relationship, he said. He explained that people can unconsciously transfer their stress to those around them. When she sees me, I would either be irritated or preoccupied, or I might be in a situation where I have to address a few important things. We will unconsciously transfer it. The kids or people around us will feel that, he said. Arvind said he eventually realised that taking care of himself was important not just for his own well-being but also for his relationships. Only if I take care of myself and be happy can I transfer this happiness. I understood that after a long time. The actor, however, does not believe that being responsible towards a family means giving up every personal need. The mindset of having to sacrifice everything - Let me work out for an hour or I have to get some fresh air - all this is important for sanity. When you come back from this, your interaction will be better with the people around you. If you constantly live in tension, how will your interaction be? Everything will be work-related problems, everything will be an interference. You will be giving out these messages, he said. Your kids will only remember how you spoke to them Arvind Swamy went on to speak about what children eventually remember about their parents. He said parents may spend years thinking about the sacrifices they made, while children may remember something much more basic - how their parents spoke to them. Thirty or 40 years will pass by quickly. At that point, you might not be working. At that point, your kids will only remember that whenever they tried to speak to you, you only spoke out of irritation, he said. He pointed out that parents can become focused on the hard work they put in for their children without realising that their children may have a very different memory of those years. You will be thinking of all the hard work you put in. You will be thinking that you sacrificed your happiness for them. This disconnect - you would have worked and done stuff, but could have spoken to me with a smile. Isnt that what makes them happy? According to Arvind, this difference in perspective is often at the heart of the disconnect between parents and children. So this disconnect happens because people have different perspectives. How much I have sacrificed is not whats important. Do what is important to you, he said. He believes making time for things that bring personal happiness or peace is important because otherwise that frustration can spill over into relationships. For that, do whatever makes you feel better. You have to allocate some time to it. If not, you will be transferring all that to others, he said. Arvind Swamys first marriage, children and custody Arvind Swamy married Gayathri Ramamurthy in 1994. The couple have two children, daughter Adhira and son Rudra. They separated in 2003 and later sought divorce by mutual consent. During the divorce proceedings, the couple agreed that their children would remain in the actors custody, while Gayathri would have visitation rights. Their divorce was granted in 2010. Arvind married lawyer Aparna Mukerjee in 2012.

articleTitle: UPSC Prelims 2027 Polity Quiz (Week 183): MCQs on removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, Mahanadi water dispute, and more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Prelims 2027 Polity Quiz (Week 183)
description: Are you preparing for UPSC CSE 2027 Prelims? Check your progress and revise your topics through this quiz on Polity and Governance.
body_raw: UPSC Essentialsbrings to you its initiative of daily subject-wise quizzes. These quizzes are designed to help you revise some of the most important topics from the static part of the syllabus. Attempt todays subject quiz onPolity and Governanceto check your progress. Your trust, feedback and continued support have shaped the magazine and encouraged us to keep improving with every edition. Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026. QUESTION 1 With reference to the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner CEC, consider the following statements 1. A motion for the removal of the CEC can be initiated in either House of Parliament through a notice of motion signed by at least 100 members of the Lok Sabha or 50 members of the Rajya Sabha. 2. The CEC can be removed from office only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. 3. The CEC can be removed only on the ground of proven misbehavior or incapacity. How many of the statements given above are correct? a Only one b Only two c All three d None Relevance The question tests the constitutional provisions governing the appointment, tenure and removal of the Chief Election Commissioner. It is relevant to Article 324, particularly the special protection accorded to the CEC to ensure the independence of the Election Commission. Explanation - Article 3245 of the Constitution states that the CEC can be removed from office only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Going by Article 1244 of the Constitution, which contains the process for removing a Supreme Court judge, removal can only be on the ground of proved misbehavior or incapacity. Misbehaviour can comprise any corrupt practices or abuse of office. Over the years, courts have interpreted this to include actions which are incompatible with the office of the CEC or the CECs failure to discharge her official duties. Incapacity refers to a situation where the officer is unable to perform her duties. Hence, statement 3 is correct. - To initiate the removal of the CEC, members of both Houses must bring a notice of motion explicitly alleging misbehaviour or incapacity. To be admitted, an impeachment motion needs to be signed by at least 100 MPs in the Lok Sabha and 50 in the Rajya Sabha. They can consult people and materials to refuse or admit the motion. If the motion is admitted, an enquiry is conducted to examine the validity of the charges. This involves forming a committee to investigate evidence of misbehaviour or incapacity. Hence, statement 1 is correct. - The motion for removal must secure the support of a majority of the total membership of each House and be passed by a two-thirds majority present and voting in both Houses of Parliament. Once passed successfully, the President orders the removal of the CEC. - There is no discretion once the constitutional requirements are met, since the President acts on the advice of Parliament in this context. Therefore, option c is the correct answer. QUESTION 2 Which of the following states are involved in the Mahanadi water dispute? 1. Telangana 2. Odisha 3. Madhya Pradesh 4. Chhattisgarh Select the correct answer using the codes given below a 1 and 2 only b 2, 3 and 4 only c 2 and 4 only d 1, 2, and 4 only Relevance The question tests knowledge of inter-State river water disputes and the geographical course of the Mahanadi River. It is relevant to Indian Geography, federalism and mechanisms for resolving inter-State water disputes. Explanation - The Mahanadi water dispute between Odisha and Chhattisgarh is back in the spotlight, with the Odisha government signalling that the two BJP-ruled states are moving closer to an amicable solution, even as the Opposition BJD has called this bid an eyewash. The Mahanadi is a lifeline for millions of people in both the States. - A meeting between the two CMs was also held in July under the chairmanship of the Union Jal Shakti Minister. At the meeting, the states agreed to share data and information on their respective water requirements with the Central Water Commission. - For Odisha, the Mahanadi is more than a water-sharing dispute. The river is central to irrigation, drinking water, flood management, hydropower and the states broader negotiations with Chhattisgarh and the Centre. Therefore, option c is the correct answer. QUESTION 3 Consider the following Articles of the Constitution of India 1. Article 1943 - It grants legislatures certain privileges and immunities. 2. Article 191b - It guarantees freedom of speech and expression. Which of the articles given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance The question tests knowledge of Fundamental Rights under Article 19 and privileges and immunities of State Legislatures under Article 194. It helps strengthen understanding of constitutional provisions relating to State Legislatures and legislative privileges. Explanation - The Supreme Court will begin hearing a long-pending reference on the scope of legislative privileges, special powers and immunities enjoyed by Parliament and state legislatures to protect their functioning, and whether they can be invoked against citizens, journalists and others on breaching the privileges of the House. At the heart of the case is whether these privileges, under Articles 105 and 194 of the Constitution, can override fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and expression under Article 19. - A seven-judge Constitutional Bench comprising the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Aravind Kumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul M Pancholi, Chandrashekhar and V Mohana will hear the matter. - Article 1943 of the Constitution grants legislatures certain privileges and immunities. Article 191a guarantees freedom of speech and expression, including press freedom. The case turns on the interplay between these two rights and whether legislative privilege can override the right to free speech. Hence, 1 is correct and 2 is not correct. - Articles 14 and 21 provide for the right to equality and the right to life. The petitioners argue that when legislatures order arrests or imprisonment for alleged breaches of privilege, they affect personal liberty. According to them, any action affecting liberty must satisfy constitutional guarantees of fairness, due process and protection against arbitrariness. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. QUESTION 4 With reference to the Bye-Elections also known as bypolls, consider the following statements 1. The winner of a by-election serves a full 5-year term. 2. A bypoll is not mandatory if the remaining term of the house is less than 1 year. 3. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, by-elections must be held within 3 months of the vacancy occurring, barring specific legal exceptions. How many of the statements given above are correct? a Only one b Only two c All three d None Relevance The question tests understanding of the constitutional and statutory framework governing by-elections in India. It is relevant to Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, including the time limit and exceptions for conducting bypolls. Explanation - Bye-Elections also known as bypolls are used to fill elected offices that have become vacant between general elections. - The elected representative serves only the remainder of the term left by the predecessor. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. - A bypoll is not mandatory if the remaining term of the house is less than 1 year, or if the Election Commission certifies that holding it is impractical due to extraordinary circumstances. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Under Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, by-elections must be held within 6 months of the vacancy occurring, barring specific legal exceptions. Hence, statement 3 is not correct. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. Source www.eci.gov.in QUESTION 5 With reference to the Legislative Councils in India, consider the following statements 1. The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed one-half 50 per cent of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State. 2. The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State shall in no case be less than forty. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance The question tests knowledge of the constitutional provisions governing Legislative Councils under Article 171. It is relevant for understanding State legislature, bicameralism and constitutional provisions related to State legislatures. Explanation - The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed one-thirdof the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. - Provided that the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State shall in no case be less than forty. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Of the total number of members of the Legislative Council of a State- a as nearly as may be, one-third shall be elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards and such other local authorities in the State as Parliament may by law specify b as nearly as may be, one-twelfth shall be elected by electorates consisting of persons residing in the State who have been for at least three years graduates of any university in the territory of India or have been for at least three years in possession of qualifications prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament as equivalent to that of a graduate of any such university c as nearly as may be, one-twelfth shall be elected by electorates consisting of persons who have been for at least three years engaged in teaching in such educational institutions within the State, not lower in standard than that of a secondary school, as may be prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament d as nearly as may be, one-third shall be elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State from amongst persons who are not members of the Assembly e the remainder shall be nominated by the Governor. Therefore, option b is the correct answer.
