articleTitle: Exchanged cash, and a ‘chemical trap’: How ACB caught a Bengal official taking Rs 20k bribe
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Bengal ACB bribe trap
description: The arrest of a Sub-Assistant Engineer while accepting bribe in West Bengal has shed light on a new 'chemical trap' operation being used by the Anti-Corruption Bureau.
body_raw: A Sub-Assistant Engineer attached to the West Bengal State Rural Development Agency WBSRDA in Hooghly was caught red-handed by the Anti-Corruption Branch ACB while accepting a bribe of Rs 20,000 inside the Zilla Parishad Office in Chinsurah on Tuesday. The operation was initiated following a complaint lodged by a government contractor who had executed a road construction project under the Panchayat Project, valued at approximately Rs 1 crore. The work order for the project was issued in 2023, and construction was completed towards the end of 2025. Subsequently, the contractor approached the officials concerned, seeking the refund of the Earnest Money deposited during the tender process, at which point the official allegedly demanded an illegal gratification to facilitate the release of the funds. Acting on the complaint, ACB officers laid a chemical trap at the Zilla Parishad Office in Chinsurah on Tuesday. The official was intercepted on the spot while accepting a sum of Rs 20,000 from the complainant. Officers seized the entire bribe amount from the Sub-Assistant Engineer, and took him into custody. Further legal proceedings and investigation into the matter are currently underway under relevant provisions of law. In a similar incident in August this year, the ACB officials had arrested another Sub-Assistant Engineer posted at the Jamboni BDO office in Jhargram district for allegedly accepting a bribe of Rs 2 lakh. The engineer was caught red-handed inside his office during another chemical trap operation after demanding illegal gratification from a sub-contractor to clear pending bills related to the construction of a local sub-health centre. The chemical trap operation These days, the Bengal ACB has been relying on a simple chemical test to catch officials red-handed while taking bribes. Before a raid, officers dust the bribe money with phenolphthalein, an almost invisible, fine white powder that adheres to the paper without leaving any visible trace or odour. When the target accepts the cash, the chemical transfers onto their hands, unnoticed. Once the exchange takes place, ACB officers step in and simply ask the suspect to dip their fingers into a bowl of clear, colourless liquid - a basic solution of sodium carbonate. The moment the suspects hands touch the liquid, the invisible chemical reacts with the alkaline base, instantly turning the clear water into a vibrant, bright pink. The rapid colour transformation serves as irrefutable forensic evidence, proving physical possession of the marked notes even if the official denies accepting the bribe. It is done to also send a message of zero tolerance towards corruption, and that anyone caught red-handed will have to face the law, an official said.

articleTitle: Bhuvneshwar Kumar is back, four years on, with the 2027 World Cup in view
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhuvneshwar Kumar
description: India recall the 36-year-old seamer for the T20I tour of New Zealand, and ask whether his body can take the load of ODI cricket again
body_raw: The decision to include Bhuvneshwar Kumar in the T20I squad for tour of New Zealand might have come out of the blue. But the call-up has been gathering pace over the last three months, particularly after the 36-year-olds IPL 2026, where he took 28 wickets and finished one behind Kagiso Rabada in the race for the purple cap. It was during the tour of the UK, after Harshit Rana picked up an injury again, that Bhuvneshwars name started doing the rounds. It is close to four years since Bhuvneshwar last played for India. It was not a case of him suddenly losing his place his last Test was in January 2018, his last ODI in January 2022, and by November that year he was out of the T20I set-up as well. In the domestic circuit, his appearances of late have been limited to the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20s and the IPL, where he has bowled Royal Challengers Bengaluru to successive titles. The India call-up still appeared far-fetched. But here he is again, back in Indias T20I squad for the tour of New Zealand, and not because the first-choice players are busy with other commitments. There is a big picture that Indias team management is hoping Bhuvneshwar will help complete. With India clearly short on balance, there are conversations around the possibility of making the seamer part of the 2027 World Cup. While there is little to no doubt regarding Bhuvneshwars skills and what he offers with the ball, the only question is whether his body can take the load of playing ODI cricket again. He last played the Vijay Hazare Trophy in 2023, and if he is to be considered seriously for next years World Cup in southern Africa, it is understood that India want to see where he stands in terms of fitness and whether he can take the extra load. ALSO READ Bhuvneshwar Kumar to captain star-studded India in 2026 Hong Kong Sixes He knows it himself, and he wants another World Cup. 100 per cent. You cant beat the feeling of playing in a World Cup, whichever sport it may be, he told Jatin Saprus YouTube channel recently. My body is ready. Ive physio and trainer at home. At this moment, Im ready. Im training, but not keeping the 50-over World Cup on mind, but because I want to. If the selection happens I would be happy. If it doesnt happen, I wont be disappointed, he said. At the end of a long conversation, asked what he might have changed about his career, Bhuvneshwar paused and said where it went wrong. I would have hired the trainer and physio a while back. I wish they were there much earlier with me, he said. Whether that lack of work off the field is why successive team managements looked past him, despite what he brought to the table, is a fair question. But over the last couple of years, the work he has put in has shown in the middle. He has looked unplayable, making the new ball talk with the movement. From Sachin Tendulkar to Virat Kohli, there has been admiration for how Bhuvneshwar exposed batsmen from different eras with his movement off the new ball the wobble seam landing on the surface and moving either way, as he intended. Off the field, Bhuvneshwar appeared more spiritual, a believer in destiny. When I was young, everything was about cricket, want to play for India and take all wickets. But over the years it has changed. I dont recall a game where I went in thinking Ive to take five wickets and I did. So Im someone who believes in destiny. What is written for me will happen. My focus is always on preparation. Ive become more spiritual, he said. He had stopped thinking about comebacks, but he firmly believed he was still a player worth considering. Of course, he said when asked if he should be part of the selection conversations. Im not playing to prove anything, but Id be happy to play for India again. Ive packed my India jersey and kept it. Im emotional at the same time Im not emotional. I wont keep looking at the jersey. I wasnt hurt, and I knew what was happening. I was at peace. My family played a big part in keeping it easy. They dont say anything. They just carried on with daily routine so that played a big part for me, he said of the years he spent in the wilderness. Now, out of nowhere, Bhuvneshwar has an opening. Rarely does Indian cricket go back to a cricketer, particularly a fast bowler, it believed it had moved on from, after four long years. But then not all are Bhuvneshwar Kumar. I have changed a lot as a bowler. When I came in, Id swing, but not much of pace. Without pace, to survive in the death overs with accuracy and perfection isnt possible. I always felt Id to increase the pace, but didnt know how to do it. So the big difference now is pace. It comes with experience. There is a big difference between what I was and what Im now, he said.

articleTitle: Stop daily drama, learn from Modi to win people’s support: BJP to Congress
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Modi
description: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju said Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, should learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP on securing people’s support on the basis of work instead of relying on “drama”.
body_raw: Describing the Congress protest against the Election Commission of India as drama, the BJP Tuesday slammed the principal Opposition party and leaders of non-NDA parties who had joined it of abusing the Commission after failing to secure the mandate of the people. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju said Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, should learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP on securing peoples support on the basis of work instead of relying on drama. It is time to stop the drama that Rahul Gandhi ji and his colleagues keep doing daily against the Election Commission and the Supreme Court. It has been going on since 2014. In a democracy, serve the people and you will get their mandate, he said. You call the Election Commission a thief, the government a thief. This will neither serve democracy nor the rise of the Congress party again. I especially want to tell Rahul Gandhi ji Learn from Modi ji, from BJP karyakartas who continue to serve, not for their own sakes but selflessly. If you serve them, you will earn the trust of the people. Doing this drama will not help, he said. Asking the Congress to stop peddling the narrative of anti-national forces, Rijiju sought to underline that the party which ruled the country for 55 years, including two years of the Emergency, was now talking of democracy. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said the Opposition leaders were venting their frustration over electoral defeats by levelling baseless allegations. Friends in the Opposition, the very system you are questioning is the one under which you won in Kerala. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Karnataka. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Himachal. Was that victory illegitimate? Opposition governments were formed in Punjab and Jharkhand. Were those victories illegitimate? he said. If you question constitutional institutions, you will commit the sin of plunging the country into the fires of anarchy. Do not commit the sin of plunging the nation into unrest and anarchy. The country and its people will never forgive you, he said. Lok Sabha MP and former Union Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad said Rahul Gandhi, Congress, and the Opposition alliance were attempting to create an atmosphere of anarchy in the country. He said the Supreme Court had held the SIR to be legally valid yet the Congress was insulting the voters of the country by blaming the Election Commission for its repeated electoral defeats. Instead of accepting the peoples verdict, the Congress is trying to undermine democratic institutions and create confusion and disorder through unfounded accusations, Prasad said. The question is whether Rahul Gandhi, the Congress party, and the Opposition alliance want anarchy in the country. Opposition leaders have gathered in Delhi and surrounded a sensitive area of the national Capital. Opposition leaders are claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Mohan Bhagwat have Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar under their control. This is extremely irresponsible, and we strongly condemn it, he said. He said Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had gone even further and said that all elections should be cancelled and conducted again through ballot papers which reflects their real intention and desire. Congress leaders cannot win fair elections and, therefore, they now want a return to booth capturing, stamping, and winning elections through pressure by pouring ink into ballot boxes. They want to prevent the poor, Dalits and marginalised sections from voting in villages. This is how the Congress used to win, whether in Bihar or Uttar Pradesh, he said. Addressing the media at the party headquarters, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra said, The Congress has been repeatedly trying to launch and re-launch Rahul Gandhi by any means necessary. When, despite numerous attempts, he failed to gain traction, the Congress and some of its allies decided that even if it meant resorting to anarchy and undermining the nations democracy, they would launch Rahul Gandhi politically at any cost. In the evening, after the Election Commission issued a statement saying no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm Tuesday and that it was later informed by police that Opposition MPs wanted a meeting at Parliament House Annexe, BJP spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed Gandhi It is clear that telling the EC anything was not his intention. Neither did he seek any appointment, and when time was given, he did not go. After that, when it was said that a representative would be sent to collect a memorandum from him, he was not ready.

articleTitle: Paramount and Warner Bros are now one Hollywood giant: Skydance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Paramount and Warner Bros are now one Hollywood giant: Skydance
description: Paramount, owned by Skydance, has completed its $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, with the deal officially closing on Tuesday.
body_raw: Its official Skydance-owned Paramount has closed its 81 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. The companies completed the deal on Tuesday, ushering in a new Hollywood giant with the now shorter Skydance nametag. The merger brings two of Americas oldest moviemaking studios together. And HBO Max, titles ranging from Harry Potter to Sinners and even networks like CNN find themselves under the same roof as Paramount, CBS and the likes of Top Gun and The Godfather. All of them will come under the helm of billionaire David Ellison, and his new co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. That further concentrates power in an industry already run by just a handful of major players. Ellisons Skydance bought out Paramount for 8 billion just last year, and set its sights on Warner - an even bigger fish - very soon after. What followed erupted into a tumultuous, roughly year-long fight over Warners fate. Skydance Corp. emerges from one of the biggest tie-ups ever in the media and entertainment industry. Including billions of dollars in debt, the Warner acquisition amounted to nearly 111 billion. Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry, Ellison said in a statement Tuesday. We couldnt be more excited to get to work. Heres a look at some of the key moments that got us here. Netflix vs Paramount The early days of Paramounts quest for Warner turned into a messy bidding war. Months after disclosing it was open to selling parts or even all of its business, Warner initially struck a studio and streaming deal with Netflix back in December. But Skydance-owned Paramount, which claimed Warner management never engaged meaningfully with its previous proposals, soon launched a hostile counterbid aimed at taking over the entire company - including networks like CNN and Discovery. The Hollywood giants spent much of early 2026 in a heated back-and-forth over who had a stronger offer on the table, with Warner leadership repeatedly backing Netflix as its preferred suitor. But Paramount eventually upped its offer to buy all of Warner for 31 per share, and Netflix opted to bow out of the race. Warner and Paramount inked a mutual merger agreement by late February. ALSO READ Tom Cruise calls Digger an honour as it bombs with 20 mn opening, set to lose 150 mn The response from Hollywood Hollywood was closely watching the fight over Warners future. And from awards shows to online petitions, A-list celebrities and other creatives made their voices known. In April, thousands of movie stars, writers, directors and other professionals announced their unequivocal opposition to the Paramount-Warner merger. The open letter - which was signed by long-outspoken critics of the deal like Jane Fonda and Mark Ruffalo, as well as Hollywood heavyweights from Denis Villeneuve to J.J. Abrams - warned of fewer jobs and less choice for audiences in the United States and around the world. Meanwhile, some other stars lined up to back Paramount as Ellison reiterated his commitments to the movies. At CinemaCon this past spring, the company debuted a glossy mini movie about the studio directed by Jon M. Chu and narrated by Tom Cruise - who ended the spot atop the iconic Paramount water tower, with the words the future is paramount and the future looks pretty great from here. Director James Cameron also doubled down on his support of Ellison. The prospect of a new Warner owner also loomed over awards season this year, from BlockTheMerger pins to more subtle nods in acceptance speeches. When accepting her Emmy last month, Remarkably Bright Creatures actor Sally Field - who also signed the open letter in opposition to the Paramount-Warner deal - stressed that unique storytelling matters and we cant let those voices be silenced, or compromised or merged. Many industry critics were also outspoken when Netflixs studio and streaming deal was on the table, with particular focus on the future of movies staying in theaters. Trump and CNN Donald Trump has regularly attacked reporting he deems unfavorable at CNN most recently attempting to bar the outlet from the White House altogether. And over the course of the Warner buyout, his administration wasnt afraid to chime in about hopes for a new owner. In December - days after Paramount launched its hostile bid for Warner - the president said that CNN spread poison and lies, adding that I think the people who have run CNN for the last long period of time are a disgrace and its imperative that CNN be sold. The White House took aim again at CNN in March, over the networks coverage of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. At the time, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told reporters that the sooner David Ellison takes over that network, the better. Ellison has said editorial independence will be maintained at CNN, and under a since-finalized settlement with the states, the company also agreed to form a News Editorial Independence Board. But critics point to turmoil already seen at CBS under Skydance ownership - and arent convinced this new body will move the needle much, because Ellison is set to have ample oversight over appointments. Outside this board, however, the combined company is retaining Mark Thompson as CNNs editor-in-chief. Trump has separately continued to criticise CBS coverage under Skydance ownership. Still, the president has held a long relationship with the billionaire Ellison family. Paramounts chief reportedly hosted a dinner in Washington in Trumps honour back in April, on the same day Warner shareholders gave their greenlight for the merger. And in June, just two days after the U.S. Justice Department said it wouldnt intervene in the deal, Ellison attended an Ultimate Fighting Championship match on the White House lawn for Trumps 80th birthday streamed by Paramount. Also Read - Digger Tom Cruise leans into one of his careers most remarkable performances with glee Gulf money To help fund its Warner buyout, Paramount racked up billions of dollars in financial backing from three Gulf countries Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. The Federal Communications Commission approved the companys request for sizeable indirect ownership from those foreign investors. Paramount previously disclosed it expected those funds to indirectly own nearly 50 of equity interests - but no voting rights - of what is now the larger Skydance. But the company asked for clearance of up to 100 to account for potential future investments, which the FCC granted, citing in part that access to more capital would strengthen the broadcast industry and was therefore in the public interest. Critics - including FCCs sole Democratic Commissioner, Anna Gomez - have called the move alarming and unprecedented. They argue that amount of money opens the door to behind-the-scenes influence. The final antitrust fight Paramount cleared antitrust hurdles for its Warner acquisition from regulators worldwide over the summer, including the Trump administrations Justice Department. But in July, Democratic attorneys general from 12 states - led by Californias Rob Bonta - sued to block the merger, alleging the combined company would extinguish competition and lead to fewer choices for consumers, particularly movie theatergoers and cable customers across the U.S. The Writers Guild of America followed suit. And Paramount agreed to put its Warner buyout on ice well into next year so the challenges could head toward a larger antitrust trial. Settlement agreements emerged in September. The states terms, eventually approved by a judge, include pledges from the company to increase film production in the U.S. over the next five years, commit millions of dollars to a fund aimed at supporting workers displaced by the merger and again establish new editorial monitoring of CNN and CBS. Settling these challenges marked a key hurdle ahead of closing the deal. Critics decried the deal as capitulating to corporate pressure and said the remedies were too weak.

articleTitle: One year of weight-loss drugs in India: What happened to the ‘Mounjaro brides’?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Clinics are now offering three-month weight-loss packages at Rs 20,000-30,000, specifically targeting brides
description: In 2025, as weight-loss drugs entered the Indian market, clinics began launching pre-wedding packages targeted at young women hoping to rapidly shed kilos before their big day. As leading endocrinologists sound a note of caution, The Indian Express traces the journeys of some of the brides who signed up — long and difficult, one that doesn’t stop at the wedding
body_raw: Down a narrow lane in Lajpat Nagar, South Delhi, half hidden by low tree branches, is a small white door with silver lettering Weight Loss Clinic. Behind it is a basement. A silver aluminium partition divides the space in two. On one side is a small, brightly lit waiting area. On the other is the doctors desk. Nearby hangs a banner meant to reassure Obesity is a chronic disease. It has genetic, lifestyle and environmental components, and it is not a reflection of who you are. In the waiting area is a woman with her mother, a few others sit on a bench. They have all come for weight-loss consultations, and some have a date by which to do it an impending wedding. The clinic is one of a growing number in South Delhi that sell weight-loss programmes built on GLP-1 drugs, a class of medications first developed for diabetes and since approved for obesity. They include semaglutide, which Novo Nordisk sells as Ozempic and Wegovy, and tirzepatide, which Eli Lilly sells as Mounjaro - drugs that entered the Indian market last year. Since then, despite limited data on its effect on Indian patients, the drugs are among the most sought-after, by value, in Indias pharmaceutical market. There have also been reports of the drug being used for cosmetic reasons, and of clinics offering Mounjaro bride packages to those aiming for quick-fix weight-loss before the big day. Now, a year into that trade, there are harder questions to tackle. Doctors have increasingly been treating obesity as a chronic disease, not something that requires a cosmetic fix. But when the GLP-1 drugs for obesity treatment, which work by altering the bodys hunger signals, are used merely for cosmetic reasons, it raises a different set of questions. What happens after the immediate weight goal is reached, say, a wedding? Do the lost kilos stay away, or do appetite and weight bounce back once the three-month package runs its course? Interviews with clinics offering weight-loss programmes on tight deadlines, leading endocrinologists and patients who were on GLP-1 drugs ahead of their weddings shine some light on the risks that come with going down the path of quick-fix weight loss packages. Inside a weight-loss clinic The Lajpat Nagar clinics offer is simple. The programme promises Mounjaro-assisted weight reduction in three months for Rs 30,000. The price covers consultations with the doctor, a complimentary dietitian, and the injections themselves, which patients take home the day they pay. Youll be added to a dietitian group, a staff member explains. They regulate your diet, and in three months, youll lose weight. A senior member of the staff says, Most of our clients come ahead of their wedding. In the last one year, we have helped close to a hundred brides reach their desired weight. Its a tidy pitch by the clinic three months to the wedding, three months to lose weight. Endocrinologists, however, point out that obesity keeps no such calendar. None of these is meant to be used for cosmetic, short-term use, says Dr Ambrish Mithal, chairman of endocrinology at Max Hospital. The drugs are for long-term use. Most, but not all, patients require a maintenance dose to keep the weight off. On the face of it, many clinics make the pitch sound reassuringly medical. A Hauz Khas clinic promises a supervised weight-loss programme, overseen by an AIIMS-trained doctor. But there is a catch. The doctor is a dermatologist, not an endocrinologist. A few kilometres away, another clinic, better known for facial aesthetics, makes a similar promise a doctor-supervised Mounjaro package. Are weight-loss drugs a good idea before weddings? Heres what Dr Ambrish Mithal, chairman of endocrinology at Max Hospital says Read - The Indian Express IndianExpress October 7, 2026 Mithal says there is a reason brides are the target. Brides are an attractive market for companies selling weight-loss drugs. The scrutiny before a wedding makes a bride especially vulnerable. When a wedding or a festival becomes the reason to take a drug, the drug itself is taken less seriously. Deciding when a patient can safely stop the drug is a slow process, says Dr Mithal, requiring months of monitoring to determine whether weight loss has been sustained, metabolic markers have normalised and lifestyle changes are strong enough to hold without the drug. He says that even those who start on the drugs with a wedding-date goal in mind would do well to consult an endocrinologist, someone who can monitor the patients health not only in the run-up to the event, but beyond it. In their desperation, not many take that route. Losing more than just kilos Six months ahead of her September 2025 wedding, the 23-year-old science graduate from Ludhiana decided she needed to shed some of her 108 kg. The push came from both social media and a cousin, says a Delhi-based endocrinologist who would eventually treat her. The cousin had taken a weight-loss injection before her own wedding and lost 50 kg, a transformation that was the topic of family conversations before the bride decided to try the drug herself. She found a local clinic that was willing to give her a weight-loss package. On her very first visit, she was handed Mounjaro in bulk, no questions asked about her medical history, no baseline tests run. She paid Rs 20,000 for a three-month course and walked out with the injections in hand, says the endocrinologist, who works at a health start-up in Delhi and agreed to speak on condition of anonymity. The Ludhiana clinic had offered the 23-year-old no tests. There was no gradual build-up of the dose, no monitoring, no plan for her and little contact with a doctor. The clinic asked her to self-inject Mounjaro and kept escalating the dose until she was at 12.5 mg, close to the maximum. She lost around 20 kg in 40 days, says the doctor. Through it all, the patient remained unaware of the other half of the treatment diet and lifestyle changes such as exercise and strength training. Almost two months before the wedding, she travelled to Delhi for her lehenga trials and jewellery appointments. But by then, the side-effects of the drug were severe enough for her to visit the endocrinologist in Delhi. When she visited us, she had nausea, exhaustion, hair fall, menstrual changes and mood shifts, and she had lost a massive amount of muscle mass. Acne flared up on her face, the doctor recalls. During the consultation she looked anxious, jittery. He says his first concern was not how much weight she had lost. We wanted to understand what was happening to her body during the process. Was she eating enough? Was she getting adequate protein? Was she losing muscle along with fat? How was her digestion and energy? the doctor says. The bigger conversation was about ensuring that weight loss was not coming at the cost of her metabolic and nutritional health. A full workup followed, and it found more than a lighter body. When we ran a full root-cause analysis, we found her hormones to be completely off, her periods were irregular, she had abnormalities in her metabolism, her thyroid was abnormal. And with all this, she was on unsupervised Monjaro, says the doctor. The drug had done what it was sold to do. The weight was gone. But she was left with a lot more to grapple with. She visited us twice after her health checkup. We gave her a proper diet chart, exercises to do, and a gradual dosage reduction of Mounjaro, till the maintenance dose, to wean off the drugs effect. She got married, but she never returned for a follow-up, the doctor says. Three months to February Akanksha Chauhan did most of it right, with her weight loss monitored by an endocrinologist. Yet, the journey sprung constant surprises, not all of it pleasant. It all began in December 2024, when Chauhan, a petroleum engineer who lives in the UK, turned 35, and seriously started considering whether she wanted to be a mother. Her gynaecologist suggested she freeze her eggs, but he was concerned about her weight. He told me he wasnt sure about the quality of the eggs we would retrieve, she says, adding that he advised her to shed some of the 99 kg that she weighed then. That was an alarm bell. I didnt want to go into a three-digit number, she says. The gynaecologist referred her to an endocrinologist, who put her on Ozempic. Her first dose was on March 25, 2025. Three days later, she met the man who would become her husband on a dating app. He was a practising lawyer, lean and athletic she recalls being embarrassed about her weight. I told him that in the next three months I was going to transform. I was almost trying to impress him, she says, laughing at the memory. But the next few months were difficult as Chauhan lived with the side effects of the drug. From April to August, I was in China on work. Suddenly, my appetite dipped, and had become zero. Along with that, I could hardly find anything that I could eat. It was mostly watermelon, she says. Then, in the middle of the trip, nausea took over. By November, the couple decided to get married and chose a February date for their wedding. It was around this time that Chauhan decided to stop the drug for a month. She weighed 58 kg then. Within days, the scale began to move the other way. Suddenly, I could see that there was some weight coming back, she says. It was also the time she began shopping for her wedding. She recalls walking into a store in Lucknow and settling on two outfits a deep olive-green lehenga, and a green-and-gold silk saree. The outfits would take three months to arrive. For Chauhan, those months were a countdown, not only to the wedding but to the lehenga and its tailored blouse. The only thing that was constantly running through my head was that I had to fit into that gorgeous lehenga and blouse, she recalls. She consulted her endocrinologist. Because I was getting married in February and I had only three months, I went back on the highest dose that I had stopped at, she says. By the time she stood in her olive-green lehenga, she had reached the weight she had been aiming for. The lehenga fitted. So did the blouse. I received compliments from everyone that day. They said I looked like I was 30 or 31, not 36. I felt so good that day. It was perfect, she says, smiling. But the wedding was the start of another chapter. On medical advice, in February, Chauhan stopped the drug again, this time for three months. She conceived, but the pregnancy ended in a miscarriage. When I got it tested, my gynaecologist said everything was normal and that my miscarriage was not related to the weight-loss drugs, she says. In June, she restarted the drug in the United Kingdom. My Indian doctor was on a holiday, she recalls. She decided to restart the dose herself, without the doctors advice. It was a big mistake, she says. The consequence was swift - severe vomiting and dehydration. She spent three days in the ICU. Chauhan is now back on Mounjaro, under her doctors supervision. I will continue it for the next six months, just to maintain my weight, and then we will try to conceive next year, she says. From the consultation room Dr Anoop Misra, executive chairman of Fortis C-DOC Hospital for Diabetes and Allied Sciences, is among the citys leading endocrinologists. He has watched the boom in GLP-1 drugs unfold from his consultation room. We are seeing particularly strong demand among urban women, including women with post-pregnancy weight gain, PCOS-associated obesity and metabolic problems around the perimenopausal period. There is also considerable social pressure on women to achieve a particular body shape, and this creates a risk of medicalising cosmetic weight loss, he says. There is a message he now repeats to his patients. The most important message is that obesity is a chronic disease, not simply a temporary excess of weight. GLP-1 drugs should therefore not be viewed like a short course of antibiotics, he says. For many patients, Dr Misra says, treatment will need to be long term, especially if the underlying tendency to obesity remains. When treatment is stopped, appetite generally returns and substantial weight regain is common. A recent analysis of 37 studies has found that cardiometabolic benefits progressively diminish after stopping anti-obesity medication, with GLP-1 drugs associated with relatively rapid weight regain, he says. That does not mean the drugs cant be stopped. In his experience, some patients can hold on to their weight loss with intensive dietary changes, more protein, physical activity and resistance training. The emerging consensus is therefore shifting from the question When can I stop the injection? to What is the appropriate long-term treatment strategy for this individuals obesity?, he says. But Dr Misra draws a clear line at using these drugs mainly for cosmetic weight loss. While the immediate side effects of the drugs are well recognised - nausea, vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea and reduced appetite - with excessive or rapid weight loss, there are broader concerns, he says, including loss of muscle and lean tissue, nutritional deficiencies, gallbladder disease and potentially loss of bone mass. Early observational data on bone outcomes need more confirmation, he adds, and should not yet be read as proof of cause. For Indian patients, I am particularly concerned about sarcopenia and micronutrient deficiency because a person can become lighter without necessarily becoming metabolically or physically healthier. This is especially relevant to women and older adults, he says. Dr Misra clarifies that his concern is not about the drugs themselves. They are a major advance in obesity and metabolic medicine. My concern is using a powerful medical therapy for the wrong indication, he says. A word of caution Chauhan has learned that the hard way. Despite the many turns in her weight-loss journey, she has had doctors monitoring her every step of the way. She has also become an informal adviser to other women weighing GLP-1 drugs before their weddings. In a WhatsApp support community, brides on weight-loss GLP-1 drugs often reach out to her, and she tells them what she wishes more people understood this is not another item on a pre-wedding checklist. I tell them about the reality this is not like a bridal skin package or a hair package. Its great to start before your wedding, but remember, its a long-term thing, she says.

articleTitle: Acidity pill Aciloc: Mundhe’s FDA shuts 3 Cadila godowns over name mix-up
articleFeaturedImageAlt: FDA licence suspended Cadila
description: Popular acidity pill Aciloc was sold in two versions with different drugs but almost identical names, says FDA
body_raw: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration FDA has cancelled the sale and distribution licences of three Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd godowns in Pune, Nagpur and Thane after finding that drugs with different active ingredients were being sold under deceptively similar names to Aciloc, a popular acidity medicine. Aciloc 150 and Aciloc 300 contain 150 mg and 300 mg of ranitidine. Aciloc 150 and Aciloc 300 contain a different drug altogether, famotidine, in strengths of 20 mg and 40 mg. Yet the only difference in the brand names is a sign, the FDA said. Both reduce stomach acid and treat heartburn and ulcers. But the FDA said the similar names could lead to patients being dispensed the wrong medicine. It also found that some wholesalers who had ordered the ranitidine versions were supplied the famotidine ones. Officials said inspections were carried out in July at the companys clearing and forwarding agent CFA godowns at Bhiwandi in Thane district, Wadki in Pune and Nimji in Kalmeshwar taluka of Nagpur district, and the stock was prohibited from sale and distribution. The action followed a petition by the company in the Bombay High Court, which on August 11 directed fresh show-cause notices at all three locations. The company was given 21 days to reply in writing and a personal hearing. The companys written reply and submissions during the hearing were found unsatisfactory, following which the respective licensing authorities passed reasoned orders under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, the FDA said. Under the rules, famotidine tablets must be sold in packs of 14. The FDA found Aciloc 150 was being sold in packs of 30 and Aciloc 300 in packs of 20. The FDA flagged another issue. Gujarats drug regulator, in a September 29 letter, cancelled manufacturing permissions for famotidine 20 mg and 40 mg tablets, with effect backdated to June 2. This was not disclosed during the show-cause and hearing proceedings, while sale and distribution continued in Maharashtra, the state FDA said. Other deficiencies cited include the absence of an inspection book, inadequate labelling of the expired-drug area, the absence of the competent person at a licensed Konkan premises and unsigned sale invoices. FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said manufacturers have a responsibility to ensure brand names do not create confusion, and urged consumers to check the generic name and strength on medicine labels. Chemists should dispense medicines strictly according to prescriptions, he said.

articleTitle: Rajnath Singh stresses on self-reliance in aerospace sector as HAL delivers its 2,000th aero-engine
articleFeaturedImageAlt: aero-engine: Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and others during the inauguration ceremony of second Shakti Engine Manufacturing line, in Koratput. (PTI Photo)
description: Describing the engine as a significant milestone, the Defence Minister called for using it as a foundation to build an aerospace industry capable of designing, developing, manufacturing and supporting advanced propulsion systems.
body_raw: Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday called for strengthening indigenous capabilities in the design, development, testing, manufacturing and maintenance of advanced aero-engines, stressing that mastery of propulsion technology is essential for self-reliance in the aerospace and defence sector. Singh, who witnessed the delivery of the 2,000th aero-engine by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited HAL, Koraput division at Sunabeda, noted that indigenisation of components and reduced turnaround time are contributing to operational readiness and extended service life of critical defence assets. Aerospace self-reliance must extend to indigenous aero-engine capability, particularly for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft AMCA programme. A sovereign aerospace ecosystem requires indigenous capabilities across materials, design, manufacturing, testing and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul MRO, said Singh. He also highlighted proposed investment of around Rs 5,000 crore, indigenisation of raw materials in partnership with Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited MIDHANI, and establishment of Indias first indigenous high-thrust engine testing facility. Urging the HAL Koraput division to raise standards in quality, productivity, indigenisation, innovation and delivery timelines, Singh described the 2,000th engine as a significant milestone and called for using it as a foundation to build an Indian aerospace industry capable of designing, developing, manufacturing and supporting advanced propulsion systems. Emphasising the need for reliable indigenous propulsion for Indias helicopter ecosystem, the defence minister stated that forces require engines that are available when needed, supported throughout their lifecycle, and upgraded with evolving technology. A long-term endeavour Aero-engine development is a long-term endeavour requiring sustained investment, specialised testing, skilled manpower and a strong industrial ecosystem, with focus on repeatable, reliable and scalable production, design, critical materials and superalloys, he added. Singh, on the occasion, hailed HALs contribution to military aviation, noting that its engines have powered frontline aircraft, including the MiG-21, MiG-27, MiG-29 and Su-30MKI since establishment of the unit in 1964. The defence minister announced that HAL is enhancing annual AL-31FP engine production capacity from 30 to 50 engines annually with an investment of Rs 335 crore. He also announced a second Shakti engine production line with an investment of Rs 218 crore. The new line will manufacture up to 100 engines annually and is scheduled to be fully established by 2028-29, catering to indigenous helicopters including Dhruv Advanced Light Helicopter ALH and Prachand Light Combat Helicopter LCH, added Singh. He also called for greater integration of MSMEs, start-ups, private industry, academia and research institutions into the propulsion ecosystem.

articleTitle: No classes till security assured, say SRFTI students; plan rally with Jadavpur University
articleFeaturedImageAlt: College students protest against Fee Hike in Chandigarh
description: According to the students, despite an urgent written appeal sent to Union Information & Broadcasting (I&B) Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw following violent clashes on campus, no response was received from the ministry.
body_raw: As the boycott of classes, workshops, and film shoots at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute SRFTI in Kolkata entered its 10th day, protesting students reiterated that they will not return to academic activity till concrete security assurances are provided and warned of a mass gathering with the students of Jadavpur University and the alumni network. According to the students, despite an urgent written appeal sent to Union Information Broadcasting IB Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw following violent clashes on campus, no response was received from the ministry. In response to escalating panic on campus, a joint delegation of student representatives from SRFTI Kolkata, the Film and Television Institute of India FTII Pune, and FTII Itanagar submitted a formal petition on October 3 to the Union Ministry requesting immediate central intervention to secure the autonomous institutes Kolkata campus. Signed by Blossom Hazarika SRFTI Students Union, Amritanshu Singh Yadav FTII Students Association, and Divyansh FTII Itanagar Students Council, the joint letter outlines four key demands for the IB Ministry. It includes deployment of adequate security personnel at vulnerable campus access points, including the main gate coordination with the West Bengal government and Kolkata Police to deny permits for public rallies near the institute implementation of preventive measures to stop outside crowds from approaching or threatening the campus and direct instructions for the SRFTI administration to maintain continuous liaison with police and student representatives until de-escalation is achieved. On Sunday, there was stone pelting two people were injured. I was one of them. I got three stitches and another student suffered a head injury, said Anamika Pal, a student representative at SRFTI. In fact, one person jumped inside the campus, and weve been constantly pelted with stones. Pal said that academic activity will remain suspended until safety guarantees are established. Till the time we are given assurance of our safety and security, we are not going to resume classes. What happened on Sunday is scary. One person jumped into the campus, but it is not difficult for many others to enter. Who will take accountability? With no official acknowledgement or safety framework provided by the IB Ministry after 10 days of disrupted academic activity, students are reaching beyond the campus perimeter to rally wider political and academic support. Classes have been off for the last 10 days, and theres no response from the IB Ministry. If we dont get support and safety from the institutions, we may go for a solidarity meeting with Jadavpur University and our alumni network, she added. Critiquing the internal response, an alumnus stated that campus officials appear more concerned about safeguarding those who are trying to disturb the peace inside the premises than the safety of the students. Neither the IB Ministry nor the local administration has issued an official security plan for the campus till the filing of this report.

articleTitle: Film City fire: AICWA seeks FIR against Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 makers, demands inquiry
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AICWA
description: AICWA has sought an FIR and inquiry into the Film City fire, alleging safety lapses on the Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set and demanding action.
body_raw: A day after a major fire broke out at Mumbais Film City, the All Indian Cine Workers Association AICWA has approached Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, demanding a time-bound inquiry, an FIR for alleged negligence and the resignation of Film Citys managing director. In a letter dated October 6, AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta said the fire broke out at around 4 pm on October 5 on the set of Colors channels reality show Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2 at Prime Focus Studio in Goregaon and spread to the adjoining set of Hustle. The association has also sought mandatory fire audits, on-set fire safety staff and firefighting equipment for every production at Film City, with licences cancelled for productions that fail to comply. AICWA said the fire brought shooting across much of Film City to a halt, affecting Kaun Banega Crorepati, several television serials and films, and causing losses running into lakhs of rupees. Fire on Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set halts shooting across Film City AICWA submits letter to Chief Minister Mumbai A fire on the set of the reality show Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2 at Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari Film City halted shooting across most of Film City. Shooting of KBC and many serials and films remained stopped for the entire day, and everyone involved suffered losses. The biggest blow fell on daily-wage workers, technicians and small artists. They are paid per day, so a day without shooting means a days wages lost for many of them. Producers also lost the full days set and shoot expenses. AICWA estimates that the fire caused losses running into lakhs of rupees across Film City. All Indian Cine Workers Association AICWA President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta has submitted a letter on the incident to the following Honourable Chief Minister of Maharashtra, Shri Devendra Fadnavis Honourable Labour Minister, Shri Akash Fundkar Honourable State Home Minister, Shri Yogesh Kadam Honourable State Labour Minister, Shri Ashish Jaiswal Honourable BMC Commissioner, Shri Ashwini Bhide AICWA AllIndianCineWorkersAssociation PatiPatniAurPanga Hustle Bollywood Filmcity DevFadnavis advakash iYogeshRKadam Ashishjaisw3Adv AshwiniBhide DevenBhartiIPS ShelarAshish ANI PTINews iansindia CMOMaharashtra sureshsgupta - All Indian Cine Workers Association aicwaofficial October 6, 2026 AICWA demands inquiry, FIR after Film City fire In the letter addressed to Devendra Fadnavis, AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta said the blaze did not remain confined to the Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2 set and spread to the adjoining Hustle set, putting workers and artistes in the complex at risk. AICWA has made four demands a thorough, time-bound inquiry into how the fire started, why it spread and why fire safety arrangements were allegedly not in place an FIR for negligence against the channel, producer and production house the resignation of Film Citys managing director and mandatory fire audits, trained fire safety staff and firefighting equipment at every shoot. The association has also sought cancellation of the licence of any production that fails to comply with the required safety measures. ALSO READ Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr This is not an accident, it is criminal negligence AICWA alleged that the Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set had been operating without adequate fire safety arrangements. There were no fire safety arrangements whatsoever on the set of Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2, which is why the fire broke out and spread. A large number of workers and artists were working on a set that had been left completely unprotected. This is not an accident, it is criminal negligence, the letter stated. The association further alleged that Film City management was aware that sets were operating without basic safety measures. The studios stand inside Film City, and the management knew well that sets were running without basic fire safety. The Managing Director of Film City therefore bears full responsibility for this failure, AICWA said. These are allegations made by the workers body and have not yet been established through an official inquiry. Fire disrupts shooting across Film City AICWA said shooting across most of Film City remained halted for the entire day. Shoot schedules for KBC, along with several television serials and films, were affected. The association estimated that the disruption resulted in losses running into lakhs of rupees across Film City. AICWA particularly highlighted the impact on daily-wage workers, technicians and junior artists, who lose a days income when shooting is cancelled. The biggest blow fell on daily-wage workers, technicians and small artists. They are paid per day, so a day without shooting means a days wages lost for many of them. Producers also lost the full days set and shoot expenses, the association said. AICWA sends letter to multiple authorities While Fadnavis is the primary recipient of the letter, AICWA has also marked copies to several other Maharashtra authorities. These include Labour Minister Akash Fundkar, State Home Minister Yogesh Kadam, State Labour Minister Ashish Jaiswal, BMC Commissioner Ashwini Bhide and Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti. The association concluded its letter by urging the authorities to act immediately. Unless accountability is fixed at the top, these fires will keep coming, and so will the loss of innocent lives. AICWA urges you to act without delay so that the lives of cine workers are given the safety they deserve, the letter stated. What did Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 team say? Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 team told Hindustan Times that the fire broke out outside its sets and that no shooting was taking place there at the time. Yes, there was a fire outside the sets. There is no casualty. Nobody was shooting at the set of Pati Patni Aur Panga. There was no shoot happening, the team told the publication. The show is hosted by Sonali Bendre and Munawar Faruqui. Hustle 5 team confirms artists were present The fire also affected the adjoining set of MTV Hustle 5, where the grand finale was being shot. The shows team confirmed that artistes were present when the fire broke out but said everyone was safe. All the artistes were there. The fire happened suddenly. As of now, there are no casualties and everyone is safe, the team told Hindustan Times. The team added that everyone evacuated the set after the fire broke out. No casualties or injuries have been reported following the Film City fire. The exact cause of the blaze remains unknown.

articleTitle: Smriti Mandhana named India women’s captain as Harmanpreet Kaur steps down
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Smriti Mandhana takes over the captaincy reign from Harmanpreet Kaur. (BCCI FOR CREIMAS)
description: Harmanpreet, who led India to the 2025 ODI World Cup title, announced earlier in the day that she was relinquishing the captaincy across formats.
body_raw: Smriti Mandhana has been appointed captain of the Indian womens cricket team, the BCCI announced on Tuesday, the day Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down from the role. Harmanpreet, who led India to the 2025 ODI World Cup title, announced earlier in the day that she was relinquishing the captaincy across formats. Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Womens Cricket Team across all formats, she wrote in a post. Reports said the decision followed a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati that assessed the teams performances over recent months, including Indias exit from the T20 World Cup before the semifinals. Smriti has been one of the leading figures in Indian womens cricket over the years and has played a key role in the teams progress across formats, the BCCI said in a release. It added that she has also demonstrated her leadership qualities in domestic and franchise cricket, most recently leading Royal Challengers Bengaluru to Womens Premier League titles in 2024 and 2026. ALSO READ Harmanpreet Kaurs real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup Mandhana, who was Harmanpreets deputy, has been part of the Indian team since 2013, and the release said she brings considerable experience into the role. She will be the full-time white-ball captain from now on, the BCCI said. She has so far led India in 18 T20Is and four ODIs. The 29-year-old was the second-highest run-scorer at the 2025 World Cup, with 434 runs, and became the first Indian woman to score international hundreds in all three formats when she made a T20I century against England in June 2025. To be given the responsibility of leading India is a very special honour, Mandhana said in the release. Representing India has always meant a great deal to me, and to now have the opportunity to lead the team is something I will value deeply. I am grateful to the BCCI, the selectors, my teammates and everyone who has supported me throughout my journey and for the trust they have placed in me. She also paid tribute to her predecessor. I would also like to acknowledge Harmanpreet and the contribution she has made as captain over the years. She has led the team with great commitment and has been an important part of our journey, Mandhana said. I understand the responsibility that comes with this role and look forward to working with the team, learning along the way and giving my best to take Indian Cricket forward. Indias next assignment is a series against Zimbabwe starting on October 16. The Womens Champions Trophy follows at home in February.

articleTitle: After nudge from selectors, Harmanpreet Kaur quits as India skipper in all formats
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down from captaincy of Indian women's team. (CREIMAS FOR BCCI)
description: The selectors felt it was time to build for the next World Cup cycle. India failed to progress to the knockouts of the T20 World Cup for the second time in a row under Harmanpreet's captaincy
body_raw: A year after leading India to the ODI World Cup, Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as captain of the national womens cricket team in all formats - a surprise decision that she announced through an Instagram post Tuesday, a day after attending a team review meeting with BCCI officials and selectors in Guwahati. The 37-year-old also said in the post that she was ready to continue playing for the country. Now, I am ready to play for the love of the game. Captaincy ends. The journey continues, she posted. The ODI World Cup at home last year was the teams first ever ICC title. But this July, the side failed to progress to the knockout rounds of the T20 World Cup for the second time in a row, prompting the selectors to decide on a change in leadership - although Harmanpreet was keen to continue, BCCI sources told The Indian Express. The decision to move on from Harmanpreet as captain was by the selectors. After the end of the T20 World Cup, a review meeting was planned. But it took place after the Asian Games where the team won gold. Harmanpreet wanted to continue as captain, but the selectors prevailed. The selectors felt it was time to build for the next World Cup cycle. There was no question of split captaincy, the sources said. ALSO READ Harmanpreet Kaurs real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup The Indian Express has learnt that womens team coach Amol Muzumdar, vice-captain Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet met separately with BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and womens selection committee chief Amita Sharma in Guwahati. Mandhana 30 took over the captaincy reins from Harman. Harmanpreets last assignment as captain was the Asian Games campaign, where India defended its title. She captained India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is, and also led the team to three Asia Cup titles. She was appointed T20 captain in 2016 and took over the reins of the ODI team in 2022 after Mithali Rajs retirement. India had reached the ODI World Cup final in 2005 and 2017 under Mithali. With Harmanpreet at the helm, India became a top contender in the international arena 2018 T20 World Cup semifinal, 2020 T20 World Cup final, 2023 T20 World Cup semifinal and, eventually, the 2025 ODI World Cup title. However, India were knocked out in the group stage of the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups. Not easy decision This is not an easy decision, Harmanpreet wrote on Instagram. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life. I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian womens cricket - my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first. In an official statement, BCCI president Mithun Manhas said Harmanpreets contribution as captain will always hold a special place in the history of Indian cricket. ALSO READ Harmanpreet will be able to bat with freedom Coach Kamaldeesh She took on the responsibility at an important stage in the growth of womens cricket and helped the Indian team build on the strong foundation laid by those who came before her. Over the years, she led India through some very important moments and helped the team compete with confidence against the best in the world. The World Cup victory in 2025 will undoubtedly be the defining achievement of her captaincy, Manhas said. Saikia also highlighted the World Cup win in his tribute. Harmanpreet, you can be immensely proud of what you have achieved as captain of India. You embraced the responsibility from the very beginning and went on to lead India through some of the most important moments in its journey, while playing an important role in the growth of Indian womens cricket, he said. You experienced the disappointment of falling short, but continued to believe in the team and its ability to achieve more. That is what made the World Cup victory in 2025 so special. You had been part of the journey for many years and eventually had the opportunity to lead India to its first womens cricket World Cup title. That will always remain one of the great moments in Indian cricket, Saikia said.

articleTitle: Trump suggests Iran to ‘take out’ Los Angeles, San Diego; sparks backlash in US
articleFeaturedImageAlt: trump on Iran
description: The Republican leader was swiftly criticised by California’s Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans.
body_raw: US President Donald Trump has courted controversy for suggesting to a crowd of his supporters in the state of Nebraska that Iran could take out major cities like Los Angeles and San Diego, the two cities held by Democrats that had been a target of his administration. The Republican leader was swiftly criticised by Californias Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans. During a political rally in Nebraska on Monday night, Trump talked about the upcoming midterm elections in November and said that he hoped to see a tremendous victory for his party. Trump cites war costs, upcoming midterms The US President discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and suggested that high prices of fuel, fertiliser, and other products due to the war with Iran that began in February were a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. Referring to Iran, Trump said in Grand Island, Its a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let em take out Los Angeles, let em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and its going to be over with very soon, amid applause from the crowd. Referring to the seven-month-old war, the US President said, Its essentially almost over with. But its going to end very soon, and its going to end one way or the other. California leaders condemn Trumps remarks Californias governor and mayor were quick to criticise Trumps comments. California Governor Gavin Newsom, in an X post, said, After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should take out Los Angeles and San Diego. He is deranged and dangerous. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass attacked President Trump for making the remarks, calling them irresponsible threats that could potentially compromise the safety of Americas second-largest city. The role of a president is to protect the country, not to actively threaten it and encourage attacks on American lives, Bass said. Republican leader distances himself from Trump Jim Desmond, a Republican leader running in a redrawn California district near San Diego, distanced himself from President Trumps remarks. I vehemently disagree with President Trumps comments. America must stand up to Iran and defend our interests, but the first responsibility of our Commander-in-Chief is to protect the American people and our homeland, Desmond wrote on X. White House defends Trumps comments The White House on Tuesday defended Trumps comments. The media freakout over President Trumps comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadnt been stopped, White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung wrote in a social media post. America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money.

articleTitle: ‘Now I don’t even look at start list’: Gulveer Singh on not fearing other runners
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gulveer Singh became the first Indian to win three middle and long-distance medals in one edition of the Asian Games. (AP)
description: India’s long-distance runner looks to level up after winning a combined five medals at the Commonwealth Games and Asiad
body_raw: There are no starting blocks in long-distance running events like 5000m and 10000m. False starts, like in the faster sprints, isnt a primary worry for a runner, but there are other fears that take its place. Indian long distance runner Gulveer Singh admits that it was only recently that he overcame the fear of the competitors around him. Pehle thoda sochta tha baaki competitors ke baare me. Earlier, I used to think about other competitors. But now I dont even look at the start list, Gulveer told The Indian Express in an interaction facilitated by SAI Media. Gulveer was one of Indias best athletes at the Asian Games 2026 with three medals - silver in 1500m, silver in 10000m and bronze in 5000m. The transformation is visible in the results. He has five major medals this year and will be eyeing the World Athletics Championships next year. Gulveers mindset has changed over the years. Now, he knows that he is operating at the same level as compared to others. So, that really helps when the athlete knows that they belong at the top level, his coach Scott Simmons had told this paper earlier. ALSO READ 5 days, 4 races, 3 medals Gulveer Singhs hectic, but productive, Asiad The other thing that has helped Gulveer is competing regularly with the top athletes who were better than him. The result you see today has come from the fact that I regularly compete with athletes who are better than me. It takes away the fear of competing against better athletes and also keeps pushing me whenever I am against these guys, Gulveer said. Late bloomer shines In the world of long-distance running, Gulveer is a late bloomer who started participating in competitions at the age of 24 after joining the Army and has never competed at the junior level. However, his rapid strides to the top echelons of Indias running depict that he was always meant to be in the space he occupies. When I started running, I had no idea that these strides would take me this far. I ran only to get selected in the army, Gulveer recalled. There is a positive to Gulveer picking up running late-he already possessed a calm mind, and the maturity that the sport needed. When I started competing, I was clear in my head about what I had to do. I think that really helped me at the international level, he said. Learning from past Gulveers participation at the World Athletics Championships in 2025 is something that helped open his eyes to the vast difference between the competition at the Asian level, and the behemoths who competed at the highest echelons of long-distance running. When I competed at the 2025 Worlds, it was my first taste of global competition. It was very different from competing at the Asian Games or Asian Championships, said Gulveer. Before competing at the World Championships in Tokyo, Gulveers only major appearances were at the Asian Games and the Asian Championships. At the Tokyo World Championships, Gulveer was well placed to qualify for the final in the mens 5000m heat but faded away at the end, losing his qualification spot. I think that was a big learning for me. I learnt there how to hold your position in a race. Long-distance running is all about the last few meters and if you fade away in that, all the hard work is gone, said Gulveer. That he learned from his mistake at the World Championships was visible in all of the races at the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games. After the Worlds, I specifically worked on my last kick and staying patient. One needs to know when that last kick has to come, if the athlete doesnt time it right, the athlete will fade away, Gulveer explained. Now, it will be some rest for Gulveer before he travels back to Colorado Springs to train under Scott Simmons for the next season. Ill be back to training soon. Once, the celebrations and felicitations are over here in India, said Gulveer. I have my eyes set on the World Championships next season and as one can see, the progression is on the right path for me at the moment.

articleTitle: 3 children suffer head injuries as ceiling collapses at government school in Udaipur
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Udaipur school ceiling collapse
description: The incident comes at a time when the state is facing increased scrutiny over the condition of schools, drawing attention of the Cockroach Janta Party whose members visited different campuses in August.
body_raw: Three children suffered head injuries after the ceiling of their classroom collapsed at a government primary school in Udaipur on Tuesday. Two other students sustained minor injuries in the incident that took place in the Bhindar area. The incident comes at a time when the state is facing increased scrutiny over the condition of schools, drawing attention of the Cockroach Janta Party CJP whose members visited campuses in different parts of Rajasthan in August. Tuesdays incident took place around 11 am at Government Primary School, Narada, under Vaniyatalai gram panchayat in the Bhindar police station area, when a portion of the plaster from a classroom ceiling suddenly came down. There were 32 children in the classroom at the time. Headmaster Lal Singh Shaktawat told The Indian Express, Class 1 students Krishna Kumari and Kartik, and Class 5 student Ganeshlal suffered head injuries. All three were taken to Bhindar Government Hospital for treatment and later sent home. Two other students sustained minor injuries. The ceiling collapsed suddenly, injuring the students. Thankfully, no one was severely injured. We sent the children back to their homes by evening. The school, which runs up to Class 5, has 37 students in all, which is why it is common for students of different classes to study in the same room. Authorities were informed of schools condition Shaktawat said the education department had earlier been informed about the poor condition of the building. The building was constructed in 2001 and had become dilapidated. We had already informed the education department about its condition. The last time the school building was repaired was in 2020, he said. Following directions from the education department and the local administration, the school building has now been locked as a precautionary measure. Classes will be shifted to a temporary location near Matajis mandir nearby. The incident comes just over a year after one of Rajasthans worst school-building tragedies. On July 25, 2025, the roof of a government school in Piplodi village of Jhalawar district collapsed, killing seven children and injuring 28 others. The National Human Rights Commission subsequently took cognizance of the incident and sought a report from the Rajasthan government, noting allegations that authorities had been informed about the buildings dilapidated condition. The safety of government schools has again emerged as a major issue in Rajasthan in recent months following the School Thik Karo campaign by the CJP. Its teams visited government schools across the state and highlighted problems ranging from unsafe and dilapidated buildings to schools functioning without proper infrastructure. Some CJP workers were also attacked while visiting a government school in Bagru. The government school at Rampura-Kanwarpura in Jaipurs Bagru area, which had been declared unsafe, was demolished after the CJP campaign highlighted its condition. The government sanctioned around Rs 18 lakh for construction of a new building.

articleTitle: 4.9 Magnitude earthquake hits Uttarakhand, tremors felt in Delhi-NCR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uttarakhand earthquake map (Credits: Credits: National Center for Seismology)
description: The depth of the earthquake was noted to be 13 kilometres, according to the National Center for Seismology.
body_raw: A 4.9 Magnitude earthquake hit Uttarakhands Chamoli on Tuesday night, with its tremors felt in the Delhi-NCR region. The depth of the earthquake was noted to be 13 kilometres, according to the National Center for Seismology, which characterised its status as reviewed. Delhi-NCR has experienced several noticeable earthquakes this year. On January 19, 2026, a mild 2.8-magnitude earthquake struck New Delhi, with its epicentre in North Delhi at a shallow depth of about five kilometres. Brief tremors were felt across parts of the capital, but no damage was reported. On April 3, 2026, tremors were felt in Delhi-NCR after a 5.9-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan. The epicentre was near Darawan, and mild shaking was also reported in Punjab, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir and Kargil. No casualties or property damage were immediately reported.
