articleTitle: ‘Caregiver’s transfer inhumane’: Rajasthan High Court quashes bank manager’s posting
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajasthan High Court bank manager caregiver thalassemia transfer
description: The court found that the bank failed to consider its Equal Opportunity Policy before transferring the manager – whose brother with thalassemia required blood transfusions every 15 days – to a branch 1,000 km away.
body_raw: Calling the transfer of a UCO Bank manager caring for his 75 per cent permanently disabled brother with thalassemia not only arbitrary but also inhumane, the Rajasthan High Court has quashed his proposed posting nearly 1,000 km away. The court held that the bank could not mechanically apply its routine transfer policy without considering its own safeguards for employees caring for persons with disabilities. The court said the managers brother required regular blood transfusions and depended wholly on him for his medical treatment, personal care and financial support. Justice Anoop Kumar Dhand was on October 5 hearing a petition filed by UCO Bank manager Rahul Agrawal against his transfer from Baneti branch in the Jaipur zone to Bhadwa branch in the Ahmedabad zone. The transfer order was issued on May 16 and the bank rejected his representation seeking cancellation of the transfer on September 8. Transferring a care-giver of a person suffering from Thalassemia, who requires blood transfusion on every 15-20 days, to a place 1000 km away, where no such facility or family support is available, without any reasonable consideration, is not only arbitrary but also inhumane and violative of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, which includes right to health and right to live with dignity of both the disabled dependent and the petitioner, the court said. The dispute centred on UCO Banks Equal Opportunity Policy for 2024-27, which contains specific provisions for employees caring for persons with disabilities. The high court found that the bank had failed to meaningfully consider those safeguards before transferring Agrawal to a branch around 1,000 km away from his present posting. Brother dependent on him for treatment According to the order, Agrawals younger brother, Ashish Kumar Agrawal, suffers from thalassemia and has 75 per cent permanent physical disability. His disability was certified by the Department of Medical Health, Government of Rajasthan, on April 19, 2022. The petitioner told the court that his brother was wholly and solely dependent on him for his day-to-day survival, including regular blood transfusions, medication, personal care and financial support. He also submitted that there was no other person in the family to look after his brother. tha The court noted that this dependency was not raised for the first time during the litigation. It had already been declared by Agrawal and recorded in the banks service and HR records. The bank had not disputed the dependency in its reply. The banks own Equal Opportunity Policy became central to the dispute. The policy, framed for 2024-27, contains provisions relating to the transfer and posting of persons with disabilities and their caregivers. It says a person with disability should not be posted far from their residence if this creates difficulties in commuting. It also provides that an employee caring for a dependent daughter, son, parent, spouse, brother or sister with specified disability may be exempted from routine transfer or rotational transfer, subject to administrative constraints. Bank cites promotion, long posting UCO Bank opposed Agrawals plea, arguing that its transfer policy required officers to be transferred after promotion. Agrawal had been promoted from Scale-I to Scale-II through an order dated April 1, 2026. The bank also pointed out that he had remained posted at Baneti and nearby places in the Jaipur zone since January 2018 and had spent around eight years there. It argued that there was no malice or mala fide intention behind the transfer and that several officers had been transferred because of administrative requirements. The high court, however, found that the bank had failed to demonstrate that it had properly considered the special policy while dealing with Agrawals representation. It described the September 8 rejection order as a non-speaking order because it did not explain why his request for retention or exemption under the Equal Opportunity Policy had not been considered. It held that the order was arbitrary and discriminatory and violated Articles 14 equality and 16 equality of opportunity in employment of the Constitution. The Special Policy framed by the respondent-Bank is, therefore, not an act of charity but a statutory obligation. It has a binding force, the court said, adding that the bank cannot be allowed to frame a policy for public display and then act contrary to it. Administrative constraints cant defeat protection The court acknowledged that transfer is ordinarily an incidence of service and courts generally do not interfere with transfer orders. But it said this principle is not absolute where a transfer violates legal rules or a binding policy, is arbitrary or falls within other grounds for judicial review. It held that the banks special policy had binding force and was intended to provide reasonable accommodation to employees caring for persons with disabilities. The expression administrative constraints, the court said, could not be treated as an omnibus or mechanical exception that defeated the protective purpose of the policy. Any departure from the exemption had to be based on genuine, relevant and demonstrable administrative exigencies. The court found that the transfer order did not refer to the disability certificate, the special policy or the relevant caregiver provisions, calling it a classic case of non-application of mind. It said the circumstances were particularly serious because Agrawals brother required blood transfusions every 15 to 20 days. The judge also made it clear that Agrawal could not claim permanent immunity from transfer. It noted that he had already served at his present place for more than seven years. The bank could hence consider transferring him to another station where a vacancy existed, provided it first considered his circumstances and the special policy. The high court quashed the May 16 transfer order and directed the bank to allow Agrawal to continue at his present posting until his case was reconsidered under the Equal Opportunity Policy and in light of his brothers medical condition and dependency.

articleTitle: ‘Missing’ land around KCR’s farmhouse: BRS leader, family to get notices
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Erravalli land row, Erravalli land survey, Revanth Reddy land probe, KCR farmhouse land, 45 acres missing Erravalli, Survey No 325 Erravalli, KCR land records, Siddipet land survey, Telangana land records, Dharani land irregularities, KCR family land, Erravalli farmhouse, KCR news, Telangana news, Indian Express news
description: Revanth Reddy has ordered officials to investigate the 45-acre gap and look into possible irregularities in the state’s land records.
body_raw: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy Tuesday ordered an inquiry into 45 acres of land in Siddipet districts Erravalli village that officials could not account for during a recent survey. The land is adjacent to a farmhouse owned by Bharat Rashtra Samithi BRS chief K Chandrashekar Rao, where he has retreated and spends most of his time after his partys defeat in the December 2020 Assembly elections. Last month, officials found a discrepancy in the land records during a routine exercise to identify land for distribution to beneficiaries in Erravalli and Venkatapuram villages of Markook mandal. In Survey No 325 of Erravalli village, records show that the parcel should contain 388 acres. However, the survey team could identify only 343 acres, leaving 45 acres unaccounted for. In a meeting Tuesday night, Reddy ordered an inquiry and directed officials to scrutinise whether any irregularities existed in the Dharani portal, which hosts land records. The chief minister sought details of Erravalli land, and directed officials, including Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju and CMO Principal Secretary V Sheshadri, to issue a notification to identify the missing 45 acres. As KCR and his family members own land near Survey Number 325, officials would issue notices requiring them to submit their land records. The CM instructed officials to distribute the land identified in Survey Number 325 to eligible beneficiaries and landless local farmers. Reddys allegations During recent public meetings, Revanth Reddy has questioned and accused KCR and his family of amassing disproportionate wealth during the partys regime between 2014 and 2023. At a public meeting in Sircilla recently, he demanded that KCR and his son K T Rama Rao, popularly known as KTR, disclose the details of the properties they owned, as well as those of nephews T Harish Rao and Santosh Kumar. He said KTR built a farmhouse in Janwada village, while his sister Kavithas farmhouse is in Shankarpally, Harish Raos in Moinabad, and KCRs farmhouses are in Erravalli. He questioned where all these properties came from. He also ordered the construction of a Telangana Martyrs Colony for the families of those who sacrificed their lives during the Telangana movement and who belong to that area. The government will allocate housing plots to the martyrs families and develop the colony with all necessary infrastructure. The chief minister assigned the Housing Department responsibility for the colonys construction and ordered officials to ensure the project is completed by June 2 next year. The chief minister also suggested establishing a Young India Integrated School and an education hub on the available lands within the limits of Velikatta village in Kondapaka Mandal.

articleTitle: Grinding your teeth at night without knowing it? Here’s what it does
articleFeaturedImageAlt: teeth
description: From worn enamel and sensitive teeth to jaw pain and headaches, sleep bruxism can cause damage before you realise there is a problem
body_raw: Lisa Shah, in her late 40s, frequently complained of morning headaches and increasing tooth sensitivity. She did not realise she was grinding her teeth at night until dentists noticed characteristic wear patterns during an examination, recalls Dr Bibhakar Ranjan, a Germany-based dentist and preventive oral health advocate. After wearing a custom-made night guard and addressing contributing factors, her teeth were protected from further wear and there was an improvement in jaw discomfort, he says, underscoring why bruxism, or teeth grinding, needs greater attention and awareness among patients as well as dentists and doctors so that it can be identified early. In India too, experts associated with the Indian Dental Association IDA, say several studies have reported an increasing prevalence of the condition across different population groups. According to estimates across various studies, sleep and awake bruxism collectively affect approximately 10 to 30 per cent of the general Indian population, with varying degrees of severity, from occasional to frequent episodes. There is also a high correlation with anxiety, academic or occupational stress and modern lifestyle habits, says Dr Jayesh Rahalkar, consultant orthodontist and past president of the Indian Dental Association, Pune. Studies have shown that the rates can rise significantly in high-stress or physically demanding environment. For instance, studies in India show awake bruxism rates as high as 68 per cent among professional weightlifters and elevated levels among dental students facing academic and clinical stress, Dr Rahalkar says. The Indian Dental Association traditionally observes Oral Health Month during October and November to promote better oral hygiene and preventive care across India. What is bruxism? Grinding or clenching of teeth? Bruxism is the medical term for the involuntary or subconscious clenching, grinding or gnashing of teeth, which can happen during waking hours or while sleeping, Dr Rahalkar says. Symptoms can range from morning headaches, dull pain around the temples, sore or tight jaw muscles and facial pain to increased tooth sensitivity and enamel wear. According to Dr Rahalkar, several factors have been linked to bruxism, including psychological stress, anxiety, sleep disorders and lifestyle habits such as heavy alcohol consumption, tobacco use and high caffeine intake. Over time, dentists say, persistent grinding can make teeth increasingly sensitive to hot and cold, while also causing cracks, fractures and, in severe cases, significant pain. Dr Ranjan says patients may not even realise that they are clenching or grinding their teeth while asleep. It is only when there are jaw pain, headaches or worn teeth that dentists often identify the signs during a check-up, he says. Bruxism is on the rise due to increased stress and sleep disorders. It is known to affect 20 per cent of the population, says Dr Mohit Kheur, consultant at Deenanath Mangeshkar Hospital and professor at M A Rangoonwala Dental College, Pune. Types of disorder Bruxism can broadly be classified as sleep bruxism and awake bruxism. While sleep bruxism occurs during sleep and may involve rhythmic or sustained clenching and grinding, awake bruxism is more commonly characterised by clenching or holding the teeth together while a person is conscious. Experts say awake bruxism may be associated with periods of stress, anxiety or intense concentration, while sleep bruxism may occur alongside other sleep-related problems. In many cases, however, people may be unaware of the habit, particularly when it occurs during sleep. Rise in use of night guards, but they do not address the underlying cause With growing awareness of bruxism, dentists are seeing greater use of night guards, which are designed to separate the upper and lower teeth and reduce the damage caused by repeated clenching and grinding. According to Dr Ranjan, a custom-made guard can provide an important layer of protection, particularly in patients who have already developed signs of tooth wear. By creating a barrier between the teeth, it can help limit further enamel loss and reduce the risk of cracks, fractures and damage to existing dental restorations. However, a night guard is primarily a protective measure and does not eliminate the factors responsible for bruxism. A custom-made mouthguard doesnt cure the underlying cause of grinding, Dr Ranjan says. Identifying and addressing triggers such as stress, anxiety or sleep-related problems therefore remains important. In cases where prolonged bruxism has already damaged the teeth, restorative treatment may also be required. Worn-down teeth due to grinding can be restored with dental fillings or crowns, Dr Ranjan says.

articleTitle: IIM Ahmedabad tweaks PGP shortlisting, lists graduation disciplines
articleFeaturedImageAlt: IIM Ahmedabad CAT
description: The basic eligibility criteria remain unchanged. Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree or an equivalent qualification with at least 50 per cent marks or equivalent CGPA.
body_raw: The Indian Institute of Management IIM Ahmedabad has made minor changes in the selection criteria for admission to its two-year Post Graduate Programme PGP in Management for the 2027-29 batch. This time, they have introduced a new classification of undergraduate disciplines and revised the way candidates academic backgrounds are assessed. IIM Ahmedabad has divided undergraduate degrees into 18 broad disciplines for its admission process, including engineering and technology, computer science and information technology, medical and health sciences, commerce, accounting and finance, economics, agriculture and allied sciences, social sciences, arts and humanities, law, management, mathematics, pure sciences, professional courses, fashion and design, journalism and media, architecture and planning, hospitality and food sciences and others. The change is part of the revised admission process for the PGP programme. IIM-A uses candidates academic performance, CAT-2026 scores and other components to shortlist applicants for the subsequent stages of selection. Read Indian student Pratyush Prabhakar elected VP of Academic Affairs at Harvard Kennedy School Under the new policy, candidates graduation marks will be awarded rating scores ranging from one to 10. Candidates scoring up to 55 per cent in graduation will receive one point, while those scoring above 55 to 60 per cent will receive two points. The rating increases to three points for scores above 60 to 70 per cent, five points for above 70 to 80 per cent, eight points for above 80 to 90 per cent and 10 points for scores above 90 per cent. IIM Ahmedabad has also retained a gender-diversity component in its selection process. Non-male candidates will receive three points under this component, while male candidates will receive no points. The basic eligibility criteria, however, remain unchanged. Candidates must hold a bachelors degree or an equivalent qualification with at least 50 per cent marks or equivalent CGPA. The minimum requirement is 45 per cent for candidates belonging to the Scheduled Caste SC, Scheduled Tribe ST and Persons with Disability PwD categories. The degree should involve at least three years of education after completing Class 12 or an equivalent examination. Candidates appearing for their final-year bachelors degree examination or awaiting results can also apply, subject to the conditions specified by the institute. Also Read IITs, IIMs see more women joining than ever as placements and salary packages rise For the 2027-29 batch, candidates must also be at least 19 years old as on June 30, 2027. IIM Ahmedabad has retained the minimum CAT-2026 qualifying cut-offs. For General and Economically Weaker Section EWS candidates, the overall cut-off is 95 percentile, with an 85 percentile sectional cut-off. The corresponding overall cut-offs are 90 for NC-OBC, 85 for SC and 75 for ST candidates. In the notice, the institute has clarified that these are minimum qualifying cut-offs and meeting them does not guarantee a call for the next stage of the admission process. The revised admission policy is applicable to candidates seeking admission to IIMAs PGP for the 2027-29 academic session.

articleTitle: Citing postpartum psychosis, court acquits mother sentenced to life for killing infant
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gauhati High Court mother infant baby postpartum psychosis
description: The woman allegedly told the police that she did not like her daughter from the day she was born, but the court said her statement was inadmissible as it could have been made under police pressure or influence.
body_raw: A case in which a mother was convicted for killing her 38-day-old daughter took a different turn before the Gauhati High Court, which found that she may have been going through the rare mental health condition of postpartum psychosis.The court acquitted the woman in the 2016 case, holding that her confession was inadmissible as it raised concerns of police pressure. Justices M Zothankhuma and Rajesh Mazumdar on October 6 allowed the womans appeal against her conviction and life imprisonment by the trial court in September 2023. The court mentioned that postpartumpsychosis is a severe mental condition which develops following delivery, and scientific research has pointed out that childbirth is a potent trigger for severe mood disorder. The woman had allegedly told the police that she did not like her daughter from the day she was born. Her confessional statement is to the effect that she was mentally unwell and that she did not like her daughter from the day she was born. On trying to understand the case where a mother does not like her newborn child, we have come across rare cases of infanticide due to Postpartum Psychosis, the court said. Postpartum psychosis is a rare and severe mental health condition that can develop after childbirth and is distinct from postpartum depression. The court added that women with this health issue can lose touch with reality, and its symptoms may include delusions, hallucinations, severe mood symptoms and cognitive symptoms. The court, however, said it was not required to decide whether the woman actually had postpartum psychosis, but noted that the issue should have been considered by the trial court before convicting her. Infant goes missing The womans husband lodged a complaint in 2016 stating that his daughter, who was one month and eight days old, had gone missing during the night. During questioning by the police, his wife allegedly confessed in the presence of local witnesses that she had killed the child on October 14, 2016, and thrown the body into the Dikhow River. The husband, however, said that when he had inquired about the missing infant, the wife stated that she did not know where the baby was. The woman was represented by advocate D Baruah. Can put mother, child in danger The court pointed out that some symptoms of postpartum psychosis can be fleeting and changeable. It noted that there is a risk to babies in around 35 per cent of postpartum psychosis cases, as mothers going through the condition may act on false beliefs, incorrectly handle their babies, become severely confused or behave unusually. The court added that such behaviour can be temporary and is caused by the effect of postpartum psychosis on the brain. The National Library of Medicine in the National Centre for Biotechnology Information states that postpartum psychosis is rare, affecting one and two per one thousand women. However, postpartum psychosis can develop rapidly and place the life of the mother and infant in danger, the court mentioned. It noted that the mothers confessional statement was signed by a woman head constable who was present when it was recorded. The same makes the said confessional statement inadmissible as evidence, as the accused cannot be said to be completely free from police pressure or influence at the time of making her confession, it added. The court held that the womans conviction could not be sustained solely on the basis of the inadmissible confession and that an admission made during the hearing on sentence could not be treated as additional evidence for conviction. It thus set aside the conviction and acquitted her of the charge of murder.

articleTitle: ‘Imaandaar CM’ hoardings flood poll-bound Punjab. But why are people upset?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhagwant Mann hoarding
description: Ludhiana residents have questioned why honesty "needs an announcement or publicity", and why crores of taxpayers' money was being spent to issue a "self-certified honesty declaration".
body_raw: With less than six months to go for the Punjab Assembly elections, the ruling Aam Aadmi Party AAP in Punjab is fighting a paradox. While the Punjab and Haryana High Court has ordered a high-level CBI probe into the serious corruption allegations linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns office, the roads, highways and streets in the state, especially in the states largest city, Ludhiana, are speaking otherwise. Huge hoardings declaring CM Mann as imaandaar honest have flooded Ludhiana at intervals of every few meters across the city- from highways, chowks, roadsides to streets. Not just Ludhiana, but the imaandaar CM hoardings have cropped up across the state -- drawing sharp reactions from the Opposition parties as well as residents. Residents in Ludhiana have questioned why imaandaari honesty needs an announcement or publicity, and why crores of taxpayers money was being spent to issue a self-certifiedhonesty declaration for the CM when polls were just months away, and people would be the only judge. The critics are also pointing to CM Manns own words, before he became the CM, when he had flayed other parties for advertising false claims. In Ludhiana, huge hoardings declaring Mann as imaandaar CM have been installed on Ferozepur Road, with his smiling face and a caption Imaandaar CM 90 households getting 600 units of free power. The honesty hoardings have also been put prominently in posh locations of Ludhiana West constituency such as Pakhowal Road near Hotel Park Plaza, Aggar Nagar locality on Ferozepur Road, near Sidhwan Canal Pakhowal Road, etc apart from highways and roundabouts. Ludhiana-based RTI activist and an environmentalist Kuldeep Singh Khaira said it is high time linguists update the definition of honesty. After the High Court order, even the word imaandaar must be thinking, What do I really mean? Now it feels we have to update the definitionof honesty. Those who are really honest never really sing about it. They dont need to announce it. Harjot Benipal, a worker of Akali Dal Waris Punjab De, said This has also probably happened for the first time in 70 years that a CM is declaring himself as honest. Sandeep Singh, a resident, said If a CM has to scream through hoardings that he is honest, there is something fishy. Moreover, can the AAP issue a White Paper on who has paid for this flood of hoardings in the city? Residents question why crores have been spent just to portray him as clean. Polls are a few months away. Let the people decide, said another resident, Kanav Sharma. Harminder Taneja, another resident, said Why is so much advertising needed if you are really honest?From where is so much money coming to spend on advertising? From the pockets of people. Echoing the view, Rashpal Singh, a student, said What kind of honesty is that when you have to shout about it through billboards?Taxpayers money is being used to promote the CMs honesty this is also a first in 70 years. With the AAP heavily banking on its kattar imaandaar a die-hard honest party pitch for the election campaigns, and the phrase repeatedly used by AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal to describe his party leaders, the residents are also taking a dig at the party for omitting kattar in the billboards. The AAP government must sue the creators of these hoardings. How dare they miss the word kattar and write onlyimaandaar for the honourable CM, said a resident, requesting anonymity. Another resident, Prince Vij, said Bhagwant Mann is such an Imaandaar CM that he has to waste taxpayers money to tell everyone that he is honest. What a waste of public funds Pulling out an old video of Mann criticising previous governments for wasting money on billboards and hoardings, senior Congress leader and MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira highlighted the splurge of the Imaandaar CM. He alleged that CM Mann and AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal used to trap others with their word power. Now, theygot caught in their own words today Once they made fun of banners, and today they are running the government based on flexboards themselves. Claims are of honesty, but development exists only on paper and hoardings Before taking over as the CM, Mann had criticised previous governments for wasting public money on banners and hoardings. What kind of development is this that has to be advertised via banners? Had hospitals actually been built, they would be visible. After 9.5 years, this is fake development being shown on banners, Mann was heard saying in the video. CMs corruption stench has reached Delhi SAD Senior SAD leader and former minister Bikram Singh Majithia also took potshots at Manns honesty hoardings. Chief Minister keeps walking around holding a board that says, I am honest, while corruption in his offices has been simmering so long that its stench has reached DelhiPeople have started reading the boards and writing underneath Yeah, we got it OK, TATA, BYE BYE he wrote on X. Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon said What kind of honesty is this that advertisements are required to publicize it? Ludhiana BJP president Sunil Moudgill, in a statement issued on Tuesday, said that the Punjab government has put hoardings of Honest CM across the state, but they should be replaced with Dishonest CM. The High Court has ordered a high-level CBI probe into corruption allegations in the working of the Chief Ministers Office CMO and his Officer on Special Duty OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman, but the CM is protecting corrupt individuals. Despite the ED writing to the Punjab Government three times, they did not get it probed. What does this prove? he asked. Imandaar CM exposed Ravneet Singh Bittu Former union minister and BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu posted on X Bhagwant Mann, who has put up billboards across Punjab proclaiming himself as Imandaar CM, has been exposed today.Acting on the direct orders of the Honble Punjab and Haryana High Court and an ED report, the CBI has registered an FIR against the Punjab CMs OSD along with 5 others, conducting coordinated raids across 8 locations.Behind the self-promoted billboards of integrity lay severe allegations of institutionalized corruption-from auctioning IASIPS transfers and manipulating government tenders to fixing land CLUs and leaking confidential policy drafts for pecuniary gain.Integrity was confined to advertisements, while power was blatantly abused behind closed doors. Hoardings are part of routine campaign However, Ludhiana AAP president urban Jatinder Singh Khangura said that such hoardings are a part of the routine campaign of the party that we run from time to time. CM Mann is the most popular face of our party, and he will lead our election campaign for 2027. His honesty doesnt need any proof. We have no idea who has paid for these hoardings-the party or the government. However, AAP Punjab spokespersons - Malwinder Singh Kang, Baltej Singh Pannu, and Neel Garg - were not available for comments.

articleTitle: Ola, Uber banned in Chandigarh. Drivers have a workaround. So do cops
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chandigarh bike taxi ban, Chandigarh taxi ban, Chandigarh bike taxi crackdown, Chandigarh Police taxi crackdown, Uber ban Chandigarh, Ola ban Chandigarh, Rapido ban Chandigarh, inDrive ban Chandigarh, banned bike taxis Chandigarh, app-based taxis Chandigarh, Chandigarh transport rules, Bharat Taxi Chandigarh, Chandigarh news, Indian Express news
description: The crackdown has so far resulted in action against 915 vehicles in Chandigarh, making it the authorities’ biggest drive yet against unauthorised app-based transport services.
body_raw: The ride may be banned, but getting one is still surprisingly easy. In Chandigarh, drivers of app-based taxis and bike taxis linked to Uber, Ola, inDrive, and Rapido are finding new ways to stay on the road - and the police are finding new ways to catch them. From switching phones to airplane mode to cancelling bookings just before the ride begins, drivers are adopting tactics to evade enforcement, while Chandigarh Police are booking rides themselves on banned platforms to catch them in the act. The cat-and-mouse game has so far resulted in action against 915 vehicles - 812 challaned and 103 impounded - in what authorities describe as their biggest crackdown yet on unauthorised app-based transport services. Modus operandi The drivers allegedly put their phones on airplane mode, ask passengers to pay the amount shown, cancel the ride just before starting, and go offline while plying routes where police are not normally deployed. Drivers also allegedly ask passengers to tell the police they found the cab parked and hired it directly. When the police catch the driver, he quickly puts his phone on airplane mode. Meanwhile, the Chandigarh Police book cabs through the banned apps themselves to catch drivers red-handed. After stopping a vehicle, they check the drivers phone and apps to establish whether the cab is being operated through a banned platform. More bikes than cabs According to State Transport Authority STA data, bike taxis accounted for the bulk of the violations, with nearly 70 per cent of all vehicles found operating in Chandigarh, underlining the scale of their continued operation in the city. Data shows as many as 569 bike taxis were challaned and 67 impounded, taking the number to 636. Among the 208 taxis, 194 were challaned and 14 impounded. Despite the ban, app-based two-wheeler services and taxis both have a significant presence on city roads, a STA senior officer told The Indian Express. The Chandigarh Administration had also written to the Centre seeking a GPS-based mechanism to restrict the operation of the suspended aggregator apps within Chandigarh. The move was proposed as the apps remain accessible despite suspension of their licences, allowing drivers to continue accepting bookings. The ban Earlier this month, Chandigarh Administration suspended the licences of Uber and Rapido for six months. STA said the two companies had failed to comply with mandatory requirements covering driver insurance and training, fares, vehicle eligibility, safety and other operational norms, despite being given several opportunities to meet the conditions. The action followed the Union Territory administrations earlier suspension of Ola and inDrive over alleged violations related to driver welfare and training. However, the ban has made commuting difficult for passengers, with fewer options and, at times, higher fares due to reduced competition. Although the Bharat Taxi app is an alternative, many commuters still dont know about it, leaving them struggling to find affordable rides.

articleTitle: Virat Kohli refutes claim he visited Premanand Ji Maharaj for Rs 5 cr: ‘Out of deep faith’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anushka Sharma and Virat Kohli visit their guru Premanand Ji Maharaj in Vrindavan
description: In a letter to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Dinesh Sharma alleged that a Rajasthan-based private company and a property builder lobby had spent Rs 5 crore to facilitate Virat Kohli’s first visit to the ashram in 2023.
body_raw: Cricketer Virat Kohli has dismissed claims that he first visited the ashram of spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj in exchange for money, calling the allegations baseless and factually incorrect. He emphasised his deep faith as the reason for his visits, along with actor wife Anushka Sharma, to the ashram. The allegations began after the death of a disciple of Premanand Ji Maharaj, Rasik Dulari, under mysterious circumstances at his Radha Keli Kunj Ashram. Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma, president of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas, claimed that Virat Kohli was paid Rs 5 crore to visit the ashram for the first time. Kohlis team, however, has categorically refuted the claim. The cricketers spokesperson issued an official statement saying, We would like to categorically state that the claims made by Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma in regards to Mr Virat Kohli are completely false, baseless and factually incorrect. The statement further read, Mr Virat Kohli visits Premanand Maharaj Ji purely out of his deep faith and reverence for Maharaj Ji. It concluded, We strongly refute these claims and urge the media to exercise due diligence, verify facts before reporting or amplifying such statements, and report responsibly. What sparked the controversy? Following Rasik Dularis death, Sharma alleged that the builder lobby and land mafia had been using the name of Premanand Maharajs ashram for public relations and running an alleged extortion racket. ALSO READ Soundarya Rajinikanth says parents changing male-dominated dynamic at home My rocks during divorce In a letter to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Dinesh Sharma alleged that a Rajasthan-based private company and a property builder lobby had spent Rs 5 crore to facilitate Kohlis first visit to the ashram in 2023. He alleged that the motive was to boost the popularity and reach of the ashram. The investigation into Rasik Dularis death is underway. When Virat-Anushka first visited Premanad Maharaj Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma first visited Vrindavan on January 4, 2023, to seek the blessings of Premanand Maharaj. Since then, the couple has made several visits to meet the spiritual leader, including before and after IPL matches and during their trips to India from London. Multiple videos from the couples visits to the spiritual leader often go viral on social media. Their most recent visit was on July 22, 2026, when they visited Premanand Maharaj at his ashram in Vrindavan. The couple made headlines after they were seen walking barefoot through the drizzle to seek his blessings.

articleTitle: Ajay Devgn doesn’t rule out Drishyam 4, says Mohanlal film ‘most suited for their audience’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn says Mohanlal's Drishyam 3 is "most suited" for the Malayalam audience.
description: Ajay Devgn reveals the Hindi and Malayalam teams of Drishyam 3 discussed their scripts with each other, before going in completely different directions.
body_raw: Abhishek Pathaks Bollywood crime thriller Drishyam 3 took a different route from Jeetu Josephs Malayalam counterpart, which released earlier this year, marking a departure from the previous two instalments of the franchise. That risk seems to have paid off, with the Ajay Devgn-starrer now crossing Rs 340 crore at the worldwide box office. But the actor maintains that it was a natural chain of events, instead of a cinematic rebellion, to tread a different path than the Mohanlal-starrer, which didnt get the rave reviews the franchise is otherwise known for. Ajay Devgn says Hindi and Malayalam teams discussed their stories After Abhishek and his father Kumar Mangat Pathaks production house Panaroma Studios acquired the Drishyam franchise from the Malayalam makers, the Hindi and Malayalam teams began working in tandem. Honestly speaking, they had not decided to make a third one. We were toying with the idea, and I think all the writers worked out some ideas and they didnt work. And finally, things fell into place, Devgn revealed in a recent interview. We spoke to them, and we were like, Lets make it, we have a script. And then they said that theyre also working on something, and they had a script. So we thought, lets hear each ot her out and decide what to do, Devgn told Gulf News. After that, Drishyam 3 Hindi co-writers Abhishek, Aamii Keeyan Khan, and Parveez Shaikh, and Drishyam 3 Malayalam writer Joseph exchanged scripts. Finally we came to the conclusion that this is a fabulous script, but it is most suited for their audience. And we were very confident about our script. So, then we decided that we will go ahead, recalled Devgn. When you work hard and then you get something which is to the point, then youre confident enough to make it the way you want to make it, he added. Ajay Devgn hints at Drishyam 4 After the underwhelming response to the Malayalam version of Drishyam 3, Joseph seems to be developing the fourth instalment. Though Drishyam 3 was billed as The Conclusion of the epic trilogy, Devgn hinted that like his deceptive character Vijay Salgaonkar, the makers may have a trick up their sleeve as well, hinting at the remote possibility of Drishyam 4. At the moment, it is a conclusion, he said, before adding, I cant predict it. However, when pressed about the possibility of another instalment in the blockbuster franchise, Devgn didnt deny it outrightly. The decision was, this is the conclusion. The decision right now is that this is the conclusion. Right now, he added. Spoilers ahead In the Malayalam version of Drishyam 3, when Siddiques character, troubled by his wifes depression treatment in the US, vows to finally get back at Georgekutty Mohanlal and his family, the protagonist ends up having the last laugh yet again, even though that comes at the grave cost of physically hurting his elder daughter. articleTitle: Travel firm ‘denies refund’ as Australia tour cancelled amid Covid, man wins Rs 2.3 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: travel tour firm agency australia covid pandemic
description: The complainant had booked a 15-night, 16-day Australia–New Zealand tour with the agency in 2020 and paid an advance of Rs 2 lakh, but it was cancelled due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
body_raw: A West Bengal consumer commission has directed a travel company to refund Rs 2 lakh paid for an Australia-New Zealand tour cancelled during the Covid-19 pandemic, noting that it deliberately failed and neglected to refund the advance amount to the complainant. A bench of president Manoj Kumar Rai and member Ashoka Guha Roy Bera of the Kolkata District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission also awarded Rs 20,000 compensation and Rs 10,000 litigation costs, holding that failure to refund the advance despite repeated requests amounted to deficiency in service. The complainant had paid Rs 2 lakh for the tour package but did not avail the services of the opposite party due to cancellation of the proposed tour. Though several requests, reminders, and personal visits were made to the opposite party by the complainant from time to time regarding refund of the advance amount, the opposite party deliberately failed and neglected to refund the advance amount to the complainant, the September 29 order read. The ruling highlighted that the conduct and irresponsible attitude of the travel company caused significant disruption and financial loss to the complainant. The said act of the opposite party proves the fact that the opposite party is deficient and negligent in rendering service to the complainant, it said. 2-week Australia, NZ tour The complainant had booked a 15-night, 16-day AustraliaNew Zealand tour with an international travel and tourism agency, scheduled to begin on October 14, 2020, and paid an advance of Rs 2 lakh. However, the tour was cancelled due to the Covid-19 pandemic and international travel restrictions. After the cancellation, the complainant sought a refund from the travel company and was assured that the amount would be returned. However, despite repeated requests and a legal notice dated February 10, 2022, the company did not refund the money. The complainant then approached the consumer commission in May 2022, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. The travel company contested the complaint, arguing that under the contract the complainant was not entitled to a refund and that it had offered a credit voucher for future services after the tour was cancelled because of Covid-19 restrictions. Company failed to refund Order The commission found that the complainant had paid Rs 2 lakh for the AustraliaNew Zealand tour and was therefore a consumer of the travel companys services. It noted that the tour was cancelled because of the Covid-19 pandemic, cancellation of international flights and travel restrictions. Despite the cancellation, the travel company did not refund the Rs 2 lakh even though the complainant had made repeated requests, reminders and personal visits, the commission observed. It further observed that the company had failed to take any positive steps towards refund, which it described as a primary duty of a service provider. Takeaway The order underscored that travel companies cannot retain customers money after cancellation of services, even when disruptions arise from extraordinary circumstances. It reinforces consumers right to timely refunds and holds service providers accountable for financial loss and harassment caused by failure to return advance payments. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states West Bengal 1800-345-2808 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: College withholds security money over lost receipt, MBBS student wins Rs 2.40 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Medical college security money refund MBBS student
description: A man who took admission in a private medical college and deposited refundable security money was later shifted to another college after the institute was closed for administrative reasons.
body_raw: A Rohtak consumer commission ordered a private medical college to pay Rs 2.40 lakh to a former MBBS student after it withheld his refundable security and library deposits because he could not produce the original receipt. The commission held that the mere failure to produce the original receipt was not, by itself, sufficient ground to permanently deny the refundable security amount, especially when the payment was supported by documentary evidence. President Nagender Singh Kadian, along with members Dr Tripti Pannu and Dr Vijender Singh, was hearing a complaint filed by a 26-year-old man who had completed his MBBS degree, including internship, in January 2019. The mere non-production of the original receipt, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, cannot by itself be treated as sufficient ground to permanently deny the complainant the refundable security amount, particularly when the payment is otherwise supported by documentary evidence and the respondents colleges have not established that the said amount was adjusted, refunded or otherwise utilised towards any lawful liability of the complainant, the September 24 order read. Shifted to another college The man claimed that he took admission in the private medical college in 2012 and deposited Rs 2 lakh as refundable security and Rs 25,000 as refundable library security with the institute on September 15, 2012. The man added that the said Institute was subsequently closed due to administrative reasons and its students were shifted to various medical colleges in Haryana. The complainant, along with other students, was shifted to another college at Hisar in 2017, where he completed his MBBS degree, including internship, in 2019. However, the man added that the security money was lying with the said college and he submitted a request letter in 2019 to the principal of the said colleges seeking refund of the security amount of Rs 2.25 lakh and enclosed a copy of the receipt. However, he was asked to produce the original receipt, which the complainant stated had been lost and was not traceable. Despite repeated requests, the security amount was not refunded, and the colleges ultimately refused to release the amount. Aggrieved, he moved the commission seeking refund and compensation for deficiency in service, causing him mental agony and harassment. The complainant was represented by advocate Anurag Malik before the commission. Colleges defence The college submitted that the complainant has not produced or furnished the original receipt of depositing the said security amount with the college, and in the absence of the original receipt of the security amount, it cannot be refunded, as the college is non-functional. It was further submitted that it was also instructed to all the candidates of each batch to submit the original fee receipts, but the complainant has not deposited the original fee receipt despite the direction to do so. Some students got refund The commission noted that it was an admitted position that the complainant had been a student of the erstwhile college and was subsequently shifted to another college. It also highlighted that the colleges themselves admitted that security amounts of other similarly situated students had been refunded pursuant to the government decision. The documents placed on record further show that even some students who subsequently submitted their receipts were thereafter granted refund, it noted. The commission further noted that the record demonstrates that the said security amount was refundable and that the university had undertaken the process of refunding the same to similarly situated students. In these circumstances, withholding the refundable security and library security amount of the complainant merely on account of non-production of the original receipt, despite the availability of a copy of the receipt and the affidavit furnished by him regarding its loss, amounts to deficiency in service on the part of the respondents colleges, it added. The commission also found that the colleges had not established that the amount had been adjusted, refunded or used towards any lawful liability of the complainant. Accordingly, the commission directed that said college pay Rs 2.25 lakh to the complainant along with Rs 10,000 towards compensation for mental agony and harassment and Rs 5,000towards litigation expenses. Takeaway This ruling highlights that non-production of the original receipt cannot, in the particular circumstances of the case, by itself justify denial of a refundable security amount when payment is otherwise supported by documentary evidence. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Haryana helpline 1800-180-2087 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.
