articleTitle: ‘Unrest, poverty brought them to India’: Court cuts jail term of 3 Bangladeshis
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bangladeshi nationals illegal immigrants detention madras high court
description: The Madras High Court, while considering the sentence, noted their economic hardship, migration from Bangladesh for employment, daily-wage work and several years of residence in India.
body_raw: The Madras High Court has upheld the conviction of three Bangladeshi nationals for residing in the State without valid travel documents however, observing that the appellants, owing to the unrest in Bangladesh and the uncertainty of their future, came to India to sustain themselves and their families, it modified their fine-default sentence and ordered authorities to complete their deportation within 30 days. Justice N Nirmal Kumar was dealing with a plea of three Bangladeshi nationals challenging their conviction under the Foreigners Act, 2004. It is not in dispute that the appellants, owing to the unrest in Bangladesh and the uncertainty of their future, and being unemployed and impoverished, came in search of employment and livelihood to sustain themselves and their families. Admittedly, they are neither involved in nor convicted of any economic offence, nor have they enriched themselves so as to assume that they possess the means to pay the fine, the court said on September 28. The court further emphasised that the appellants had come to India in search of livelihood they had stayed in Tiruppur for quite some time, and the first and second accused had also given birth to two children. It noted that the appellants had also been employed in banian factories in Tiruppur on a daily-wage basis. Three Bangladeshi nationals arrested The case arose from the arrest of three Bangladeshi nationals by the Veerapandi Police in Tiruppur in February 2025. Police found them with two children at Iduvampalayam and, during inquiry, they admitted that they were Bangladeshi citizens who had entered India without valid passports, visas, or other travel documents. According to the accused, they had been living and working in Tiruppur for over six years and had twin sons born at Tiruppur Government Medical College Hospital in September 2023. They said they had migrated from Bangladesh because of political unrest, unemployment, and poverty and had come to India in search of livelihood. The police registered a case, and the prosecution examined six witnesses and produced 12 exhibits. The trial court convicted all three under the provisions of the Foreigners Act, 2004. It sentenced each to two years rigorous imprisonment and a Rs 10,000 fine, with three months simple imprisonment in default. They challenged the conviction before the high court. Appearing for the petitioners, advocates M Mohamed Saifulla and R Bakiyalakshmi argued that they had not committed any other offence, had lived peacefully in Tiruppur, and were willing to return to Bangladesh. They also questioned whether proper procedures had been followed regarding their detention and deportation. They stated that due to political unrest, unemployment, and poverty, they moved from Bangladesh to Tiruppur seeking employment for their livelihood. At the time of crossing the border post, they informed their entry. They are very poor Court The court held that the prosecution had established that the three appellants were Bangladeshi citizens. Their Bangladeshi national identitycitizenship documents and birth certificates were produced in evidence, and they had entered India without valid travel documents. The court found no reason to interfere with their conviction under the Foreigners Act, and confirmed the two-year rigorous imprisonment imposed by the trial court. They hold, to date, a Bangladesh voter ID and citizenship card. They are natural citizens living here and have also begotten two children for their livelihood and subsistence, they are living in Tiruppur to make earnings and livelihood. They are law-abiding citizens and have not come under any adverse notice from the law-enforcing authorities. Now they are willing to go back to their country, the court noted. However, while considering the sentence, the court took note of their economic hardship and circumstances. They had migrated from Bangladesh in search of employment, worked as daily-wage workers in Tiruppur, and had been living there for several years. Two children were also born to the first and second accused at a government hospital in Tiruppur. The court observed, There is no doubt that they are very poor, are seeking livelihood, have migrated in search of employment, and are in penury and unable to pay the fine amount. Considering their financial circumstances, the court reduced the default imprisonment for non-payment of the Rs 10,000 fine from three months to one week, while retaining the fine and two years rigorous imprisonment.

articleTitle: Man caught recording Bombay HC proceedings; fined, phone confiscated
articleFeaturedImageAlt: bombay high court video recording
description: The high court also noted that such recordings are "manipulated in ways unimaginable, and then distorted versions are posted on social media" and "in fact, it has become quite rampant."
body_raw: Noting incidents of court proceedings being recorded without permission, the Bombay High Court has ordered the confiscation of the mobile handset used and imposed a Rs 10,000 fine on a man after he was caught doing so. Emphasising that the incidents have been unfortunately on the rise, the Bombay High Court also noted that such recordings are manipulated in ways unimaginable, and then distorted versions are posted on social media and in fact, it has become quite rampant. A bench of Justices Girish S Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale took suo motu on its own cognisance on October 5, noting that while the court was in session, around 1223 pm, a person sitting in the last row held a mobile phone, with its flash on. Suspecting he was recording court proceedings, the court staff, on the judges instructions, seized his phone and sent it for examination. The person, identified as Dilip Wagh, who works at the Education Inspectors office, was visiting the Government Pleader. He deleted the video recording after being caught. The video was later retrieved by the courts IT department. The HC noted that except for the HC registrys written permission, there was an express bar under HCs Rules to record court proceedings, which Wagh did not obtain, and he was fully aware of these basic expectations. There cannot be any objection for any member of the public to attend the Court and witness the Court proceedings, as they are open proceedings. However, certainly, restrictions on any member of the public to adhere to the rules and regulations governing the Court proceedings, when inside the Courtroom, need to be followed in letter and spirit, the HC noted. Thus, considering the seriousness, casualness and frequency of such instances happening, it is high time that actions as the law would mandate are taken by the Court, the order added. The judges stated they would be falling in our duty if they overlook the Rules by not taking any action. While the court accepted Waghs apology and did not initiate contempt proceedings, it ordered confiscation of the mobile handset, removal of all data with a registry panchanama, and its disposal as per legal procedures. He was also ordered to pay Rs 10,000 to the High Court Legal Services Authority within two weeks, and compliance was sought by October 19.

articleTitle: Paying Rs 5,000 by UPI after Oct 15? Who pays new charge and what RBI governor said today
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra
description: Starting October 15, select high-value UPI person-to-merchant transactions will attract an merchant discount rate (MDR) of 0.4%
body_raw: The National Payments Corporation of Indias NPCIs recent decision to introduce a merchant discount rate MDR on select Unified Payments Interface UPI transactions marks a significant shift in the economics of the countrys digital payments ecosystem. However, the Reserve Bank of Indias RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has sought to make one thing clear - the new charge, according to him, is unlikely to dent the enormous scale of UPI. On UPI-MDR, a decision has already been taken, Malhotra said on Wednesday. As of now, we do not see any drop in UPI volumes, and I dont personally think that a small fee will have a major impact on the volumes. Starting October 15, select high-value UPI person-to-merchant P2M transactions will attract an MDR of 0.4. The charge will apply to transactions above Rs 2,000, with a cap of Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. RBI repo rate news LIVE The crucial point, however, is where the burden falls. The MDR will be paid by merchants within the digital payment ecosystem, while consumers will not be charged. That distinction is important. UPI has become synonymous with frictionless digital payments, and any change to the cost structure of transactions inevitably raises questions about whether users and merchants will alter their behaviour. The RBI, at least for now, does not appear concerned that the introduction of a fee for certain transactions will undermine the platforms momentum. Growing volumes The latest numbers offer some support to that assessment. UPI transaction volumes grew 22.2 in the second quarter of 2026-27, although this was slower than the 24.2 growth recorded in the first quarter. While the central bank regulates the payment system, the government has created the legal framework. The current UPI MDR structure has been introduced by NPCI under that framework. The numbers point to continued expansion, but they also underline the scale of the challenge. UPI is not merely another payment mechanism. Its strength lies in its reach and volume, and the policy question is whether introducing MDR on a segment of transactions can coexist with that growth without altering the behaviour that has made UPI so pervasive. Malhotras argument is straightforward a small fee should not materially change volumes. But the real test begins after October 15, when the new framework will move from policy announcement to actual transactions. Bankers said the fact that consumers will not bear the charge directly could help limit any immediate impact on usage. Yet merchants are at the centre of the MDR framework, and the eventual effect on the digital payment ecosystem will depend on how they respond to the additional processing cost, they said. For now, the RBI is betting that UPIs scale and convenience will outweigh the impact of the new charge. The data shows that volumes continue to rise, even as the pace of growth has moderated. The coming months will reveal whether the RBIs confidence is justified. If UPI volumes remain resilient, the MDR may prove to be a limited adjustment to a rapidly expanding payments ecosystem. If growth weakens sharply, however, the decision could face tougher questions.

articleTitle: ‘Tried to kidnap me’: Nagaland woman pulled towards car by 3 men at Delhi 5-star hotel
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi crime
description: Police sources said the three men have been bound down and an FIR has been lodged in the case.
body_raw: Three men who allegedly harassed a woman from Nagaland and forcibly pulled her towards a Mercedes car in the parking lot of a five-star hotel in Chanakyapuri have been bound down by the Delhi Police, sources said. To be bound down means to be required to appear before an investigating officer on a given date. The incident took place around 3.15 am Sunday, police said. According to police officers, the three men were sitting in the car parked at the hotel and were playing loud music. As the woman and her friends came towards the parking lot, one of them objected to the music. When the woman moved towards the exit gate, one of the men sitting in the car pulled her hand towards the vehicle. As per the FIR registered in this case, the woman alleged that they were trying to kidnap her. The womans three male friends intervened, after which the men in the Mercedes allegedly started a brawl. When my friend came to save us, they beat him with hockey sticks and punched his face. When my two other friends came, they beat them with hockey sticks as well, the woman alleged in the FIR. One of the friends suffered injuries to his teeth., an officer said. The medico-legal case report of one of the victims friends cites swelling in the right hand. The accused allegedly fled from the spot in their car after police reached the location. The complainant had noted down the cars registration number, which helped investigators trace the men, police said. The three accused were booked at Chanakyapuri police station. The woman was taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, where she underwent a medical examination. Police said the case was registered on the basis of her complaint and the medical report. Police are examining CCTV camera footage from the hotel and other evidence to establish the sequence of events. The medical reports are also being examined to ascertain the injuries suffered by those involved, they said.

articleTitle: ‘No one believed in Hanuman Ansh, declared flop on day 8’: Producer on miracle that saved it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hanuman Ansh sequel update by Anupriya Nagar
description: In an exclusive conversation, Anupriya Nagar shared an update on the second instalment of Hanuman Ansh, she even spoke about start a production house.
body_raw: After successfully running for 62 days at the box office and earning over Rs 425 crore, Hanuman Ansh has emerged as more than a film - it has become a moment in Indias cinematic history, a lot like Jai Santoshi Maa that once gave competition Sholay back in the day. The devotional film, based on Neem Karoli Baba, was made on a budget of a shade less than Rs 2 crores. Amid its massive commercial success, SCREEN spoke to its co-producer, Anupriya Nagar, about its trajectory at the ticket windows, and how that Hanuman Ansh has been planned as a trilogy. It has also become the catalyst for Anupriya, who is 22, to write a book on it and set up a production house. Anupriya Nagar on the success of Hanuman Ansh The film, which started its journey with Rs 10 lakh collection, has emerged as the best return on investment seen in the Hindi film industry in decades. Talking about this feat, Anupriya shared, To be very honest, I didnt become a part of this film for it to become a financial project, for me it was an emotional project. There were no expectations. Even the team never expected the film to do so well. We just wanted the devotees and kids to watch the film and learn about Indian culture. The first two weeks, the film didnt work at all, and on the eighth day, the industry declared the film a flop. We became a little nervous and thought, If devotees are not supporting us, how will the rest of the audience watch the film? Also Read A 21-year-old gave up Zurich job to fund Hanuman Ansh, earned Rs 50 cr on Rs 50 lakh share We knew that this film would only work through word-of-mouth since it had no known faces, a first-time director. While Maharajji is the biggest superhero of the film, from a general perspective, this was the thought. Even before I came on board, people never believed in the film. They asked how this film would work. While people were craving this kind of content, not too many films were made like this. When the screens went down from 300 to 30, we were told that only a miracle could save the film from being pulled down at theaters. I couldnt sit with my hands tied, I did whatever I could, Anupriya Nagar added. I gave all my savings for Hanuman Ansh Talking about how the film has been loved for its simplicity, Anupriya shared they initially thought of releasing the film on OTT. Hanuman Ansh doesnt align with the formula in which films are made these days. Its a simple period film, so its normal to question if the audience will relate to it. Everyone thinks before the release they have made a Mughal-e-Azam, its only when it releases do you understand how the film is received. There were also conversations about taking the film to OTT first. But we wanted to build a community, so we went with a theatrical release, she said. Giving up a job opportunity at Zurich was not the only risk Anupriya took she even invested her lifes savings in Hanuman Ansh. When Ragini Sona told me they needed funds, I decided to give what I had saved. I used to work during Christmas holidays and get extra salary so I could invest it I thought I would go to Zurich and live a comfortable life. Later, I used all of those savings for Hanuman Ansh, Anupriya shared. Sharing what she plans to do with the profit of Hanuman Ansh, she said, After Hanuman Ansh, people started calling me Chasmewali Producer bespectacled producer fame has come my way. But I am still the same. Everyone is telling me to get a holiday house with the money Hanuman Ansh has made. I am not going to gift myself anything. I have everything I want. It is only because of the people that the film is doing so well, so I just want to give it back to society. I want to help children and provide proper education and health facilities and I am in the process of starting my foundation. It will be my greatest gift. I celebrated the films success with my family and we all went to Kaichi Dham after a really long time. It was the best celebration. Hanuman Ansh would be a trilogy While Anupriya shared how the film and political industry have come to support the film now, she recalled a conversation she had with Premanand Maharaj. Anupriya shared, I met Premanand Maharajji after the film released and was doing well. I thought he wouldnt recognize me. But he was so happy to see me. He told me, main bohot khush tha ke aap aaye, film ke pehle, aur uske baad bhi. Apne santo ke liye bohot bada kaam kiya hai He told me I am very happy you came here before the film and after its success. You have done a great service to the spiritual leaders. It was such a huge thing to say. Sharing that Hanuman Ansh is supposed to be a trilogy, Anupriya added, I am writing a book on my journey with Hanuman Ansh and with Maharajji. I am in the process of establishing my own production house, where I can tell these wonderful stories. We will take the film to OTT now. Regarding the rest of the stories, even 10 films will not be enough for it. From the very beginning, we thought of making a trilogy, this is the first part. We have to sit and plan the second film, and now the responsibility is greater. We need to decide the timeline. Right now we are trying to do justice to the film. The numbers are increasing, and we are still trying to reach more and more people. The film has now gone global as it was released overseas on September 11. Hanuman Ansh was released in theaters on 7 August 2026.

articleTitle: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis and women’s team coach each other
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis returns to coach a women's football team.
description: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis' titular character returns to Richmond to coach a women's football team -- only to learn life lessons in return.
body_raw: Ted Lasso season 4 was an afterthought. Ted Lasso, having hung his UK boots and relocated back to his home turf of the US, is summoned back to Richmond, this time to coach a womens team. The premise was enough for the Indian audience to churn out memes of Ted Lasso delivering the climactic sattar minute speech in the womens locker room, a la Shah Rukh Khans hockey coach Kabir Khan in Shimit Amins 2009 seminal Bollywood sports drama Chak De India. But Ted Lasso is no vindictive, defamed coach trying to get back his lost glory. Hes just an average American Joe pulled back to a land thousands of miles apart to do what he does best - live. Fish out of water - two times over Co-creator and lead actor Jason Sudeikis had signed off as the titular buoyant football coach after season 3 of Apple TVs Emmy Award-winning show before he had an epiphany. As he returns to Richmond to coach its second-division womens football team - he faces resistance, particularly from their coach Alice Chilton Tanya Reynolds. And just like that, its like season 1 all over again. A soccer player roped in to train a British football team? Heck, he doesnt even like tea. But thats not important. Whats key here is how Lasso makes his way in, not by blending into the British way of life, but by dialling up his infectious, charming self. Hes inherently a team player, so divisions - whether theyre nationality or gender - have little bearing on his being. Not that he vowed to, but instead of relishing tea, he ends up getting Rebecca Welton Hannah Waddingham, the uptight AFC Richmond owner, addicted to shortbread biscuits. Coach Alice is too messed up and amour-propre to exchange her head position with a man - however ebullient and chivalrous he may be - for the womens football team. The way episode 1 ends, one does feel that the male wagon of creators and showrunners - Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, and Brett Goldstein - are using the audiences unabating love for Ted to shortchange Alice. Take it or leave it with a shrug of shoulders - that seems to be Teds tone, even though hes trying to be as unobtrusive and friendly as possible. So, when Alice caves in - and doesnt accept Teds farewell gift - it feels like feminism just walked backwards by a few steps. Its natural then that Alice feels a strong surge of jealousy when she sees Ted warm his way into the womens locker room - even though it was she who handheld him and Coach Beard the first time, making them close their eyes and wait until the women are dressed. Ted isnt even the most abhorrent of men who mansplain women into learning football. Hes considerate, patient, and most crucially, in touch with his feminine side. He urges his players to cry out their emotions - theres crying in football - and not bottle them up like Alice. Hes also as conscientious - cleaning up a bar with the women after they make a mess out of it during an impromptu brawl with a bunch of men did Kabir Khan and the Chak De India girls clean up the McDonalds? No. Learning from life - and everything that it throws at you But theres something that Ted is bound not to get as a man. In an affecting and strikingly relevant episode, we see members of the team deal with personal crises - from taking up odd jobs to make ends meet since second-division womens football doesnt exactly pay handsomely, or doubling up as a mother of two because your husband treats her ambition as inconvenience. Teds go-to magic word - Believe - doesnt exactly cut it here, as thats easier said than done. It then takes an Alice to step in and make a tiny addition to get the women all pumped up - Believe. and win. Its this added adrenaline and call to action that season 4 of Ted Lasso needed to make it as effective as its predecessors. The individual arcs of all the women players couldve made for a far more impactful and well-rounded season than wasting it on side plots like a secret investor buying their way into AFC Richmond. Not all side plots are as tepid though. Rebecca giving new love a chance, before sabotaging it, and then giving it yet another lease of life, couldve made the most patient of men run out of the virtue. But it makes the audience comfort her like Phil Dunster does in his memorable cameo. Roy Goldstein and Keeley Juno Temple are arguably the Ross and Rachel of Ted Lasso, though even the Friends pair couldnt pull off the downright adorbs football commentary scene with a makeup set, including what Roy calls a squishy pencil makeup brush, as Keeley corrects him. Also Read - When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood bunch of thieves for stealing his bestseller plots The strength of Ted Lasso, thus, remains in the quiet, slow change it brings about, just like its central character and his constant nudging towards a fair, equal, and kinder world. The audience is invited into the heads of all characters as they struggle with their feelings. But when they finally let them out to the ones theyve been wanting to confide in, were gently drawn out. That not only prevents the show from getting preachy, but also helps us come to terms with leaving the beloved characters to their lives, if this is indeed the last season. A voiceover from the grave - one for the ages - by the shows old guard surely helps you tug it into the bed like its a child you want to kiss goodbye - I think of each name as a comfortable music in the mouth. tending, as all music does. towards silence.

articleTitle: Rate hike was expected. But RBI reinforces hints that more are coming
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Members of the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra (centre); and (from left) Deputy Governors Shirish Chandra Murmu, Swaminathan Janakiraman, Poonam Gupta, and Rohit Jain in Mumbai on October 7. (PTI)
description: The RBI has tightened its stance from "neutral" to "calibrated tightening". But neither inflation figures nor the central bank’s own forecasts have changed dramatically since August. So what explains the shift?
body_raw: It was almost a foregone conclusion that the Reserve Bank of India RBI would increase the policy repo rate by 25 basis points bps to 5.5 on Wednesday. What was not as widely expected was that the RBIs Monetary Policy Committee MPC would also make the policy stance more restrictive - from neutral to calibrated tightening. This shift is important. As Governor Sanjay Malhota pointed out, the change in the stance means interest rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook. According to Madhavi Arora, Chief Economist at Emkay Global Financial Services, the change in the stance feels more like a forward guidance and the RBI has clearly prepared markets for a higher-for-longer interest rate environment. While some economists did and continue to predict only a shallow rate hike cycle of 50 bps one basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point or so, financial markets had - even before the MPC decision to increase the repo rate for the first time in more than three-and-a-half years on Wednesday - already priced in a long-ish hiking cycle of at least 100 bps. This was despite the MPCs unexpectedly dovish statement and language on August 5, when the central bank said there were little signs of generalisation of price pressures so far. Generalisation of inflation means higher prices spreading to other parts of the CPI basket. We have already seen a stark example of this generalisation with commercial cooking gas getting expensive after the start of the West Asia war, restaurants and cafes sharply increased their menu prices. Consider the following the number of items in the CPI basket whose inflation was more than 4 was 65 in January and rose to 110 in August. Moreover, prices of 314 of the 358 items were higher in August compared to July. In February, this number was 236. Data for September, which will be released next week, may show more of the same. Little change in data When the MPC last met, it had with it the Consumer Price Index CPI inflation data for June, which had risen to 4.38 from 3.93 in May. Meanwhile, Wholesale Price Index WPI inflation had edged up similarly to 9.87 from 9.68. Since then, inflation developments on both fronts have not been outsized while retail inflation has risen to 4.82 in August, wholesale prices rose by 9.92. The RBI is mandated to target a CPI inflation rate of 4 in the medium-term in a band of 2-6. Of course, the MPC must be forward-looking and cant decide interest rates based on data for two months ago - it needs to take a view on what it thinks inflation might be a year or so down the line because interest rate changes impact growth and inflation in the economy with a delay of 9-12 months. However, the RBIs own projections have not moved dramatically, as the chart below shows. Governor Malhotra said in his statement on Wednesday that recalibrating the policy rate is imperative because headline inflation is seen averaging almost 5.8 over the next three quarters and core inflation is projected at 4.4 in 2026-27. The Governors statement emphasising that average Inflation of 5.8 over the next three quarters with core inflation projected at 4.4 needs policy recalibration reinforces the hawkishness, said Puneet Pal, PGIM India Mutual Funds Head of Fixed Income. Pal expects incrementally 75-100 bps of rate hikes over the next nine months. But even back in August, these forecasts were not markedly different CPI inflation or retail inflation was expected to average almost 5.6 in the three quarters starting October, while the RBI had predicted an average core inflation rate of 4.3 this fiscal. But it is only now that the MPC sees some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and generalisation of inflation after saying in August that there were little signs of the same. Economists were not convinced by the assessment made in August. On the monsoon front, the rain deficit this season has been 13, not very far off from 11 or so at the time of the August policy. And the West Asia conflict has never really shown crystal-clear signs of resolution, with matters remaining uncertain. New developments What has materially changed is the growth outlook, with the GDP seen expanding 7.1 this fiscal versus 6.7 in August following the unexpectedly high 7.8 growth in April-June. However, the MPC has noted on Wednesday that there is limited evidence of demand side pressures, although risks in view of strong growth in monetary and credit aggregates exist. Apart from faster-than-anticipated domestic growth, what has also changed since August 5 is that central banks around the world have increased their policy rates, including the US Federal Reserve, which last month raised the federal funds rate target range by 25 bps to 3.75-4 - its first rate-hike in three years. Like the MPC now, all 12 voting members of the Fed favoured this rate hike. Another one is expected in what remains of 2026. Other central banks to have raised interest rates last month include the Bank of Japan, the European Central Bank, and the Reserve Bank of Australia, among others. But the RBI focuses on domestic inflation and growth developments. And signs have been apparent for a while now that price pressures are spreading due to weak rains, the El Nino, and higher memory chip prices, among others. The reasons behind the MPCs turn between August and now may explain what lies ahead.

articleTitle: Between starlight and Antarctic ice — another neutrino is on its way
articleFeaturedImageAlt: physics, nobel, ice
description: Thanks to Nobel Prize winner Francis Halzen and his team, the ice is ready
body_raw: For an astronomer, light is the easy part Hold up a lens or a mirror and starlight is yours. Neutrinos are another matter. Born in the most violent places in the cosmos, these ghost-like particles pass through planets, people and most detectors almost without a trace. It took decades to turn a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a telescope for these deep-space messengers. This years Nobel Prize in Physics goes to the man who stayed with that hunt Francis Halzen, a Belgian-born physicist at the University of WisconsinMadison. Why chase a particle so hard to catch in the first place? You could see things in the universe you couldnt see any other way, Halzen once said in an interview. Neutrinos barely interact, so they escape from deep inside their sources while light gets stuck on the way out. Think of a journalist trying to reach the one official who was in the room where a major policy was made. The press conference is easy to attend that is astronomy with visible light. But the insider who knows what was really decided avoids reporters. Catching a neutrino is harder still. The gigantic IceCube Neutrino Observatory near the Amundsen-Scott South Pole station in Antarctica has lowered 86 cables into the ice, the deepest reaching almost 2.5 kilometers down. To place them, scientists had to melt holes in the ice with hot water. Each cable sports sixty sensitive light detectors, like beads strung on a thread. On rare occasions, a neutrino strikes a nucleus of an atom in the ice, and the collision generates high-energy particles. The resulting particles move faster than light travels in ice, and generate an eerie, bluish flash, much like a sonic boom of a supersonic jet. That glow, the signature of a far traveling neutrino, is what the sensors on the strings pick up. Such an instrument couldnt be built overnight. What Halzen himself once called a cute idea took smaller trials to hone the skill and show what a larger detector could potentially deliver. Conceived in the 1980s, the last cable in IceCube was dropped in 2010. Since then, it has been eavesdropping on far-away violent phenomena in the universe. Some strange galaxies, unlike our own Milky Way, host massive black holes that churn the gas in their cores and spew spectacular jets. These jets accelerate high energy particles called cosmic rays, which collide and produce neutrinos. These neutrinos point back to where cosmic rays are produced. The discoveries at IceCube have been helping astronomers to peek inside the core of these galaxies. In 2017, a single neutrino hurtled through the observatory, and its path indicated it was coming from the direction of the constellation Orion. Alerted astronomers worldwide swiveled their telescopes in that direction and found a blazar, a giant galaxy whose central black hole, weighing hundreds of millions of suns, spits out a jet aimed straight at Earth. The discovery gave a major boost to multi-messenger astronomy, where scientists use visible light, neutrinos, and gravitational waves to study the same cosmic event, pulling together the clues from all the light we cannot see. IceCube has also confirmed a prediction from the 1960s about how an antineutrino interacts with an electron. Halzen, the principal investigator of this unique venture, has long been drawn to astroparticle physics, the area of research that marries astronomy with particle physics. Born in 1944, he studied at KU Leuven, Belgium, where he completed his masters degree and PhD. Then, while working at CERN, Geneva, in early 1970s, he was invited to the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he has been since. But IceCube was never a one-man project It is the work of an international collaboration of hundreds of scientists and engineers. Starlight can be caught with a mirror. Neutrinos take patience. IceCube received its first major expansion only this year, and physicists are already proposing a successor eight times its size. Somewhere out there, another neutrino is on its way. Thanks to Halzen and his team, the ice is ready. The writer, visiting professor, IISER Mohali, was an astrophysicist at the Raman Research Institute, Bengaluru

articleTitle: Thai woman accuses Kanpur ‘husband’ of Rs 60 lakh fraud, hiding another marriage
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kanpur
description: The businessman was arrested after the woman alleged he assaulted and pressured her to convert; police invoke anti-conversion law
body_raw: Travelling 3,000 km from Thailand to Kanpur, a 35-year-old woman went looking for the man she said she married - and the Rs 60 lakh she had lent him. The man, a tannery businessman named Mohammad Irfan, had stopped answering her calls and cut off contact. When she went to his Kanpur home, she allegedly discovered that he was already married and had children. The woman approached Kanpur Police on Tuesday, alleging that Irfan and his family members assaulted and threatened her when she confronted him and pressured her to convert to Islam. Based on her complaint, Kanpur Police arrested Irfan and registered an FIR against him at Anwarganj police station under charges including assault. Police also invoked provisions of the anti-conversion law against him. We have arrested Irfan in connection with the case. The womans allegations are being examined, and necessary verification is being carried out, said Assistant Commissioner of Police, Kanpur, Manjay Singh. He added that Irfan has admitted to marrying the woman and is being produced before the court. The woman has been sent for medical examination and the report is awaited. We got married two years ago According to police, the woman, who runs a restaurant and a canteen in Thailand, met Irfan through social media around four years ago. She told police he introduced himself as a prominent Kanpur businessman involved in the tannery business who frequently travelled abroad for work. The woman said Irfan would stay at her house whenever he travelled to Thailand and that they subsequently entered into a relationship. Around two years ago, he proposed to her and the two later married in Thailand, she claimed. She said Irfan continued visiting her every two months. During this period, he allegedly took around Rs 60 lakh from her in several installments, saying he needed the money to expand his business. She told police that she arranged the money by borrowing from relatives and friends. When she later asked Irfan to return the money, he allegedly gave her different excuses. She also said she asked him to stay with her in Thailand, but he refused. She alleged that Irfan returned to India this year and stopped responding to her calls and messages. With her businesses in Thailand facing financial difficulties and her struggling to repay the loans she had taken to provide money to Irfan, she decided to travel to India to recover the money. She came to Kanpur with an acquaintance on a tourist visa on October 5 and visited Irfans house as she knew his address. It was there that she allegedly learned for the first time that he was already married and had children. She alleged that when she confronted Irfan, he and his family members abused and insulted her, and Irfan told her that she would first have to convert to Islam if she wanted to stay with him.

articleTitle: ‘I won’t stop’: In PM’s Viksit Bharat pledge, a message for Opposition
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Narendra Modi
description: The Prime Minister has often spoken about his vision for India becoming a developed country by 2047, when it celebrates 100 years of Independence. But these remarks are significant against the backdrop of political developments
body_raw: Contrasting the gloom and immense challenges under the UPA era with the energy, enthusiasm, self-confidence of India in the current global order, Prime Minister Narendra Modi Wednesday coined the mantra of we will do it, saying the country will not stop, nor tire, nor waver on the road to a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Speaking at the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha-Seva Jyoti Yatra, organised at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi to mark 25 years of his continuous leadership as head of government, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat and then as Prime Minister, Modi said, Even today, I consider myself a student. I try to learn something new each day. That is why today, I prayed. that my power to learn does not wane. The more I learn, the more my capacity to do something for the nation will increase. I am beholden to every person and every incident which taught me something or the other. What brought me victory taught me to be humble, and what made me stumble made me learn how to stand up. Well-wishers encouraged me and critics taught me to look within. Those who supported me showed me the strength of belief. Whoever opposed me taught me the power of democracy. Every crisis was a test of my patience, every success expanded my sense of responsibility. Everything I accomplished gave me the strength, the drive to move towards larger goals, he said. Stating that he began his day with a visit to the Shri Vinayak temple where he prayed for the nation and its 140 crore citizens, he said, I express my gratitude to all of you and to all my fellow countrymen. When I took the oath as Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001, I never imagined that this milestone would also come. Today, I have completed 25 years of continuously serving as head of government. This is the result of the continuous blessings of the janata janardan. I express my gratitude to all political colleagues of the BJP, NDA and all those who hold immense reverence for democracy. I bow my head at the feet of the people of the nation, he said. He said the Morbi floods inculcated in him a spirit of service and showed him the path to round-the-clock relief and service work, the Bhuj earthquake taught him to remain steadfast on reconstruction, and the Chandrayaan taught him to rise after failure. Similarly, the Covid pandemic, he said, underlined the importance of the nations collective consciousness, and the media gave him the inspiration to move forward through both bitter and sweet experiences. Praising the RSS swayamsevaks, whom he called the guardians of the countrys cultural soul, he said he never felt alone on his journey of selfless service. Modi said the occasion was not one of merely recalling memories but also of adding new energy to predetermined goals and commitment. Hum kar ke rahenge we will do it. Viskit Bharat by 2047, we will do it. Top three economies, we will do it. Aatmanirbhar Bharat, we will do it. Global manufacturing hub, we will do it. Organising the Olympics, we will do it. Steps in outer space, we will do it. This energy, this enthusiasm, this self-confidence is incredible, he said. That we have been born in this timeless land of Bharat is amrit itself, he said, saying while high office can be obtained anywhere, there is no sacred land such as Bharat. Taking a swipe at the UPA years, he said, In 2014, the nation expanded my responsibility as Pradhan Sevak. The nation was confronting immense challenges, only problems were visible. Each citizen was seeking a new path. Regarding Bharats economy, the world had begun saying its a gone case, growth was nowhere to be seen. Adding that a nation facing such severe disappointment needed a new confidence, he said he responded by doing the only thing he knows I urged the janshakti, repeated to them we will do it. And today, 12 years later, the picture has changed entirely. Earlier, when a crisis used to emerge, Indias economy jolted. When a crisis comes now, Bharats perseverance is discussed. Its resilience is discussed, he said. Back then, policy paralysis used to be discussed. Now the Reform Express is discussed. Back then, new avenues of imports used to be discussed. Today, records of exports are established. Back then, we used to import mobile phones even for our own use. Now, there is a jalwa of Made-in-India mobile phones, he said. Referring to flydubais Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, hailed as a hero for averting a catastrophe despite being attacked and wounded in the cockpit, he said, There will come a time when Made-in-India planes will be discussed. There are problems in our country, but we also have 140 crore solutions. This time is not to rest, but to move forward with enthusiasm. Today, the youth of Bharat have a huge opportunity. I want to tell the youth Your children will not go through the trials that your grandparents and parents were put through. That is what I am working for, he said. Asking the gathering to take a pledge, Modi said, Nation First will be my commitment. Serving the nation will be my goal. And the mantra of nagrik devo bhava will be my mantra, karma will be dharma, delivering on my responsibilities will be my commitment. Until Bharat become viksit, I will not stop, nor tire, nor waver.

articleTitle: Mumbai civic body cracks down on tax defaulters, puts Imperial Grand Palace Hotel up for auction
articleFeaturedImageAlt: imperial grand palace
description: This will be the first time since 1984 that the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has auctioned attached properties to recover pending tax dues.
body_raw: In a major move to recover tax dues and boost revenue, the Mumbai civic body has put three commercial Mumbai properties, including the famous Imperial Grand Palace Hotel at the Royal Palms in Aarey Forest, up for auction. This will be the first time since 1984 that the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation BMC has auctioned attached properties to recover pending tax dues. This is also the first time the BMC has attached a property linked to the contentious Royal Palms project to recover property tax. In total, the BMC will be auctioning three properties to recover Rs 74.98 crore. According to civic records, the Imperial Grand Palace Hotel auction shall recover pending dues of Rs 41.52 crore. The Royal Palms project, a contentious project that took off in the 1990s, aimed to transform a portion of the Aarey Forest into a luxury venue for leisure activities by constructing a chain of hotels, restaurants and a golf course. The project, however, nosedived after the properties got entangled in several financial cases. The current outstanding tax from this property stands at Rs 41.52 crore. The proprietors have been sent multiple notices, and we have had meetings with them. However, despite multiple deliberations, they have failed to pay the pending dues. Therefore, we have attached the property and will be putting it up for auction soon, a civic official told The Indian Express. The property has a carpet area of 38,143 square meters and has 422 rooms. It is located in a quaint corner of the Aarey Forest. The Imperial Palace was a five-star hotel listed as part of the Royal Palms project. In the early 2000s, this hotel was a preferred venue for luxurious activities however, its popularity dwindled after 2012. At present, the property lies unused and in a dilapidated state. Civic officials said the last conference recorded in this hotel was in 2012. Besides this hotel, the civic body will auction another commercial property in Malad Kurar for Rs 3.46 crore and another in Bandra for Rs 30.6 crore. In February, civic authorities attached 12 properties to recover pending dues up to Rs 269.62 crore. Civic officials said that after these properties were listed, some of their owners reached out and settled their claims while the remaining owners approached the court. The civic body put them up for auction after the owners of these three properties didnt make any effort to save them. Of the 12 properties that were listed, management of six properties settled the bill while six properties are still listed as default subjects. Of these six properties, two are open land parcels. Since the court has ordered us to revise the existing method of calculating the tax rate on land, we will be sending them a fresh bill. One of the remaining owners approached the court, and the case is sub judice. As a result, we will be putting out these three properties for auction, the official said. The civic authorities levy property tax on all real estate and commercial properties located within the BMC jurisdiction. Once the property owners default on paying taxes, the civic authorities send them notices, adding penalties. If owners still do not pay the taxes, these properties are seized or attached temporarily and put up for auction after legal proceedings. Property tax is one of the highest sources of revenue for the BMC, and this year, it has collected Rs 7,611 crore against an annual target of Rs 7,341 crore till March 31.

articleTitle: ‘80% NDA, 20% PDA’: Yogi Adityanath back with claim ahead of Assembly polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Yogi Adityanath 80-20 UP Assembly polls
description: Since the Samajwadi Party has not fielded a third candidate, there will be no contest between it and the BJP in the Rajya Sabha polls.
body_raw: After the Samajwadi Party SP decided not to field a third Rajya Sabha poll candidate from Uttar Pradesh, paving the way for the unopposed election of its two and the ruling BJPs eight candidates to the Upper House, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Wednesday that the state would again see an 80-20 fight in upcoming Assembly polls. Adityanath said in Lucknow that the Rajya Sabha elections would predict the Assembly election results. Yeh ladaai 8020 ki fir aa gai hai. 80 per cent NDA me, aur 20 per cent PDA me. Aur PDA ka kya haal hone wala hai, yeh aapke saamne fir aane wala hai The fight has again become 80 and 20. Eighty per cent in NDA and 20 per cent in PDA. PDAs fate will be before everyone, he said at the Seva Jyoti Yatra-Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha, which marks Prime Minister Narendra Modis completion of 25 years in elected office. Since the SP has not fielded a third candidate, there will be no contest between it and the BJP in the Rajya Sabha polls. The SP has renominated veteran leader Ram Gopal Yadav, uncle of party president Akhilesh Yadav, and fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani as its second Rajya Sabha candidate. The party has enough strength in the Assembly to get its two candidates elected to Rajya Sabha. The SP chief first floated the abbreviation PDA-Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak backward classes, Dalits, and minorities-in June 2023. The formulation was projected as the SPs social coalition against the BJP-led NDA, with Akhilesh repeatedly claiming, PDA hi NDA ko harayega it is the PDA that will defeat the NDA. Ahead of the 2022 Assembly elections, Adityanath had remarked that the Assembly election contest would be an 80 per cent vs 20 per cent fight, with the 20 per cent interpreted as a reference to the population of the minorities in the state. Adityanath later defended his 80 vs 20 remark. In an interview with ANI, he said, Its a reaction to an action. I spoke about 80 vs 20. Eighty per cent support the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP, while 20 per cent always oppose. We havent spoken about caste or religion.

articleTitle: Rahul Gandhi detained again: How does detention differ from arrest, what rights do detainees have?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is detained at Akashvani Bhawan on Tuesday. (Gajendra Yadav)
description: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita does not define 'detention' per se. Instead, it gives police a set of powers that allows them to stop, remove or temporarily hold people in certain situations, including when a crime has actually taken place.
body_raw: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi was detained on Wednesday October 7 as Opposition leaders protested in New Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision SIR exercise. This was the second time in as many days that the Congress leader had been detained - on Tuesday, too, he along with Opposition leaders including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was taken into custody by Delhi Police after protesting for nearly eight hours inside Akashvani Bhavan in New Delhi. On Wednesday, before Gandhis latest detention, police had registered a case of trespass into the Akashvani Bhavan premises. Since October 2, Delhi police have detained hundreds of protesters, including Advocate Prashant Bhushan, and AISA national president Neha Bora. Legally speaking, what exactly is detention? How does it work? And what rights does law provide to police and detainees? How does detention differ from arrest? Police, under the law, are empowered to maintain law and order, particularly during protests and demonstrations. In practice, this may sometimes look like an arrest and at other times a detention, often because these terms are used interchangeably. Arrest is a formal act of police taking a person into custody in connection with an offence, marking the beginning of criminal proceedings. Once a person is arrested, a range of constitutional and statutory safeguards immediately come into play. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita or BNSS, which replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure or CrPC does not define detention per se. Instead, it gives police a set of powers that allows them to stop, remove or temporarily hold people in certain situations, including when a crime has actually taken place. This is why disputes arise after protests. Someone may be taken away by police, kept in custody for several hours, and released without any case being registered. To the person involved, it can feel very much like an arrest. Legally, however, police may say that they were exercising preventive powers rather than arresting the individual for an offence. Senior Advocate Sanjay Hegde drew a distinction between a formal arrest and the short-term custody often seen during protests. They are temporarily not allowed to leave wherever they are detained, and they are not put under a formal arrest either, he told The Indian Express. Advocate Soutik Banerjee told The Indian Express that the distinction is often used to avoid the scrutiny that accompanies a formal arrest. The police know that the power to arrest cannot be exercised casually when there is no cognizable offence punishable with more than seven years being committed by the protestors. If they are arrested, courts will come down heavily on them. That is why they choose to abduct people and release them within hours, he said. A cognizable offence is one for which police can arrest without a warrant. Section 170 of the BNSS allows preventive action before any offence is committed. A police officer, knowing of a design to commit any cognizable offence may arrest, without orders from a magistrate and without a warrant, the person so designing, if it appears to such officer that the commission of the offence cannot be otherwise prevented. Section 172 of the BNSS says that a police officer may detain or remove any person resisting, refusing, ignoring or disregarding a lawful direction. The officer must then take the person before a magistrate or, in petty cases, release them within 24 hours. Unlike the earlier CrPC, this provision expressly allows police to detain or remove a person who refuses to comply with a lawful direction. Section 1722 BNSS is new. The CrPC had no equivalent, Senior Advocate Hegde said. The CrPC let police prevent cognizable offences and arrest to prevent them. It did not bind citizens to obey police directions, nor let police detain those who refused. Section 172 adds both. The idea came from state police statutes, not the CrPC. The 24-hour limit was itself a late addition. He added that the law on safeguards applicable to such short-term detentions remains largely untested no short-term detention and the consequences of not following safeguards have been litigated up to the Supreme Court. This position is different from preventive detention which allows a person to be held without trial under special laws such as the National Security Act. Banerjee said that the practice of briefly taking protesters into custody should not be confused with preventive detention powers under the law. He said This so-called detention has no place in law and is wholly illegal. Of course there are preventive detention powers available, but they are subject to strict rigours of the law and cannot be casually applied spontaneously. None of the abductions and excursions to Narela or Kingsway Camp in buses is carried out under legal provisions for preventive detention. When can police detain people? Most protest-related detentions begin with a claim that police are trying to prevent a law and order problem. Often, there is already a prohibitory order in place. On October 2, the Delhi Police imposed Section 163 of the BNSS across New Delhi. If protestors refuse to disperse or continue activities prohibited by such an order, police may invoke preventive powers to remove them from the spot or hold them temporarily. Disobeying such an order is itself an offence under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita or BNS, which replaced the Indian Penal Code or IPC. That is the point at which a detention can turn into an arrest with an FIR first information report. Courts have, however, said that such actions cannot be arbitrary. Police must be able to explain why restricting a persons liberty was necessary. The Supreme Court, in Joginder Kumar v State of UP 1994 held that the existence of the power to arrest is one thing and the justification for the exercise of it is quite another. In Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 2014, the court told police not to arrest automatically in offences punishable up to seven years. In Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan v Union of India 2018 the court held that restrictions on protests should be regulatory rather than eliminating the right to protest altogether. What rights does a detained or an arrested person have? Once the state restricts a persons liberty, a number of protections become relevant. Article 22 is a fundamental right under the Constitution that deals with protection of an accused against arrest and detention. It requires production of an accused person before a magistrate within 24 hours information about the grounds of arrest and the right to have legal representation. The Supreme Court, in multiple cases, has held that written grounds of arrest must be furnished. Just last month, the court held that if an arrest violates the safeguards prescribed under Article 22, it would be unconstitutional. Article 221 also provides for the right to consult and be defended by a lawyer of ones choice. Section 38 BNSS allows an arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation, though not throughout interrogation. If a person cannot afford a lawyer, free legal aid is provided to them at the States cost. Section 435 of the BNSS bars the arrest of a woman between sunrise and sunset, except in exceptional circumstances and with the prior permission of a judicial magistrate. The Supreme Court in DK Basu v. State of West Bengal 1997 laid down safeguards for all cases of arrest or detention. Officers must wear visible name tags. An arrest memo must be attested by at least one witness. Injuries must be recorded, and family members should be informed. The court also made clear that these safeguards are not merely advisory and officers who fail to comply can face departmental action or even contempt proceedings.

articleTitle: 22-year marriage not consummated, Calcutta High Court grants divorce, Rs 10 lakh alimony
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Calcutta High Court marriage divorce consummate alimony
description: The husband claimed before the Calcutta High Court that the marriage was never consummated as the wife allegedly said that she was not interested in physical intimacy.
body_raw: The Calcutta High Court recently granted divorce to a man after a 22-year marriage that was never consummated and directed him to pay Rs 10 lakh as permanent alimony to his wife. The court noted that the couple lived together as husband and wife for barely a month after their marriage in 2004 and separated after that, barring a brief period when they were required to stay together by a court order. Justices Debangsu Basak and Aryak Dutt held that the marriage was not consummated and that there was no valid reason or evidence of physical incapacity preventing consummation. There is no valid reason for the marriage not being consummated. There is no material on record suggesting that any of the parties were incapable of consummating the marriage. The materials on record suggest that they voluntarily withdrew from the society of the other, the October 5 order read. Lived together for 1 month The man claimed that the couple married in April 2004, but allegedly never consummated the marriage, and they started living separately after the wife left the house within one month. The husband later filed a divorce case on the grounds of cruelty and desertion in July 2016. He said that his wife refused to consummate the marriage, saying that she was not interested in intercourse because her figure would become shapeless and nobody would notice her after that. The mans counsel, advocate Kaushal Paul, submitted that there was an interim period in which the parties were required to live as husband and wife in the wake of an order of the high court. He added that the couple, however, never cohabited and neither was the marriage consummated during that period. The husband did not reside at the house with the wife at the time, the counsel added. On the contrary, the woman, through advocate Prantick Ghosh, argued that the husband did not give any particulars of her alleged cruelty. He also stated that the husband had not given particulars of the dates of the alleged non-consummation of the marriage. No amicable settlement The high court noted that the marriage was proved to have not been consummated and that the wife had admitted in her cross-examination that there had been no cohabitation between the couple. It also mentioned having made efforts to help the couple arrive at an amicable resolution of their disputes, but they could not agree to settle the same. The bench acknowledged that both lawyers tried their best to help the parties arrive at an amicable settlement and went out of their way in the process. The bench found that there was an irretrievable breakdown of marriage. The cruelty which was occasioned in the facts and circumstances of the present case emanates out of denial of conjugal rights and non-consummation of marriage, it added. The court also considered the assets available to the husband and found it appropriate to grant permanent alimony of Rs 10 lakh, payable in four monthly instalments starting November 15, 2026. It noted that the wife was gainfully employed.

articleTitle: Bengaluru gym trainer likely died of strangulation after party: Police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru gym trainer death
description: The police on Monday arrested three fellow gym trainers who were with the victim on Saturday night
body_raw: A preliminary investigation into the death of a gym trainer in North Bengaluru early on Sunday suggested that the 25-year-old man allegedly died of strangulation following a violent altercation with three other gym trainers in the bathroom of a flat, the police said on Wednesday. However, the police are awaiting the final post-mortem report to establish the precise cause of death of M Nandan, who worked at Masiv Gym in Sahakaranagar. The police on Monday arrested three fellow gym trainers - Vishwanath, 22, Sharath, 27, and Nishanth, 24, who were with Nandan at the flat on Saturday night - and booked them for murder. According to police sources, a group of four gym trainers, including Nandan, gathered at a flat in Kempapura following the gyms first anniversary celebrations on Saturday, where they reportedly consumed alcohol and drugs. Investigators suspect the men were heavily intoxicated when an altercation broke out inside the bathroom, escalating into a physical brawl. The police noted broken mirrors and fittings in the bathroom, along with injuries on the victim and the accused. Nandan sustained injuries to his face, while the other trainers also had injuries to their hands and knees, said an officer. Nandan was also found to have several bite marks on different parts of his body. The police are examining the injuries to determine how and when they were caused. Prima facie, authorities suspect Nandan died of strangulation, though final post-mortem and forensic reports are awaited. The police said Nandan was seriously injured after the fight but was not taken to hospital immediately. The men allegedly remained at the flat and attempted to pacify the situation. Nandan subsequently lost consciousness and was taken to hospital, where he was declared dead. Anush Shetty, owner of the flat where the gathering was held, was among those initially detained. The police have issued him a notice for inquiry and are examining his role in the incident. Gym trainers version A senior police officer said the accused gave investigators their account of what happened inside the bathroom. According to their version, Nandan vomited in the bathroom and suffered seizures, and that the injuries and bite marks occurred while attempting to prevent him from biting his tongue-a claim police are verifying against medical evidence. They have told us that Nandan was attempting to bite his tongue, and that they tried to prevent him from doing so by slapping and biting him, the officer said. Police rule out sexual act angle The police are also examining an allegation that Nandan and one of the men may have been involved in a sexual act during the gathering. However, investigators have not found evidence so far to establish that a sexual act took place, a senior police official said. The bite marks and other injuries are being examined as part of the investigation, but the police have not established that they were connected to any sexual activity. The police are also awaiting forensic reports, including the results of samples collected from the accused, to establish whether they had consumed narcotic substances and to corroborate their account of the incident. The arrested men are being questioned to establish the sequence of events inside the flat. The flat owner has told police that he was sleeping in another room and woke up later in the morning, when he found Nandan injured and unconscious. He then contacted a doctor and called an ambulance.

articleTitle: Blood on his face, legs tied: Man found dead in Kolkata cab
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kolkata cab driver death, Kolkata cab driver murder, Entally cab driver death, Kolkata cab driver found dead, Entally murder case, Kolkata crime news, Entally crime news, Kolkata cab murder probe, Indian Express news, Kolkata news, Kolkata police news
description: The Kolkata police suspect the body and cab may have been dumped in Entally after he was killed elsewhere, but are probing all angles.
body_raw: A cab parked by the roadside in central Kolkatas Entally area drew residents attention Wednesday morning when repeated calls to the occupant went unanswered. When the police arrived and found the vehicle locked from the inside, they called a mechanic to break open the door. Inside was the body of a man with blood marks on his face and both legs tied with a rope. According to police sources, officers traced the vehicles registration number and contacted the app company to identify the man. The man was subsequently identified as Bhagwan Prasad Gupta, 45, the vehicles driver, said a source. The discovery has raised suspicion that Gupta may have been murdered, although the police are yet to officially confirm the cause of death. Officers from Entally Police Station recovered the body and sent it for an autopsy. Officers from the Homicide Section and the Intelligence Branch at Lalbazar, Kolkata Police headquarters, also visited the spot and collected evidence. CCTV, booking history The police said they are examining how and when Gupta died and whether he was killed inside the cab or elsewhere before his body was brought to Entally. Investigators are checking CCTV footage from the area to establish a timeline and identify people who may have entered or travelled in the cab. They are also examining the vehicles booking history and contacting the app company to determine Guptas last passenger, where the cab travelled after the last ride, and its last known location. The police suspect, as one possibility, that Gupta may have been killed elsewhere and that his body and the cab were later abandoned at the Entally location. Investigators are probing this and other possible explanations. According to police sources, investigators are also contacting Guptas family, relatives, and friends to establish his movements Tuesday night, including who he was last seen with and whether he had any known personal disputes or enmity.

articleTitle: Bethlehem Kudumba Unit effect: Arvind Swamy-Sridevi’s shelved film to be revived after decades
articleFeaturedImageAlt: After 'Yavanakathayil' went viral in Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, Joshiy's shelved film Anna is set for revival.
description: After 'Yavanakathayil' went viral in Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, producer Tomichan Mulakuppadam has acquired the rights to revive director Joshiy's shelved film Anna, originally starring Arvind Swamy and Sridevi.
body_raw: Movies getting shelved isnt a new phenomenon in Malayalam cinema. From Randamoozham, Swarnachamaram, Australia, and Karnan to Dhanushkodi, Kaaliyan, and Antichrist, several films never progressed beyond the initial stages. Recently, director Girish ADs blockbuster romantic comedy Bethlehem Kudumba Unit brought one such film, Anna, back into the spotlight. Now, the movie is finally set for revival, with a new team taking over. Veteran producer Tomichan Mulakuppadam - best known for bankrolling blockbusters such as Pulimurugan, Pokkiri Raja, and Ramaleela - recently announced he has acquired the rights to Anna and is gearing up to give it a new lease of life. Taking to social media, he expressed his elation at the endeavour and stated he would announce the cast and crew details later. Also Read No one is to blame Kalaranjini lost her voice after consuming fake blood containing acid Tomichan Mulakuppadam acquires rights to shelved film Anna I am happy to share that I have acquired the rights to the film Anna, which started in the 1990s but was shelved for various reasons. Years later, when the song Yavanakathayil from the film became a sensation again through Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, there were many enquiries and discussions about Anna, he wrote. Tomichan added, It is with the desire to bring the story and associated memories of that film to the new generation through new writers that I have taken over the production rights of Anna. A new beginning for a film that stopped midway three decades ago. More details, including the director and cast, will be announced later. Anna is coming back to the silver screen through Mulakuppadam Films. What happened to Anna? For the unversed, master filmmaker Joshiy was set to helm the film in the 90s, with Arvind Swamy and superstar Sridevi in the lead roles. According to Onmanorama, veteran writer and novelist N Mohanan originally scripted Anna, and Balram of Ambu Films was supposed to produce it. The movie centred on the love story of Hari Arvind Swamy, a Brahmin boy, and Anna Sridevi, a Christian girl. Anna was envisioned with music given the utmost prominence, and legendary composer Ouseppachan and veteran lyricist Shibu Chakravarthy were brought on board for the same. They crafted eight songs for Anna and completed their recordings even before the filming began. ICYMI Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr However, the project soon ran into scheduling problems, as the makers couldnt match the dates of Arvind Swamy and Sridevi. Team Anna even considered replacing Sridevi with Meena. Yet, Arvind Swamys availability remained an issue, further delaying the project. Joshiy also had other movies lined up. Thus, Anna was shelved without any of its scenes being filmed. Nevertheless, the movies music found its way to the public in 1995 when Magna Sound released a cassette containing all eight songs recorded for Anna. Yavanakathayil was one of those songs, which director Girish AD included in Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, allowing Anna to rise from the ashes like a phoenix. Must Read Bethlehem Kudumba Unit review Nivin Pauly leads a sweet, non-creepy age-gap rom-com About Bethlehem Kudumba Unit Featuring Nivin Pauly and Mamitha Baiju in the lead roles, Bethlehem Kudumba Unit opened to rave reviews and emerged as the highest-grossing Malayalam film of all time, earning Rs 330.89 crore worldwide, according to industry tracker Sacnilk. Also starring Sangeeth Prathap, Suresh Krishna, Vinay Forrt, Roshan Shanavas, and Shyam Mohan, the romantic comedy was bankrolled by Dileesh Pothan, Fahadh Faasil, and Syam Pushkaran under the banner of Bhavana Studios.

articleTitle: Mobile phone bursts inside man’s pocket, consumer commission grants Rs 41,139
articleFeaturedImageAlt: mobile phone consumer court
description: The commission held that there was no rebuttal to the complainant's allegations and said that the mobile phone was defective and there was deficiency in service.
body_raw: A consumer commission in Uttar Pradesh recently directed a mobile phone manufacturer and a local electronics retailer to either replace a mobile phone or refund its cost after the phone allegedly burst inside a mans pocket in 2023, causing injury. President Hasnain Qureshi and member Purnima Singh Rajpoot also directed the opposite parties to pay compensation of Rs 36,139 and Rs 5,000 as litigation expenses. As there is no rebuttal of the pleadings of the complainant and therefore it is held that the mobile set was defective and there was deficiency in service, the order read. Phone burst According to the complainant, he purchased the mobile phone for Rs 29,500 in 2020. He alleged that the phone started heating up. After he complained, he was allegedly told that such heating sometimes occurred. After he complained, he was allegedly told that such heating sometimes happens. The phone allegedly heated up again, but his complaint to the local retailer was allegedly ignored. The complainant said that the phone burst while inside his pocket, injuring his thumb. He then lodged a police complaint. The complainant further alleged that the incident damaged photographs and videos from his marriage. He claimed that he was hospitalised after learning about the damage and that he and his wife had to hold another marriage celebration and arrange fresh photography and videography. He sought Rs 51 lakh towards the expenses of recreating the marriage ceremony and Rs 48 lakh as compensation for the shock, depression and treatment he claimed to have suffered. His total claim was Rs 99.29 lakh, though he restricted it to Rs 50 lakh citing the commissions pecuniary jurisdiction. The manufacturer filed its response beyond the prescribed period, which the commission said was of no importance, while the local retailer did not contest the case. The commission held that there was no rebuttal to the complainants allegations and concluded that the mobile phone was defective and there was deficiency in service. It noted that the complainant remained hospitalised and incurred Rs 36,139 in treatment expenses, as supported by the medical records. The commission directed the opposite parties to either replace the mobile phone with a new one or refund Rs 29,500. It also awarded Rs 36,139 towards medical expenses and Rs 5,000 as litigation costs. Takeaway Manufacturers and sellers can be held liable when a defective mobile phone causes injury to a consumer. Where the defect and resulting loss are not rebutted, consumer commissions can order replacement or refund of the product and award compensation for proven medical expenses and litigation costs. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Uttar Pradesh helpline 1800180030 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.
