articleTitle: Stabbed 7 times while sealing petrol pump, IOC officer’s killing echoes 2005 Manjunath case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Indian Oil official stabbed to death while sealing petrol pump, 4 held
description: The IOC officer was identified as Mahesh Shelke, 37. He worked as Manager (Retail Sales) and Field Officer with IOC and was posted in Nanded North.
body_raw: In a case bearing striking similarities to the 2005 Manjunath murder case in Uttar Pradesh, an Indian Oil Corporation IOC field officer was allegedly stabbed seven times during an altercation while he was attempting to seal a non-functional petrol pump in Hingoli district on Tuesday evening. Kurunda police have arrested four people, including a mother and her son, in connection with the murder and are searching for a fifth suspect. The deceased was identified as Mahesh Shelke, who worked as Manager Retail Sales and Field Officer with IOC and was posted in Nanded North. According to police, Shelke, along with three to four members of his team, went to the Sai Umesh petrol pump in Ambachondi village in Basmat tehsil on October 6 to officially take over and seal the retail outlet. The pump had remained closed for nearly three months but recently resumed operations. Police said the petrol pump owner was not present at the spot. However, his wife, son and some others were present when the IOC team arrived. An argument broke out, and the situation escalated when the group allegedly began pelting stones at the officials, a senior IPS officer said. During the confrontation, Umesh Pandvir, 24, allegedly attacked Shelke with a knife and stabbed him seven times in the abdomen, chest and back. Shelke died on the spot, and the accused allegedly fled the scene, another officer said. Four persons, identified as Umesh Pandvir his mother, Lata Sahebrao, 46 Shravan Gangadhar Wakude, 24 and a family friend, were arrested within 12 hours. A team is moving to trace a fifth accused. The Indian Oil Officers Association IOOA and IOC have demanded a swift investigation and strict action against the accused. The issue has been taken up with the senior-most officials of the Maharashtra Government and Police to ensure swift and strict action against those responsible, in accordance with law. The safety, dignity and security of our energy-sector personnel, who work tirelessly to serve the nation, remain paramount, Petroleum Minister Hardeep Puri said on social media platform X. Shanmugam Manjunath, a 27-year-old IOC sales officer, was allegedly shot dead in Uttar Pradesh. Manjunath was killed after he conducted a surprise inspection of one of the outlets allegedly involved in selling adulterated fuel that had resumed operations despite the action.

articleTitle: Flydubai attack: Saudi probe could test global aviation rules and pilot hiring processes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Israel Mideast Emergency Landing
description: Saudi Arabia has opened an air safety probe into the September 30 cockpit attack on a flydubai jet, while the UAE runs a separate criminal case.
body_raw: Saudi Arabia has started an air safety investigation into last weeks cockpit attack on a flydubai jet, three people close to the matter told Reuters. The probe will run alongside a separate criminal case led by the United Arab Emirates. Flight FZ1073, a Boeing 737 MAX bound for Israel, was in Saudi airspace on September 30 when the co-pilot allegedly tried to bring the plane down by attacking the captain with an axe. The jet dropped sharply but survived, and all 172 people on board were unhurt. Experts say the case could test a global system that aims to make flying safer without blaming anyone. What Saudi Arabia has said According to Reuters sources, Saudi Arabia has told aviation agencies abroad that it will carry out a safety probe under international rules. One of the sources said it was not clear whether Saudi investigators would make their findings public. Saudi Arabias National Transport Safety Center, which leads accident probes in the country, did not reply to a request for comment. The Saudi government and the aviation regulator also did not respond, Reuters said. Safety probes are normal after an accident, but they are not required when a deliberate act is involved, as is suspected here. Who else is involved The US National Transportation Safety Board has named a representative to the probe, Reuters reported. The agency would play a key role because the aircraft was built in the United States. Under international rules known as Annex 13, the UAE will also take part automatically, as the jet is registered there and flydubai is based in Dubai. UAE officials did not respond to Reuters. The UAE has opened its own criminal investigation, and its prosecutor general has called the incident a terrorist attack. The co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, had planned to crash the flydubai flight into Tel Avivs Ben Gurion International Airport. Photo AP enhanced via AI Israel, whose citizens made up nearly all of those on board, has offered to join the Saudi probe but has not been invited, Ofer Vaknin, head of Israels Aircraft Safety Investigation Authority, told Reuters. He added that Israel may not need to take part, as the aircraft itself had no operational or safety fault. Why the Saudi probe matters Safety officials say a deliberate act can still teach the industry something, Reuters reported. A probe into this case can look at areas such as how pilots are hired and how cockpits are kept secure, even though prosecutors lead when a crime is suspected. That is the main reason the Saudi probe is closely watched. It also matters because Saudi Arabia did not have to open one. Safety probes are not required when a deliberate act is involved, and until now it was unclear if the country would go ahead. Experts say the case could test a system of global cooperation that makes safety recommendations without trying to assign blame. Past cases show how this has worked, and where it has come under strain 2020 After Iran shot down a Ukrainian jet, US and Iranian aviation officials still took part together in the playback of cockpit recordings at the offices of Frances BEA agency, participants said. Reuters said such work has generally stayed out of diplomatic disputes. 2015 The BEA went ahead with a safety probe into the Germanwings crash, caused by the pilot, after a dispute with prosecutors over access to evidence. Friction between safety investigators and prosecutors has grown in recent years. Saudi Arabia and Israel have no diplomatic ties, yet experts say the UN-backed system, decades old, has worked across political divides. The Annex 13 rulebook gives observer status to countries with many deaths or injuries among their citizens, but it does not say what happens when nobody is hurt, as in this case. That gap leaves open the question of whether Israel will be invited to join.

articleTitle: Punjab: Supreme Court sets aside polls in 50 wards, orders re-elections in six weeks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court, Punjab ward elections, Punjab ward re elections, Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, Punjab and Haryana High Court, Indian express news, current affairs
description: To ensure that re-elections are conducted in a free, fair, and transparent manner, the top court asked the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court to appoint, within one week, a monitoring committee comprising a retired judge of the HC to oversee the process.
body_raw: The Supreme Court has set aside the elections to 50 wards in Punjab after a fact-finding commission appointed by it found widespread obstruction during the nomination process, whereby nomination papers were snatched, torn or destroyed, and candidates were assaulted, detained or threatened in the local body polls. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana ordered fresh elections in 50 wards - 28 in Patiala district and 22 in Moga. .the Commission found 50 ward elections to be vitiated and deserving of being set aside. We accept the recommendations and direct that fresh elections be conducted in the relevant 50 wards.The entire process of re-election shall be completed within 6 weeks, the bench ordered. In the September 28 order, which was made available Wednesday, the bench took note of the fact that Kapil Sibal, appearing for the State of Punjab states that the State has no objection to the acceptance of the recommendations made by the Commission. To ensure that re-elections are conducted in a free, fair, and transparent manner, the top court asked the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court to appoint, within one week, a monitoring committee comprising a retired judge of the HC to oversee the process.

articleTitle: ‘Bhakti is getting lost’: How Durga Puja at Delhi’s CR Park has changed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chittaranjan Park, Chittaranjan Park Durga Puja, durga puja, durga puja celebrations, Durga Puja pandals, delhi Durga Puja pandals, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: From door-to-door chanda to corporate sponsorships, CR Park’s Durga Puja has grown into a large-scale operation — and not everyone is happy with what that has brought.
body_raw: Devyani Rudra, 60, recalled her earliest memories of Durga Puja from Chittaranjan Parks J Block helping her mother, cutting vegetables for bhog - the traditional community meal offered to the Goddess and distributed as prasad - and joining the neighbourhoods cultural programmes. Earlier, only 50 to 100 people would turn up for the pujas, she said. Rudra and her family moved to CR Park from Delhi Cantonment in 1975. Back then, it was known as the East Pakistan Displaced Persons Colony, established as part of the governments rehabilitation efforts for those uprooted by Partition. It housed only 15-20 families, mostly government officials. The celebrations later shifted to Mela Ground and the Shiv Mandir in 1976, now known as Kali Mandir. Five decades later, Durga Puja has become a much larger affair. The colony now has nearly 50,000 residents and hosts around 10 major community pujas, besides several private household celebrations. Lakhs of visitors from across Delhi-NCR descend on the neighbourhood. But as the festivities kick off on October 16 this year, some of CR Parks old residents feel the celebrations have moved away from the intimacy of a festival once centred on the community. What does a puja cost? At Kali Mandir, the annual Durga Puja budget is around Rs 1 crore to Rs 1.5 crore, while other major CR Park pujas have annual budgets of around Rs 80-90 lakh. The temporary pandal and tent structure at Kali Mandir alone costs around Rs 25-30 lakh, said Jaya Ray, a member of the Kali Mandir Society and its Durga Puja organising committee. The bhog operation costs Rs 30-40 lakh. The kitchen serves at least 7,000 people within about four hours on a single afternoon, with 300-500 kg of food prepared on 10 wood-burning stoves, Ray added. The five-day cultural programme, featuring dance, music, orchestras and other performances, costs another Rs 5-10 lakh. The Mandir committee also spends on printing, decoration, logistics and the salaries of priests and support staff who work through the year. At other venues, the scale is similarly large. Narayan Dey, secretary of the Mela Ground Durga Puja Samiti, said during the festival, the committee runs a daily langar serving around 10,000 meals. Its pandal has expanded to around 180 feet by 85 feet. Saurav Chakravorty, General Secretary of K-Block Cooperative Ground, said that they see a daily footfall of around 1-1.5 lakh people during the festival while cultural shows feature artists who fly in from Kolkata and Mumbai. Who pays for the celebrations? Ray said the celebrations were once funded almost entirely by residents. In the 1970s and 80s, the celebrations relied entirely on personal resident contributions. We would go door to door collecting chanda. Back then, the pandals cost Rs 1 lakh or Rs 2 lakh. But now, that will not cut it, she said. The major shift came in the early 2000s, when corporate houses and public sector undertakings began sponsoring the pujas. At Kali Mandir, corporate sponsorships now account for around 70 of the Durga Puja budget, according to the organising committee. Individual resident contributions make up the remaining 30. Sponsors are given visibility through stalls at the venue, LED screens, backdrops and flexes at the gates. At Mela Ground, Dey said the committee puts up panels within the pandal area carrying the names of sponsors. The ecosystem behind the pujas The scale of the celebrations has also created a wider ecosystem around the festival. Kali Mandirs idol-making workshop, which began in 1972, produced only around three to five idols a year in its early days. By the late 1980s and 1990s, production had risen to around 100 idols. Today, the Kali Mandir workshop, along with its second workshop at Chandralok Cinema in G Block, produces more than 800 idols every year for puja committees across Delhi-NCR, other parts of India and overseas. The idols are made on commission and sold to other puja committees, providing the temple with an additional source of income. While commissioned idols generally cost around Rs 40,000 to Rs 80,000, larger and more elaborate custom installations can cost more than Rs 10 lakh. The workshops also employ artisans and other workers, allowing traditional idol-making expertise to remain within the community. At K-Block, Chakravorty said the idols are constructed completely in-house, from scratch, inside the pandal. At Mela Ground, 250-300 artisans and staff come from outside Bengal to craft the idols on site. But what is lost? The transformation has also brought criticism from some long-time residents. Rudra called it a commercialisation of the festival. Earlier, there were just a small number of food stalls. And that too, they were set up at no cost. But now the puja venues charge you in lakhs to put up stalls. She added that cultural programmes used to be conducted by the locals, and then film screenings. But now, if you see, popular reality show stars and singers fly in for the event, and local talent is no longer promoted. It is more entertainment than the puja itself. The growing crowds and high footfall have also raised safety concerns, Rudra claimed. The bhakti of the festivities is getting lost, and the present generation no longer understands that, she added.

articleTitle: IMC 2026: Ericsson to export made-in-India antennas to Europe and other global markets
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ericsson
description: As 5G networks evolve, Ericsson is looking to India as a manufacturing and export hub.
body_raw: Ericsson on Wednesday, October 7, announced plans to ramp up local production of antennas and other telecom equipment in India, while also exporting made-in-India gear to global markets such as Europe, for the first time. The Swedish manufacturer said that more than 15,000 antennas and 25 million components have been produced in India since July 2025. Its antenna portfolio is designed to support 5G standalone and AI-ready networks as well as future network evolutions. Ericsson made the announcement regarding its India-manufactured, export-ready antennas at the tenth edition of the India Mobile Congress 2026 organised jointly by the Department of Telecommunications DoT and the Cellular Operators Association of India COAI. The four-day annual telecom conference and exhibition is being held at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi from October 7 to October 10, 2026, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi expected to formally inaugurate the event today October 8. Ericssons export-ready antennas manufactured in India were first rolled out in 2025. Since then, the company said it has continued to expand local capabilities across sourcing, engineering, manufacturing and exports, serving customers in India and international markets. As mobile networks move towards 5G Standalone, AI-driven operations and future network architectures, antennas are becoming increasingly important to network performance. Ericssons push to manufacture more of this telecom equipment locally also aligns with Indias broader drive to strengthen domestic telecom manufacturing and build the country into a global export hub for such gear. India is an important part of Ericssons global innovation, engineering and manufacturing footprint. The production of more than 15,000 antennas and 25 million components shows how quickly this ecosystem is developing and the contribution it can make both in India and globally. Together with our partners, we are developing the capabilities needed for the next generation of high-performing, energy-efficient and AI-ready networks, Andres Vicente, CEO, Southeast Asia, Oceania and India, Ericsson, said onstage at the companys booth in the IMC 2026 Exhibition Hall. We are building an end-to-end antenna ecosystem that combines local sourcing and manufacturing with Ericssons global engineering capabilities. As networks become more intelligent and programmable, antenna performance will be increasingly important in getting the most from spectrum, sites and network investments. Expanding these capabilities in India strengthens both our ability to serve customers locally and Indias contribution to Ericssons global operations, Mikael Eriksson, Head of Ericsson Antenna System, Ericsson, said in a statement. Ericssons antenna system is designed as a solution for network impact, helping communications service providers improve coverage and capacity, strengthen uplink performance, use spectrum more efficiently, and reduce network energy consumption. The companys expanding antenna portfolio also supports the industrys transition toward more intelligent, programmable and energy-efficient networks. Ericsson said it will continue to strengthen its antenna ecosystem in India, and advance local engineering, manufacturing, and export capabilities while supporting communication service providers in building high-performing, energy-efficient, and future-ready networks.

articleTitle: Texas executes 46-year-old, first US execution since Christa Pike survived lethal injection
articleFeaturedImageAlt: This photo provided by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice shows Jamaal Howard on Oct. 28, 2022.
description: Before the drugs were administered, Jamaal Howard apologised repeatedly to members of his victim’s family, who were watching from a room just a few feet from the execution chamber.
body_raw: Texas executed Jamaal Howard on Wednesday evening putting the 46-year-old to death for killing a convenience store clerk during a robbery in 2000. According to Associated Press,Howard was pronounced dead at 8.03 pm at the state prison in Huntsville after receiving a lethal dose of pentobarbital. He became the 30th person executed in the United States this year and the first since Tennessees failed attempt to execute Christa Pike last week. Before the drugs were administered, Howard apologised repeatedly to members of his victims family, who were watching from a room just a few feet from the execution chamber. He said, I wish that you accept my apology and I wish for your forgiveness.Im sorry for what happened. I wish you can learn to forgive me one of these days. He thanked his family and friends and said he was ready to find peace and the Lord. He ended his final statement by telling those watching to enjoy life. Jamaal Howards execution As the pentobarbital began flowing, Howard took several breaths and gasped. He then began making snoring sounds, coughed and resumed breathing heavily before the sounds gradually became quieter. Within 30 seconds he stopped moving and was pronounced dead 19 minutes later. Howards sister, who was among those watching the execution, became distressed and said, Get me out of here. And then officers helped her leave the witness room. How Jamaal Howard was caught Howard was sentenced to death for killing 42-year-old Vickie Swartout during a robbery at a convenience store in Silsbee, a small town about 100 miles northeast of Houston. Howard was 20 when he entered the store in 2000 and shot Swartout once in the chest. According to court records, he took 114 and a carton of cigarettes. Surveillance footage of the shooting was taken as evidence at his trial. His lawyers made several last-minute attempts to stop the execution, including arguments that Howard was intellectually disabled and that Texas use of pentobarbital posed concerns similar to those raised by the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee. The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals rejected two late challenges over the states execution drugs. His lawyers also appealed to the US Supreme Court, arguing that he should not be executed because of an intellectual disability. The Supreme Court declined to intervene late Wednesday, clearing the way for the execution, as per AP reports. Latest development in Christa Pikes case Tennessee inmate Christa Pike was expected to die last week in a Tennessee execution chamber. Instead, after surviving two lethal injections, the 50-year-old death row prisoner has begun speaking from a hospital bed, leaving her family, lawyers and doctors shocked and raising questions about what happens now. According to one of her lawyers Randy Spivey, Pike was declared brain dead on Monday. Her team was told that life support would be removed the next day. But then on Tuesday morning everything changed. To the shock of everyone, including me, including her team and including the medical team, Christa woke up and began talking, her lawyer Spivey said at a press conference on Wednesday. Her first words after waking up was, Where am I? And who are you? Pike is now conscious but seriously ill. Her lawyers said she has pneumonia and a blood clot in one arm. She cannot swallow or move, while both her hands and arms are severely swollen. There is a long road to recovery, Spivey said. Her lawyer said she is angry and confused and is trying to understand what has happened to her. She has asked about her legal team and about the victim Colleen Slemmers family, Pike was convicted of killing in 1995. Despite her condition, Pike remains physical restraint to her hospital bed, her lawyers said. Medical staff have reportedly asked prison officials to remove the restraints, but those requests have been denied. What happened after the lethal injections failed Pike was taken from Tennessees execution chamber to hospital last Wednesday after prison officials administered two doses of the barbiturate pentobarbital, intended to kill her. Witnesses said Pike appeared to struggle after the first injection, with her heavy breathing. She was later taken to hospital after the second dose also failed to kill her. Spivey said that the execution attempt was cruel and torturous. He said seven needles had been used in Pikes left arm and that one appeared to have been bent when it was removed. Pike had also complained during the procedure that her arms were burning. Her lawyers had warned before the execution that finding a suitable vein could be difficult and that the process could cause her severe pain. Medical experts have since speculated that some of the drug may have entered tissue rather than a vein, that a vein may have ruptured, or that there could have been a problem with the drug itself. The exact reason for the failed execution remains unclear. A new legal battle in Pikes case While Pike fights to recover, her lawyers have begun preparing for another battle in court. During a hearing in Nashville on Wednesday, Judge IAshea Myles ordered Tennessee officials to preserve evidence from the attempted execution, including anything that was inside the execution chamber. Pikes legal team accused state officials of secreting away evidence that could become important if the state seeks to execute her again. According to her another lawyer Luke Ihnen, The motion that we filed is just to preserve evidence. Its the very first step of what will be a long legal battle we presume. Ihnen said the state had not promised that Pike would not face another execution. He argued that preserving evidence was therefore crucial to any future legal challenge.

articleTitle: When Nana Patekar said he ‘never found time to live’: ‘Zindagi udhar ki hai’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nana Patekar
description: Commenting on the life of an artiste, Nana Patekar said, “Humari zindagi udhar ki hai na (Our life belongs to others, doesn’t it?)". He said the applause will stop the day one dies.
body_raw: Veteran actor Nana Patekar died at the age of 75. The actor, who dedicated nearly five decades to the film industry, first took up acting to grab the attention of his father, Dinakar Patekar. Initially juggling theatre and work, Nana eventually chose to pursue theatre full-time. The actor, whose death has shocked the entire country, once admitted that he had never really found the time to live for himself. Speaking in an interview once, the actor said, Humari zindagi udhar ki hai na Our life belongs to others, doesnt it?. Nana Patekar Death Updates Actor Dies at 75 in Goa, Death Reason, Tributes and Funeral Updates Speaking to The Lallantop just two years ago, Nana, who was 73 at the time, said, Our life belongs to others, doesnt it? When do we ever get to live our own life? We never really found the time to live for ourselves. Today, we are living the life of one character tomorrow, it will be another character. Maybe the day we finally stop and pause, we will realise it. We will think about ourselves. But that day never comes. It becomes a habit. He added, I have said this before-when you are performing on stage, theres darkness in front of you, isnt there? We are on the stage. And perhaps that is simply the nature of an artist we have to find our own happiness in that darkness. And the echo of applause becomes an addiction. We cant break away from it. He concluded, That is life for us. The day that voice-the sound of applause-stops, that is the day we die. After that, you wont cast us anymore. You wont even take us. While many actors enter the profession driven by their passion for acting, for Nana, the journey began with a much more personal motivation he simply wanted to impress his father. He once participated in a school play about the saint Valmiki. I was one of his henchmen, Nana Patekar recalled. His performance had such an impact on him that his father travelled from the city to their village to watch him perform. I assumed that my father loved my brothers more than me. After all, I wasnt very good-looking. But when I did the Valmiki play, even though I was playing the henchman, my father travelled to our village to see me perform. I thought this was a great way to pull his attention towards me, he said. That journey continued until his final years. Nana Patekar remained actively involved in films over the years. From The Vaccine War in 2023 to the Marathi film Ole Aale in 2024, Vanvaas in the same year, Housefull 5 in 2025 and ORomeo in 2026, the veteran actor continued to remain a familiar presence on screen. He was last seen in the Anil Kapoor-starrer Subedaar, where he made a special appearance as Nana Waghmare. He was also part of filmmaker Prakash Jhas Sankalp, starring Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub, Kubbra Sait, Sanjay Kapoor and Neera Kabi, among others. The show is streaming on Amazon MX Player.

articleTitle: 3 FIRs against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka for ‘assaulting cops’ during Delhi protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during INDIA bloc MPs' protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Windsor Place near Jantar Mantar, in New Delhi on Wednesday. (ANI Photo/Amit)
description: Both leaders were detained by the police for the second consecutive day during their protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar
body_raw: At least three FIRs have been registered against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra for allegedly assaulting officers during the INDIA bloc MPs protest on Wednesday, Delhi Police sources have said. According to police officers, the FIRs were registered under sections pertaining to assault and obstructing police officers in conducting their duties. Wednesday was the second consecutive day when opposition MPs had protested, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar. It was also the second consecutive day when Rahul, Priyanka and several other senior leaders were detained by the police. Lunch, protest, then detention The MPs had initially boarded a bus after lunch at Sagar Ratna restaurant in Connaught Place, but were stopped from going towards the Election Commission office near Windsor Palace by security forces. The parliamentarians led by Rahul Gandhi got off their buses and attempted to begin an impromptu sit-in. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay on the road with a copy of the Constitution, shielded by other MPs and party workers, while her brother stood guard, pushing back the police personnel attempting to break up the protest. This is my sister, the LoP had shouted at the police. A scuffle followed with the police, with some purported videos showing Priyanka Gandhi allegedly elbowing a woman police officer. In another clip, a police officer was allegedly kicked in the back by a protester. Constable Ankit Kasana also sustained bruises during the scuffle with the MPs. Is it my mistake, doing my duty, he told mediapersons later. Both the LoP, Priyanka Gandhi, and other Opposition leaders were eventually pushed into police buses amid allegations that the police used force on them. Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra sustained injuries to her face and hands, and was seen showing her counterparts that she had been left bloodied. The Congress has called for more protests at state, district and block levels on Thursday.

articleTitle: Nana Patekar saved Rs 1.5 cr to buy car, TV report changed his life; helped 77 lakh farmers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nana Patekar
description: Nana Patekar helped over 77 lakh farmers, 51,000 disaster-relief families and supported nearly 5,000 widows through the Naam Foundation. The actor died on Thursday at the age of 75.
body_raw: With the death of Nana Patekar, fans lost their favourite actor. But for lakhs of people, they lost something more a ray of hope. Nana Patekar wasnt just an exceptional actor he had also become a source of hope for thousands of farmers and their families. Over the past decade, through the Naam Foundation, Nana helped over 77 lakh farmers, 51,000 disaster-relief families and supported nearly 5,000 widows through its widow welfare programme. It all began after the agricultural region of Marathwada in Maharashtra suffered devastating crop losses and farmer deaths in the summer of 2015. Maharashtra recorded 3,228 farmer suicides that year, with Marathwada alone accounting for 1,130. At the time, Nana was preparing to buy a luxury car. But one night, something he saw on television changed the purpose of his life forever. I had saved up Rs 1.5 crore with the intention of buying a new car. In the evening, I was sipping my drink and watching television. They were playing an interview with the family members of a farmer who had died by suicide. More than the mourning for the dead, I could feel their starvation. It was visible in their eyes, the actor told The Lallantop. The images and their pain unsettled Nana, who was living a vastly different, more privileged life at the time. Suddenly, the luxury he had been accustomed to felt meaningless. That scared me and made me think Why do I need this car? I decided to donate Rs 15,000 each to 1,000 farmers. However, my friend advised me to first meet the women who had lost their husbands before distributing the cheques, and that changed my life, he recalled. ALSO READ Nana Patekar Death Updates Nana Patekar will be accorded state funeral, PM Narendra Modi remembers his intensity, individuality The experience prompted Nana, along with actor Makrand Anaspure, to start the Naam Foundation. Nana soon realised that handing out a single cheque of Rs 15,000 would not solve the larger problems faced by farmers and their families. What began as an attempt to help a few families soon grew into a much larger movement. Within two months, the foundation collected Rs 60 crore. And these are not some big industrialists, but the middle class and lower middle class people who helped, Nana said. Speaking to The Indian Express in 2016, Nana said the response had been overwhelming. We have set up an account for NAAM Foundation and in a day nearly Rs 80 lakh was collected. Its not true that people are not willing to help those affected, its just that theyre not assured if their money goes to the right place or not. But now they have faith in us that were doing honest work. Nana didnt just raise money to support farmers he also became their voice and advocate, repeatedly speaking about the circumstances that pushed many of them towards suicide. Speaking to NDTV in 2016, Nana said, When I see the farmers, I dont see them, I see myself. I understand why they take such drastic steps. I can see that they cannot afford to buy medicines for their family, food for their children, hay for their cattle. I can see their hopelessness, their shame in it. And for a man, that is a horrible feeling. He feels as if theres nothing left for him. He feels helpless, and thats when his hand goes towards the noose. He also urged people not to look away from the crisis and encouraged them to take responsibility for the welfare of farmers. Speaking at an event at Sanjay Ghodawat University, Nana said, When one accepts the reality of death, life becomes beautiful. Dont look away from farmer suicides or other crises. Face the hard truths. Thats when you start living with real purpose. Even as he continued to act, Nana maintained his association with the foundation and its work. In May this year, while addressing the Jal Kranti Parishad in Nagpur, he spoke about how the work had changed his own understanding of happiness. The happiness Naam Foundation has given me is greater than all awards and money from cinema, he said. Naam Foundation also made headlines for providing financial assistance to the families of Army and paramilitary personnel. Nana, in association with the Army, also participated in initiatives aimed at improving educational opportunities for children living in remote areas near the Line of Control following the abrogation of Article 370. For Nana Patekar, acting may have given him fame, awards and recognition. But his work beyond cinema gave him something he valued even more a sense of purpose. And for the millions who saw him as more than an actor, his loss is not merely the loss of a familiar face on screen. It is the loss of someone who chose to turn his privilege into a lifeline for others.

articleTitle: India is signing bilateral investment treaties again. What changed after the 2016 reset?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Modi UAE treaty
description: India is revisiting its bilateral investment treaty framework after terminating dozens of pacts a decade ago. New agreements show greater flexibility on when foreign investors can seek international arbitration.
body_raw: A decade after unilaterally terminating multiple bilateral investment treaties BITs signed between 2016 and 2017, India has kicked off a significant overhaul of its investment treaty network. There are now expectations that the government would seal 4-5 agreements by year-end. Following the 2025-26 Union Budget announcement of undertaking the review of 2016 model BIT to make it more investor-friendly and attract sustained foreign investment, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said the new BIT template would be approved by the Cabinet shortly. However, a number of fresh agreements, including with Saudi Arabia, Israel and the UAE, have already been signed keeping this new framework in mind. So, what is a bilateral investment treaty? A bilateral investment treaty or a BIT is an agreement between two countries which spells out the rules governing private investment in either nation from companies in the other. As such, they help promote, protect, and provide clarity to foreign investments. Amid sharp slowdown in net inflow of investments, the new pacts show the countrys readiness to a higher degree of flexibility when it comes to exhaustion of local remedies ELR - a rule which requires a foreign investor to seek redress in the host states domestic courts or administrative bodies before bringing an international claim. While India agreed to a three year ELR rule in its BIT with the UAE in 2024, an investor from Saudi Arabia, as per the deal finalised last week can approach international arbitration in two years. The deal comes amid expectation of Saudi investment in Indian refineries. Cautious approach to BITs This comes as trade partners have even sought a one year ELR rule under the treaty, but India has not agreed to such demands so far. After the conclusion of BIT with Saudi Arabia, a government official said India-Saudi Arabia BIT would provide legal certainty and protect the interests of investors of either country in the territory of another. The 2-years exhaustion of local remedies requirements provides investors enhanced access to the Investor State Dispute Settlement ISDS mechanism. At the same time, the agreement carefully balances investor protection with the States right to regulate in the public interest, thereby preserving sufficient policy space for sovereign governance, the official said. Investor State Dispute Settlement is a mechanism designed to protect foreign investments by allowing investors to bring claims against host states for alleged treaty violations. Indias insistence of a five-year ELR after terminating BITs in 2016-17 had been a major challenge flagged by foreign investors. Prabhash Ranjan, Professor at Jindal Global Law School said that India should have a uniform treaty practice on this issue. The model BIT should provide for a one to two year period for pursuing local remedies, and no more. Furthermore, the overall limitation period to bring an ISDS claim should not be too strict. It should be something that is workable for foreign investors, Ranjan said. State vs investors While several partners have criticized Indias decision to terminate scores of BITs unilaterally, balancing state and inventors rights has been a key challenge for India and several other developing nations after a spate of adverse orders from international courts. India was not the only country to terminate BITs in the past. Developing countries like South Africa and Indonesia also did the same to preserve policy space as the decisions by international tribunals were seen to be encroaching on domestic policy space. Jos Miguel Ahumada and Ha-Joon Chang in their research report titled A New International Economic Order said that the Global South economies face significantly tighter constraints and often their efforts to establish regulatory frameworks that compel technology transfer from FDI to domestic productive networks are obstructed by the legal architecture of BITs and ISDS mechanisms. Ahumada and Chang pointed out that there is compelling evidence that the tribunals tend to favor foreign corporations over state rights, impose substantial legal defense costs on states, establish strict limitations on national policy space, and generate a regulatory chilling effect on host countries. Indeed, recent actions by the rich economies are proving the limitations of the current system. The EU has withdrawn from the Energy Charter Treaty because its ISDS is considered incompatible with the Paris Agreements. Similarly, the United States and Canada removed ISDS clauses from the USMCA United StatesMexicoCanada Agreement, and New Zealand has opted out of ISDS provisions in the CPTPP Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership. In this sense, a new order should institutionalize this wave of exits and reestablish the national level as the primary scale for regulating FDI foreign direct investment, the reports said. Arbitration at the heart of BIT debate RV Anuradha, Partner at Clarus Law Associates said that rule mandating specific time periods for exhaustion of local remedies can be a way for the government to effectively assess the nature of the dispute and try to resolve genuine investor grievances - thereby pre-empting the move to ISDS arbitration. But any provision such as this in our BITs will be effective only if there is a fast-tracking of investor disputes. Such fast tracking will need a statutory basis. Practically speaking, it would not be possible to deal with investor concerns based on the investors nationality. The judicial process will treat all investors on equal footing. A foreign investor cannot claim preference to be heard by Indian courts based on a BIT provision, Anuradha said. What we need, therefore, is a statutorily backed mechanism which is available for all investors - regardless of whether they are Indian or foreign investors, Anuradha said, adding that timely grievance redressal can in fact potentially have a dispute preventionmitigation effect. Before the 2016 model, India had signed bilateral investment treaties with 83 countries based on the model BIT of 1993, and as amended in 2003. Out of these, 74 were ratified. Among these 74 BITs, notice of termination was issued to 68 countries with request to re-negotiate based on the 2016 model, according to government data shared in the Parliament in March 2023. Since the revised 2016 model, India has signed BITs with Belarus, Kyrgyz Republic, Investment Cooperation and Facilitation Treaty ICFT with Brazil, the UAE and Uzbekistan, a Lok Sabha reply from April 2025 showed. In the BIT with the UAE, the window for exhaustion of local remedies was reduced to three years from five. A Bilateral Investment Agreement has also been signed between India Taipei Association and Taipei Economic and Cultural Centre, it said.

articleTitle: ‘The Orange Plague’: Naked Trump statue unveiled near European Parliament
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Trump naked statue in Europe
description: Created by Danish sculptor Jens Galschiøt, the eight-foot-long sculpture depicts US President Donald Trump holding a golf club in one hand and the scales of justice in the other.

articleTitle: Sonali Kulkarni says a scolding on Taxi No. 9211 set launched lifelong bond with Nana Patekar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sonali kulkarni Nana Patekar death
description: In an exclusive conversation with SCREEN, actress Sonali Kulkarni spoke about her friendship with Nana Patekar.
body_raw: Actor Sonali Kulkarni, who has shared screen with veteran actor Nana Patekar is unable to process his loss. Nana, 75, died after suffering a cardiac arrest in Goa early on Thursday morning. Nana was at his family home when his health deteriorated. He was rushed to the hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for 45 minutes. The senior actor was declared dead at 520 am. In an exclusive conversation with SCREEN, the actress spoke about their friendship, and shared some beautiful memories from their time together. Sonali Kulkarni on Nana Patekars death Sonali and Nana have worked together in several Marathi films, and also shared screen space in Taxi No. 9211. Talking about their friendship, Sonali expressed her sadness and said, I still cant process what I have heard. What would it mean, Nana sir, not being with us? I dont know. I will take time to process this. We have worked on three projects Taxi No. 9211, Deool, which won the National Award for Best Film, and the third was Dr Prakash Baba Amte. Nana sir had also come for my book publication and spoke so fondly about it. I have seen the change - from me being scared of someone called Nana Patekar to him becoming so close to me and my family. I have had a beautiful friendship with him. I knew him well enough to the extent of making fun of him. He was a dear friend who had complete authority to call me anytime. Also Read Hours before death, Nana Patekar messaged friend at 230 am he was unwell View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nana Patekar nanapatekarfc I am happy for him he would have hated to be ill or hospitalized, and recover. He was always fit, passionate, and easy. Now, he will meet his dear mother, and all the farmers who committed suicide I am sure he will scold all of them. I am still not able to believe that we are talking about a man who won a Padma Shri award not being there, Sonali Kulkarni added. Sonali on working with Nana Patekar in Taxi No. 9211 Recalling a memory of working with him in Taxi No. 9211, Sonali said, I have seen him act in a very unscripted manner. I remember a scene from Taxi No. 9211 where I leave him, he comes to meet me, and the train has already gone. The kind of longing, pathos, and loss he had on his face said a lot about him as an actor. He was so funny in films like Welcome I always appreciated his comedy, and he enjoyed that compliment. He lived life on his own terms. One thing he did very nicely was give love, splurge money, and give compliments abundantly he never counted these things. She also recalled, Taxi No 9211 was my first film with Nana sir. I was a little scared because Id never worked with him. He and John Abraham were already shooting when I was called for a look test. When I wore the costume and exited my vanity van, Nana sir saw me. He said, Makeup utaar. Itna make up nahi chalega I just said impromptu, Maine makeup kia bhi nahi hai, sir My hairdresser said, Kisko jawab de rahi hai Take it easy. But it somehow set the tone for what our characters shared in the movie. It was a very nice nok-jhok throughout the film. View this post on Instagram A post shared by SCREEN ieentertainment Sonali went on to praise the actor and said, I got a lot of screen time to understand this person and actor. Hes so nice. He only wants some love and a chocolate. If you give a good shot, thats a good chocolate for him. He thrives on his co-actors performance. Hes a very performance-hungry actor. He told me about his journey, and I agreed with him. He had no looks or glamour that industry demanded, but thrived on his performances. His struggle was his struggle, but I enjoyed all three films with him. Our chemistry is totally different in all of them. Its hilarious in Deool. In front of other people, Im a decent wife. But in front of him, Im like, Tu kaun hai re? laughs. Sonali on Nana Patekars philanthropic work and memories from Deool Speaking fondly about Nana Patekar, Sonali also mentioned his philanthropic work and said, His heart was beating for the farmers who were thinking of committing suicide. He worked a lot through the NAAM Foundation. As much as he gave to society and farmers, he didnt get back the same amount of love. He never bothered about what he got in return he loved everyone unconditionally. He lived life without any worries, so it will take us some time to fill that void. She even recalled their bond when they worked on the Marathi film Deool. I have a beautiful picture of Nana sir when he came to meet me after I delivered my daughter Kaveri. It was hilarious. When we were promoting Deool, I was pregnant throughout the film. From the day he learned I was pregnant, first he got upset that I didnt tell him, then he took so much care of me. For the films launch, I had gone to PVR with my mother I was eight and a half months pregnant, and he was laughing. He said it was the first time he was posing with a heroine who was heavily pregnant. Deool was released on my birthday, and it was my first outing after my daughter was born he insisted and made sure I saw the film with my husband, Nachiket. Once he had come to see my daughter when she was two months old, he came in an auto. The auto driver didnt realize that Nana Patekar was sitting behind until Sir got off and asked him to wait for 30 minutes. When he figured it was Nana Patekar, he started trembling. When Nana sir was leaving, the auto-driver was unable to drive, so he told him, itna darta kyun hai, main chalau kya? and we laughed a lot. He has always loved me a lot, Sonali added as she got emotional. While the industry has been mourning Nana Patekars loss, the veteran actor will be laid to rest with state honors. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, CM Devendra Fadnavis, Amit Shah, Smriti Irani, and many others have also expressed their grief on Nana Patekars demise.

articleTitle: INDIA bloc lunch at Delhi’s Connaught Place, a hat-trick of SIR protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: INDIA bloc, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi
description: Sources said there'll be a protest after lunch, just like Wednesday. "It will be decided during lunch where we will protest and how," said a source
body_raw: A day after the INDIA bloc MPs lunch meet at Sagar Ratna in Janpath became the prelude to a dramatic street protest, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has again invited Opposition MPs for lunch, this time at Moets in Connaught Place on Thursday. I invite your good self and all your members in both LS and RS for lunch today i.e. 8 October 2026 at 1.45 pm at Moets K-14, Outer Circle, Connaught Place, New Delhi, the invite from the Congress chief said. The back-to-back invites suggest that the Congress and its allies want to keep the pressure on the government as it steps up its campaign for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over issues linked to the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter rolls. Sources said therell be a protest after lunch, just like Wednesday. It will be decided during lunch where we will protest and how. More MPs and parties, including the Samajwadi Party, are scheduled to join us, said the source. The Samajwadi Party had skipped Wednesdays lunch. Protest timeline MPs of the INDIA bloc took out a march to the Election Commission on Tuesday. Police stopped them midway, but Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi and his sister and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra managed to enter the Akashvani Bhavan premises and stayed there for hours. The sit-in, which the Congress said was an impromptu plan, eventually ended when police detained the siblings and the Congress leaders with them and shifted them to a police station. They were released later. On Tuesday, a lunch hosted by Congress chief Kharge became a rendezvous for INDIA bloc MPs, who then headed to Jantar Mantar. The Gandhis, Mamata TMCs Derek OBrien, CPIMs John Brittas and CPIs Sandosh Kumar were among the MPs who joined the protest on Wednesday. Police stopped them near Windsor Place, leading to dramatic scenes. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay on the road, clutching a copy of the Constitution. And Rahul Gandhi said the protests wont stop till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. The protesting MPs were detained on Wednesday, too, and later released. Wednesdays lunch plan will be attended by more MPs, and a much larger protest than Tuesdays may follow, sources in the Opposition have said. Also, the Cockroach Janta Party, which led the mega protest against paper leaks in Jantar Mantar in July, has called for another agitation on October 10. This will then be a week of protests in Delhi on the same issue. A unity message through lunch The lunch invites, besides becoming a rendezvous for Opposition MPs, are also sending a message of unity in the INDIA bloc. The Gandhis sit-in at Akashvani Bhavan had grabbed headlines, but left some Opposition parties grumbling. The Indian Express reported that some Opposition leaders felt the INDIA bloc protest on Tuesday became a Rahul Gandhi show because of the siblings sit-in while other Opposition leaders were detained. Senior Congress leaders then reached out to INDIA bloc allies and told them that the Akashvani Bhavan sit-in was an unplanned move. Some questions, however, remain. DMK, which broke up with Congress after the Tamil Nadu poll results, and AAP have stayed away from the INDIA bloc protests. The DMK, however, is blowing hot and cold, with one of its spokespersons praising Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday. The AAP faces a poll fight against the Congress in Punjab and will weigh its options before deciding on joining the INDIA bloc campaign. The Samajwadi Party joined the march on Tuesday, but was conspicuously absent on Wednesday. Party MPs have blamed Congresss poor coordination for this. The allies are also locked in a tussle over seat-sharing for the Uttar Pradesh election, but party leaders say that was not why they skipped Wednesdays lunch. They pointed out that many of them had left Delhi by the time the lunch was planned. Congress leaders, too, downplayed the Samajwadi Partys absence, saying that the lunch was planned late.

articleTitle: Delhi Police bans gatherings at Rajghat after Congress announces protest against EC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Police detain Congress supporters during a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. (ANI)
description: Delhi Police bans gatherings at Mahatma Gandhi memorial after Congress announces protest against EC
body_raw: Congress and other INDIA bloc MPs began arriving for a second consecutive lunch meeting in Delhi on Thursday, with leaders expected to march to Rajghat afterwards to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The meeting is being hosted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. Congress MP Kodikunnil Suresh said the Opposition would continue its protest and demanded Gyanesh Kumars resignation. He said the next strategy would be decided at the meeting, with Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc leaders expected to lead the subsequent protest. The meeting comes a day after Delhi Police stopped an INDIA bloc march towards Jantar Mantar and detained several Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi. Police said three FIRs have been registered over the protest, including allegations of assault and manhandling of police personnel, obstruction of government work and misbehaviour. Sources in the INDIA bloc told The Indian Express that MPs from the alliance will meet for lunch at Moets restaurant in Connaught Place, a day after a lunch gathering turned into a street protest. Those expected to attend include TMCs Derek OBrien and Mahua Moitra, CPIMs John Brittas, IUMLs ET Mohammed Basheer, CPIs P Sandosh Kumar, and Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Mallikarjun Kharge. The Samajwadi Party has sent two representatives for the lunch being hosted by Mallikarjun Kharge.Ghosi MP Rajeev Rai and Rampur MP Mohibbullah Nadvi will be in attendance. Rai confirmed to The Indian Express that the two MPs have been told by the party to attend the lunch. We are going there, said Rai. This comes a day after the SP skipped Wednesdays lunch and protest led by the Congress in Delhi demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumars resignation.
